<header>Preface</header>

## Preface -

All forms of knowledge are called <term>Veda</term> <note>literally "knowledge," referring to the primary sacred texts of Hinduism</note>, which are divided into six parts known as <term>Vedanga</term> <note>the "limbs" or auxiliary disciplines of the Vedas</note>. Among them, <term>Jyotish</term> <note>Astrology and Astronomy</note> is considered the eye, as stated by the great sage Narada—

> "The stainless and pure science of light (Jyotish) is the clear eye of the Veda, consisting of three branches: Siddhanta (Theory), Samhita (Compilation), and Hora (Predictive). Without this, no Vedic or traditional rituals can be successfully accomplished. Therefore, for the welfare of the world, this was created by Brahma in ancient times." <note>original Sanskrit: "Siddhānta-saṃhitā-horā-rūpaṃ skandhatrayātmakam..."</note>

Jyotish has two parts: <term>Ganita</term> <note>Mathematics/Astronomy</note> and <term>Phalita</term> <note>Predictive Astrology</note>. Because mathematics is definitive, it is called <term>Siddhanta</term> <note>established conclusion or doctrine</note>, such as the *Surya-Siddhanta* and others. Because predictive astrology is stated based on the strength of inference, it is called <term>Sambhavanatmaka</term> <note>probabilistic or based on possibility</note>. It has two parts: that in which collective results are stated is called <term>Samhita</term>, and that in which individual life results [differing for every human or living being based on their specific birth-ascendant (Hora)] are stated is called <term>Hora</term> or the <term>Jataka Skandha</term> <note>the branch of natal horoscopy</note>. Human society generally does not have as much interest in understanding collective results as it does in knowing the auspicious or inauspicious future results of its own lives. Nowadays, Western scientists, having researched Indian predictive astrology, have also come to the firm belief that all auspicious or inauspicious events occurring on Earth (such as abundance or famine) happen only through the mutual radiation-contact of the planets and constellations in the sky. Because planets and constellations are luminous, they are called <term>Jyotish</term> <note>derived from 'Jyoti' meaning light</note>. Lexicographers have said— *'Jyotir-brahmani vishveshe nakshatra-graha-mandale'* <note>Light refers to the Supreme Spirit, the Lord of the Universe, and the circle of stars and planets</note>. The study related to this is called <term>Jyotish</term>.

## The Purpose of Astrology -

> "The purpose of the science of light is the prediction of auspicious and inauspicious results. And that, the ancient sages have said, is dependent on the strength of the Ascendant (Lagna). The equal divisions of the zodiac are called the twelve signs. The rising of these signs—Aries, Taurus, etc.—is called the Lagna." <note>original Sanskrit: "Śubhāśubhaphalādeśo jyotiḥśāstra-prayojanam..."</note>

The zodiac sign (group of constellations and planets) that is attached to the rising horizon at the time of a creature's birth is called the <term>Lagna</term> <note>Ascendant</note>. For a detailed description of this, see the book titled *'Sodaharana Lagnaviveka'* <note>Discernment of the Ascendant with Examples</note>. Here, we provide only a brief description of the <term>Jataka Shastra</term> <note>Natal Astrology</note> as described by the sages (in the form of life-results for living beings). In the scriptures and Puranas, the title of <term>Rishi</term> <note>Sage/Seer</note> is given only to those whose teachings are definitively true and who are themselves without doubt in their knowledge of the subject. For example, in ancient times Narada, Vasistha, etc., and in the Kali Yuga <note>the current age in Hindu cosmology</note>, Parashara. The words of all these were generally always true; therefore, people accept their teachings as <term>Shastra</term> <note>Sacred Scripture/Science</note> and place their faith in them. However, in the opinion of the learned, the only scripture worthy of trust is that which is <term>Pramanasangata</term> <note>consistent with evidence</note>. There are three types of evidence: Word (Testimony), Inference, and Direct Perception. Those who believe where only 'Word' (Scripture or the word of a perfected person) is the evidence are considered <term>Astika</term> <note>Orthodox/Theist</note>, otherwise they are considered 'Nastika' <note>Heterodox/Atheist</note>. It has also been said—

It defines the "Lagna" (Ascendant) as the foundation for individual horoscopy and discusses the requirements for authoritative scripture.</summary>

<meta>This page serves as the preface to a commentary on the Brihat Jataka, establishing the author's rationale for a new Hindi translation and addressing historical discrepancies in astrological texts.</meta>

<page-num>10</page-num>
<header>Preface</header>

->“In those sciences which are not perceptible to the senses, there is only dispute;<-
->But Astronomy/Astrology is a visible science, where the stars and planets are the evidence.”<-
<note>original: "यान्यप्रत्यक्षशास्त्राणि विवादस्तत्र केवलः । प्रत्यक्षं ज्योतिषं यत्र प्रमाणं तारकाग्रहाः ।।"</note>

One only trusts evidence when it is perceptible. Now, listen regarding the evidence of words (scriptural testimony). For example: “Liberation is attained by dying in Kashi.” “The sins accumulated over ten million births are destroyed by bathing in the Ganges.”

No one can show or see this perceptibly. In the science of <term>Jyotish</term> <note>Vedic astrology and astronomy</note>, even the words of a Sage are considered unacceptable if they contradict direct perception. As Kamalakara says:
->“In this science, even a statement made by a Sage should not be accepted if it is contradicted by observation.”<-
<note>original: "सुयुक्ता न मुन्युक्तरप्यत्र शास्त्रे भवेत् कार्यवर्यस्य या दृग्विरुद्धा।"</note>

After Parashara, <term>Varahamihira</term> <note>a 6th-century Indian astronomer and polymath</note>, a member of King Vikramaditya’s court, took the subjects of the Jataka (horoscopy) texts composed by the Sages and arranged them into various meters of his own creation, naming it ‘<term>Horashastra</term>’. However, finding that work somewhat extensive, he wrote a condensed version of all the subjects described therein. The introductory sentences of that work are:
->“Having examined the scriptures, I composed the Horashastra in various meters;<-
->I shall now proclaim the essence of that very work in Arya verses.”<-
<note>original: "होराशास्त्रं वृत्तैर्मया निबद्धं निरीक्ष्य शास्त्राणि । यत् तस्याप्यार्याभिः सारमहं संप्रवक्ष्यामि ।।"</note>

Because it was small, people named it ‘Svalpa Jataka’, and the previously composed <term>Horashastra</term> was named ‘<term>Brihat Jataka</term>’ <note>The Great Birth Story/Large Compendium</note>. Among the Jataka texts composed by teachers other than the ancient Sages, this one (<term>Brihat Jataka</term>) is considered the best. Due to human nature, <term>Varahamihira</term> occasionally faced confusion and doubt regarding the meaning of the Sages' words. For instance, in the ‘Chapter on Non-Human Births’, the Sages mentioned specific planetary combinations after observing non-human births (animals, birds, or even trees and shrubs) from a human womb. Similarly, in the ‘Chapter on Shape Combinations’, he doubted combinations like the Vajra (Thunderbolt) and Yava (Barley), and wrote critical words regarding the Sages:
->“I have described the Vajra and other combinations according to the ancient scriptures;<-
->But how can Mercury and Venus be in the fourth house from the Sun?” etc.<-
<note>original: "पूर्वशास्त्रानुसारेण मया वज्रादयः कृताः । चतुर्थे भवनेसूर्याज्ज्ञ-सितौभवतः कथम्? ।।"</note>

Nevertheless, it is superior in many respects to other Jataka texts. We have provided a resolution to these issues with logical reasoning in our Hindi commentary. Although ‘Bhatta Utpala’ has written a Sanskrit commentary on it, even he remained confused in those places of error. Despite this, his work is extremely suitable for Sanskrit scholars. For the understanding of the general public, I have also prepared a Hindi commentary named ‘<term>Sararthadipikakhya</term>’ <note>The Lamp of Essential Meanings</note>. I am confident that the entire public will surely benefit from this commentary. Finally, in the editing of this commentary—specifically in the examples, mathematics, and proof-reading—Pandit Juharilal Vishwambhar (Veda-Jyotishacharya), Arjun Jha ‘Pathik’ B.A. (Jyotishacharya), and Mannalal Abhimanyu (M.A.) provided their cooperation. Therefore, I express my gratitude to these three individuals and, as is human nature, I seek forgiveness for my own errors.

Varanasi, Thursday &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Sincerely—
Samvat 2031, Chaitra Shukla 5 <note>Approx. March 1974</note> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Sitaram Jha

## Composed by the Great Astrologer Varahamihira

# **The Brihat Jataka**
<note>The Great Compendium of Natal Astrology</note>

### The "Sarartha Deepika" Sanskrit Commentary by Bhattotpala
### Including a Hindi Explanation

---

The auspicious invocation and statement of purpose by the astrologer Bhattotpala:
->Having bowed to Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva, the Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter,<-
->Venus, Saturn, Ganesha, and the Teachers;<-
->I shall fully explain that compendium written by the resident of Ujjain <note>original: "Avantika"</note>,<-
->whose intellect was purified by the great grace of the Sun God. ||1||<-

To that Radiant Sun, whom those skilled in liberation <note>spiritual seekers</note> describe thus: "The science of the stars which the Sun originally created in three vast branches <note>The three branches or 'skandhas' are Astronomy/Mathematics, Omens, and Horoscopy</note>, he—fearing its destruction in the Kali Yuga <note>the current dark age in Hindu cosmology</note>—returned to this earth and recomposed it all in a concise form under the guise of Varahamihira." ||2||

Because those of small intellect, though greedy for the meaning, wander aimlessly in the ocean of Varahamihira—which is turbulent with the waters of many variations, filled with the sea-monsters of planets and constellations, and shining with the gems of numerous planetary yogas <note>special planetary combinations</note>—I, Utpala, hereby construct a raft in the form of this commentary using my own understanding. ||3||

In this science, the "Relationship, Subject Matter, and Purpose" <note>term: Sambandha-Abhidheya-Prayojana; a traditional Sanskrit scholarly framework for introducing a text</note> are stated as follows:
The **Relationship** is defined by the signifier and the signified; the signified is the meaning and the signifier is the word. Alternatively, the relationship is that of means and end: this scripture is the means, and the resulting knowledge is the end. Or, the relationship is that it is a Limb of the Veda <note>term: Vedanga; astrology is considered the 'eye' of the Vedas</note> descended from Brahma and others.

The **Subject Matter** <note>Abhidheya</note> consists of: understanding the nature of the zodiac signs, the Horas, Drekkana, Navamsha, Dwadashabhaga, and Trimshatbhaga <note>various divisional charts used in Vedic astrology</note>; the nature of the planets; the strength and weakness of planets and signs; animal births; the moment of conception; amazing effects at the time of birth; longevity and its afflictions; planetary periods <note>Dashas</note> and sub-periods; the Eight-fold divisions <note>Ashtakavarga</note>; livelihoods; Royal Yogas; celestial combinations; lunar combinations; combinations of two or more planets; asceticism; the character of the signs; the results of planetary aspects; the results of the twelve houses; miscellaneous topics; inauspicious combinations; female horoscopy; and the qualities of the decans <note>Drekkanas</note> at death.

The **Purpose** <note>Prayojana</note> is to manifest the ripening of the past karma <note>actions</note> of people. By telling the good and bad fortunes to a worthy recipient, one achieves success in this world and the next. Why are these things stated? It is said: because by stating the Relationship, Subject Matter, and Purpose, faith is born in the hearts of the listeners regarding the subject of the scripture. As it is said regarding the meaning of mantras: "Since the success of the listeners' engagement comes from stating the relationship, therefore, in all scriptures, the relationship is stated first." If one asks what the subject matter here is...

# Brihat Jataka - Chapter on the Divisions of the Signs

By someone. "If the purpose is not explained to him, the study becomes fruitless. For any scripture or any action, as long as the objective is not stated, who will accept it?" <note>This refers to the 'Anubandha Chatushtaya' or the four preliminary considerations of a classical text: subject, goal, relation, and eligible student.</note> Regarding who is eligible for this science, it is said: only the twice-born <note>term: Dvija (Twice-born); referring to the three upper social classes who undergo the sacred thread ceremony</note>. Since they must study and understand the Veda with its six limbs. What are these limbs? It is said: ***"Phonetics, Ritual, Grammar, Etymology, the movement of the Heavenly Bodies (Astronomy/Astrology), and Prosody are called the six limbs of the Veda."***

And so it is said in the limb itself: "The Vedas are directed toward the performance of sacrifices, and sacrifices are prescribed according to the sequence of time. Since this science is the instrument for determining time, he who knows Astrology knows the sacrificial rites." Astrology is indeed a limb of the Veda. Now, why is the status of being a Vedic limb attributed to Astrology? It is explained: because it declares the auspicious times for solar and lunar eclipses, the sun's entry into signs, various astronomical junctions, the "Elephant's Shadow" <note>a rare and holy astronomical alignment</note>, the eleventh day of the lunar fortnight, the new moon, and so on; because it reveals the timing of sacrifices; and because it declares the timing for other actions mentioned in the Hearkened (Shruti), Remembered (Smriti), and Ancient (Purana) scriptures.

Thus, in the *Siddhanta* of Bhaskara: "The Vedas are engaged in the work of sacrifice; the sacrifices are said to depend on time. Since the knowledge of time comes from this science, the status of a Vedic limb is granted to Astrology. Grammar is the mouth, Astrology the eyes, Etymology is called the ears, and Ritual the hands. Phonetics is the nose of this Veda, and Prosody the two lotus feet, according to the ancient wise ones. This Astrology is remembered as the Eye of the Veda, and it is called the chief among the limbs. Even if a man is possessed of other limbs like ears and nose, if he is deprived of the eye, he is nothing. Therefore, this should be studied by the twice-born; it is merit-giving, a secret, and the highest truth. The man who knows Astrology thoroughly attains Virtue, Wealth, Liberation, and Fame."

It is the conduct of the virtuous that at the beginning of a treatise, one desires the accomplishment of the intended goal through salutation, praise, and special devotion to a favored deity. Therefore, this teacher from Avanti, named the illustrious Varahamihira—a twice-born who obtained the grace of a boon from the Sun, and who, having composed the compendium of the mathematical branch of Astrology, now desires to compose the branch on Horoscopy (Natal Astrology)—speaks with a *Shardulavikridita* <note>original: "tiger-sporting" meter; a complex Sanskrit poetic meter of 19 syllables</note> verse to obtain the perfection of speech coming from the Divine Sun to his own soul, for the pacification of all obstacles:

> **He who is imagined as a Form of the Moon-bearer <note>Shiva</note>, the Path for those who will not be born again,**
**The Soul for the knowers of the Soul, the Sacrifice for the sacrificers, and the Lord of the immortal lights;**
**The Sovereign of the destruction, origin, and maintenance of the worlds, who is heard of in many ways in the Revelation;**
**May that Sun, the lamp of the three worlds, possessed of many rays, grant us speech. || 1 ||**

"He who is imagined as a Form..." etc. May that Sun, the Divine Aditya, grant or bestow speech to us. What kind of Sun? One with many rays; he who has not just one ray, meaning many rays. It means the "Thousand-Rayed One." Furthermore, what kind? The lamp of the three worlds. The three worlds are the Earth, the Atmosphere, and the Heavens; he is a lamp there due to the similarity of illuminating. Also, "imagined as a form of the Moon-bearer"—the Moon-bearer is he who bears or holds the *Shasha* (the hare-like mark), meaning the Moon...

<meta>This page continues the commentary on the opening invocation of the Brihat Jataka, focusing on the various divine and physical attributes of the Sun (Surya) as described by the commentator Bhattotpala.</meta>

<page-num>13</page-num>
<header>With the Bhashya-Bhashya commentary and the Sanskrit commentary by Bhattotpala</header>

The Moon is conceived as his form or body. It is established that "the Sun is the form of the Moon" because the Moon, being composed of water, is said to be devoid of its own light; the expansion and spread of moonlight in it is due to the reflection of the Sun's rays. As stated by the Teacher <note>referring to Varahamihira</note> himself in the *Great Compilation* <term>Brihat Samhita: a foundational encyclopedic work on omens and natural astrology</term>:

> "One half of the Moon, which is always situated below [the Sun], is made white by the rays of the Sun. The other half is dark due to its own shadow, like a pot placed in sunlight. As the Moon leaves the vicinity of the Sun, whiteness attaches to its rear. Because of the Sun, the Moon's light appears from the bottom upward during its rising. In the watery Moon, the rays of the Sun are reflected and destroy the nocturnal darkness, like rays reflected from the surface of a mirror inside a house."

And so it is said in the *Treatise of Bhaskara* <term>Bhaskara Siddhanta: a major work on Indian astronomy</term>:

> "Due to contact with the Sun's rays, this orb of nectar <note>the Moon</note> shines with moonlight in the direction of the Sun. In the other direction, it is as dark as a young girl's hair, like a pot in sunlight darkened by the shadow of its own form."

And so it is in the *Veda* <term>the most ancient sacred scriptures of Hinduism</term>: "The Sun-rayed Moon is named Sushumna." Alternatively, he is conceived as the form of the Moon-bearing Lord <note>Shiva/Mahadeva</note>. Since the Lord is "Eight-formed" <term>Ashtamurti: the eight manifestations of Shiva</term>—namely Earth, Water, Air, Fire, the Sacrificer, Space, the Moon, and the Sun—therefore the Sun is the form of the Great Lord. "Of the Moon-bearer" is the correct reading.

Furthermore, he is the **Path of those who do not return to birth.** Those who have no rebirth are the liberated ones; he is their path, meaning the Gateway to Liberation <term>Moksha</term>. For there are two types of paths: the Path of the Gods <term>Devayana</term> and the Path of the Ancestors <term>Pitriyana</term>. There, the Moon is the gateway for the Path of the Ancestors, by which those going to heaven travel. The Sun is the gateway to Liberation. For by piercing the solar orb, they become sharers of liberation and reach the gate of freedom. And so says the Holy Vyasa in the *Great Bharata* <term>Mahabharata</term>: "The gateway to heaven, the gateway to progeny, the third heaven."

He is the **Soul of the knowers of the Soul.** Those who know the Soul are the Yogis; for them, he is the Soul, the principle of consciousness. He resides within the heart in the form of light and life-breath <term>Prana</term>. And so says the Revelation <term>Shruti/Veda</term>: "The Sun is the Soul of the moving and the unmoving." The Sun alone is the soul of the world, both animate and inanimate.

He is the **Sacrifice of the sacrificers.** For those who perform sacrifices, he is the Sacrifice itself. As stated by Manu <term>the legendary lawgiver</term>:

> "An offering cast properly into the fire reaches the Sun. From the Sun, rain is born; from rain, food; and from that, living beings."

He is the **Lord of the immortal lights.** The "immortals" are the Gods; the "lights" are the planets and stars. He is their Lord, meaning their Chief. For all those of divine origin pay him attendance. The daily rising and setting of the planets and stars are solely under his control. As it is said:

> "The Sun is a globe of light; the globes of the planets, stars, and water are seen to be luminous only because they are illuminated by the Sun's rays."

Thus, due to his abundance of qualities, he is the Lord of the immortal lights. He is the **Master of the destruction, origin, and maintenance of the worlds.** The "worlds" refer to the Earth and others; he is the Master—Vishnu—in their destruction (dissolution), origin (creation), and maintenance (preservation). He is the Lord of the past, present, and future time—

# Brihat Jataka: Chapter on the Divisions of the Signs

...because it is the sign of the three divisions <note>referring to the three worlds or the three-fold time: past, present, and future</note>. The word "and" is used here for emphasis. "He who is described in many ways in the Scriptures": In the Vedas, He is recited in various forms. As the Scripture says: "They call Him Indra, Mitra, Varuna, Agni, and He is the heavenly, noble-winged Garutman. To what is One, the sages give many a title; they call it Agni, Yama, Matarishvan" <note>original Sanskrit: "इन्द्रं मित्रं वरुणमग्निमाहुरथो दिव्य: स सुपर्णो गरुत्मान्..." from Rigveda 1.164.46</note>. || 1 ||

->**Auspicious Invocation by the Editor (Vernacular Commentator)**<-

->The noble Jataka spoken by the illustrious Varāhamihira,<-
->Which was explained by Bhattotpala in the language of the gods <note>Sanskrit</note>;<-
->For the understanding of those with little knowledge of Sanskrit,<-
->Having bowed to Goddess Lakshmi, I explain it in the language of men <note>the vernacular/Hindi</note>. || 1 ||<-

**Vernacular Translation—** May that Lord Sun grant us the power of speech—He who exists reflected in the nectar-filled orb of the moon; who is the path for those seeking liberation from rebirth; the Soul of those who know the Self; the sacrificial form for the sacrificers; the sustainer of the immortals <note>the gods like Indra</note> and the lights <note>the luminous bodies, stars, and planets in the sky</note>; who is capable of the destruction, creation, and preservation of the entire universe; who is described by many names in the Vedas; and who possesses infinite rays of light and divine qualities. || 1 ||

**Special Meaning—** In many books, the reading "Shashibhuta" <note>becoming the moon</note> is found, but that is an error of the scribes. It is inconsistent to call the creator of the three gods and three worlds a mere limb of Mahadeva <note>Shiva</note>. Therefore, "Shashabhrita" <note>reflected in the moon</note> is the correct reading. Because He is reflected in the lunar disc and provides light even at night, the adjective "Lamp of the Three Worlds" is appropriate. || 1 ||

Now, wishing to avoid the charge of uselessness since this science has been treated by others, and demonstrating the superior quality of this work over other treatises, the author speaks in the *Shardulavikridita* meter:

->Though many treatises, endowed with proper grammar and logic,<-
->Have been seen by those of sharp intellect to teach the results of horoscopy;<-
->For those whose efforts have failed in crossing the vast ocean of Horoscopic Tantra,<-
->I begin this "Scripture-Boat"—brief, in varied meters, and rich in meaning. || 2 ||<-

**Commentary—** "By many..." and so on. The *Tantra* of *Hora* <note><term>Hora: The branch of astrology dealing with horoscopes and individual destiny</term></note> is *Horatantra*. Or, *Hora* itself is the *Tantra* (system). It is like a "Great Ocean" because it is difficult to cross. That by which the meaning is extended or crossed is called *Tantra*. I begin this "Scripture-Boat" for those whose efforts have been broken in the task of crossing the Great Ocean of Horoscopic Tantra. The science of horoscopy is the Great Ocean; in the matter of crossing it, I create a "Scripture-Boat" for those who have lost heart. The scripture itself is the boat. Just as a boat—

# Page 15
### Accompanied by the Sanskrit Commentary of Bhattotpala and the Hindi Language Interpretation

Just as a boat quickly brings those desiring to cross to the other shore, so does this work. It shares the characteristics of a raft for those whose efforts have been frustrated in attempting to cross the great ocean of the <term>Hora Tantra</term> <note>The system of natal astrology</note>. Why is it that even those with great effort have failed to cross the great ocean of the Hora Tantra? He answers: "By many." By many what? By those of "sharp intellect." Those whose intelligence is sharp and abundant. Even though the scriptures have been seen and contemplated for a long time. What kind of scriptures? Those "endowed with words and logic." The logic of words is <term>Shabda-Nyaya</term> <note>The science of grammar and linguistic analysis</note>, specifically <term>Mimamsa</term> <note>The school of hermeneutics or interpretation</note>. As it is said: "That power belongs to the words themselves, while logic relies upon the person." Or, "words and logic" refers to meaningful words and the system of Mimamsa; endowed or joined with these. Were they seen only once? He says: "No, many times." This means they were composed in various ways, through both expansion and contraction, and studied repeatedly. For what purpose were they seen? For the "knowledge of the results of the hour" <note>Horafala: the fruits or predictions derived from the birth chart</note> for those of sharp minds. To make those of clever intellect understand the results of the <term>Hora</term>. <term>Hora</term> refers to the ripening of past karmas; its result is <term>Horafala</term>. To know that result, whether auspicious or inauspicious. What kind of <term>Scripture-Raft</term> <note>Shastra-plava: a metaphor for a book that carries one across a sea of ignorance</note> is this? It is "brief," a small volume. Furthermore, what is it like? It is "variegated in its meters." It is charming and diverse due to meters such as <term>Shardulavikridita</term> <note>Literally 'Tiger's Sport,' a complex 19-syllable Sanskrit meter</note> and others. Therefore, its excellence lies precisely in its brevity. Because of this, their effort will not be frustrated here. By saying "brief," he shows the ease of grasping and retaining the text. As the elephant-physician Virasena says: "A scripture spoken in concise form is easy to grasp and retain." By "variegated in meters," he shows its poetic excellence. Now, one might ask: will a small scripture not have a small amount of meaning? He says: "Rich in substance," meaning it has much to communicate. For this reason, it has more weight/importance than previously composed scriptures. Otherwise, because other scriptures already exist, there would be the fault of tautology <note>repetition</note>. This is what is being said: The previously spoken scriptures are excessively vast, and therefore those whose efforts were frustrated in them are the reason I begin this "Scripture-Raft." Now, could it be that they failed because of low intelligence? Where did that idea come from? Since they failed because of the vastness of previous scriptures, this one is made small for that reason. By saying "for those of sharp minds," this is demonstrated. It is not because they lacked intelligence that their efforts failed in those scriptures; rather, it was due to the defects of the scriptures themselves. Otherwise, their efforts would be frustrated here as well. A raft that is small, in light and short meters, variegated and charming, and rich in substance—full of wealth—is extremely comfortable for those desiring to cross. || 2 ||

---

**Language Interpretation—** Even after repeatedly observing many scriptures with their own sharp intellects, including Grammar and Logic (including the reasoning of <term>Mimamsa</term> etc.), those wise men of mature intellect whose efforts were frustrated in reaching the far shore of the <term>Great Ocean</term> <note>Maharnava</note> of the <term>Hora Tantra</term> (the science indicating the results of a birth based on the rising sign)... [the text explains] the results of the Hora (life-results from the birth sign) for them.

# Brihat Jataka — Chapter on Zodiacal Variations

For the sake of knowledge, I begin the construction of this small scientific treatise, which serves as a <term>Plava</term><note>A small boat or raft</note> marked by various poetic meters. || 2 ||

**Special Meaning—** Sages such as Jaimini and Parashara have described the auspicious and inauspicious fruits of life at length based on the rising sign at birth. The teacher Varahamihira has presented the essence of all those results in a brief form. Just as large ships are built to cross the ocean but require the assistance of many others to operate, a person can board a small boat alone and, carrying their own provisions, slowly cross the sea by their own effort. Similarly, the vast scriptures created by the ancient sages require the constant guidance of teachers, but by repeatedly studying this small treatise, a wise person can understand the results of <term>Hora</term><note>Horoscopy/Astrology</note> on their own. || 2 ||

Now, explaining how the science of Horoscopy reveals the ripening of actions performed in previous lives, and demonstrating the etymology of the word by removing two letters, he speaks in the <term>Indravajra</term><note>A specific Sanskrit poetic meter</note> meter:

> Some claim the word *Hora* is derived from *Ahoratra* <note>Day and Night</note> by dropping the first and last letters. It fully reveals the ripening of the good and evil effects of the actions earned by an individual in previous births. || 3 ||

**Commentary:** Regarding *Hora*: Some desire the science of *Hora* to be a variation of the word *Ahoratra*. "Day and night" together is called *Ahoratra*, and the word *Hora* is used for it. How is this said? By the "dropping of the first and last letters." In the word *Ahoratra*, the first letter is 'A' and the last letter is 'Tra'; by making these invisible (dropping them), the word *Hora* remains. Why is the word *Hora* derived from *Ahoratra*? It is said here: The twelve zodiac signs starting with Aries are contained within the span of a day and night (*Ahoratra*). Knowledge of the Ascendant depends on time, and knowledge of good and bad fortune depends on the Ascendant. Therefore, because it relies on the day and night, the word *Hora* is derived from it. This is also the intention of the Teacher <note>Varahamihira</note>, as it is a principle that "that which is not contradicted is accepted." Thus, it is said in the *Saravali*:

> <gloss>By dropping the initial and final letters of *Ahoratra*, the word *Hora* is formed for us. Because of this, the entire movement of the planets and the zodiac is considered through it.</gloss>

What is the purpose of this? He says: "Actions earned." It clearly manifests the "ripening" or the full expression of the good, bad, or mixed actions earned in a previous existence. Thus, it is said in the *Laghu Jataka*:

> <gloss>Whatever good or bad was accumulated in another birth, this science reveals the ripening of that karma, just as a lamp reveals objects in the darkness.</gloss>

Now, does it reveal that which is inevitable, whether good or bad? It is said: Good and bad actions are of two types—those earned through "firm actions" (<term>Dridha-Karma</term>) and those earned through "non-firm actions" (<term>Adridha-Karma</term>). Among these, it reveals the results of the "firm actions" through the sequence of planetary periods (<term>Dasha</term>). By knowing the inauspicious results of a period, one should avoid journeys and such; by knowing the auspicious, one should engage in journeys and charity with excellence. For "non-firm actions," the results are known through the <term>Ashtakavarga</term><note>A system of points used to calculate planetary strength</note>...

...the manifestation of results. Knowing that [result] to be inauspicious, one should bring it to peace through pacification rituals <note>Shanti: rituals performed to avert evil or calm planetary influences</note> and other means. As the Lord of the Greeks <note>Yavanesvara: an influential early author in Indian astrology, likely of Greek descent or translating Greek works</note> says:

> "Whatever destiny is fixed for living beings, arising from the combination of planets and constellations at birth—those are called 'fortunes' in the context of human life-cycles. Experts describe this in two ways: 'Fixed' and 'Portentous.' That which is determined by the birth chart and unfolds in chronological order is called 'Fixed.' The results given by the seven planets as they move through the positions established at birth are called 'Portentous.'"

By this, it is shown that the "unstable" [portentous] influences can be pacified through rituals. It was also said by the holy Vyasa: "A wise man may overcome a weak destiny through personal effort." || 3 ||

**Vernacular Language —** (The etymology of the word *Hora*: Lexicographers have used the name *Hora* for both the Ascendant and the half-sign. Because 12 Ascendants and 24 half-signs pass within a day-and-night, Varahamihira says here—) <term>Hora</term> <note>The Greek word 'Hora' (hour) adapted into Sanskrit</note> — Many teachers say this is simply a variation of the word 'Ahoratra' [day-and-night]. If you take the four-syllable word 'A-ho-ra-tra' and remove the first syllable 'A' and the last syllable 'tra,' the two syllables 'Hora' remain in the middle. This (<term>Hora-shastra</term> <note>The science of judicial astrology</note>) indicates the time for receiving the fruits of good or bad deeds earned by living beings in their previous births. || 3 ||

**Special Meaning —** Therefore, people record the position of the Ascendant and planets at the time of birth or conception, which is called a birth-chart. Through this, by putting in even a little effort during a period of auspicious results, one surely gains the benefit. And during a period of inauspicious results, the bad effects can be avoided through religious observances, or the suffering is exhausted quickly with only minor worry. || 3 ||

-> Now, for practical application, he describes the limbs of the "Time-Person" <note>Kala Purusha: Time personified as a cosmic being whose body is composed of the zodiac</note> starting from the head with Aries and so on, in the Shardulavikridita meter: <-

> **The limbs of <term>Time</term> are the head, face, chest, heart, belly, waist, pelvis, genitals, the two thighs, the two knees, the two shanks, and then the two feet.**
> **The signs, starting with Aries and the constellation Ashwini, are situated in the zodiac circle, each composed of nine quarter-constellations.**
> **The terms Rashi, Kshetra, Griha, Riksha, Bha, and Bhavana all refer to the same concept [a Zodiac Sign].** || 4 ||

"Limbs of Time" means the body parts of the personified Time. These are the signs starting from Aries, which are measured by "nine quarter-constellations" <note>Each of the 12 zodiac signs consists of 2.25 constellations (Nakshatras); since each constellation has 4 quarters (padas), each sign equals 9 quarters</note>. "Starting with Ashwini" means that nine quarters of the constellations starting from Ashwini are the measure of each sign. This means the signs starting with Aries are joined with the constellation quarters starting from Ashwini. Such signs are the "limbs" or components.

# Brihat Jataka — Chapter on the Classification of Signs

And so says Yavaneshvara <note>A historical figure in Indian astrology, often associated with the "Lord of the Greeks" who translated Greek astronomical texts into Sanskrit</note>:

> "Two and a quarter [constellations] go to each house."

And so says the Lord Garga:

> "Ashvini, Bharani, and the first quarter of Krittika constitute Aries. The remaining three quarters of Krittika, Rohini, and half of Mrigashira constitute Taurus. The other half of Mrigashira, Ardra, and three quarters of Punarvasu constitute Gemini. The remaining quarter of Punarvasu, Pushya, and Ashlesha are known as the sign Cancer. Magha, Purva Phalguni, and a quarter of Uttara Phalguni are declared to be Leo. The remaining three quarters of Uttara Phalguni, Hasta, and half of Chitra constitute Virgo. The other half of Chitra, Svati, and three quarters of Vishakha constitute Libra. The remaining quarter of Vishakha, Anuradha, and Jyeshtha are called Scorpio. Mula, Purva Ashadha, and a quarter of Uttara Ashadha constitute Sagittarius. The remaining three quarters of Uttara Ashadha, Shravana, and half of Dhanishtha constitute Capricorn. The other half of Dhanishtha, Shatabhisha, and three quarters of Purva Bhadrapada constitute Aquarius. The remaining quarter of Purva Bhadrapada, Uttara Bhadrapada, and Revati constitute Pisces."

"Situated in the wheel" refers to those signs placed within the zodiacal circle, or arranged like a wheel; by this, their structure is demonstrated. Therein, the head of the limb of the one named Time is <term>Aries</term> <note>Mesha</note>. The face or mouth is Taurus. The chest or breast is <term>Gemini</term> <note>Mithuna</note>. The heart is <term>Cancer</term> <note>Karkata</note>. The belly or stomach is <term>Leo</term> <note>Simha</note>. The hip or waist is <term>Virgo</term> <note>Kanya</note>. The bladder (the area between the navel and the genitals) is <term>Libra</term> <note>Tula</note>. The genitals, by which masculinity is manifested, is <term>Scorpio</term> <note>Vrishchika</note>. The pair of thighs is <term>Sagittarius</term> <note>Dhanvi</note>. The pair of knees is <term>Capricorn</term> <note>Makara</note>. The two shanks are <term>Aquarius</term> <note>Kumbha</note>. The two feet are <term>Pisces</term> <note>Mina</note>. And so says Badarayana:

> "Aries is the head, then the face is Taurus of the Creator; the chest would be Gemini, and the heart Cancer. Leo is the stomach, then the maiden (Virgo) is the waist, and the bladder is Libra; the genitals would be the eighth (Scorpio). Sagittarius is his pair of thighs, Capricorn is the two knees. The pair of shanks is Aquarius, and the two feet are the two fish (Pisces)."

The purpose of this: At the time of birth, whichever sign is occupied by a malefic planet, an injury or affliction should be predicted for that specific limb of the Personification of Time. Where a benefic planet is situated, there is strength and health. And so it is said in the Saravali:

> "One should imagine the limbs of the Man of Time in human beings at the time of birth. From the conjunction of good or bad planets, these limbs are either strong or afflicted."

Regarding the terms "Sign," "Field," etc.: Each of these has the name "Rashi" (Sign), and these are its synonyms: *Kshetra* (Field), *Griha* (House), *Riksha* (Star/Constellation), *Bha* (Luminous body). Although the term "House" is established by the word *Bhavana*, the repetition of "House" is done to include all synonyms for a residence. Even though the term *Bha* is established by *Riksha*, its repetition shows this: wherever in the science of horoscopy (*Hora-shastra*) the terms *Bha* or *Riksha* are used, they should be understood as referring to the entire Sign, and not just a single <term>Lunar Mansion</term> <note>Nakshatra</note>. These words—Sign and the rest—are synonymous, meaning they convey the same object. | 4 |

---

**Vernacular Explanation** — (In all the Vedas, Smritis, and Puranas, this moving and unmoving universe is described as the manifest form of the Supreme Brahman, the Lord, which is called the Universe or the Zodiac Wheel...

<page-num>16</page-num>
<header>With the Sanskrit commentary of Bhattotpala and the Hindi Bhashya commentary</header>

It is said: (Here the divisions of the limbs are explained—) In the zodiac, starting from the beginning point of Aries and the Ashwini <note>The first lunar mansion or Nakshatra</note> constellation (divided into 12 equal parts), the 12 signs—each consisting of 2.25 constellations or 9 quarters—are the limbs of the Lord Time-Man <term>Kalapurusha; the personification of Time as a cosmic being</term> from head to foot. Specifically: Aries is the head, Taurus the face, Gemini the chest, Cancer the heart, Leo the stomach, Virgo the waist, Libra the lower abdomen, Scorpio the genitals, Sagittarius the thighs, Capricorn the knees, Aquarius the calves, and Pisces the feet.

**Special Meaning:** Varahamihira has stated in the **Laghujataka** <note>A foundational "Brief Compendium" on astrology by the same author</note> that just as the signs represent the limbs of the Time-Man, they should be understood similarly for all living beings. At the time of birth, the limb corresponding to a sign occupied by a benefic planet will be strong and healthy, while a limb corresponding to a sign occupied by a malefic planet should be understood as afflicted (by wounds or disease). || 4 ||

->Now, the physical forms of the signs are described in the Vasantatilaka meter:<-

> Two fish, a man with a water-pot, a human couple with a club and a lute,
> A man with a bow whose lower half is a horse, a Capricorn with a deer’s face,
> A man with a scale, and a maiden in a boat with grain and fire;
> The rest are like their names, and all move in their respective habitats. || 5 ||

**Commentary:** "Two fish": The sign Pisces consists of two fish with their tails turned toward each other's heads. How is this known? It is said because it is a "double-rising" sign. As will be stated later: "The pair of large-scaled fish rises from both sides." "Water-pot": Aquarius is a man carrying an empty pot on his shoulder. "Couple": Gemini is a human couple, a male and a female. The male holds a club and the female holds a lute. "A man with a bow whose lower half is a horse": Sagittarius is a man holding a bow whose lower body is that of a horse; meaning he is a quadruped <note>Centaur-like</note>. "Capricorn with a deer’s face": The sign Capricorn is a *Makara* <note>A mythical sea-monster</note> but with the face of a deer. "Scale," etc.: Libra is a man holding a scale. "Maiden": Virgo is a young girl sitting in a boat, holding grain and fire. "The rest": The remaining signs—Aries, Taurus, Cancer, Leo, and Scorpio—look like their names. That is: Aries is a ram, Taurus is a bull, Cancer is a crab (an aquatic creature), Leo is a lion, and Scorpio is a scorpion (an insect).

So says Satyacharya: "The ram, the bull, the couple holding a lute and club, the crab in the water, the lion in the mountains, the maiden in a boat holding a lamp and grain, the man holding the scales, the scorpion, the man with a bow whose rear half is a horse, the Capricorn whose front is a deer, the man with the water-pot..."

# Brihat Jataka — Chapter on the Classification of Signs

The sign **Pisces** is also known as the **Fish**. All signs are "self-moving" <note>original: "svachara"</note>, meaning they all move within their respective domains or reside in the places observed for them. Specifically: Aries, Taurus, and Leo are village-dwellers by day and night; Gemini is a village-dweller; Cancer is a water-dweller; Leo is a forest-dweller; Virgo resides in specific designated regions; Libra stays in the marketplace; Scorpio moves in holes or cavities; the first half of Sagittarius is a village-dweller; the first half of Capricorn is a forest-dweller while the second half is a water-dweller; Aquarius is a village-dweller; and Pisces is a water-dweller.

Thus, the Great Sage **Yavanesvara** <note>literally "Lord of the Greeks," referring to an influential early authority in Indian astrology who transmitted Greco-Egyptian techniques</note> says:

> 1. The first sign is remembered as having the form of a **Ram** (**Aries**). The ancients say it represents the **Head** of Time. Its lands include sheep and goat pastures, caves, mountains, and places containing fire, minerals, mines, and precious gems.
> 
> 2. The second is famous as the **Bull** (**Taurus**). It is the **Face and Throat** of the Creator. Its habitats are forests, mountain peaks, elephant-stables, cow-pens, and the lands of farmers.
> 
> 3. The third is the **Twins** (**Gemini**), a couple holding a lute and a staff. It represents the **Shoulders, Arms, and Chest** of the Lord of Creatures. Its places are those of dancers, singers, artisans, women, and areas for play, sexual enjoyment, and gambling.
> 
> 4. The fourth is **Cancer**, having the form of a **Crab** and residing in water. It is assigned to the **Chest** of the Creator. Its lands are meadows, ponds, sandbanks, and the beautiful pleasure-grounds of celestial maidens.
> 
> 5. The ancients call the fifth sign **Leo**, the **Lion**, residing on a mountain and representing the **Heart** of the Lord of Creatures. Its regions are forests, fortresses, caves, mountain jungles, and the lands of hunters.
> 
> 6. They say the sixth is **Virgo**, a **Maiden** in a boat on the water holding a lamp. Those wise in the meaning of Time call it the **Stomach** of the Creator. It is a land of grassy fields, women, sexual pleasure, and handicrafts.
> 7. **Libra** is a man standing in a marketplace holding a scale. He resides in the **Navel, Hips, and Bladder** region. Its lands are white-goods markets, shops, cities, roads, caravans, and high ground with ripening crops.
> 
> 8. The eighth is **Scorpio**, with the body of a **Scorpion**, said to be the **Genitals and Anus** of the Lord. Its lands are caves, holes, cavities, poisonous hiding places, anthills, and the haunts of insects, pythons, and snakes.
> 
> 9. **Sagittarius** is a man whose lower half is a **Horse**. They call it the **Thighs** of the Ruler of the World. Its lands are level ground, places for horses, gods, weapon-bearers, sacrifices, chariots, and stallions.
> 
> 10. **Capricorn** is the tenth, with the front half like a **Deer** and the back half like a **Water-creature**. It is the **Knees** of the Creator. Its habitats are rivers, forests, jungles, lakes, marshes, and holes.
> 
> 11. The eleventh is **Aquarius**, a man with an empty **Water-pot** on his shoulder. The noble ones call it the **Shins**. Its places are dried-up waterbeds, areas with Kusha grass, bird habitats, and the homes of women, tavern-keepers, and gamblers.

In the water, the sign of Pisces is depicted as two fish; these are ordained as the supreme feet of the Time-Person <note>The "Time-Person" or Kalapurusha is the personification of the universe as a human body, where each zodiac sign rules a body part</note>. Its abode is in holy places, lands of gods and Brahmins, and collections of water such as rivers and oceans. |12|

->"From the signs, one knows the time, direction, and place." || 5 ||<-

**Vernacular Translation—** The form of the Pisces sign is like two fish with their mouths and tails joined together. Aquarius is like a man carrying a water-pot on his shoulder. Gemini is the form of a pair consisting of a woman with a lute and a man with a mace. Sagittarius is like a man with the thighs of a horse, holding a bow in his hand. Capricorn is like a crocodile with the face of a deer. Virgo is like a maiden sitting in a boat, holding grain and fire in her hands. The remaining signs are similar to their names (meaning Aries is like a ram, Taurus like a bull, Cancer like a crab, Leo like a lion, and Scorpio like a scorpion), and all signs reside in their respective designated places. || 5 ||

**Special Meaning—** The intent is that Aries and Taurus reside in the forest during the day and in the village at night. Gemini resides in the village, Cancer in the water, Leo in the forest, Virgo in a boat on the water, Libra in the marketplace, Scorpio in a hole or pit, Sagittarius in the village, the first half of Capricorn in the forest and the second half in the water, Aquarius in the village, and Pisces in the water. This knowledge is used through the "Question Chart" <note>Prashna Lagna: a chart cast for the moment a question is asked</note> to understand the location of lost or stolen goods, or from the birth chart to understand the place of delivery. This is because knowledge of the region, direction, and time is obtained only through the signs. || 5 ||

# The Great Birth: Chapter on the Distinctions of the Signs

Mars is the lord of Aries. In whichever sign the <term>Navamsha</term><note>A sub-division of a zodiac sign equal to 3 degrees and 20 minutes, or 1/9th of the sign.</note> of Aries rises, Mars is also the lord of that division. This applies to the remaining signs as well. Regarding how those ninth-parts are determined, the text says: *The rule for the ninth-parts begins with the Ram, the Goat, the Balance, and the House of the Moon.*

"Ram" refers to Aries. "Goat" refers to Capricorn. "Balance" refers to Libra. "House of the Moon" refers to Cancer. The phrase "the rule for the ninth-parts begins with" applies to each of these respectively. The connection is understood as follows: The rule for ninth-parts starting from Aries, Capricorn, Libra, and Cancer applies to all signs.

Among them, the Aries-starting rule applies to Aries. Therefore, the ninth-parts belonging to Aries are Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, and Sagittarius.
The Capricorn-starting rule applies to Taurus. Therefore, the ninth-parts belonging to Taurus are Capricorn, Aquarius, Pisces, Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, and Virgo.
The Libra-starting rule applies to Gemini. Therefore, the ninth-parts belonging to Gemini are Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, Pisces, Aries, Taurus, and Gemini.
The Cancer-starting rule applies to Cancer. Therefore, the ninth-parts belonging to Cancer are Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, and Pisces.

In this same way, Leo is like Aries. Virgo is like Taurus. Libra is like Gemini. Scorpio is like Cancer. Again, Sagittarius is like Aries. Capricorn is like Taurus. Aquarius is like Gemini. Pisces is like Cancer.

As stated in another text:
> "For Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius, the ninth-parts are said to start from Aries.
> For Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn, the nine parts are said to start from Capricorn.
> For Libra, Gemini, and Aquarius, the nine parts are celebrated as starting from Libra.
> For Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces, the ninth-parts start from Cancer."

The purpose of this is for determining results such as <term>the thief, the enjoyer, the scholar, etc.</term><note>These are specific character archetypes assigned to different sub-divisions in predictive astrology.</note>

Regarding the lords of the <term>Dvadashamshas</term><note>A sub-division of 2 degrees and 30 minutes, or 1/12th of a sign.</note>, the text says: *The lords of the equal parts of the house follow in order from their own house.* "Equal parts of the house" means the twelve divisions of a sign. These are to be counted starting from the sign itself for each respective sign.

For example: For Aries, the twelve parts belong to Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, and Pisces. These have the lords of Aries and the following signs.
Similarly, for Taurus, they start with Taurus and end with Aries.
For Gemini, they start with Gemini and end with Taurus.
For Cancer, they start with Cancer and end with Gemini.
For Leo, they start with Leo and end with Cancer.
For Virgo, they start with Virgo and end with Leo.
For Libra, they start with Libra and end with Virgo.
For Scorpio, they start with Scorpio and end with Libra.
For Sagittarius, they start with Sagittarius and end with Scorpio.
For Capricorn, they start with Capricorn and end with Sagittarius.
For Aquarius, they start with Aquarius and end with Capricorn.
For Pisces, they start with Pisces and end with Aquarius.

The purpose of these is for calculations such as "the one joined with the Moon at that time in the twelfth-part," and so on. || 6 ||

---

**Vernacular Translation**—Mars, Venus, Mercury, Moon, Sun, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Saturn, and Jupiter are the lords of the 12 signs starting from Aries in order. Furthermore, the lords of the ninth-parts and other divisions of the signs starting from Aries are also these same lords (Mars, etc.) in their respective order.

Commentary: *Kuja* means Mars; *Ravija* means Saturn; *Guru* is Jupiter; *Jna* is Mercury; *Shukra* is Venus. Thus, the portions of Mars, Saturn, Jupiter, Mercury, and Venus are respectively defined by the words *Pavana*, *Samirana*, *Kaurpi*, *Juka*, and *Leya*. To explain: *Pavana* (the winds) represents five; thus, five degrees belong to Mars. Above that, *Samirana* (also meaning wind/five) belongs to Saturn, making ten. Above that, the term *Kaurpi* represents eight for Jupiter; *Kaurpi* refers to Scorpio, which is the eighth sign in counting, thus eighteen. After that...

The seven parts designated as <term>Juka</term> <note>original: "Juka-samjna"; a Greek-influenced term for Libra</note> belong to Mercury; "Juka" is the name for Libra, and by counting it is the seventh, thus making twenty-five degrees in total. Above that, the five parts designated as <term>Leya</term> <note>original: "Leya-samjna"; a Greek-influenced term for Leo</note> belong to Venus; "Leya" is the name for Leo, and by counting it is the fifth, thus making thirty degrees. Why is this generally stated? He says: "In odd and even signs." In an <term>odd sign</term> <note>Aries, Gemini, Leo, Libra, Sagittarius, Aquarius</note>, the planets starting with Mars are the lords of the portions starting with the Wind <note>referring to the elemental or numerical sequence of the Trishamsha degrees</note> in their regular order. This is the sequence for the odd signs: Aries, Gemini, Leo, Libra, Sagittarius, and Aquarius.

However, in an <term>even sign</term> <note>Taurus, Cancer, Virgo, Scorpio, Capricorn, Pisces</note>, they are "placed in reverse." In an even sign, the portions and the planets are situated in reverse order. For example: first, five degrees for Venus, then seven for Mercury (making twelve), then eight for Jupiter (making twenty), then five for Saturn (making twenty-five), and finally five for Mars (making thirty). Thus, Taurus, Cancer, Virgo, Scorpio, Capricorn, and Pisces are the even signs, and the five "star-planets" <note>The non-luminary planets: Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn</note> are the lords of these thirty degrees.

On this point, some say: by "placed in reverse," only the numerical sequence of the portions should be reversed, not the order of the planets like Mars and the others. But that is incorrect. Because the word "that" is used here to include the group of planets starting with Mars. As <term>Shrutakirti</term> <note>An ancient astrological authority</note> says:

> "Five, five, eight, seven, and five are the degrees in the odd houses for Mars, Saturn, Jupiter, Mercury, and Venus respectively. In the even houses, the degrees are five, seven, eight, five, and five for Venus, Mercury, Jupiter, Saturn, and Mars."

The purpose:

> "A girl may be wicked, fall into slavery, be virtuous, or possess a bad character..." <note>This verse begins to explain the character results of a woman born in different Trishamsha divisions.</note>

<meta>This page continues the technical definitions of planetary divisions and zodiacal junctions, following the discussion of the Trimsamsha (thirty-degree divisions) and the specific terminology for the twelve signs.</meta>

<page-num>25</page-num>
<header>Page 25 of the Sanskrit Commentary by Bhattotpala with Hindi Translation</header>

---

"In the signs of the Son of the Earth (Mars), the portions belong respectively to Mars, Saturn, Jupiter, Mercury, and Venus," and so forth. <note>This refers to the Trimsamsha system where degrees within a sign are ruled by specific planets.</note>
The term <term>Riksha-sandhi</term> (junction of the stars) refers to the end of the House of the Moon (Cancer), the end of Scorpio, and the end of Pisces. The word "end" applies to each of these individually.
The very end of the House of the Moon, the very end of Scorpio, and the end of Pisces constitute the <term>Riksha-sandhi</term> <note>original: "Riksha-sandhi" - a sensitive transitional point in the zodiac</note>. The House of the Moon is Cancer; Ali is Scorpio; Jhasha is Pisces. The end of these—specifically the ninth <term>Navamsha</term> <note>a 3°20' division</note> where both the lunar mansion (Nakshatra) and the zodiac sign (Rashi) end simultaneously—is called the junction. This is because the end of the Ashlesha mansion coincides with the end of Cancer; the end of Jyeshtha with the end of Scorpio; and the end of Revati with the end of Pisces. In common worldly parlance, this is famously known as <term>Gandanta</term> <note>a "knot's end," considered an inauspicious time for births or new beginnings</note>.
It is said: "Ashwini, Magha, and Mula begin the signs of Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius respectively... they exist at the end of the odd signs with a quarter-increase." The purpose of knowing this is stated: "If the Moon is at the junction and influenced by a malefic planet, the person will be dull-witted, unless there is an aspect from a benefic planet." || 7 ||

**Vernacular Translation—** In odd-numbered signs, the first 5 degrees belong to Mars, the next 5 to Saturn, the next 8 to Jupiter, the next 7 to Mercury, and the final 5 degrees are the <term>Trimsamsha</term> <note>thirty-part divisions</note> of Venus. In even-numbered signs, this is reversed (meaning the first 5 degrees belong to Venus, then 7 to Mercury, then 8 to Jupiter, then 5 to Saturn, and finally 5 to Mars). Furthermore, the ends of Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces are called <term>Riksha-sandhi</term>. || 7 ||

**Special Meaning—** Where the end and beginning of both a Nakshatra (lunar mansion) and a Rashi (zodiac sign) occur simultaneously, it is called <term>Riksha-sandhi</term>. In other signs, the transition of the sign happens in the middle of a Nakshatra, or a Nakshatra begins in the middle of a sign. Therefore, those do not possess the <term>Sandhi-dosha</term> <note>the flaw or affliction of the junction</note>. <term>Riksha-sandhi</term> is also called <term>Gandanta</term>. Birth at such a junction results in inauspicious fruits. Beyond this, the auspicious and inauspicious effects are considered via the <term>Trimsamsha</term>. Why do only the five planets from Mars onwards own these divisions, and why are the degrees not equal for everyone? For the reasoning behind this, see the discussion on the <term>Shadvarga</term> <note>the six-fold division system</note> in the text 'Lagna-viveka.' || 7 ||

->Now, for the sake of common worldly usage, he states the names of Aries and the other signs in a Pathyarya verse:<-

### Kriya, Taburi, Jituma, Kulira, Leya, Pathona, Juka, Kaurpya;
### Tauksika, Akokera, Hridroga, and the last is Itthama. || 8 ||

**Commentary—** The signs starting from Aries should be known by these alternative names <note>These are Sanskritized versions of Greek zodiac names, e.g., Kriya for Krios/Aries</note>. They are as follows:
Kriya is <term>Aries</term>, Taburi is <term>Taurus</term>, Jituma is <term>Gemini</term>, Kulira is <term>Cancer</term>, Leya is <term>Leo</term>, Pathona is <term>Virgo</term>, Juka is <term>Libra</term>, Kaurpya is <term>Scorpio</term>, Tauksika is <term>Sagittarius</term>, Akokera is <term>Capricorn</term>, Hridroga is <term>Aquarius</term>, and the final sign is <term>Pisces</term>. The purpose of these names is seen in verses such as: "Taurus and Leo, Gemini is the eighth, Aries and Libra," etc. || 8 ||

<header>Brihat Jataka — Chapter on the Distinctions of the Signs</header>

->**Vernacular Translation:** Kriya (1), Taburi (2), Jituma (3), Kulira (4), Leya (5), Pathona (6), Juka (7), Kaurpi (8), Taukshika (9), Akokera (10), Hridroga (11), and Antyabha (12)—these are the names of the twelve signs starting from Aries in sequence.<- <note>original: "क्रिय, ताबुरि..." These are Sanskrit transliterations of the Greek names for the zodiac signs: Krios, Tauros, Didymos, etc.</note> || 8 ||

| Odd Signs | Mars | Saturn | Jupiter | Mercury | Venus | Lord of the Trimsamsha |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| Degrees | 5 | 5 | 8 | 7 | 5 | |
| **Even Signs** | **Venus** | **Mercury** | **Jupiter** | **Saturn** | **Mars** | **Lord of the Trimsamsha** |

*Now, in the Indra-vajra meter, the author describes the technical term "Varga" (Division) for the practical use of a planet's Place, Hora, Drekkana, Navamsha, Dwadashamsha, and Trimsamsha:*

### The Drekkana, Hora, Ninth-part (Navamsha), and the Thirtieth-part (Trimsamsha),
### Along with the Twelfth-part (Dwadashamsha) and the Place (Kshetra) belonging to a planet, are called its "Varga."
### "Hora" refers both to the Ascendant and to one-half of a Sign. || 6 ||

**Commentary:** The six items—Drekkana and the others—are designated as the <term>Varga</term><note>Varga literally means "set" or "division"; it refers to the strength a planet gains by being in its own territory across different mathematical divisions.</note> of their respective planets. Among these, a <term>Drekkana</term><note>A 10-degree division; one-third of a sign.</note> is the third part of a sign. A <term>Hora</term> is half of a sign. A <term>Navamsha</term> is the ninth part. These are the names given to them. The <term>Trimsamsha</term> is the thirtieth part, and the <term>Dwadashamsha</term> is the twelfth part. Whichever <term>Kshetra</term> (Place/Sign) belongs to a specific planet, that is its Varga. By the word "Varga" here, the <term>Shadvarga</term> (Six-fold Division) is intended. All of these are the personal divisional names for a planet. Thus, a sign is six-fold; when a planet is situated in its own divisions among these six, it is said to be "established in its Varga."

One might object: "The six-fold divisions are not possible for all planets. For instance, the Sun and Moon have no Trimsamsha divisions, and Mars and others lack certain Hora divisions." Therefore, it is possible in part; a planet is considered "in its Varga" if it stays in five of its own divisions. This is also an illustrative point. Thus, a planet situated in two or more of its own divisions is called "Varga-bound." As the Sage <term>Garga</term><note>An ancient legendary seer of Indian astronomy/astrology.</note> says:

> "The Place, Hora, Drekkana, Navamsha, Dwadashamsha,
> and Trimsamsha—this is declared the Varga for everyone.
> Even if situated in two or more of its own divisions, a planet is in its own Varga.
> A planet becomes powerful when it attains five divisions, and not otherwise."

**The Purpose:** "Even a single planet reaching its Varga, if placed in a <term>Kendra</term><note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses; the 'pillars' of a chart.</note>, brings good or bad fortune to men. A planet in its Varga at the time of the Ascendant can cause various types of destruction for travelers," and so on.

Regarding the dual meaning of "Hora" and "Lagna" (Ascendant), he says: *Hora is the Ascendant and half of a sign.* The term "Hora" is used to mean the Ascendant. The purpose is seen in rules like: "The Hora (Ascendant) should be aspected by its lord, Jupiter, or Mercury." Additionally, "Hora" is half of a sign (15 degrees). The purpose is seen in rules like: "In odd signs, the Sun and Moon's Horas are..." || 6 ||

<summary>This page defines the "Shadvarga" or six-fold divisional system used to calculate planetary strength and introduces Sanskritized Greek names for the zodiac signs. It also clarifies that the term "Hora" can refer to both the rising sign (Ascendant) and a 15-degree division of a sign.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the technical definitions of astrological divisions and the physical characteristics of the zodiac signs, specifically their orientation during rising and their strength relative to day or night.</meta>

<page-num>27</page-num>
<header>Accompanied by the Sanskrit commentary of Bhattotpala and the vernacular explanation</header>

**Vernacular—** The *Drekkana* <note>a 10-degree subdivision</note>, *Hora* <note>a 15-degree subdivision</note>, *Navamsha* <note>1/9th part</note>, *Trimshamsha* <note>1/30th part</note>, *Dwadashamsha* <note>1/12th part</note>, and the *Kshetra* <note>the sign or 'field' itself</note>—whichever of these belongs to a specific planet is called its *Varga* <note>divisional strength</note>. Furthermore, the word 'Hora' is understood to mean both the Ascendant and half of a zodiac sign. However, here in the context of the *Shadvarga* <note>the six-fold divisional system</note>, the word 'Hora' should only be taken to mean half of a zodiac sign. || 6 ||

Now, the author describes the classification of signs as nocturnal or diurnal, and as rising by the rear or by the head, using the *Vasantatilaka* meter:

> ->Taurus, Aries, Sagittarius, Cancer, and Gemini, along with Capricorn, are called nocturnal;<-
> ->These same signs, excluding Gemini, are said to be rear-rising.<-
> ->The remaining signs are head-rising and possess strength during the day,<-
> ->While the pair of "large-scaled ones" <note>Pisces</note> meets the horizon with both ends. || 10 ||<-

**Commentary:** Regarding "Taurus, Aries...": The word *Go* refers to Taurus; *Aja* is Aries; *Ashvi* <note>literally 'the one with a horse'</note> refers to the Archer or Sagittarius; *Karki* is the Crab or Cancer; Gemini is well-known. These—Taurus, Aries, Sagittarius, Cancer, and Gemini—along with *Mriga* <note>the Deer/Goat</note> or Capricorn, are the six signs known as nocturnal, meaning they are defined as having strength at night. 

"These same signs, excluding Gemini, are rear-rising": These same nocturnal signs, when Gemini is excluded, are defined as *Prishthodaya* <note>rising with the back first</note>. This means they come into view by their rear. Gemini, however, is head-rising. 

"The remaining are head-rising": The signs remaining from those mentioned—Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, and Aquarius—are *Shirshodaya* <note>rising with the head first</note>; they come into view head-first and possess strength during the day. 

Here, the terms "nocturnal strength" and "diurnal strength" are merely technical designations. This is because the author will later state their actual strength based on categories like bipeds, etc., during the day, night, or the two twilights. If this were not just a designation, the teacher <note>Varahamihira</note> would be contradicting his own words. Therefore, "strength" here is a formal name. The purpose of this is seen in rules like "In nocturnal and diurnal signs, the birth is in reverse order," etc. Similarly, it applies to "those born in rear-rising or both-rising signs." In the context of *Yatra* <note>journeys/expeditions</note>, it will be said: "Success in the desired task is achieved in a head-rising sign; failure and loss of strength occur in a rear-rising sign." Also: "Travel is auspicious during the day in a day-strong sign, and at night in a night-strong sign; travel is not auspicious when the strength is reversed." 

Furthermore, he mentions a specialty of Pisces among these: "The pair of large-scaled ones meets the horizon with both ends." *Prithu-roma* <note>large-scaled</note> means fish; a pair of them is the sign Pisces. That sign comes to the horizon from both sides—both the rear and the head <note>rising horizontally</note>. || 10 ||

**Vernacular—** Taurus, Aries, Sagittarius, Cancer, Gemini, and Capricorn—these six are strong at night (*Ratribali*). Among these, excluding Gemini, the other 5 are rear-rising (*Prishthodaya*). The remaining signs are head-rising (*Shirshodaya*) and strong during the day (*Dinabali*), but Pisces is both-rising (*Ubhayodaya*). || 10 ||

| Zodiac Sign | Designation / Strength |
|----------|----------|
| Aries, Taurus, Sagittarius, Cancer, Capricorn | Rear-rising, Night-strong |
| Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Aquarius | Head-rising, Day-strong |
| Gemini | Head-rising, Night-strong |
| Pisces | Both-rising, Day-strong |

# Brihat Jataka — Chapter on the Varieties of Signs
<page-num>28</page-num>

**Special Meaning** — This application of "night and day signs" is used in *Nashta-Jataka* <note>The art of reconstructing a lost birth chart</note> and similar contexts. Likewise, regarding travel: "Success in desired work is achieved when a sign rises by the head (*Shirshodaya*); failure and loss of strength occur when it rises by the back (*Prishthodaya*)." Furthermore: "Travel is auspicious during the day for signs strong in the day, and at night for those strong at night; travel is not recommended when the strength is reversed." This concludes the commentary on verse 10.

Now, the author describes the classification of signs into cruel and mild, male and female, moveable, fixed, and dual-natured, as well as the lords of directions, *Horas*, and *Decans* <term>Drekkana: a 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign</term>, using the *Mandakranta* meter:

### Cruel and mild, male and female; these are moveable, fixed, and dual;
### The lords of the East and other directions are Aries, Taurus, Gemini, and Cancer, along with their respective trines.
### In odd signs, the Horas belong to the Sun and Moon; in even signs, to the Moon and Sun.
### (1) The Decans belong to the lords of the first, fifth, and ninth houses from themselves. || 11 ||

->**Cruel and Mild**<-: These signs, starting from Aries, are designated as cruel and mild in sequence. Among them, Aries is cruel, Taurus is mild, Gemini is cruel, and Cancer is mild. This pattern should be applied to all. Thus, odd-numbered signs are termed "cruel" and even-numbered signs are "mild." The purpose is: "Those born in cruel signs possess a cruel nature; those born in mild signs possess a mild nature." As the Teacher says: "Know that odd signs are male and even signs are female in order; cruel natures arise in fierce signs, and mild natures in mild, even houses."

**Male and Female**: These same signs starting from Aries are known as male and female respectively. Thus, Aries is male (man) and Taurus is female (woman). This applies throughout. Therefore, the six odd signs are male, and the six even signs are female. The purpose is that those born in male signs are energetic/splendid, while those born in female signs are gentle.

**Moveable, Fixed, and Dual**: These same signs starting from Aries are respectively called moveable, fixed, and dual-natured. There, Aries is moveable (*Chara*), Taurus is immovable/fixed (*Sthira*), and Gemini is dual-bodied or dual-natured (*Dvisvabhava*). This should be applied to Cancer and the rest. Thus, Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn are moveable. Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius are fixed. Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces are dual-natured. The purpose is: "Those born in moveable signs have a restless nature; in fixed signs, a stable nature; and in dual signs, a mixed nature." So says Satyacharya.

<insert>
(1) **Consideration of the Decan (Drekkana)**: "Drekka, Drekkana, and Drikkana are synonymous," according to the *Paradvirupa* dictionary. Also: "*Drik* means knowledge or the knower; *Kana* means extremely subtle," according to the *Amarakosha* dictionary. The state of an extremely subtle particle is *Kana*; therefore, the portion used for discerning one's own intellectual and inherent nature is called the *Drekkana* division. For this reason, the lords of the first, fifth, and ninth houses are fit to be its masters.
</insert>

Alternatively, according to the rules of the *Mahasiddhanta*: "Numbers are derived from the letters starting with Ka, Ta, Pa, and Ya in alphabetical order" <note>referring to the Katapayadi system of numerical notation</note>. (Drik = 81, which when divided by twelve leaves a remainder of 6; Ka = 1; Na = 5). Thus (6, 1, 5). Therefore, it is clearly established that "The Decan belongs to the lords of the first, fifth, and ninth."

> "The signs are known as Moveable, Fixed, and Dual-natured in sequence. The temperaments of those born are shaped according to the inherent nature of these signs." <note>This quote establishes that a person's character is influenced by whether their birth sign is active/changeable, stable/stubborn, or a mix of both.</note>

The lords of the East and other directions: <term>Kriya</term> <note>original: "Kriya" is a Greek-derived term for Aries</note> is <term>Aries</term>; <term>Vrisha</term> is the well-known <term>Taurus</term>; <term>Nriyug</term> is <term>Gemini</term>; and <term>Karkataka</term> is <term>Cancer</term> (also called <term>Kulira</term>). These signs—Aries, Taurus, Gemini, and Cancer—along with their "trines" (the signs occupying the 5th and 9th positions from them), are the lords of the four directions starting with the East. Aries, along with its 5th and 9th signs, rules the East. Similarly, Taurus with its 5th and 9th rules the South. Gemini with its 5th and 9th rules the West. So too for <term>Karka</term> (Cancer). Therefore: Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius rule the East. Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn rule the South. Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius rule the West. Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces rule the North. The purpose of this is:

> "To determine the direction of a thief or lost property in inquiries regarding theft or loss."

And also:

> "Success is achieved easily when moving toward the direction ruled by the rising sign; effort becomes fruitless if the rising sign is contrary to the direction of travel."

Regarding the Sun and Moon: <term>Martanda</term> (<term>the Sun</term>) and <term>Indu</term> (<term>the Moon</term>) respectively rule the <term>Horas</term> <note>A "Hora" is a half-sign, or 15 degrees of the zodiac</note> in odd-numbered signs. In an odd sign, the first half belongs to the Sun and the second half belongs to the Moon. In even-numbered signs, the order is reversed: the first half belongs to the Moon and the second half to the Sun. The purpose is:

> "Those born in the Sun's Hora are energetic and powerful, while those born in the Moon's Hora are of a gentle temperament."

Regarding the <term>Drekkana</term> <note>A "Drekkana" or Decan is a one-third division of a sign (10 degrees)</note>: The three divisions of a sign belong to the lords of the sign itself, the 5th house from it, and the 9th house from it. The first <term>Drekkana</term> belongs to the lord of the sign itself. The second belongs to the lord of the 5th house. The third belongs to the lord of the 9th house. For example: for Aries, the first decan belongs to <term>Bhauma</term> (<term>Mars</term>), the second to the Sun (lord of Leo, the 5th), and the third to <term>Guru</term> (<term>Jupiter</term>, lord of Sagittarius, the 9th). For Taurus: 1st is <term>Venus</term>, 2nd is <term>Mercury</term>, 3rd is <term>Saturn</term>. For Gemini: 1st is Mercury, 2nd is Venus, 3rd is Saturn. For Cancer: 1st is Moon, 2nd is Mars, 3rd is <term>Jiva</term> (<term>Jupiter</term>). For Leo: 1st is Sun, 2nd is Jupiter, 3rd is Mars. For Virgo: 1st is Mercury, 2nd is Saturn, 3rd is Venus. For Libra: 1st is Venus, 2nd is Saturn, 3rd is Mercury. For Scorpio: 1st is Mars, 2nd is Jupiter, 3rd is Moon. For Sagittarius: 1st is Jupiter, 2nd is Mars, 3rd is Sun. For Capricorn: 1st is Saturn, 2nd is Venus, 3rd is Mercury. For Aquarius: 1st is Saturn, 2nd is Mercury, 3rd is Venus. For Pisces: 1st is Jupiter, 2nd is Moon, 3rd is Mars. The purpose is mentioned in verses such as:

> "By the divisions of the signs, the best results..." etc. || 11 ||

**Vernacular Commentary—** The twelve signs starting from Aries are, in order: malefic and benefic, masculine and feminine, movable, fixed (immobile), and dual-natured. Furthermore, Aries, Taurus, Gemini, and Cancer—along with their respective fifth and ninth signs—are the lords of the directions starting from the East. In odd-numbered signs, the first half of the sign <term>Hora; a 15-degree division of a zodiac sign</term> belongs to the Sun and the second to the Moon. In even-numbered signs, the first belongs to the Moon and the second to the Sun. Additionally, within each sign, the first <term>Decan; a 10-degree division of a zodiac sign</term> belongs to its own lord, the second to the lord of the fifth sign from it, and the third to the lord of the ninth sign from it.

**Special Meaning—** Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius are the Eastern signs; Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn reside in the South.
->Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius are known as West; Cancer, Pisces, and Scorpio are considered North.<-

**Purpose—** The temperament of the native <note>the person whose birth chart is being read</note> is determined by the nature of the sign. For example, a cruel nature arises in a cruel sign, and a gentle nature in a gentle sign. In a movable sign, the nature is restless; in a fixed sign, it is stable; and in a dual sign, it is stable in the first half and restless in the second half.

### Now, he describes the characteristics of the lords of the Horas and Decans according to a different school of thought using the Indravajra meter:

> Some authorities desire the first Hora to belong to the lord of the sign, and the second to the lord of the eleventh house (the house of gains). They also describe the Decans as belonging to the lords of the sign itself, the twelfth sign, and the eleventh sign respectively.

**Commentary:** "Some" refers to authorities such as Yavaneshwara <note>literally "Lord of the Greeks," referring to historical Greco-Indian astrological traditions</note> and others. They desire the first Hora to belong to the lord of the sign and the second to the lord of the eleventh house. For example, in Aries, the first Hora belongs to Mars <note>the ruler of Aries</note> and the second belongs to Saturn, the lord of the eleventh sign, Aquarius. This should be applied to all signs. Regarding the Decans: they describe them as belonging to the lords of the sign itself, the twelfth, and the eleventh. For example, in Aries, the first Decan belongs to Mars, the second to Jupiter <note>lord of Pisces, the 12th</note>, and the third to Saturn <note>lord of Aquarius, the 11th</note>. This should be understood for the others as well. As Yavaneshwara says: "The first Hora belongs to the lord of the house; the second to the lord of the eleventh field. The three Decans here belong respectively to the lords of the sign itself, the twelfth, and the eleventh." Thus, according to Yavaneshwara’s view, all planets have lordship over the Horas. However, this is not the intention of the Author <note>Varahamihira</note>, nor of Satyacharya and others. As Satyacharya says: "In odd signs, the first Hora belongs to the Sun..."
