# Page 31
## With the Bhashya Commentary and Bhattotpala’s Sanskrit Commentary 31

In even signs, the second half belongs to the Moon. These should be known in order at birth when planets are in their own <term>Hora</term><note>A division of a zodiac sign into two halves (15 degrees each), used to determine planetary strength and gender influence.</note>.
The lords of the <term>Drekkana</term><note>A decan, or one-third of a zodiac sign (10 degrees).</note> are the lords of the first, fifth, and ninth houses from that sign. Planets are strong when situated in their respective decans. || 12 ||

**Vernacular Translation—** The <term>Yavana</term><note>Literally "Ionian" or Greek; refers to the school of Indo-Greek astral sciences.</note> teachers and others say the first Hora belongs to the lord of the sign, and the second Hora belongs to the lord of the eleventh sign from it. They also say the first Drekkana belongs to the lord of the sign, the second to the lord of the twelfth from it, and the third to the lord of the eleventh.

**Special Meaning—** Because they contradict the teachings of Sage Satyacharya and others, the Hora and Drekkana systems mentioned by the Yavanas are not accepted here. || 12 ||

->Now, he describes the exaltation and debilitation divisions of the planets in the <term>Pushpitagra</term><note>A specific Sanskrit poetic meter characterized by a "flowering tip" rhythm.</note> meter:<-

(1) Aries, Taurus, Capricorn, Virgo, Cancer, Pisces, and Libra are the exaltations of the Sun and the other planets respectively. By the degrees ten, three, twenty-eight, fifteen, five, twenty-seven, and twenty, they are at their highest exaltation; at the seventh sign from these, they are at their deepest debilitation. 13

**Commentary:** "Aries etc." The signs Aries and so forth are respectively the exaltation signs of the Sun and the other planets. Specifically: Aries is the exaltation of the Sun; Taurus is for the Moon; Capricorn is for Mars; Virgo is for Mercury; Cancer is for Jupiter; Pisces is for Venus; and Libra is for Saturn. These same signs, at the degrees starting from ten, are the points of "Deep Exaltation" for the Sun and others. There, the Sun is at deep exaltation in the 10th degree of Aries. The Moon in Taurus at the 3rd degree (represented by the word *Shikhi* <note>original: "shikhi-sankhya" - a system of using words to represent numbers; Shikhi (fire/arrow) represents 3.</note>). Mars in Capricorn at the 28th degree (represented by *Manu-yuk* <note>original: "Manu" is 14; "yuk" means joined/doubled, so 14x2 = 28.</note>). Mercury in Virgo at the 15th degree (represented by *Tithi* <note>The 15 lunar days of a fortnight.</note>). Jupiter in Cancer at the 5th degree (represented by *Indriya* <note>The 5 senses.</note>). Venus in Pisces at the 27th degree (represented by *Tri-navaka* <note>3 times 9.</note>). Saturn in Libra at the 20th degree. 

Now, one might ask: if the entire sign is called the exaltation, and a sign consists of thirty degrees, then the 10th and other degrees are already included; why specify them? It is true, but the specific degrees are mentioned to indicate the point of **Maximum Exaltation**. Otherwise, the entire signs are simply called exaltations. Therefore, planets situated at these specific degrees are said to be in "Deep Exaltation."

->(1) Table of Exaltation and Debilitation.<-

| | Planet | Sun | Moon | Mars | Mercury | Jupiter | Venus | Saturn |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Exaltation** | Sign | Aries | Taurus | Capricorn | Virgo | Cancer | Pisces | Libra |
| | Degree | 10 | 3 | 28 | 15 | 5 | 27 | 20 |
| **Debilitation** | Sign | Libra | Scorpio | Cancer | Pisces | Capricorn | Virgo | Aries |
| | Degree | 10 | 3 | 28 | 15 | 5 | 27 | 20 |

# Brihat Jataka — Chapter on the Distinctions of the Signs

<page-num>32</page-num>
->The Great Compendium of Nativity — Chapter on the Distinctions of the Signs<-

Knowledge of the highest point of exaltation <term>Paramoccha: the specific degree within a sign where a planet's influence is most potent</term> serves a purpose beyond just knowing the exaltation sign itself. As the venerable Sage Garga says:

> "The Sun and Moon, when in their highest exaltation, produce a sovereign ruler. Even if they are merely in their exaltation signs or their root-trines <term>Mulatrikona: a specific area of a sign, second only to exaltation in strength</term>, they produce a wealthy and famous person."

And likewise, Yavanesvara <note>literally "Lord of the Greeks," referring to the historical transmission of Hellenistic astrology into Sanskrit</note> states:

> "When all planets are in their highest degrees of exaltation and possess maximum strength, and if the Ascendant is auspicious and the Moon is full, the person born is a ruler of the three worlds."

Now, the Sun and the other planets should be seen as situated in these highest exaltations. Here, the Teacher <note>referring to Varahamihira, the author of the Brihat Jataka</note> did not use ordinal numbers (like "tenth") for the degrees to avoid breaking the poetic meter of the verse. That these are intended as specific degrees is known from the words of Yavanesvara. As Yavanesvara says:

> "The tenth degree for the Sun, the third for the Moon, the fifth for Jupiter, the twentieth for Saturn <insert>correction: the text later specifies Saturn's degree as twenty or thirty depending on the tradition</insert>, the twenty-seventh for Venus, and the fifteenth for Mercury. For Mars, the twenty-eighth degree is the highest exaltation."

Regarding the phrase "they are in debilitation at the setting": These planets, the Sun and others, have their "setting" or "fall" <term>Nicha: the point of maximum weakness, opposite to exaltation</term> at the seventh sign from their exaltation. For example: The seventh from the Sun's exaltation (Aries) is Libra; that is its sign of debilitation. Similarly, the seventh for the Moon is Scorpio. For Mars, the seventh is Cancer. For Mercury, Pisces. For Jupiter, Capricorn. For Venus, Virgo. For Saturn, Aries. In these cases also, the planets should be understood to be in their "deepest debilitation" at the corresponding degrees. As Yavanesvara says:

> "The seventh house from one's exaltation is called the debilitation, and it occurs at the same numerical degree."

Now, the Sun and others in such states are in deep debilitation. Garga has shown that planets in deep debilitation produce unfavorable results. As Garga says:

> "The Sun and Moon, if placed in their deepest debilitation, make a man blind, naked <note>meaning destitute</note>, foolish, and dependent on others for food." ||13||

**Vernacular Translation:** The exaltation of the Sun is at 10 degrees in Aries, the Moon at 3 degrees in Taurus, Mars at 28 degrees in Capricorn, Mercury at 15 degrees in Virgo, Jupiter at 5 degrees in Cancer, Venus at 27 degrees in Pisces, and Saturn at 20 degrees in Libra. All these planets are in deep debilitation at the same degrees in the seventh sign from their respective exaltations.

**Special Meaning:** The purpose of this is seen in the results of birth charts, such as "a king is born with three planets in exaltation, while one is miserable with planets in debilitation." The reason for specifying degrees within the exaltation signs is to resolve doubts when a sign serves multiple roles. For example, Virgo is Mercury's home, its root-trine, and its exaltation. If Mercury is in Virgo, which status should be applied? To resolve such confusion for all planets, the exaltation has been categorized by specific degrees. ||13||

<summary>This page defines the specific degrees of "deep exaltation" and "deep debilitation" for the seven classical planets, citing authorities like Garga and Yavanesvara to explain their impact on a person's status and wealth.</summary>
<keywords>Exaltation, Debilitation, Paramoccha, Paramonicha, Garga, Yavanesvara, Varahamihira, Planetary Strength, Degrees, Brihat Jataka</keywords>

<page-num>33</page-num>
<header>With the Bhashyopeta commentary and the Sanskrit sub-commentary by Bhattotpala</header>

Here is the statement from the *Saravali* <note>A foundational 8th-century astrological text by Kalyanavarman</note> regarding specifics:
> 'The first twenty degrees in Leo are the <term>Mulatrikona</term> <note>A "root-trine" position where a planet is highly potent, stronger than its own sign but less than its exaltation</note>; the remaining parts are the Sun's own house.
> The first three degrees in Taurus are the Moon's exaltation; the remaining degrees are its <term>Mulatrikona</term>.
> The first twelve degrees in Aries are the <term>Mulatrikona</term>; the rest is Mars's own house.
> In Virgo, the first fifteen degrees are Mercury's exaltation—this should always be considered.
> Beyond that, five degrees are its <term>Mulatrikona</term>, and the remaining ten degrees are its own house.
> In Sagittarius, the first ten degrees are Jupiter's <term>Mulatrikona</term>, and the rest is its own house.
> For Venus, fifteen degrees in Libra are its <term>Mulatrikona</term>, and the remaining fifteen are its own house.
> In Aquarius, the <term>Mulatrikona</term> of Saturn is like that of the Sun in Leo—twenty degrees.'

The Sun has its <term>Mulatrikona</term> up to 20° in Leo, and the remaining 10° are its own house. The Moon is exalted up to 3° in Taurus, and the remaining 27° are its <term>Mulatrikona</term>. Mars has its <term>Mulatrikona</term> up to 12° in Aries, and the remaining 18° are its own house. Mercury is exalted up to 15° in Virgo, the next 5° are its <term>Mulatrikona</term>, and the final 10° are its own house. Venus has its <term>Mulatrikona</term> up to 15° in Libra, and the next 15° are its own house. Saturn has its <term>Mulatrikona</term> up to 20° in Aquarius, and the remaining 10° are its own house. ||13||

Now, the author describes the knowledge of <term>Vargottama</term> <note>The "best division," where a planet occupies the same zodiac sign in both the main chart and the ninth-divisional chart</note> and <term>Mulatrikona</term> for the planets using the *Vasantatilaka* meter:

->**The Vargottamas in Moveable signs and the others are the first, middle,**<-
->**and final ninth-parts, respectively; these ninth-parts yield auspicious results.**<-
->**Leo, Taurus, Aries, Virgo, Sagittarius, Libra,**<-
->**and Aquarius are the Mulatrikona houses starting from the Sun.**<- ||14||

Regarding "The Vargottamas": In the Moveable, Fixed, and Dual signs <note>The three categories of zodiac signs: Moveable (Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn), Fixed (Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius), and Dual (Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces)</note>, respectively, the first, middle, and final parts—or the beginning, middle, and end—are known as <term>Vargottama</term>. Another reading says "going through the first, middle, and end." These nine divisions <note>The <term>Navamsha</term> or 1/9th division of a sign</note> are called <term>Vargottama</term>, meaning the "best among the divisional groups." They are the primary ones. Specifically: in Moveable signs (Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn), the first <term>Navamsha</term> is called <term>Vargottama</term>. In Fixed signs (Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius), the middle or fifth <term>Navamsha</term> is <term>Vargottama</term>. In Dual signs (Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces), the final or ninth <term>Navamsha</term> is <term>Vargottama</term>. This means that in each of these cases, the planet is in its own <term>Navamsha</term> <note>original: "svanavamsaka"</note>. As Yavanesvara <note>An early authority on Indianized Greek astrology</note> says: "Those which are in their own houses and their own house-divisions are declared by the Yavanas to be Vargottama." These ninth-part divisions called <term>Vargottama</term> give auspicious results at birth. As will be stated later: "Birth in a Vargottama is auspicious." Similarly, Satyacharya says: "The first divisions in Moveable signs, the middle in Fixed..."

# Brihat Jataka — Chapter on the Distinctions of the Signs

<page-num>34</page-num>
<header>Brihat Jataka — Chapter on the Distinctions of the Signs</header>

...and in the dual <note>mutable</note> signs, the final ones. These are declared to be the **Vargottama** <note>literally "the best division"; refers to a planet occupying the same sign in both the main chart and the ninth-divisional chart</note>; those born in these divisions become leaders in their families.
The purpose [of knowing this] is: "With planets in exaltation or retrograde, the results are tripled; with those in Vargottama, their own divisions, or decanates, the results are doubled."

**Leo, Taurus, and so on:** The signs Leo and the others, in the order they are recited, are the **Mula-Trikona** <note>primary root-trine; a position of strength second only to exaltation</note> houses of the Sun and the other planets. Specifically: Leo is the Mula-Trikona of the Sun; Taurus is that of the Moon; Aries (the first) is that of Mars; Virgo (the sixth) is that of Mercury; Sagittarius (the horse-bodied) is that of Jupiter; Libra (the scales) is that of Venus; and Aquarius is that of Saturn. The purpose is: "Kings are born from humble families when three or more planets are in exaltation or their own Trikonas and are strong," etc. ||14||

**Vernacular Translation** — In the movable, fixed, and dual-natured signs, the first (1st), middle (5th), and last (9th) **Navamshas** <note>one-ninth division of a sign</note> respectively are called **Vargottama** and yield auspicious results. Furthermore, the signs Leo, Taurus, Aries, Virgo, Sagittarius, Libra, and Aquarius are the Mula-Trikonas of the planets starting with the Sun. ||14||

**Special Meaning** — The Navamsha of any sign that is the same as the sign itself is called the "best." For example, in movable signs like Aries, the 1st Navamsha is its own; in fixed signs like Taurus, the middle (5th) is its own; and in dual-natured signs like Gemini, the last (9th) is its own. The application of this is found in the sayings: "Birth in a Vargottama is auspicious" and "Kings are born from humble families when planets are in exaltation or their own Trikonas," etc. ||14||

Now, the author describes the twelve names of the houses starting from the Ascendant, and the **Upachaya** <note>houses of growth or improvement</note> designations for the third, sixth, tenth, and eleventh houses, using the *Vasantatilaka* meter:

-> **The Ascendant and following houses are named: Body, Family, Siblings, Kin,** <-
-> **Son, Enemy, Wife, Death, Virtue, Rank, and Income.** <-
-> **The twelfth is called Loss. The houses of Enemy, Action, Gain,** <-
-> **and the 'Difficult to Conquer' (3rd) are the Upachayas; some say this is not permanent.** <- ||15||

**The Ascendant and following:** Starting from the Ascendant (*Hora*), the names are given in order. The first house (the Ascendant) is named **Body** (*Tanu*). The second is **Family** (*Kutumba*). The third is **Sibling** (*Sahottha*), meaning a brother born with one. The fourth is **Kin** (*Bandhu*), a word signifying relatives. The fifth is named **Son** (*Putra*). The sixth is **Enemy** (*Ari*). The seventh is **Wife** (*Patni*). The eighth is **Death** (*Marana*). The ninth is **Virtue** (*Shubha*). The tenth is **Rank** (*Aaspada*). The eleventh is **Income** (*Aaya*). The twelfth is **Loss** (*Ripha*). The word "etc." indicates these are categories. Therefore, it should be understood that synonyms for "Body" and the others also serve as technical names for the houses.

**The houses of Enemy, Action, Gain, and the 'Difficult to Conquer' are the Upachayas:** The Enemy (6th), Action (10th), Gain (11th), and the house named *Dushchikya* (3rd) are the **Upachaya** <note>increasing</note> houses. "Some say this is not permanent" [refers to the fact that these houses only provide growth if they are not aspected by malefic planets].

<meta>This page continues the technical definitions of the twelve houses of the zodiac, specifically focusing on the "Upachaya" (improvement) houses and introducing alternative names for each house.</meta>

<page-num>35</page-num>
<header>With the Sanskrit commentary of Bhattotpala and the Hindi vernacular explanation</header>

Thus, some authorities describe these houses as not being "permanently" <term>Upachaya</term><note>Upachaya means houses of "increase" or "accumulation," specifically the 3rd, 6th, 10th, and 11th houses.</note>. Their intention is this: if these houses are aspected by a malefic planet or by an enemy of the house's own lord, then they are not considered Upachaya. Regarding this, there is a verse by Garga and others: "The 3rd, 11th, 6th, and 10th shall have the name Upachaya, provided they are not aspected by malefics or the enemies of their own lords."

This view is not intended by the Teacher Varahamihira, because he always treats them as having the name Upachaya. Satya and others agree. Thus, Satya says: "The 10th, 11th, 6th, and 3rd houses from the Ascendant and the Moon are the Upachaya houses; the remaining signs are called Anupachaya (non-increase)." And Yavanesvara says: "The 6th, 3rd, 10th, and 11th signs are called the Upachaya signs from the perspective of the Ascendant and the Moon; the rest are the Apachaya (decreasing) signs." The purpose of this is: "Prosperity is desired when planets are in Upachaya houses, friendly signs, or their exaltation; wealth is not gained when they are in Apachaya houses, debilitation, or enemy signs," and so on. || 15 ||

**Vernacular Translation:** Body (1), Family (2), Co-born (3), Relative (4), Son (5), Enemy (6), Wife (7), Death (8), Auspicious (9), Rank (10), Income (11), and Loss (12)—these are the names of the twelve houses starting from the Ascendant. Also, the four places 6, 10, 11, and 3 have the name Upachaya (growth). Some teachers hold the opinion that these are not "permanently" Upachaya. || 15 ||

**Special Meaning:** For the reasoning behind why the Ascendant and others were given names like "Body," see my commentary on the *Laghu Parashari*. Regarding the Upachaya not being permanent, Garga's verse states: "The 3rd, 11th, 6th, and 10th are Upachaya only if they are not aspected by malefics or enemies of their lord." However, Varahamihira, following Satyacharya, considers them permanently Upachaya. In this way, the places different from Upachaya are known as <term>Apachaya</term><note>Apachaya refers to houses of "decrease" or "decline."</note>. || 15 ||

Again, he states other names for the houses starting from the Ascendant in the Vasantatilaka meter:

### Form, Wealth, Valor, House, and Intelligence, Wound,
### Desire, Chasm, Teacher, Honor, Gain, and Loss.
### The fourth and eighth from the Ascendant are called "Square,"
### The seventh house is "Partner," and the tenth sign is "Command." (1) || 16 ||

**Commentary:** These twelve houses starting from the Ascendant also have names like "Form" (Kalpa) in sequence. For example: the 1st house is called *Kalpa* <note>original: "Kalpa"</note>. The word Kalpa signifies strength or power. The 2nd is *Sva* (Wealth). The 3rd is *Vikrama* (Valor). The 4th is *Griha* (House). The 5th is *Pratibha* (Intelligence). The 6th is *Kshata* (Wound).

<note>(1) The reading "The tenth is the Sky and Command" is also considered correct.</note>

<header>In the Brihat Jataka: Chapter on the Classification of Signs</header>

The seventh house is called <term>Chittottha</term><note>literally "born of the mind/desire," referring to the house of marriage and partnerships</note>. The eighth is <term>Randhra</term><note>meaning "aperture" or "flaw," referring to the house of death and mysteries</note>. The ninth is <term>Guru</term><note>referring to the teacher or fortune</note>. The tenth is <term>Mana</term><note>meaning "honor" or "status"</note>. The eleventh is <term>Bhava</term><note>meaning "gain" or "acquisition"</note>. The twelfth is <term>Vyaya</term><note>meaning "expenditure" or "loss"</note>. Regarding the fourth and eighth from the Ascendant: the fourth and eighth houses from the Ascendant are known by the name <term>Chaturasra</term><note>meaning "quadrangular"</note>. The seventh house from the Ascendant is called <term>Dyuna</term><note>the house of union</note>. The tenth sign is called <term>Ajna</term><note>meaning "command" or "authority"</note>. These names should be known for practical application in astrology. || 16 ||

**Vernacular Commentary—** <term>Kalpa</term> (1), <term>Sva</term> or Wealth (2), <term>Vikrama</term> (3), <term>Griha</term> (4), <term>Pratibha</term> or Intellect (5), <term>Kshata</term> (6), <term>Chittottha</term> or Desire (7), <term>Randhra</term> (8), <term>Guru</term> (9), <term>Mana</term> (10), <term>Bhava</term> (11), and <term>Vyaya</term> (12)—these are the names of the twelve houses starting from the Ascendant. The 4th and 8th houses from the Ascendant are called <term>Chaturasra</term>. The 7th is called <term>Dyuna</term>. <term>Kha</term><note>meaning "sky"</note> and <term>Ajna</term> are names for the 10th house. || 16 ||

->Now, the names of the Centers and the strength of the signs therein are stated in the Dodhaka meter:<-

# The names Kantaka, Kendra, and Chatushtaya refer to the seventh, first, fourth, and tenth houses.
# In these houses, as specified, the Insects, Humans, Water-dwellers, and Quadrupeds are respectively strong. || 17 ||

**Commentary on "Kantaka" etc.**—The seventh, first, and fourth houses are well-known. <term>Khabha</term> refers to the tenth house. <term>Kha</term> means the middle of the sky; the sign residing there at that moment is called <term>Khabha</term><note>the "sky-sign" or Midheaven</note>. Each of these houses—the seventh, first (Ascendant), fourth, and tenth—has three names: <term>Kantaka</term><note>meaning "thorn" or "pivot"</note>, <term>Kendra</term><note>Center</note>, and <term>Chatushtaya</term><note>Quaternary</note>. In these places, as specified, the Insect, Human, Water-dwelling, and Quadruped signs become powerful. Specifically:

*   **Insects:** Scorpio is strong in the 7th house.
*   **Humans:** The human signs—Gemini, Virgo, Libra, the first half of Sagittarius, and Aquarius—are strong when situated in the 1st house (Ascendant).
*   **Water-dwellers:** The aquatic signs—Cancer, Pisces, and the latter half of Capricorn—are strong in the 4th house.
*   **Quadrupeds:** The four-footed signs—Aries, Taurus, Leo, the latter half of Sagittarius, and the first half of Capricorn—are strong in the 10th house.

As the venerable Sage Garga says:
> "Gemini, Aquarius, Virgo, and the first half of Sagittarius—these are known as Human signs, strong when in the Ascendant. Cancer, Pisces, and the latter half of Capricorn are always known as Water signs, strong in the 4th house. Scorpio is the Insect, declared strong in the 7th. The latter half of Sagittarius, Leo, Aries, and Taurus are Quadrupeds, strong in the <term>Kha</term> (10th house)." Here, the word "half" also includes the first half of Capricorn. || 17 ||

**Vernacular Commentary—** **Names of the Centers:** The four places—7th, 1st, 4th, and 10th from the Ascendant—have three names: <term>Kantaka</term>, <term>Kendra</term>, and <term>Chatushtaya</term>. In these houses, in the order read (7, 1, 4, 10), the Insect, Human, Water-dweller, and Quadruped signs are respectively strong. || 17 ||

The first half of Sagittarius, Virgo, Gemini, Aquarius, and Libra are Humans.
The latter half of Capricorn, Pisces, and Cancer are Water signs.
Taurus, Aries, Leo, the first half of Capricorn, and the latter half of Sagittarius are Quadrupeds.
Scorpio is called the Insect. Thus, the signs are of four types.

<page-num>37</page-num>
->Language Commentary with Sanskrit Commentary by Bhattotpala<-

Now, he describes the alternative names for the remaining houses using the *Vasantatilaka* meter—

### **The houses following the Angles are called Panaphara, and those beyond them are Apoklima.**
### **The fourth house is known as Hibuka, Ambu, Sukha, and Veshma.**
### **The seventh is Jamitra and Astabhavana; the fifth is Sutabha and Trikona;**
### **The tenth is Meshurana, and here one should also know it as Karma. || 18 ||**

**From the Angles:** The second house from every Angle <note>Kendra</note> is called **Panaphara** <note>original: "पणफर" - likely derived from the Greek 'epanaphora'</note>. Thus, the 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th houses bear the name Panaphara. **And those beyond:** Every house following a Panaphara is called **Apoklima** <note>original: "आपोक्लिम" - likely derived from the Greek 'apoklima' (decline)</note>. Thus, the 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th houses are named Apoklima. **Hibuka, Ambu, Sukha, and Veshma:** The word *Veshma* is a synonym for "home." The fourth house, previously called Veshma, is also named **Hibuka** <note>original: "हिबुक" - likely from Greek 'hypogeion' (underground)</note>, **Ambu** (Water), and **Sukha** (Happiness). **Jamitra and Astabhavana:** The "Setting House" <note>Astabhavana</note> is the 7th house. Since all planets set in the sign seventh from the rising sign, it is called the Setting House or **Jamitra** <note>original: "जामित्र" - likely from Greek 'diametros' (diameter)</note>. **Sutabha and Trikona:** The 5th house, or *Sutabha* (House of Children), is named **Trikona** (Trine). **Meshurana and the Tenth:** The 10th house is named **Meshurana** <note>original: "मेषूरण" - likely from Greek 'mesouranema' (mid-heaven)</note>. In this 10th house, one should also know the name **Karma** (Action/Work). || 18 ||

**Vernacular Translation:** The four places following the Angles (1, 4, 7, 10)—namely the 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th—are named **Panaphara**. The others (3, 6, 9, 12) are designated **Apoklima**. Hibuka, Ambu, Sukha, and Veshma are four names for the 4th house. Suta and Trikona refer to the 5th house. Meshurana and Karma are names for the 10th house. || 18 ||

Now, he describes the strength of the houses and signs for practical use and their measurements using the *Shardulavikridita* meter—

### **The Ascendant is powerful when aspected by its Lord, Jupiter, or Mercury, and not by others.**
### **Bipeds and others are strong in the Angles during day, night, and the two twilights.**
### **(1) In the first half, the senses and others are multiplied by four for the measure, and the reverse for the rest.**
### **The third house is Duschikya and Sahaja; the ninth is Tapas and the first Trikona. || 19 || 16 ||**

<margin>(1)</margin> **(1) In the first half:** By this, the rising periods <note>ascensional timings</note> in degrees for signs like Aries are calculated for a region where the equinoctial shadow <note>Palabha</note> is approximately 7.5 digits. To demonstrate the calculation of local rising times and the ascensional difference <note>Charapala</note>, the method from the *Grahalaghava* is provided:

**'When the Sun is at the beginning of Aries with its precession, the midday shadow is the Palabha. This, placed in three positions and multiplied by 10, 8, and 10, then divided by the respective divisors, gives the half-ascensional differences...'**

Following this verse, in a region with a 7.5-digit equinoctial shadow, the ascensional differences <note>Charapala</note> for the first three signs are: Aries = 75; Taurus = 60; Gemini = 25. Then—

# Brihat Jataka: Chapter on the Distinctions of the Signs

‘The rising times at the equator <note>original: "Lankodaya"</note> in *vighatikas* <note>a unit of time equal to 24 seconds</note> are 278, 299, 323, 323, 299, and 278. These are increased or decreased by the ascensional difference <note>original: "cara-dala"</note> in direct and inverse order. This does not follow a simple sequence from Aries, but rather these specific values.’
According to this verse, in a place where the equinoctial shadow <note>original: "palabhā"</note> is approximately seven and a half digits, the rising times in *palas* <note>units of time</note> are as follows:

->Equatorial Rising, Ascensional Difference, Local Rising<-

| Sign | Calculation | Result | Rounded Value |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Aries Rising | 278 - 75 | = 203 | = 200 (approx.) |
| Taurus Rising | 296 - 60 | = 236 | = 240 (approx.) |
| Gemini Rising | 323 - 25 | = 298 | = 280 (approx.) |
| Cancer Rising | 323 + 25 | = 348 | = 320 (approx.) |
| Leo Rising | 296 + 60 | = 356 | = 360 (approx.) |
| Virgo Rising | 278 + 75 | = 353 | = 400 (approx.) |

Here, the Teacher <note>referring to Varāhamihira</note> has adopted values increasing by forty *palas* for practical utility in results, as they are close enough to the truth. These, divided by ten, give the values in degrees <note>original: "amshas"</note> for the rising of the six signs starting from Aries:

Aries Rising = 200 ÷ 10 = 20 = 5 X 4.
Taurus Rising = 240 ÷ 10 = 24 = 6 X 4.
Gemini Rising = 280 ÷ 10 = 28 = 7 X 4.
Cancer Rising = 320 ÷ 10 = 32 = 8 X 4.
Leo Rising = 360 ÷ 10 = 36 = 9 X 4.
Virgo Rising = 400 ÷ 10 = 40 = 10 X 4.

These same values in reverse order apply to the six signs starting from Libra.
As stated in the *Siddhanta Shiromani* <note>a famous 12th-century astronomical treatise by Bhāskara II</note>:
> Whichever sign rises in a certain amount of time, its seventh sign sets in that same amount of time. This is because half of the ecliptic <note>original: "apamandala"</note> is always situated above the horizon.
Thus, the logic is established.

**Regarding the term "Horā" <term>Horā: Here refers specifically to the Ascendant or the rising sign (Lagna)</term>:** The *Horā* or Ascendant becomes **exceedingly powerful** <note>original: "vīryotkaṭā"</note> when it is aspected <note>viewed</note> by its own lord <note>the planet ruling that sign</note>. Likewise, it is powerful when occupied by its lord. It is also powerful when aspected or occupied by Jupiter <note>original: "Guru"</note> or Mercury <note>original: "Jña"</note>. "And not by others": this means it does not gain strength if aspected or occupied by planets other than its lord, Jupiter, or Mercury. If it is aspected or occupied by a mixture of those mentioned and those not mentioned, it has medium strength. If it is aspected or occupied only by those other than its lord, Jupiter, or Mercury, it is weak.
As Badarayana <note>an ancient authority on astrology</note> says: "The *Horā* is powerful when occupied or aspected by Jupiter, its own lord, the Moon, or Mercury. It is weak with the remaining planets, and of medium strength with a mixture. It is also weak if not aspected or occupied by any at all." The phrase "situated in the centers" <note>original: "kendrasthāḥ"</note> implies they are exceedingly powerful. Here, the word "etc." should be understood as implied. All signs situated in the *Kendras* <term>Kendra: The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, considered the pillars of a horoscope</term> are strong. Those in the *Panaphara* <term>Panaphara: The 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th houses</term>...

<meta>This page continues the technical commentary on planetary and zodiacal strength, specifically discussing the potency of signs based on their house positions and the calculation of rising times (ascensional periods).</meta>

<header>With the Sanskrit commentary of Bhattotpala and the vernacular explanation</header>

Those situated in *Apoklima* <note>the 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th houses</note> possess weak strength. Here, some interpret the strength of biped, quadruped, and insect signs as being powerful when situated in *Kendra* <note>1st, 4th, 7th, 10th houses</note>, *Panaphara* <note>2nd, 5th, 8th, 11th houses</note>, and *Apoklima* respectively. That is incorrect. Because Badarayana states:

> "All signs situated in the *Kendra* are said to be exceedingly powerful; those in *Panaphara* are considered of medium strength; and all signs in *Apoklima* are said to be of weak strength."

Regarding bipeds and others: "at night and in the two twilights." The phrase "exceeding in vigor" follows from the previous context. Biped, quadruped, and insect signs become exceedingly vigorous during the day, the night, and the two twilights respectively. During the day, bipeds are strong; at night, quadrupeds; and during the two twilights, insects. Here, not only Scorpio, but all watery signs should be understood by the term "insect" <term>Keeta: literally 'insect' or 'creature', referring here to Scorpio and other water signs</term>. On this, Shri Devakirti says:

> "Gemini, Libra, Aquarius, Virgo, and the first half of Sagittarius are strong by day. Aries, Taurus, and Leo are strong at night, as are the first and second halves of Capricorn and Sagittarius <note>referring to specific portions of the signs</note>. Scorpio, Pisces, Cancer, and the latter half of Capricorn are strong during the twilight."

Regarding "In the first half, the *Vishayas* <note>senses</note> multiplied by four": The *Vishayas* refer to the five senses. These, starting from five, are five, six, seven, eight, nine, and ten, and are "multiplied by four" <note>original: *kritaguna*, where *krita* represents the number 4</note>. All these values multiplied by four represent the measure in the first half. Of what? Because it is the subject at hand, it means in the first half of the zodiac—the first six signs. "And inversely": whatever the measure of the six signs starting with Aries is in the first half of the zodiac, that same measure is applied inversely to the six signs starting with Libra.

Specifically: 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10. These, when multiplied by four, become 20, 24, 28, 32, 36, and 40. These are the measures for Aries and the following signs, and by inversion, for Libra and the following. As Satyacharya says:

> "There are twenty parts increasing by four for each sign starting with Aries in the first half; in the latter half starting with Pisces, the measure is the same but in reverse order."

Regarding the usage of "parts" <note>degrees</note> in the celestial sphere: one part corresponds to ten *Chashakas* <term>Chashaka: a unit of time equivalent to 6 seconds</term> in time. This is because a minute of arc in space is a *Prana* <term>Prana: a 'breath' or unit of time</term> in time. As Brahmagupta stated:

> "The Earth rotates one minute of arc on the terrestrial sphere in one *Prana* of time relative to the west of Lanka."

Thus, these parts multiplied by ten become *Chashakas*. From this, it is understood: a *Ghatika* <note>24 minutes</note> of time multiplied by 360 becomes *Pranas*. In space, these are the same as seconds of arc; dividing them by sixty gives the degrees in space. Thus, the "breath-parts" of Aries and the others multiplied by ten become *Chashakas*. Therefore, 200 is the measure for Aries and Pisces. Similarly, 240 for Taurus and Aquarius; 280 for Gemini and Capricorn; 320 for Cancer and Sagittarius; 360 for Leo and Scorpio; and 400 for Virgo and Libra. These same *Chashakas*, divided by ten, are conceptualized as "parts." Since ten *Chashakas* make one part in space.

It is said here: This knowledge is utilized for understanding the meaning in matters such as <term>Nashtachinta</term> <note>astrology concerning lost objects or unspoken thoughts</note> and for determining the short or long stature of a person's limbs. Thus says **Yavaneshwara** <note>An ancient authority on Greek-influenced Indian astrology</note>: "The rising duration of the signs from the first to the last is prescribed as exactly two <term>Muhurtas</term> <note>a unit of time equal to 48 minutes</note> each. Through direct and inverse order, one should know the rising proportions of the two halves of the zodiac. Having understood the houses as short, medium, or long in this way, one should determine the proportions of the body parts corresponding to the divisions of the zodiac." The classification of body parts will be explained later in the verse beginning with "The body parts are divided starting from the Ascendant." In whichever limb a "long" sign or a planet that is the lord of a "long" sign is situated, that limb becomes long; in "medium" signs it is medium, and in "short" signs it is short.

So it is also stated in the **Saravali**: "Pisces, Aries, Aquarius, Gemini, Sagittarius, Cancer, and Capricorn are short and medium <note>specifically: Pisces, Aries, Taurus, and Aquarius are short; Gemini, Sagittarius, Cancer, and Capricorn are even/medium</note>. Scorpio, Virgo, Leo, and Libra are known as long. When these signs are in the Ascendant or other houses, the limbs of all living beings, starting from the head, are born resembling them and the planets occupying them." Likewise, **Satyacharya** says: "A lord of a long sign situated in a long house makes the limb long." In such matters, these distinctions should be applied. The determination of the rising of the Ascendant should be done only through the methods established in the mathematical branch of astronomy. <term>Duschikya</term> is the name for the third house, and <term>Tapas</term> is the name for the ninth house. That ninth house is also called <term>Tri-adyam Trikona</term> <note>the first of the trines</note>.

**Vernacular Commentary:**
If the Ascendant (<term>Lagna</term>) is occupied or aspected by its own lord and by Mercury or Jupiter, and is not occupied or aspected by other planets, it is particularly strong. This implies that if it is also occupied or aspected by other planets, it has medium strength. If it is not aspected by its lord, Mercury, or Jupiter, it is weak. Furthermore, biped (human), quadruped (animal), water-dwelling, and insect signs are strong when in the <term>Kendra</term> <note>angular houses: 1st, 4th, 7th, 10th</note>. They are considered of medium strength in <term>Panaphara</term> <note>succedent houses: 2nd, 5th, 8th, 11th</note> and weak in <term>Apoklima</term> <note>cadent houses: 3rd, 6th, 9th, 12th</note>. Biped signs are strong during the day, quadrupeds at night, and both water-dwelling and insect signs are strong during the twilight. By multiplying the digits starting from five (5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10) by 4, we get (20, 24, 28, 32, 36, 40) which are the rising values in degrees for the first six signs starting from Aries. The third house is named <term>Duschikya</term>, the ninth is <term>Tapas</term>, and it is also called <term>Tritrikona</term>.

*Special Meaning:* For general practice, the teacher has recorded here the values in degrees based on a latitude where the equinoctial shadow (<term>Palabha</term>) is 7.5. This cannot be used in every country. For example, using a <term>Palabha</term> of 7.30, one calculates the ascensional differences (<term>Charakhanda</term>) as 75, 60, and 25. By subtracting and adding these in direct and inverse order to the right ascensions (<term>Lankodaya</term>), the local rising times (<term>Swadeshodaya</term>) in <term>Palas</term> are found. Dividing these <term>Palas</term> by 10 results in the value in degrees.

**Red, white, parrot-green, pale red, smoky-grey,**

"Red" etc. — These colors belong to the signs starting from the first house, Aries, in sequence. Among them, Aries is red (blood-red). Taurus is white (bright). Gemini is the color of a parrot's body, meaning green. Cancer is pale red, the color of the Trumpet Flower <note>original: "Patala"</note>, meaning a slightly blackish-red. Leo is smoky-grey or slightly white. Virgo is variegated, meaning many-colored. Libra is black. Scorpio is like gold (golden-hued). Sagittarius is tawny (yellowish). Capricorn is brindled, a mixed color of white and brownish-grey. Aquarius is deep brown, similar to the color of a mongoose. Pisces is transparent, the color of water or fish. The purpose of this: "In determining non-human births, one should look at the rising degree," as will be explained later.

Regarding "The slope is toward the direction of the lord": The direction of the lord is the "Lord's direction." "Slope" <term>Plavatvam: the inclination or downward direction of a sign</term> refers to the low-lying direction. Every sign's slope is toward the direction associated with its ruling planet. For example, Mars is the lord of Aries and Scorpio; his direction is South, so those two signs are designated as sloping South. Venus is the lord of Taurus and Libra; her direction is Southeast, so they slope Southeast. Mercury is the lord of Gemini and Virgo; his direction is North, so they slope North. The Moon is the lord of Cancer; her direction is Northwest, so it slopes Northwest. The Sun is the lord of Leo; his direction is East, so it slopes East. Jupiter is the lord of Sagittarius and Pisces; his direction is Northeast, so they slope Northeast. Saturn is the lord of Capricorn and Aquarius; his direction is West, so they slope West. Thus, the slope of a sign is known by the direction of its ruler. The purpose: "In cases of theft or loss, it indicates the direction the thief has faced." It is also used in matters of travel.

As stated in the *Saravali* <note>A classic 8th-century astrological text by Kalyanavarman</note>:

> "The slope of the houses is described by the Yavanas <note>The Greeks/Westerners</note> as being toward the village of the lord. For a long time, the King..."

It is said that the planet situated in the second house from the one occupied by the Sun is called <term>Veshi</term> <note>original: "veshi"; a specific solar yoga or configuration</note>. *   The second house is <term>Kutumba</term> (Family). Through this, one investigates one's lineage and wealth.
*   The third house is <term>Sahaja</term> (Siblings) and <term>Vikrama</term> (Valor). Through this, one investigates brothers and personal prowess.

*   The ninth house is <term>Shubha</term> (Auspicious), <term>Guru</term> (Teacher/Elder), and <term>Tapas</term> (Penance). Here, 'Shubha' refers to Virtue (Dharma), 'Guru' refers to mother, father, and elders, and 'Tapas' refers to vows and austerities.
*   The tenth house is <term>Aspada-Karma</term>. 'Aspada' means profession or rank; through these, one investigates actions and status.
*   The eleventh house is <term>Bhava-Aya</term>. 'Bhava' here refers to the acquisition of qualities like knowledge, and 'Aya' refers to income/gain.
*   The twelfth house is <term>Vyaya</term> (Expenditure); through this, one investigates loss or spending.

The third, sixth, tenth, and eleventh houses are called <term>Upachaya</term> (Increasing) houses because they cause growth. Their "increasing" nature is such that even malefic planets situated there can give auspicious results. As it is said: "Except for the sixth house, benefic planets increase the prosperity of every house..."

# Chapter 2: On the Nature and Sources of the Planets

Now begins the explanation of the chapter concerning the varieties of planetary natures. The entire world, moving and unmoving, is composed of the planets. Previously, the division of the limbs of the "Time-Person" <note>original: "Kalapurusha," the personification of Time as the Zodiac</note> was shown through the signs and constellations starting with Aries. By showing that, the Time-Person is revealed to be composed of planets, since the lords of the signs are the planets themselves. Now, the author describes the soul and other attributes as planetary, as well as the planetary roles like "King" which protect the world, using the **Shardulavikridita** meter:

> The Sun is the Soul of the universe; the Moon is the Mind; Mars is Strength; Mercury is Speech; Jupiter is Knowledge and Happiness; Venus is Desire; and Saturn is Sorrow. Of the planetary cabinet, the Sun and Moon are the Kings; Mars is the Leader (Commander); Mercury is the Prince; Jupiter and Venus are the Ministers; and Saturn is the Servant. ||1||

# Brihat Jataka: Chapter on Planetary Natures and Differences
<page-num>44</page-num>

The Sun is the soul of Time. <note>original: "Kalatma" - the soul of the personified Time or the Universe</note> The Moon, whose rays are cool like frost, is the mind. Mars represents strength. <note>original: "Sattva" - here interpreted as courage or vital energy</note> The definition of strength is: "Strength is that which enables action when the desire for success arises." Here, the word strength is a synonym for valor, such as that possessed by lions. As it is said: "Even though he lives alone in the forest, lacks the marks of royalty, and knows no political science, the lion is called King because he relies on his own strength." This implies an excellent innate nature. Mercury is speech. Jupiter represents knowledge and happiness. Venus is desire or passion. Saturn, the son of the Sun, is sorrow.

The mention of "Time" here is to show that Time is all-pervading. Not only are the zodiac signs from Aries onwards the head and other limbs of the Time-Person, but the planets from the Sun onwards are the soul and other internal divisions of the entire world. The practical application is this: "When a planet is afflicted, one must predict suffering for the corresponding limb of the body or the internal quality it represents; when the planet is strong, those qualities are nourished." This applies not only to the general world but to birth charts; strong planets make these qualities (soul, mind, etc.) auspicious, while weak planets make them weak—except for Saturn, where the opposite is true. Thus it is said in the *Saravali*: <note>A classical 8th-century astrological text by Kalyanavarman</note>

-> "The soul and other qualities are strongest when the planets are strong in the sky; <-
-> they are known to be weak when the planets are weak, except for Saturn, for whom the reverse is remembered." <-

Regarding the "Two Kings" and so forth: The Sun and the Moon are the Kings or rulers. Mars, the son of the Earth, is the Leader or Commander-in-Chief. Mercury is the Prince <note>original: "Kumara" - the heir apparent or youth</note>; some say he is the King's son. Jupiter and Venus (the teacher of the demons) are the two Ministers or advisors. Saturn, born of the Sun, is the Servant or slave. One might ask: why is Saturn called a servant in the governance of the world? Even a servant is a protector of his own duties. The application is: if a planet is strong and placed in an "Upachaya" <term>Upachaya: Houses of increase (3, 6, 10, 11) where planets grow stronger over time</term> at the time of birth or inquiry, the person represented by that planet (King, Minister, etc.) will accomplish the seeker's goals; otherwise, they will cause harm.

**Vernacular Translation—** The Sun is the soul of Time (the Supreme Lord in the form of Time), the Moon is the mind, Mars is strength (power), Mercury is speech, Jupiter is knowledge and happiness, Venus is desire, and Saturn is the sorrow of the Time-Person. The Sun and Moon are Kings, Mars is the Commander-in-Chief, Mercury is the Prince, Jupiter and Venus are both Ministers, and Saturn is the Servant (attendant).

**Special Meaning—** The purpose of this is found in the verse: *"The soul and others are stronger when the heavenly bodies are strong..."* When the planets representing the soul, etc., are strong, those qualities are robust; when weak, those qualities are feeble. Furthermore, if the planets representing the King and others are strong at the time of birth or inquiry and are in an increasing house (Upachaya) from the Ascendant, the person will become a King or achieve success through such figures.

Now, for the purpose of practical usage <note>referring to the calculation and interpretation of horoscopes</note>, the author describes the names of the Sun, Moon, Mercury, Mars, and Saturn in the *Shalini* meter—

->**The Sun is Heli; the Moon is Shitarashmi; Mercury, the son of the Moon, is Hemna, Vid, and Bodhana.**<-
->**Mars is Ara, Vakra, Kruradrik, and Avaneya; Saturn, the son of the Sun, is Kona, Manda, and Asita. || 2 ||**<-

**Heli etc.** || The Sun (*Surya*) or *Aditya* is named *Heli* <note>original: "Heli" is likely derived from the Greek "Helios"</note>. The Moon (*Chandrama*) is named *Shitarashmi*, meaning "he whose rays (*rashmi*) are cool (*shita*)." The son of the Moon (*Induputra*), Mercury (*Budha*), has the names *Hemna*, *Vid*, and *Bodhana*. Mars (*Bhauma*) is called *Avaneya* because he is the son of the Earth (*Avani*); his other names are *Ara*, *Vakra* <note>meaning "the twisted" or "retrograde"</note>, and *Kruradrik* <note>meaning "the cruel-eyed"</note>. The son of the Sun (*Suryaputra*), Saturn (*Saura*), has the names *Kona*, *Manda* <note>meaning "the slow one"</note>, and *Asita* <note>meaning "the dark one"</note>. || 2 ||

**Hindi Translation**—The Sun's name is Heli. The Moon's is Shitarashmi. Mercury's names are Induputra, Hemna, Vid, and Bodhana. Mars's are Ara, Kruradrik, and Avaneya. Saturn's are Kona, Manda, Suryaputra, and Asita. || 2 ||

Now, the author describes the names of Jupiter, Venus, Rahu, and Ketu in the *Vasantatilaka* meter—

->**Jupiter is Jiva, Angira, Suraguru, Vachasampati, and Ijya;**<-
->**Venus is Shukra, Bhrigu, Bhrigusuta, Sita, and Asphujit.**<-
->**Rahu is Tamas, Agu, and Asura; Ketu is Shikhi.**<-
->**One should also use other synonyms found in common usage. || 3 ||**<-

**Jiva etc.** || *Jiva* is Jupiter (*Brihaspati*); he is also called *Angira*, *Suraguru* (the teacher or *Guru* of the gods or *Suras*), *Vachasampati* (Lord of Speech), and *Ijya* (the one to be worshipped by the gods). These are the names of Jupiter. *Shukra* is *Bhargava*; he is also *Bhrigu*, *Bhrigusuta* (son of Bhrigu), *Sita* (the white/bright one), and *Asphujit* <note>original: "Asphujit" is likely derived from the Greek "Aphrodite"</note>. The word "and" (*cha*) is used for inclusion. These are the names of Venus. *Rahu* is *Svarbhanu*; he is also *Tamas* (darkness), *Agu* (meaning "without rays," from *a-* "not" and *gu* "rays"), and *Asura* (the demon). These are the names of Rahu. *Ketu* is called *Shikhi*, meaning "he who possesses a crest or tail" (*shikha*). One should also speak of other synonyms obtained from common usage or other scientific texts. For example:

*   **For the Sun:** *Ravi*, *Tikshnamshu* (sharp-rayed), *Divakara* (day-maker), *Bhasvan*, *Tikshnarashmi*, *Bhanu*, *Vivasvan*, etc.
*   **For the Moon:** *Shashanka*, *Tuhinagu* (cold-rayed), *Mriganka* (deer-marked), *Shashi*, *Nishakara* (night-maker), *Nakshatrapati* (lord of the stars), etc.
*   **For Mars:** *Kuja* (earth-born), *Lohita* (the red one), *Bhauma*, *Kshmatanaya* (son of the earth), etc.
*   **For Mercury:** *Saumya*, *Rauhineya*, *Chandri*, *Mrigankatanaya* (son of the moon), *Induja*, etc.
*   **For Jupiter:** *Suri*, *Sureya*, *Vakpati*, *Devapurohita* (priest of the gods), *Indramantri* (advisor to Indra), etc.
*   **For Venus:** *Bhargava*, *Ushanas*, *Daityejya* (priest of the demons), *Asuraguru*, *Daityartvig*, etc.
*   **For Saturn:** *Yama*, *Ravija* (born of the sun), *Patangi*, *Chhayasuta* (son of Chhaya), etc.
*   **For Rahu:** *Saimhikeya*, *Svarbhanu*, *Danava*, *Amritachaura* (thief of the nectar), *Vidhuntuda*, etc. || 3 ||

<meta>This page continues the technical exposition of planetary characteristics and deities, following the previous discussion of planetary colors and natures. It focuses on the presiding deities of the planets and their directional influences.</meta>

# Page 47
### From the Sanskrit Commentary by Bhattotpala, with Hindi-style Explanatory Notes

Knowledge of the color of stolen or lost property is determined by the planet's color; in a birth chart or at the time of a query <note>Prashna: a branch of astrology where a chart is cast for the moment a question is asked</note>, the gain or loss of said property is predicted accordingly.

In the worship of the planets, flowers of the corresponding color should be used. As **Yajnavalkya** <note>An ancient sage and legal authority</note> states: "With colors in the mandalas <note>Sacred circular diagrams</note>."

Regarding the phrase *Vahni* etc.: The phrase "Lords of the Sun and others" follows. The lords of the Sun and the other planets are as follows:
*   **The Sun's** lord and master is **Agni** (Fire).
*   **The Moon's** is **Ambu** (Water).
*   **Mars's** is **Agnija** (Fire-born), meaning **Kumar** or **Kartikeya** <note>The god of war</note>.
*   **Mercury's** is **Keshava** (Vishnu).
*   **Jupiter's** is **Indra** (Shatakratu).
*   **Venus's** is **Shachi** (Indrani, the wife of Indra).
*   **Saturn's** is **Ka** (Prajapati), meaning **Brahma** <note>The creator god</note>.

**The Purpose:** In the ritual worship of planets, these specific presiding deities must be worshipped. Thus says **Yavaneshwara** <note>Literally "Lord of the Greeks," a title for authorities in the Indo-Greek astrological tradition</note>:

> "The deities of the planets are Water, Fire, Vishnu, Prajapati, Skanda, and Mahendra. One should perpetually worship these during sacrifices for the Moon, Sun, Mercury, Saturn, Mars, Jupiter, and Venus."

Furthermore, when determining the name of a thief, one uses the synonymous names of the deity associated with the strongest planet. Also, before a journey, one should worship the deity of the planet ruling that direction and then depart. As stated in the **Saravali** <note>A classic 8th-century astrological text by Kalyanavarman</note>:

> "Copper, white, red, green, yellow, variegated, and black are the colors of the Sun and others. Fire, Water, Guha (Skanda), Keshava, Indra, Shachi, and Brahma are the lords. By worshipping the planetary deities of the East and other directions with their respective mantras, a King quickly obtains gold, elephants, and vehicles from his enemies."

Regarding the phrase *Pragadyah* (East and others): The directions begin with the East. The Sun and others are the lords of these directions:
*   In the **East**, the **Sun** (Aditya) is the lord.
*   In the **South-East**, **Venus**.
*   In the **South**, **Mars** (Angaraka).
*   In the **South-West**, **Rahu** (Tamas).
*   In the **West**, **Saturn** (Sauri).
*   In the **North-West**, the **Moon** (Indu).
*   In the **North**, **Mercury** (Vit).
*   In the **North-East**, **Jupiter** (Suraguru).

**The Purpose:** This is used to determine the location of the door in a birth-room based on the planet in the center (Kendras), or the direction a thief has fled in cases of lost property.

Regarding the phrase *Kshinendu* (Waning Moon): The Moon is considered "waning" from the second half of the eighth day of the dark fortnight until the second half of the eighth day of the bright fortnight. In the context of calculating longevity (Ayurdaya), the Moon is waning from the end of the thirteenth day of the dark fortnight until it emerges from the Sun's orb at the end of the New Moon. However, **Yavaneshwara** does not wish for the Moon to ever be considered truly "malefic" (Papa); his statement is:

> "In the month, from the start of the first day of the bright fortnight, the Moon has medium strength for ten days. It is at its best (full strength) during the second ten days, and of little strength in the third ten days. If aspected by benefics, it is always strong."

And further:

> "The Sun is a cruel planet; Mars and Saturn are malefic. Venus, the Moon, and Jupiter are benefics. Mercury is a benefic when with benefics, but becomes malefic when mixed with others, taking on the nature of those it joins."

Therefore, the Sun, Mars, and Saturn are always malefic. Mercury, when joined with them, is also malefic. The rest are benefics. The Moon is a benefic from the middle of the bright eighth day to the middle of the dark eighth day. Mercury is a benefic when free from malefic influence. Jupiter and Venus are always benefics.

**The Purpose:** From the strength of the malefic or benefic planets, one knows whether a person's nature will be sinful or virtuous. || 5 ||

**Vernacular Commentary—** Copper-colored, white, blood-red, green, yellow, variegated, and black—the planets starting from the Sun are the lords of these colors respectively. Furthermore, Agni <note>the Fire god</note>, Varuna <note>the Water god; original: "Jala"</note>, Kartikeya <note>the god of war</note>, Vishnu, Indra, Indrani, and Brahma are the presiding deities of the planets starting from the Sun in order. The Sun, Venus, Mars, Rahu, Saturn, the Moon, Mercury, and Jupiter are the lords of the directions starting from the East. Additionally, the waning Moon, the Sun, Mars, and Saturn are considered malefic planets <term>Papagraha: planets that exert a challenging or unfavorable influence</term>; if Mercury is joined with these, it also becomes a malefic. All others (the Full Moon, Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus) are benefic planets <term>Shubhagraha: planets that exert a favorable or auspicious influence</term>. || 5 ||

**Special Meaning—** The knowledge of colors is used to identify the color of lost items or to determine the color of objects gained or lost based on the strongest planet at the time of birth. In the propitiation <note>Shanti: rituals to pacify planetary influences</note> of planets, the respective presiding deities are worshipped. Similarly, in the worship of a deity, their corresponding planet is honored. The direction of the strongest planet in a quadrant <note>Kendra</note> determines the direction of the door of the delivery room <note>Sutika-griha</note> or the direction in which a thief has fled. Furthermore, on the day associated with a directional lord, that direction possesses directional strength <term>Digbala</term>, while the opposite direction contains a directional "spike" or obstacle <term>Dikshula</term>. || 5 ||

->Now, the author describes the gender classification and the lordship over the Great Elements using the Aupachhandasika meter:<-

**Mercury and the son of the Sun (Saturn) are called eunuchs; the Moon and Venus are female; the remaining are male.**
**The lords of Fire, Earth, Ether, Water, and Air are the planets starting with the son of the Earth (Mars) in sequence. || 6 ||**

**Mercury and the son of the Sun:** Mercury (the son of the Moon) and Saturn (the son of the Sun) are known as eunuchs <note>neuter gender</note>. The Moon and Venus (the descendant of Bhrigu) are designated as female. The remaining—the Sun, Jupiter, and Mars—are designated as male. **The Purpose:** In birth charts, queries, or matters of lost property, the strongest planets represent their own gender. If these planets are afflicted, those represented by that gender suffer affliction. **Fire, Earth, Ether, Water, and Air:** Of these five Great Elements <term>Mahabhutas</term>, the five planets starting with Mars are the lords in sequence. Specifically: Mars (the son of the Earth) is the lord of Fire <note>Shikhi</note>. Similarly, Mercury is the lord of Earth. Jupiter is the lord of Ether <note>Akasha</note>. Venus is the lord of Water. Saturn is the lord of Air. The word "qualities" <note>Guna</note> is used here to complete the poetic meter. One might ask why the Sun and Moon are not mentioned here; it is because it was stated previously that they represent Fire and Water respectively, and they are well-known as such. **The Purpose:** During their major periods <term>Dasha</term>, they manifest the "aura" or "shadow" <note>Chhaya</note> produced by their respective Great Element, as will be stated later: "All planets manifest the shadow created by the Great Elements." || 6 ||

**Vernacular Commentary—** Mercury and Saturn are neuter. The Moon and Venus are female planets. The rest (Sun, Mars, and Jupiter) are male planets. Furthermore, the lords of the five elements—1. Fire, 2. Earth, 3. Ether, 4. Water, and 5. Air—are respectively the five planets: Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn. || 6 ||

## With the Sanskrit Commentary of Bhattotpala and Hindi Explanation

**Special Meaning**—At the time of birth for a newborn, or at the time of inquiry for a thief and others, their male or female nature is understood through the male and female planets. Furthermore, during the auspicious period <note>Dasha</note> of planets, happiness is derived from the qualities related to their respective elements <note>Tattvas</note>; during inauspicious periods, suffering arises from those same elemental qualities. ---

Now, in the *Upajati* meter, he describes the planets' lordship over the social classes beginning with Brahmins, and the division of their inherent qualities:

**Venus and Jupiter rule the Brahmins and others; Mars and the Sun rule the warriors; the Moon rules the merchants, and Mercury the laborers; while Saturn rules the outcasts. The Moon, Sun, and Jupiter; Mercury and Venus; and Mars and Saturn represent, in order, the qualities of Purity, Passion, and Ignorance. || 7**

**Venus and Jupiter and others** || Regarding the four social classes beginning with the Brahmins, the planets are the lords or masters. Venus <note>Bhargava</note> and Jupiter <note>Brihaspati</note>—these two are the lords of the Brahmins. Mars <note>Bhauma</note> and the Sun <note>Aditya</note>—these two are the lords of the Kshatriyas <note>the warrior/ruling class</note>. The Moon <note>Shashi</note> is the lord of the Vaishyas <note>the merchant/landowner class</note>. Mercury is the lord of the Shudras <note>the laborer class</note>. Saturn <note>Asita</note> is the lord of the outcasts <note>Antyajas</note> and those born of mixed or inverse social orders, such as the Chandala, Magadha, and Nishada. 

**The Purpose:** In matters of theft or lost property, the influence of the thief's social class is determined by the strength of the planets. If these planets are afflicted, the corresponding class is afflicted. As Sage Satya says:

> "Jupiter and Venus; the Sun and Mars; the Moon and Mercury; and Saturn—these are the lords of the Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, Shudras, and the mixed classes. In victory or defeat, in satisfaction or displeasure, in loss of wealth or gain, they bestow merits and faults upon those respective groups."

**The Moon, Sun, and Jupiter, etc.** || The Moon, the Sun, and Jupiter are designated as *Sattva* <note>Purity/Goodness</note>. Mercury <note>Jna</note> and Venus <note>Sita</note>—these two are designated as *Rajas* <note>Passion/Activity</note>. Mars <note>Angaraka</note> and Saturn <note>Arki</note>—these two are designated as *Tamas* <note>Ignorance/Inertia</note>. These planets are the lords of the qualities of *Sattva* and the others in that order. 

**The Purpose:** "The nature of the person is like the quality—Sattva, Rajas, or Tamas—of the planet in whose thirtieth-division <note>Trimshansha</note> the Sun is placed." Others describe the nature based on the strength of the planets. As Shri Devakirti says:

> "The person born possesses the quality of whichever planet is strongest."

Here, the Author <note>Varahamihira</note> has a difference of opinion with Yavaneshwara <note>The Lord of the Greeks/Ionians</note>. By the latter, Mars is called *Sattvic* <note>Pure</note>. As his statement says:

> "The Sun, Mars, and Jupiter are high in Sattva; the son of Bhrigu (Venus) and the Moon are Rajasic; Saturn is Tamasic, while Mercury gains specific qualities from its associations."

The Author prefers the word of Satya. As Satya says:

> "Mars and Saturn are Tamasic; Venus and the son of the Moon (Mercury) are Rajasic; Jupiter, the Moon, and the Sun are Sattvic. The natures of men are like the planets."

Thus, wherever the Author differs from Yavaneshwara, he accepts the opinion of Satya. Now, it was previously mentioned that Mars represents *Sattva*. Why then was it said that the Moon, Sun, and Jupiter are *Sattva*? It is explained: Here, the word *Sattva* refers to a quality synonymous with "courage" or "spirit," which exists even in lions and others who engage in actions (right or wrong), and by which they live alone in the forest. As it is said: "In solitude..."

# Chapter on the Varieties of Planetary Natures

...one who dwells in forests, lacks royal marks, and is ignorant of the sciences of ethics. However, if the Lion <note>the zodiac sign Leo</note> is occupied by a planet in the state of *Sattva* <note>purity/goodness</note>, the words "He is a King" come to fruition.

Now, the nature of the three *Gunas* <note>the three fundamental qualities of nature: Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas</note>:
**"One who is dominant in *Sattva* possesses compassion, stability, truthfulness, honesty, and devotion to spiritual teachers and the divine. One dominant in *Rajas* <note>passion/activity</note> is a man whose mind is attached to poetry, arts, rituals, and women, and who is exceedingly brave. One dominant in *Tamas* <note>darkness/ignorance</note> is a deceiver of others, foolish, lazy, prone to anger, and excessively sleepy."**

**Vernacular Translation:** Venus and Jupiter are the lords of the Brahmins <note>the priestly class</note>; Mars and the Sun are the lords of the Kshatriyas <note>the warrior/ruling class</note>; the Moon is the lord of the Vaishyas <note>the merchant class</note>; and Saturn is the lord of the lower classes. Furthermore, the Moon, Sun, and Jupiter are of the *Sattva* quality; Mercury and Venus are of the *Rajas* quality; and Mars and Saturn are of the *Tamas* quality.

**Special Meaning:** The purpose of this is to understand the caste or class of a thief, etc., based on the strongest planet at the time of a query. It is also used to understand the qualities of a person born under a specific birth chart, as in "the nature is according to whichever quality—Sattva, Rajas, or Tamas—the Sun occupies in the thirty-degree division <note>Trimsamsa</note>."

->Now, the physical forms of the Moon and the Sun are described in the *Totaka* meter:<-

**The Sun has eyes tawny like honey, a square body, a bilious temperament, and sparse hair. The Moon has a thin but rounded body, is dominated by the humors of wind and phlegm, is wise, possesses soft speech, and has beautiful eyes.**

**Commentary:** "Eyes tawny like honey" means his gaze is the color of honey, slightly reddish-brown. "A square body" means his height is equal to the span of his outstretched arms. "A bilious temperament" means an excess of bile <note>Pitta</note>. "Sparse hair" means thin hair. Such is the Sun. "A thin but rounded body" means his limbs are slender yet circular. "Wind and phlegm" refers to an abundance of the *Vata* and *Kapha* humors. "Wise" means intelligent. "Soft speech" means he speaks gently. "Beautiful eyes" means his eyes are pleasant to look upon. Such is the Moon.

**Vernacular Translation:** Honey-colored eyes, a square-shaped body (equal in length and width), an excess of bile, and little hair—this is the form of the Sun. A small and rounded body, an excess of wind and phlegm, wise (intelligent), soft-spoken, and beautiful eyes—this is the form of the Moon.

**Special Meaning:** The purpose of this is to describe the physical appearance and temperament of the person born, based on the rule that "the body resembles the lord of the rising sign or the lord of the Navamsa <note>the ninth-part sub-divison</note>."

->Now, the forms of Mars and Mercury are described in the *Swagata* meter:<-

**Mars has a cruel gaze, a youthful form, is generous, bilious, very fickle, and has a slender waist. Mercury possesses a stuttering speech, is always fond of laughter, and has a temperament composed of bile, wind, and phlegm.**

**Commentary:** "Cruel gaze" means Mars has a harsh or fierce look. "Youthful form" means his body and appearance always look young. "Generous" means he is a giver. "Bilious" means an abundance of bile...

Regarding the knowledge of the garments of the woman in childbirth <note>Sutika: a woman who has recently given birth</note> and in inquiries regarding stolen or lost items, the knowledge of the material is derived from the strongest planet. "Copper shall be," etc.: Copper belongs to the Sun; gems to the Moon; gold to Mars; and for Mercury, <term>Yukti</term> <note>literally "joining" or "alloy"</note> is appropriate, meaning brass, bell-metal, and the like. Silver belongs to Jupiter, and also gold when he is situated in his own place <note>his own zodiac sign</note>. Pearls belong to Venus. Iron (black metal), lead, and tin belong to Saturn. This was likewise stated in the <term>Sukshma Jataka</term> <note>The "Short Book of Births," a concise astrological treatise</note>:

> "Copper, gems, gold, alloys, silver, pearls, and iron are to be declared by the Sun and the following planets when they are strong; gold is also for Jupiter when in his own place."

And so says <term>Badarayana</term> <note>An ancient sage and authority on astrology</note>:

> "The Sun's is copper; the Moon's are gems; Mars' is gold; and the son of the Moon (Mercury) has alloys. They say silver belongs to Jupiter when staying in his own house, and gold as well; pearls belong to Venus. Those who know these things declare lead and black iron for the one born of the body of the hot-rayed one (Saturn)."

The application: In the <term>Sutika-griha</term> <note>the delivery room</note>, the presence of these materials is determined by the strongest planet; in inquiries about stolen or lost items, it is for the identification of the lost object. During a favorable planetary period <note>Dasha</note>, if that planet is in an "upachaya" <note>improving/growing</note> house, the object is recovered; if the opposite is true, it is lost. Regarding the phrase "By the Decans" <note>Drekkana: a 10-degree division of a zodiac sign</note>, etc.: Here, the author has indicated the planets starting from Saturn and ending with Jupiter using the initial letters of the verse (Sha, Shu, Ru, Cha, Jna, Gu) to fit the meter. When Saturn, Venus, Mars, the Moon, Mercury, or Jupiter are rising in the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note>, the six seasons beginning with Winter <note>Shishira</note> are to be known. There, Saturn (indicated by 'Sha') rising in the Ascendant indicates the Winter season. Venus ('Shu') indicates Spring <note>Vasanta</note>. Mars ('Ru' for Rudhira) indicates Summer <note>Grishma</note>. The Moon ('Cha') indicates the Rainy season <note>Varsha</note>. Mercury ('Jna') indicates Autumn <note>Sharad</note>. Jupiter ('Gu') indicates the Pre-winter season <note>Hemanta</note>. When the Sun rises, it is also Summer. As Badarayana says:

> "They declare Summer for Mars and the Sun."

The word "or" connects with "By the Decans." The seasons beginning with Winter are known by the rising Decans belonging to Saturn and the others. This is what is meant: if there is no planet in the Ascendant, and a Decan of Saturn is rising, it is Winter. Likewise, a Decan of Venus indicates Spring; a Decan of Mars indicates Summer; a Decan of the Sun also indicates Summer; a Decan of the Moon indicates the Rainy season; a Decan of Mercury indicates Autumn; and a Decan of Jupiter indicates Pre-winter. It should be understood that the primary method for indicating the season is by the planet rising; if no planet is present, then by the Decan. Even if many planets are rising, some say it is by the Decan alone. Others explain that if many are rising, it is by the strongest planet. As <term>Manittha</term> <note>An ancient authority on astrology, often associated with Greek/Yavana traditions</note> says:

> "When the Sun and others have reached the Ascendant, the indication of the season belongs to whichever planet is strongest."

Thus it is known: the season mentioned for the planet situated in the Ascendant should be declared. If many are in the Ascendant, use the strongest; if no planets are present, the season is indicated by the Lord of the Decan. The application:

> "The indication of the season is used in 'Nasta-Jataka' <note>the reconstruction of a lost birth chart</note> and in inquiries regarding stolen or lost items."

The Teacher <note>Varahamihira</note> has not mentioned the planetary lordship over the Vedas here. However, it is stated in the <term>Svalpa Jataka</term>:

> "Jupiter, Mercury, Mars, and Venus are the lords of the Rig, Atharva, Sama, and Yajur Vedas."

Jupiter is the lord of the Rig Veda; Mercury is the lord of the Atharva Veda...

<meta>This page continues the technical commentary on planetary aspects (drishti) in Vedic astrology, specifically following the rules of how planets "look" at other houses from their current position.</meta>

<page-num>55</page-num>
<header>With the Sanskrit commentary of Bhattotpala and the vernacular explanation</header>

**The Three-Ten and so on:** In whichever place the planets are situated, they look upon the third, tenth, and other positions with an increase of one quarter <term>charana-avriddhitah; a gradual increase in visual strength by 25% increments</term>. A planet situated in a particular zodiac sign looks at the third and tenth signs from itself with a "quarter-sight" <note>25% strength</note>. Likewise, it looks at the "Trine" positions—the ninth and fifth—with "half-sight" <note>50% strength</note>. In the "Square" positions—the eighth and fourth—it looks with "three-quarters sight" <note>75% strength</note>. It looks at the seventh house with "full-sight" <note>100% strength</note>. The word *abhi* in the phrase "increase of quarters" denotes repetition or sequence. This means they look with increasing quarters of vision and provide results in proportion to that strength of sight. As stated in the *Svalpajataka*:

> "At the tenth and third, the ninth and fifth, the fourth and eighth, and the spouse <note>the 7th house</note>; they look with an increase of quarters and grant fruits accordingly."

Furthermore, a planet does not look at positions not mentioned here. As stated in the *Saravali*:

> "All planets always look to the left with an increase of quarters, reaching the third/tenth, the trines, the squares, and the seventh in sequence. Saturn <note>original: Ravija, 'Son of the Sun'</note> sees the third and tenth with full sight; Jupiter <note>original: Jiva</note> the trines; Mars <note>original: Bhumisuta, 'Son of the Earth'</note> the squares; while Venus, the Sun, Mercury, and the Moon look fully at the seventh <note>original: Kalatra, 'the spouse'</note>."

Likewise, Yavaneshwara <note>The "Lord of the Greeks," an early authority in Indian astrology</note> says:

> "Excluding the two signs behind, the sixth, and the second from their occupied sign, a planet looks at the remaining signs at all times; the desired sight is ordained among these. Full fruit of the sight is in the seventh house <note>Jamitra-bha</note>, one quarter less in the two squares, half the fruit in the two trines, and one quarter in the third <note>Duschikya</note> and tenth."

**Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars:** The word *kila* <note>translated as 'it is said'</note> is used here to indicate traditional oral transmission. The rule of "increase by quarters" follows. These planets, Saturn and the others—

*(The place of knowledge)* the ninth and *(the place of righteousness)* <insert>the Dharma-sthana</insert> are seen with two quarters of vision. Even more than knowledge and righteousness, sight is cast upon happiness and death; therefore, it is appropriate that planets look upon the house of happiness (the fourth) and the house of death (the eighth) with three quarters of vision. Likewise, it is a well-known fact of nature that everyone casts their full gaze upon the wife (the woman). As said by Bhartrihari:

### "Even the likes of Vishvamitra and Parashara, who lived on air, water, and leaves,
### fell into delusion the moment they saw the lovely lotus-face of a woman."

And so on. Therefore, what wonder is there that all planets look upon the seventh (the house of the wife) with a full gaze?

Furthermore, the special rules for Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars are explained through logic: Saturn is a servant, and thus it is his duty to protect the kingdom and its power; therefore, it is fitting that Saturn looks at the third <note>valor</note> and tenth <note>kingdom/career</note> with full sight. Likewise, the protection of knowledge and righteousness is the work of the Teacher <note>Jupiter</note>; thus, it is appropriate that Jupiter looks at the trines <note>5th and 9th houses</note> with full sight. Similarly, the protection of death and happiness is the work of a leader; therefore, the leader Mars looks at those places (the squares). Finally, Kings, Princes, and commoners are all attached to their wives; thus, it is appropriate that they (Sun, Moon, and Mercury) look at the seventh (the house of the wife) with full sight.
