# Chapter on the Nature and Differences of the Planets

Through a gradual increase of one quarter <note>The text refers to 'pada' or quarters of sight</note>, the planets provide progressively greater results in their viewing or "aspecting" of other positions. **Saturn** (the son of the Sun) provides a quarter-result in its sight. **Jupiter** (the immortal light) provides a half-result. **Mars** (the blood-red one) provides a result minus one quarter <note>i.e., three-quarters result</note>. The others—the **Sun, Moon, Mercury, and Venus**—give full results in their viewing. This is the natural strength of the planets' aspects. Some explain that the primary result of these aspects depends on their specific positions; others say this refers to the strength of the house or place.

Therefore, when looking at planets or zodiac signs located in the third, tenth, and other houses, Saturn and the others become more effective in their sight. For example: Saturn, when looking at planets or signs in the 3rd and 10th houses, is more effective than other planets. This means he sees them "fully." Similarly, Jupiter sees those in the trine <note>the 5th and 9th houses</note>, Mars those in the square <note>the 4th and 8th houses</note>, and the Sun, Moon, Mercury, and Venus those in the 7th house. This is the opinion of many teachers. As the Lord **Garga** says:

-> "Saturn for the 3rd and 10th, Jupiter for the trines, Mars for the 4th and 8th, and the rest for those situated in the 7th; these planets are always said to have superior strength in their viewing." <-

**Vernacular Explanation:** From their respective occupied positions, planets look at the 3rd and 10th houses with one quarter sight; the 5th and 9th with two quarters; the 4th and 8th with three quarters; and the 7th house with four quarters (full) sight. Having stated this general rule, the specific rule is given: Saturn also sees the 3rd and 10th, Jupiter the 5th and 9th, and Mars the 4th and 8th with full sight. The remaining planets see only the 7th with full sight.

It is thus established that they do not "see" houses other than these (namely the 1st, 2nd, 6th, 8th, 11th, and 12th). They grant results according to the strength of this sight. As stated in the *Laghu Jataka*:

> "They see with an increase of quarters and grant results in the same way."

Now, the author describes the time periods and tastes associated with the planets in the *Vaitaliya* meter:

**A half-year, a moment, a day, a season, a month, a fortnight, and a year—these belong to the planets starting from the Sun.**
**Pungent, saline, bitter, mixed, sweet, sour, and astringent are the tastes in the same order. || 14 ||**

**Commentary:** Starting from the Sun, the time periods are assigned. A half-year <term>Ayana: the six-month period of the sun's transit</term> is indicated by the Sun. A moment <term>Kshana: specifically a Muhurta or 48-minute period</term> is indicated by the Moon. A day is indicated by Mars. A season <note>consisting of two months</note> is indicated by Mercury. A month is indicated by Jupiter. A fortnight <note>half a month or Paksha</note> is indicated by Venus. A year is indicated by Saturn.

**The Application:** In a query chart <note>Prashna: a chart cast for the moment a question is asked</note>, one should look at the planet ruling the rising <term>Navamsha: a one-ninth division of a zodiac sign</term>. The number of divisions that planet has moved through indicates the number of half-years, moments, etc., that will pass before the good or bad results manifest.

## With the Sanskrit Commentary of Bhattotpala and the Hindi Language Explanation

(1) Others explain it this way: Whatever number the <term>Navamsha</term><note>A 1/9th division of a zodiac sign, used for precision in Vedic astrology.</note> is that has risen in the Ascendant, the time period should be stated according to that number and the lord of that portion. Thus says Manittha: "The time is equal to the lord of the Ascendant's portion, and the number is equal to the portions risen in the Ascendant. This should be declared in matters of victory over enemies, conception, or the undertaking of a task." Regarding "Pungent, Salty," etc.: the instruction of tastes like pungent starts from the Sun. Among them, from the Sun comes the instruction of the pungent taste, such as black pepper. From the Moon, salty. From Mars, bitter, such as Neem. From Mercury, a mixture of all six tastes. From Jupiter, sweet. From Venus, sour. From Saturn, astringent. The application: At the time of conception, whichever planet is strongest, the pregnant woman will have a <term>dohada</term><note>A specific pregnancy craving believed to reflect the nature of the soul entering the womb.</note> for the taste associated with that planet. Thus it is said in the *Saravali*: "In the third month of women, a craving necessarily arises. That should be considered through the planetary lordship of tastes and the combinations in the Ascendant." Also, in a question regarding food, one can know the taste of the meal consumed or to be consumed based on the planet rising or the rising Navamsha. || 14 ||

**Vernacular Translation—** One should understand the divisions of time—Half-year, <term>Muhurta</term><note>A unit of time approximately 48 minutes long.</note>, Day, Season, Month, Fortnight, and Year—sequentially from the Sun and other planets. Similarly, from the Sun and other planets, one should understand the tastes: Pungent, Salty, Bitter-mixed (all tastes combined), Sweet, Sour, and Astringent. || 14 ||

**Special Meaning—** This is applied in questions regarding the victory or defeat of an enemy, the arrival of a foreigner, etc. For example, whatever number the Navamsha of a planet is in the Ascendant, the auspicious or inauspicious result should be understood in that planet's specific unit of time. As the verse from *Saravali* states: "The time is equal to the lord of the Ascendant's portion, and the number is equal to the portions risen in the Ascendant..."

**Example—** Suppose someone asks, "In how many days will my work be accomplished?" If the calculated Ascendant at the time of the query is 3s 15° 20' 24" (Cancer), it falls in the 5th Navamsha. Therefore, the lord of the Navamsha is Mars. Since Mars indicates "Months," one should say the work will be completed in the 5th month. Similarly, if someone asks, "What taste did I eat today, or will I eat?" one should calculate the Ascendant and look at the planets therein...

---

(1) The method for knowing which Navamsha a planet occupies relative to the Ascendant's portion is shown:
Subtract the planet's position from the Ascendant and convert the remainder into degrees. Then use the proportion: if 30 degrees yield 9 Navamshas, then how many do the degrees of the interval between the Ascendant and the planet yield? The result is the number of Navamshas. Furthermore, for the Sun's Navamsha number, divide by two; if the remainder is one, it is the Northern Solstice <note>original: "Uttarayana"</note>, if two, the Southern Solstice <note>original: "Dakshinayana"</note>. Similarly, the Moon's Navamsha number divided by fifteen gives the <term>Muhurtas</term>. The Navamsha number of Mars indicates the days starting from Sunday. Mercury's Navamsha number divided by six gives the Season. Jupiter's Navamsha number divided by twelve gives the month starting from Chaitra. Venus's Navamsha number divided by two gives the Fortnight. Saturn's Navamsha number indicates the number of years. This is the direction of calculation.

**Now, the method for determining friends and enemies is stated in the Shardulavikritita meter—**

# **Jupiter; Jupiter and Mercury; Venus and the Son of the Moon; all except the Sun; all except Mars;**
# **all except the Moon and Sun; and all except Mars, the Moon, and the Sun are the friends respectively. This is the opinion of some.**
# **According to the statement of Satyacharya, friends are the lords of the 2nd, 12th, 5th, 9th,**
# **the lord of the planet's exaltation sign, the 8th, and the 4th from one's own Mula-Trikona sign; others are not, due to conflict with their own characteristics. ।। 15 ।।**

Regarding "Jupiter" etc. ।। Jupiter and the others are the friends of the planets starting with the Sun in sequence. Among them, for the Sun, Jupiter is the friend. For the Moon, Jupiter and Mercury are the friends. For Mars, Venus and the Son of the Moon <note>Mercury</note> are the friends. For Mercury, all planets except the Sun are friends. For Jupiter, all planets except Mars are friends. For Venus, all planets except the Moon and the Sun are friends. For Saturn, all except Mars, the Moon, and the Sun are friends. This is the opinion of some <note>referring to older authorities</note>, not of many. In this view, they only recognize the behavior of friends and enemies, not neutral behavior; therefore, some authorities like the Yavana masters <note>Greek/Ionian astrologers</note> believe that those other than friends are simply enemies. Thus says Yavaneshvara:

> 'Jupiter is the friend of the Sun, others are otherwise. For Jupiter, all are friends except Mars. For the son of Bhrigu <note>Venus</note>, all are declared friends except the Sun and Moon. For Mars, Venus and the Moon are friends. For the Moon, one should know Mercury and the Teacher of the Gods <note>Jupiter</note> as friends. For Saturn, the friends are those excluding Mars, the Moon, and the Sun; know the rest to be the same for men.'

Regarding "According to the statement of Satyacharya" <note>Satyacharya was a highly respected ancient authority often cited by Varahamihira</note>. In the authoritative Shastra of Satya, from one's own <term>Mula-Trikona: a specific favorable sign position for a planet</term>, the lords of the 2nd, 12th, 5th, 9th, the lord of the planet's exaltation sign, the 8th, and the 4th are the friends of that planet. Here, "Trikona" refers to the Mula-Trikona sign. From that sign: the lord of the 2nd house, the lord of the 12th house, the lord of the 5th house, the lord of the 9th house, the lord of the planet's exaltation sign, the lord of the 8th house, and the lord of the 4th house—these planets become friends. This division of friends and enemies should not be imagined with other planets who are lords of houses not mentioned here, because of conflict. "Conflict with their own characteristics" means that because of their own nature, there is an opposition. This is what is being said. That which—

The specific rules for the classification of friendly characteristics have been shown; therefore, the planets that are lords of other houses <note>houses not mentioned in the rule</note> are not friends of the planet. And so says Satyacharya:

> "From the trine house of a planet, the lords of the **fifth**, the **twelfth**, the **second**, the **fourth** <note>original: *svajana* - kinsmen, referring to the 4th house</note>, the **eighth**, the **ninth**, and the house of its **exaltation** are friends; the others are not."

The fourth house is designated as "kinsmen." From this, the lord of two [favorable] houses is termed a "friend"; the lord of one [favorable] house is "neutral" <note>original: *madhyama* - middling</note>; and the lord of houses not mentioned is an "enemy." As he will say later:

> "Consider the lords of two, one, or no [favorable] houses as friends, neutrals, and enemies respectively, along with their natural relationships."

Regarding the statement that the lord of one house is neutral: it is said that the lords of the Moon and Sun <note>the Moon and Sun only rule one sign each</note> are also termed friends. Because they lack lordship over two signs, the planet that is the lord of two signs attains the status of "lord of two houses" by virtue of being the lord of an exaltation sign; nevertheless, it should be understood as a lord of two houses because it is distinct from its own sign. 

For the enlightenment of those with duller intellects, this is explained more clearly as follows:

For the **Sun** <note>Aditya</note>, Leo is the trine. The Moon is the lord of Cancer, which is the twelfth house from that. Even though the Moon is the lord of only one house, because it lacks a second sign to rule, it is a friend of the Sun. Scorpio is the fourth from Leo and Aries is the ninth; Mars <note>Bhauma</note> is the lord of those two. Aries is the Sun's exaltation; Mars is the lord of that. Because Aries is the ninth from Leo and is the Sun's exaltation, and because Mars rules both Aries and Scorpio, Mars becomes the lord of two [favorable] houses; therefore, it is a friend of the Sun. The fifth and eighth from Leo are Sagittarius and Pisces; Jupiter <note>Jiva</note> is their lord. Because he is the lord of those two mentioned places, he is a friend of the Sun. The second and eleventh from Leo are Virgo and Gemini; Mercury <note>Budha</note> is their master. Since the second house is mentioned but the eleventh is not, Mercury is neutral to the Sun as the lord of only one [favorable] house. The sixth and seventh houses from Leo are Capricorn and Aquarius, which are not mentioned; because of his lordship over them, Saturn <note>Shanaishchara</note> is the enemy of the Sun. The tenth and third from Leo are Taurus and Libra; because of his lordship over those unmentioned houses, Venus <note>Shukra</note> is the enemy of the Sun. Thus it is for the Sun.

Now, for the **Moon** <note>Chandra</note>: Taurus is her trine. The fourth house from that is Leo, whose lord is the Sun. He is the lord of one house, but since he lacks a second sign, he is a friend of the Moon. The second from Taurus is Gemini and the fifth is Virgo; Mercury is their master. Because he is the lord of those two mentioned houses, Mercury is a friend of the Moon. The seventh and twelfth from Taurus are Scorpio and Aries; Mars is their master. ## Commentary of Bhattotpala with Hindi Translation

Since the third house is not mentioned <note>referring to the rules for determining planetary friendship</note> and because he rules one of the prescribed houses, **Saturn** is neutral to **Jupiter**. The sixth and eleventh houses from Sagittarius are Taurus and Libra; **Venus** is their lord. Since both these houses are unmentioned, **Venus** is an enemy to **Jupiter**. This concludes the analysis for Jupiter.

Now for **Venus**: The Moola-Trikona <note>The "root-trine" or primary sign of power for a planet</note> of Venus is Libra. The ninth and twelfth houses from Libra are Gemini and Virgo; **Mercury** is their lord. Since he rules two of the prescribed houses, he is a friend to **Venus**. The fourth and fifth houses from Libra are Capricorn and Aquarius; **Saturn** is their lord. Since he rules two of the prescribed houses, he is a friend to **Venus**. The second and seventh houses from Libra are Scorpio and Aries; **Mars** is their lord. Here, the second is mentioned but the seventh is not; thus, by ruling one prescribed house, **Mars** is neutral to **Venus**. Pisces is the exaltation sign of Venus; the third and sixth houses from Libra are Sagittarius and Pisces; **Jupiter** is their lord. Although he rules one sign, he lacks a second sign to balance it; therefore, the **Sun** is an enemy to **Venus**. The lord of the tenth house from Libra is Cancer, ruled by the **Moon**. Though he rules one sign, he lacks a second sign; therefore, the **Moon** is an enemy to **Venus**. This concludes the analysis for Venus.

Now for **Saturn**: The Moola-Trikona of Saturn is Aquarius. The fifth and eighth houses from Aquarius are Gemini and Virgo; **Mercury** is their lord. Since he rules two prescribed houses, he is a friend to **Saturn**. The second and eleventh houses from Aquarius are Sagittarius and Pisces; **Jupiter** is their lord. Since the second is mentioned and the eleventh is not, by ruling one prescribed house, **Jupiter** is neutral to **Saturn**. The sixth from Aquarius is Cancer, ruled by the **Moon**; since it is unmentioned, the **Moon** is an enemy to **Saturn**. The seventh from Aquarius is Leo, ruled by the **Sun**; since it is unmentioned, the **Sun** is an enemy to **Saturn**. The third and tenth houses from Aquarius are Aries and Scorpio; **Mars** is their lord. Since both are unmentioned, **Mars** is an enemy to **Saturn**. || 15 ||

**Vernacular Translation:**
**Jupiter**: For the Sun, the friends are Jupiter and Mercury. For Venus, Mercury. For the Sun, all planets except the Sun. For Mars, all planets except Mars. For the Sun and Moon, all planets except them. And for Mars, Moon, and Sun, the remaining planets are friends to the Sun and others respectively. This is the opinion of some (such as the Yavana <note>Greek</note> teachers). However, according to the opinion of **Satyacharya**, the lords of the 2nd, 12th, 5th, 9th, 4th, and 8th houses from a planet's Moola-Trikona are its friends. This means the lords of the remaining houses are enemies. Those who possess characteristics of both friend and enemy are neutral (indifferent). Therefore, because of the contradictions in their characteristics, one should not accept the friendship-analysis as stated by others (the Yavanas), but rather follow this rule. || 15 ||

# Brihat Jataka: Chapter on the Varieties of Planetary Natures

An example of the friendship rules stated by Satyacharya—The lords of the 2nd, 12th, 5th, 9th, 8th, and 4th houses from a planet's <term>Moolatrikona</term><note>A specific sign where a planet is particularly strong, similar to its "office" or "home base."</note> are considered its friends. The lords of the remaining houses (1st, 3rd, 6th, 7th, 10th, and 11th) are considered its enemies. One should deliberate keeping this in mind. 

For example, from the Sun's <term>Moolatrikona</term> (Leo):
* **Mercury** is the lord of the 2nd house (Virgo), making it a friend; however, it is also the lord of the 11th house (Gemini), which is an "unmentioned" house, making it an enemy. Because it is both a friend and an enemy, Mercury becomes **Neutral** (<term>Sama</term>) to the Sun.
* **Venus** is the lord of the 3rd and 10th houses (Libra and Taurus), both of which are unmentioned; therefore, Venus is the Sun's **Enemy**.
* **Mars** is the lord of the 4th and 9th houses (Scorpio and Aries), both of which are mentioned; therefore, Mars is the Sun's **Friend**.
* **Jupiter** is the lord of the 5th and 8th houses (Sagittarius and Pisces), both of which are mentioned; therefore, Jupiter is the Sun's **Friend**.
* **Saturn** is the lord of the 6th and 7th houses (Capricorn and Aquarius), both of which are unmentioned; therefore, Saturn is the Sun's **Enemy**.
* **The Moon** is the lord of the 12th house (Cancer), which is mentioned; therefore, the Moon is a **Friend**.

In this manner, one should understand the Friends, Neutrals, and Enemies of all planets by calculating from their respective <term>Moolatrikona</term> signs. || 15 ||

Thus, lords of two "mentioned" houses are Friends; lords of one mentioned and one unmentioned house are Neutral; and lords of unmentioned houses are Enemies. Here is the established example—

-> Now, [the author] speaks of the friends, neutrals, and enemies of the planets based on the two, one, or zero mentioned house-lordships stated by Satyacharya, using two verses in the <term>Shardulavikridita</term> meter: <-

> Saturn and Venus are enemies; Mercury is neutral; the rest are friends of the Sun.
> The Sun and the son of the Moon (Mercury) are friends; the rest are neutral to the Moon.
> Jupiter, the Moon, and the Sun are friends of Mars; Mercury is the enemy; Venus and Saturn are neutral.
> The Sun and Venus are friends of Mercury; the Moon is the enemy; the others are neutral. || 16 ||

**Commentary:** "Saturn and Venus are enemies..." Regarding the Sun: Saturn and Venus are the two enemies. The son of the Moon, Mercury, is neutral—meaning neither an enemy nor a friend, but indifferent. The remaining planets—Moon, Mars, and Jupiter—are friends. "The Sun..." etc. Regarding the Moon: The Sun and Mercury are the two friends; the rest—Mars, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn—are simply neutral or indifferent. "Jupiter, Moon, Sun..." Regarding Mars: Jupiter, the Moon, and the Sun are friends; Mercury is the enemy; Venus and Saturn are neutral. "The Sun and Venus are friends..." The Sun and Venus are the two friends of Mercury; the Moon is the enemy; the others—Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn—are neutral. || 16 ||

**Vernacular Translation—** For the Sun: Saturn and Venus are enemies; Mercury is neutral; and the remaining Moon, Mars, and Jupiter are friends. For the Moon: Sun and Mercury are friends, and all other planets are neutral.

<header>The Brihat Jataka — Chapter on the Varieties of Planetary Natures</header>

**Vernacular Commentary:** For Jupiter, Mercury and Venus are enemies; Saturn is neutral; and the Sun, Moon, and Mars are friends. For Venus, Mercury and Saturn are friends; Mars and Jupiter are neutral; and the rest (Sun and Moon) are enemies. Likewise, for Saturn, Venus and Mercury are friends; Jupiter is neutral; and the others (Sun, Moon, and Mars) are enemies. What was previously stated as "natural friendship" starting with the verse *'from one's own trine'* etc., I have clearly restated here as an example. || 17 ||

Having thus explained the division of natural friends, enemies, and neutrals, the author now describes the **temporary** (situational) division of friends and enemies in the *Shardulavikridita* meter:

### Those situated in the 2nd, 12th, 11th, 3rd, 10th, and 4th houses from one another
### are friends for that time; some say even those in one's exaltation sign; otherwise, they are enemies.
### Considering the natural friends, neutrals, and enemies as previously declared,
### one should then classify them as "Great Friend," "Friend," etc., combined with the temporary state. || 18 ||

**Commentary:** *From one another* means mutually. When planets are situated in these specific places relative to each other at the time of birth, a journey, a marriage, or a query, they become "temporary friends." The places are: the House of Wealth (2nd), the House of Loss (12th), the House of Gains (11th), the House of Siblings (3rd), the House of Business or Action (10th), and the House of Kinsmen (4th). In whichever of these houses a planet is placed relative to another, it becomes a friend to that planet, and vice versa. This is why the text says "from one another."

*Some say even those in one's exaltation sign:* Other teachers hold that a planet situated in another's sign of exaltation is also a temporary friend. These teachers include the <note>Yavaneshwara refers to "The Lord of the Greeks," an influential early authority in Indian astrology who integrated Hellenistic techniques.</note> Yavaneshwara and others. Their statement is as follows:

> "Planets located in the 2nd, 9th, 4th, 5th, and 12th from the <term>Mula-trikona</term> <note>A specific favorable sign position for a planet, slightly less powerful than exaltation.</note> are temporary friends, as is one who is in its exaltation and possesses great strength."

However, this is not the intent of the Author (Varahamihira), as he himself stated in his shorter work, the *Svalpa Jataka*:

> "Planets situated in the 10th, 11th, 4th, 3rd, 2nd, and 12th are friends at that time."

*Otherwise, they are enemies:* If planets are situated in any other manner relative to each other, they are temporary enemies. Specifically, those in the same sign, or in the 5th, 6th, 7th, 8th, and 9th houses, become temporary enemies.

*Considering the natural friends, etc.:* One must first understand the natural friends, neutrals, and enemies as previously shown in the text <term>"Saturn and Venus are enemies..."</term> <note>original: "शत्रू मन्दसितौ"</note>. Then, at the time of birth, one calculates the final relationship by combining the two systems:
1. A **Natural Friend** who is also a **Temporary Friend** becomes a **Great Friend** (Adhi-mitra).
2. A **Neutral** who is a **Temporary Friend** becomes a **Friend**.
3. An **Enemy** who is a **Temporary Friend** becomes **Neutral**.
4. A **Natural Friend** who is a **Temporary Enemy** becomes **Neutral**.
5. A **Neutral** who is a **Temporary Enemy** becomes an **Enemy**.
6. An **Enemy** who is a **Temporary Enemy** becomes a **Great Enemy** (Adhi-shatru).

Now, the four types of planetary strength are mentioned: Positional, Directional, Motional, and Temporal strength. || 18 ||

# With the Hindi Commentary and Bhattotpala's Sanskrit Commentary

**Vernacular Commentary—** At the desired time of birth, inquiry, or any other event, planets situated in the 2nd, 12th, 3rd, 11th, 4th, and 10th houses from each other are considered <term>Temporary Friends</term> <note>Sanskrit: Tatkalika Mitra; these are friendships based solely on the current positions of planets in a specific horoscope</note>. Planets situated in other houses are considered enemies. According to the opinion of some (such as the <term>Yavanas</term> <note>referring to Greek or Western astrologers who influenced early Indian astronomy</note>), a planet situated in its sign of exaltation is also a friend. However, this is not the intent of <term>Satyacharya</term> <note>A highly respected ancient authority in Vedic astrology</note>. This is because in his work *Laghujataka*, he has stated: "In the temporary state, planets in the 10th, 11th, 4th, 3rd, 2nd, and 12th are friends."

Now, the <term>Five-fold Friendship</term> <note>Panchadha Maitri; the final synthesized relationship between planets</note> is explained—Previously, we discussed the <term>Natural</term> <note>Naisargika; inherent relationships based on planetary nature</note> friends (where owners of two specific houses are friends, one house is neutral, and unmentioned houses are enemies, such as "Saturn and Venus are enemies of the Sun"). By considering those natural relationships alongside these temporary ones, one must then determine if they are: Great Friend, Friend, Neutral, Enemy, or Great Enemy. || 18 ||

**Special Meaning—** A planet that is both a Natural and a Temporary friend becomes a **Great Friend**. One that is Natural Neutral but a Temporary friend becomes a **Friend**. One that is a Natural enemy but a Temporary friend becomes **Neutral**. One that is Natural Neutral but a Temporary enemy becomes an **Enemy**. Finally, one that is an enemy in both categories becomes a **Great Enemy**.

**Example—** Look at the temporary birth chart <note>Kundali</note>. From the Sun, Saturn, Moon, and Mars are in the 10th, 11th, 12th, and 2nd houses; therefore, these four are the Sun's temporary friends. The remaining planets—Mercury and Jupiter—are enemies. In this manner, the relationships for all planets are calculated from their respective positions and placed in the table. || 18 ||

->Now, he describes Positional and Directional Strength in the Dodhaka meter<-

**A planet gains Positional Strength when it is in its sign of exaltation, in the sign of a friend, in its own Moola-Trikona, in its own Navamsha, or in its own residential sign. Mercury and Jupiter are strong in the East; the Sun and Mars in the South; Saturn in the West; and Venus and the Moon in the North.** || 19 ||

*A planet gains Positional Strength...* <note>Sanskrit: Sthana-bala</note> The word "own" applies to each subsequent term. A planet situated in its exaltation is strong. Situated in the field of a temporary friend, it is also strong. Situated in its own *Moola-Trikona* <note>A specific favorable portion of a sign, literally "root-trine"</note>, in its own *Navamsha* <note>The ninth-part harmonic division of a sign</note>, or having reached its own house/zodiac sign, it is strong. A planet placed in any of these becomes endowed with Positional Strength. 

Here, Leo is the *Trikona* of the Sun, and that is also its own house. For the Moon, Taurus is its exaltation, and that same sign is its *Trikona*. For Mars, Aries is its *Trikona* and its own field. For Mercury, Virgo is its exaltation, its *Moola-Trikona*, and its own field. For Jupiter, Sagittarius is its *Trikona* and its own field. For Venus, Libra is its *Trikona* and its own field. The Teacher <note>Referring to Varahamihira, the author of the Brihat Jataka</note> has not mentioned the specific degree-based distinctions for these. For the benefit of the students, we write them here, having brought them from other horoscopic treatises. Thus, it is said in the *Saravali*:

> "The first twenty degrees of Leo are the Sun's *Trikona*, and the remaining degrees are his own house. The third degree of Taurus is the Moon's exaltation, and the remaining degrees are the *Trikona*..."

## Commentary by Bhattotpala with Hindi Translation

> In Aries, the first twelve degrees are the exaltation of Mars, the next are his trine <note>original: "Trikona"</note>, and the remainder are his own sign.
> In Virgo, the exaltation of Mercury is to be considered at fifteen degrees.
> Beyond that, five degrees are his trine, and the remaining ten degrees are his own sign.
> For Jupiter, the trine results are in the first ten degrees of Sagittarius, and the rest of the sign is his own.
> For Venus, the first three degrees of Libra are the trine, and the rest is her own sign.
> For Saturn, the trine and own sign divisions in Aquarius are like those of the Sun in Leo.

These four verses are easy to understand. Regarding the phrase <term>Dikshu-Budhangirasau-adi</term> <note>Mercury and Jupiter in the directions, etc.</note>: Mercury and the others become strong in the four directions starting from the East. There, in the East, Mercury and Jupiter <note>original: "Jna-Jiva"</note> are strong. This means when they are located in the Ascendant <note>the 1st House</note>. In the South, the Sun and Mars are strong, meaning when they are in the tenth house. In the West, the son of the Sun, Saturn, is strong, meaning in the seventh house. In the North, Venus and the Moon <note>original: "Sita-Shitakara"</note> are strong, meaning in the fourth house. Whichever planet is strong in a certain place becomes weak when situated in the seventh house from that spot. Everywhere, the rule of proportion should be applied for intermediate positions. This applies to the divisions of planetary exaltation and debilitation, as well as the <term>Directional Strength</term> <note>original: "Digbala"</note> of the signs.

---

### And so says Yavanashvara:
> "Jupiter, the Moon, and Mercury situated in the Eastern Ascendant; the Sun and Mars in the Mid-heaven;
> Saturn in the Setting [West]; and Venus and the Moon in the Water [North]—these are the sources of strength."

By accepting the primary strengths, a proportional calculation for the intervals is appropriate. This is the <term>Directional Strength</term> of the planets. ||16||

### **Vernacular Translation (Hindi)**
A planet gains "Positional Strength" by being in its exaltation, a friend's sign, its own trine <term>Mula Trikona</term> <note>A specific favorable area of a sign, often translated as "root trine"</note>, its own ninth-division <note>Navamsha</note>, or its own house. Furthermore, Mercury and Jupiter are strong in the East; the Sun and Mars in the South; Saturn in the West; and Venus and the Moon in the North. This is called <term>Directional Strength</term>. ||16||

### **Special Meaning**
Look at the birth chart: the First House (Ascendant) is East, the Tenth House is South, the Seventh House is West, and the Fourth House is North. As it has been said:
> "Where the ecliptic meets the horizon, that point is called the Ascendant.
> The Eastern and Western horizons are the Rising and Setting points; the South and North are the Meridian points."

Therefore, Mercury and Jupiter are strong in the Ascendant (East), the Sun and Mars in the tenth house (South/Midheaven), Saturn in the seventh house (West), and the Moon and Venus in the fourth house (North/IC). Conversely, they are weak in the opposite directions. Therefore, the precise calculation of strength is performed through proportional distribution—following the method of "From Saturn to the Ascendant, from the Sun and Mars to the fourth house," etc., as clearly explained in the *Keshaviya Jataka-Paddhati* <note>A classical manual on horoscopic calculations by Keshavarka</note>.

->Now, the author describes Motional Strength (Cheshta-bala) in the Dodhaka meter:<-

**The Sun and the Moon are endowed with strength when they are in the northern course (Uttarayana). The remaining planets are strong when in retrograde motion or in conjunction with the Moon. Furthermore, those with expansive rays and those situated to the north in a planetary combat are to be considered possessed of motional strength (Cheshtita-virya).**

*Commentary:* Regarding "In the northern course": The six signs starting from Capricorn constitute the Northern Course (Uttarayana), and the six signs starting from Cancer constitute the Southern Course (Dakshinayana). In the Northern Course, the Sun and the Moon become strong. The "remaining" planets—Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn—are strong when they are in "retrograde" <term>Vakra: retrograde motion where a planet appears to move backward</term> or in "conjunction" (Samagama). Conjunction with the Moon is specifically called *Samagama*. A planet's meeting with the Sun is called "combustion" (Astamaya), while the meeting of Mars and the others with each other is called "combat" (Yuddha). As stated by the teacher Vishnuchandra:

> "Meeting with the Sun is combustion; meeting with the Moon is conjunction. The meeting of the sons of Earth (Mars) and the others with one another is termed combat."

Regarding "Expansive rays": Those whose rays are large or wide are strong. A planet usually attains expansive rays when situated in the second quadrant of its fast-moving anomaly <note>referring to its proximity to the Earth</note>, as it is then near its retrograde point. In "combat" (Yuddha), those situated in the northern direction are strong. It was mentioned that combat occurs between Mars and the others; therein, the one situated in the northern portion is the victor and is strong. Here, "northern position" is an indicative term; essentially, whoever is the victor is the strong one. The characteristics of a defeated planet are as follows: "One situated in the southern direction, trembling, retreating, minute in size, mounted upon (by another), distorted, lusterless, and discolored is the defeated one." One possessing the opposite characteristics is designated the victor. However, "One who is large, glossy, and radiant is victorious even if situated in the southern direction." This typically applies to Venus. As the teacher Pulisha <note>referring to the author of the Pulisha Siddhanta</note> states: "All are victorious when in the north, but Venus is victorious even in the south." This constitutes Motional Strength (Cheshta-bala). A planet joined with any of these conditions is considered possessed of motional strength.

**Vernacular Translation—** The Sun and the Moon are strong in the Northern Course (Uttarayana). The remaining five planets (Mars, etc.) are strong when in retrograde motion or in conjunction with the Moon. Additionally, planets with expansive (abundant) rays and planets situated to the north during planetary combat are strong. A planet with such strengths should be understood as having Motional Strength (Cheshta-bali).

*Special Meaning—*
> "Meeting with the Sun is combustion; meeting with the Moon is conjunction.
> The meeting of Mars and the others with one another is termed combat."

# The Brihat Jataka with the Sanskrit Commentary of Bhattotpala and Hindi Exposition
## Page 66

When Mars and the other planets are positioned with the Sun, they are called "combust" <note>astam; rendered invisible by the Sun's light</note>, and when they are with the Moon, it is called a "conjunction" <note>samagama</note>. When these same planets (Mars, etc.) are joined with each other, it is called a "war" <note>yuddha; a planetary skirmish occurring when two planets are in close proximity</note>. Among them, the planet situated to the North is considered the victor or the stronger one. However, Venus is considered strong even when situated in the South, provided it possesses abundant rays. As the teacher Pulisha states: "All are victors when in the North; Venus is the victor when in the South." If a planet's fast moving center <note>shighra-kendra; a term from Hindu astronomy related to calculating planetary velocity</note> is in the second quadrant, it possesses abundant rays. ||20||

->Now, the author describes the Temporal Strength (Kala-bala) of the planets in the Malini meter:<-

### The Moon, Mars, and Saturn are strong at night; Mercury is strong always; the others are strong by day.
### The Cruel and Benign planets are strong during the dark and light fortnights respectively.
### Strength is gained through the lords of the Year, Day, Hour, and Month.
### Saturn, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Moon, and Sun are progressively stronger in order. ||21||

->Thus ends the Second Chapter, titled "The Distinctions of Planetary Origins,"<-
->in the Brihat Jataka composed by the venerable teacher Varahamihira.<-

**Commentary:** Regarding "Nishi" (at night): The Moon, Mars, and Saturn are powerful at night. Mercury is strong at all times, both day and night. The others—the Sun, Jupiter, and Venus—are strong during the day. The "Cruel" <note>krura; the natural malefics</note> previously mentioned are strong during the dark fortnight <note>krishna-pakshe; the waning moon</note>. The "Benign" <note>saumya; the natural benefics</note> are strong during the light fortnight <note>shukla-pakshe; the waxing moon</note>. During the dark fortnight, even the Moon is considered "cruel" and becomes strong <note>The Moon's nature changes based on its proximity to the Sun</note>. As the Lord of the Greeks <note>Yavaneshwara; an influential early authority in Indian astrology</note> says: "In the lunar month starting from the first day of the light fortnight, the Moon has medium strength for the first ten days, is excellent/strongest during the second ten days, and has little strength during the third ten days; however, if aspected by benefics, it is always strong."

Regarding "Dvayayana" (the two solstices/year): The term refers to the year. A planet is strong in its own year (the year over which it presides), on its own day of the week, in its own hour <note>hora; the planetary hour</note>, and in its own month. The lords of the year, day, hour, and month should be recognized as possessing temporal strength. Some read the text as "lords of the year, day, hour, and month," while others read "those occurring in their own day, hour, and month." The latter is considered a flawed reading. In all these cases, the planets become strong. This constitutes the "Temporal Strength" <term>Kala-virya; the strength a planet derives from the specific time of birth</term>.

Regarding the sequence "Sha-Ru-Bu-Gu-Shu-Cha-Sa": These syllables represent the planets in increasing order of strength. Saturn (Sha) is the weakest of all. Mars (Ru/Rudhira) is stronger than Saturn. Mercury (Bu/Budha) is stronger than Mars. Jupiter (Gu/Guru) is stronger than Mercury. Venus (Shu/Shukra) is stronger than Jupiter. <note>The sequence continues to the Moon and Sun as the strongest</note>.

# Brihat Jataka — Chapter on Planetary Natures and Varieties

The letter "ca" <note>original: "चकाराद्यश्चंद्र:" - referring to a grammatical connector in the source verse</note> implies that the Moon is stronger than Venus. The letter "sa" implies that the Sun is stronger than the Moon. This constitutes the **Natural Strength** <term>Naisargika-bala: the inherent, unchanging strength of a planet regardless of its position</term> of the planets. As the author himself stated in his shorter work, the *Svalpa Jataka*: "Saturn, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, the Moon, and the Sun are each progressively stronger than the last. This is their natural strength; one should consider this when other strengths are equal." Where two or more planets have equal strength in other categories, their relative power should be determined by this natural hierarchy.

The Author <note>referring to Varahamihira</note> has not explicitly detailed the specific results of the four types of planetary strengths here; therefore, for the benefit of students, I shall record them from other authoritative texts. Thus, it is said in the *Saravali*:

> "A planet endowed with the strength of its **Exaltation** <term>Ucha-bala</term> grants supreme prosperity.
> One with the strength of its **Moolatrikona** <term>a specific favorable sign position</term> grants the status of a minister or a commander.
> One strengthened by being in its **Own Sign** <term>Sva-kshetra</term> brings joy and the accumulation of wealth.
> One positioned in a **Friendly Sign** <term>Mitra-bha</term> produces a man of great fame.
> One possessing the strength of its own **Navamsha** <term>a one-ninth divisional chart</term> makes a person illustrious, very happy, possessing stable wealth, and a recipient of riches from the king."

It is also stated in the *Sukshma Jataka*: "A planet is powerful when it is in a friendly sign, its own house, its exaltation, or its own Navamsha, and is also aspected <note>viewed by the astrological 'glance' of another planet</note> by benefics. The Moon and Venus are strong in even (feminine) signs; the rest are strong in odd (masculine) signs."

The results of being aspected by benefic planets are as follows:

> "A planet aspected by benefics and possessing strength makes a man wealthy, famous,
> charming, a leader of all, handsome of body, and gentle.
> Through the strength of being in a masculine or feminine sign, it makes one honored by the people, skilled in the arts <term>Kala-kushala</term>,
> cheerful of mind, capable, and God-fearing.
> A planetary lord endowed with **Directional Strength** <term>Dig-bala</term> leads a man toward that planet's specific compass direction,
> and having led him there, provides him with clothing, ornaments, vehicles, and happiness.
> A planet possessing **Motional Strength** <term>Chesta-virya: strength derived from specific movements like retrogression</term> grants various results:
> sometimes a kingdom, sometimes honor, sometimes wealth, and sometimes fame.
> Benefic planets that are **Retrograde** <term>Vakri</term> possess great strength and grant kingdoms;
> however, malefic planets in retrogression cause sorrow and aimless wandering.
> A planet in a 'healthy' state <margin>The reading 'Healthy in body and union' is the correct version.</margin> grants the pleasure of physical union and victory in battle.
> The Moon, when auspicious and peerless, grants a kingdom and the total defeat of enemies.
> Those full of **Night and Day Strength** <term>Kala-bala</term> grant land and elephants, increase courage,
> and allow a man to overshadow his enemies and enjoy all things openly.
> The Lords of the Year, Month, Day, and Hour <term>Hora</term> grant progressively double the results;
> they bring happiness, wealth, and fame during their respective periods <term>Dashas</term>.
> From **Fortnightly Strength** <term>Paksha-bala: strength based on the lunar cycle</term>, planets grant the destruction of enemies, and wealth in gems, clothes, and elephants;
> they grant women, gold, land, and fame as bright as the rays of the Moon.
> Planets fully laden with all types of strength, shining with a net of pure rays,
> constantly grant kingdoms and happiness beyond one's wildest dreams."

Men born when the gentle planets <note>The "benefics": Jupiter, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon</note> are strong are endowed with good conduct, happiness, auspiciousness, and purity; they are handsome, energetic, knowers of history and traditions, and devoted to the twice-born <note>The priestly or learned class</note> and the gods. They are fond of fine clothes, garlands, people, and ornaments.

**Vernacular Commentary—** The Moon, Mars, and Saturn are strong at night; Mercury is always strong; the remaining planets are strong during the day. The Lord of the Day is strong on its day, the Lord of the Hora <note>Planetary hour</note> during its hour, and the Lord of the Month (Sun, Jupiter, and Venus) during its month. The Lord of the Year is strong during its year. This is known as <term>Kala-bala</term> <note>Temporal strength based on time cycles</note>.

The Sanskrit commentator has clearly written the results of planets endowed with such strengths.

# Chapter 3: On Non-Human Births

Now, the chapter on non-human births is explained. What is the meaning of "non-human birth"? It refers to the birth of various non-human species such as animals, birds, and immobile beings <note>plants or minerals</note>. By knowing the time of birth or the time of a query from a seeker, the certainty of a non-human birth is determined. This is stated in the Vasantatilaka meter:

> If the cruel planets are very strong and the gentle planets are weak, 
> and a eunuch planet <note>Saturn or Mercury</note> is in a cardinal house <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note> or aspects it, 
> one should declare a creature whose form is equal to the <term>Dvadasamsa</term> <note>A 1/12th division of a zodiac sign, roughly 2.5 degrees</note> occupied by the Moon, 
> provided that it is designated as a non-human sign. 1.

"If the cruel planets are very strong..." etc. Regarding "equal to the form of the twelfth-part occupied by the Moon": whichever twelfth-part the Moon has entered and is situated in, one should declare a living being of a non-human birth whose form is similar to that part. One should only declare this if that twelfth-part is designated as non-human, and not otherwise. For instance, if the Moon is situated in the twelfth-part of Aries, it is of the form of a ram. If situated in the twelfth-part of Taurus, it is of the form of a bull or buff—

# On Non-Human Births

<page-num>72</page-num>
->**From the Brihat Jataka: Chapter on Non-Human Births**<-

...and from the signs: If the Moon is situated in the twelfth-part <note>Dvadashamsha: a 2.5-degree division of a zodiac sign</note> of Cancer, the birth is of a crab or similar creature. If situated in the twelfth-part of Leo, the birth is of lions, tigers, jackals, cats, or similar animals. If in the twelfth-part of Scorpio, it is of snakes, insects, and the like. If in the second half of the twelfth-part of Sagittarius, the birth is of horses, donkeys, etc. In the first half of the twelfth-part of Capricorn, it is of deer. Others suggest that in the latter half, it is of frogs and other aquatic creatures. In Pisces, it is of fish alone.

How is the certainty of a non-human birth determined? The text says: By the "cruel planets" <note>Malefics</note> and so on. When the cruel planets—the Sun, Mars, and Saturn—along with Mercury, are joined with a waning Moon and are very strong, while the "gentle planets" <note>Benefics</note> are weak and devoid of power, and if the "neuter" planets (Saturn or Mercury) are in a "quadrant" <term>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of a horoscope</term>, this constitutes one yoga <note>astrological combination</note> for a non-human birth. 

Alternatively, if the Moon is in a non-human twelfth-part as described, and the strong malefics and weak benefics are present, and the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note> is aspected <note>viewed</note> by either Mercury or Saturn, this is the second yoga for knowing a non-human birth. However, if the Moon is in a "two-footed" <note>human</note> twelfth-part and the aforementioned combinations are absent, the birth is human. Thus it is said in the *Saravali* <note>A classic 8th-century astrological treatise by Kalyanavarman</note>:

> ‘When the malefics are endowed with great strength and the benefics are weak, and the Moon is in a non-human division, while Mercury and Saturn are in quadrants or aspecting the Ascendant, a non-human birth occurs.
> The teachers say that if the Moon is in the portion of Aries, the birth is of goats and the like.
> In the portion of Taurus, it is of cows and buffaloes; in the third portion (Gemini), it is of human forms.
> In the fourth portion (Cancer), it is of tortoises and those born in water.
> Beyond that (Leo), it is of tigers and such, and then again of humans (Virgo).
> In the portion of Libra, human forms; in the Scorpio portion, snakes and the like.
> In the ninth (Sagittarius), donkeys, horses, etc.; in the tenth (Capricorn), deer and peacocks.
> Various trees and diverse types of grass are also known there.
> In the eleventh (Aquarius), humans; and in the final (Pisces), various water-born creatures.’

Regarding the knowledge of the number of offspring for dogs, cats, mice, etc.: In the birth of dogs and such, the wise person should say there are as many offspring, of male and female gender, as there are twelfth-parts in the Ascendant. || 1 ||

**Vernacular Explanation—** If all the malefic planets are strong and all the benefic planets are weak, and Mercury and Saturn are in a quadrant—in such a combination, one should describe the form of the creature according to the twelfth-part (Dvadashamsha) in which the Moon is situated. If that twelfth-part is designated as non-human (other than two-footed), understand it to be a non-human birth. Alternatively, if the malefics are strong and benefics weak, and the Ascendant is aspected by Mercury or Saturn, then also call it a non-human birth. If the Moon is in a two-footed twelfth-part, then understand the birth to be human. || 1 ||

## Commentary of Bhattotpala with Hindi Translation

*Special Meaning—* "If the Moon is in a non-human sign <note>Viyoni: literally 'of a different womb,' referring to animals or plants</note> while cruel planets <note>malefics</note> are strong and gentle planets <note>benefics</note> are weak; or if the Moon is in the center <term>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</term> with Mercury and Saturn, and the Ascendant is aspected by them, a non-human birth occurs. The ancient teachers say that if the Moon is in Aries or its divisional portion, the birth of goats and similar animals is predicted; if in the portion of Taurus, cows and buffaloes; if in the portion of Gemini, human-like forms." etc.

That is to say, if the Moon is in the <term>Dvadasamsa: a 1/12th division of a sign</term> of Aries, one should understand the birth of a goat, ram, etc. If in the portion of Taurus, cows, buffaloes, etc.; in the portion of Cancer, crabs, tortoises, etc.; in the portion of Leo, tigers, lions, cats, etc. Similarly, if in the portion of Scorpio, scorpions, snakes, etc.; in the latter half of Sagittarius, horses, donkeys, etc.; in the first half of Capricorn, deer, etc.; in the latter half of Capricorn, iguanas and aquatic creatures; and if in the portion of Pisces, fish and other aquatic animals. However, if the Moon is in the portion of Gemini, Virgo, or the remaining two-footed <note>human</note> signs, a human birth should be understood. | 1 |

-> Now, another combination for knowing non-human birth is stated in the Vaitaliya meter: <-

**If the cruel planets are strong and in their own divisions, and the auspicious planets are weak and in the divisions of others, and the Ascendant is a non-human sign, then in this case also, one should predict a non-human birth. || 2 ||**

*Cruel planets...* The rule regarding the form matching the Moon's division continues here. The "cruel" or malefic planets previously mentioned must be strong and not just strong, but "in their own divisions," meaning situated in their own <term>Navamsa: a 1/9th division of a sign</term>. Here, the word "division" should be understood specifically as the Navamsa. The "auspicious" or benefics must be in the Navamsa of another planet and "weak," meaning devoid of strength. If the Ascendant at that time is also a non-human sign, then in this planetary combination, one should declare that a creature has been born whose form matches the <term>Dvadasamsa</term> occupied by the Moon. || 2 ||

**Vernacular Translation—** If malefic planets are powerful in their own Navamsa and benefics are weak in another's Navamsa, and the Ascendant is a non-human (other than two-footed) sign, then in such a yoga <note>astrological configuration</note>, the birth is of a non-human type corresponding to the Moon's position. || 2 ||

-> Now, since four-footed animals are the most prominent among non-humans, <-
-> the division of their body parts according to the signs is stated in the Upajati meter: <-

**Aries is the head; Taurus the face and throat; the next signs are the feet and shoulders, the back, the chest, the flanks, the belly, the anus, the hind legs, the penis and testicles, and the buttocks and tail—thus are the limbs of a quadruped described. || 3 ||**

*Aries...* Aries represents the head of the quadruped. Taurus represents the face and the throat (the dewlap). The others, Gemini etc., follow in order: Gemini represents the [front] feet and the shoulders. Cancer represents the back.

# Brihat Jataka — Chapter on Non-Human Births
## Page 74

The chest is represented by Leo. The word "Atha" <note>original: "अथ"</note> implies sequence. The two sides or flanks are Virgo. The two sides of the belly are Libra. The anus or rectum is Scorpio. The hind legs are Sagittarius. Here, the word "Atha" is used as a filler for the meter. The penis and testicles are Capricorn. The buttocks (1) are Aquarius. The tail is Pisces. This is the manner of the description. Some authorities describe this division of signs specifically for the bodies of four-legged animals <term>quadrupeds: four-footed creatures like cattle or lions</term>. By saying "some say," the Teacher (Varahamihira) implies this is a traditional view. The mention of quadrupeds is illustrative; for birds, the wings take the place of the forelegs, while the rest remains the same. The purpose of this system is to identify where scars, wounds, or injuries will appear on the animal's body based on the signs. || 3 ||

**Vernacular Translation—** 1. Aries: head; 2. Taurus: mouth and neck; 3. Gemini: forelegs and shoulders; 4. Cancer: back; 5. Leo: chest; 6. Virgo: both flanks (ribcage); 7. Libra: stomach; 8. Scorpio: anus; 9. Sagittarius: hind legs; 10. Capricorn: penis and scrotum; 11. Aquarius: buttocks; 12. Pisces: tail. In this way, the division of signs in the limbs of a four-legged creature is told. || 3 ||

*Special Meaning—* One should understand the health or loss of specific limbs in a non-human birth through the conjunction of benefic and malefic planets.

-> Now, the knowledge of the color of the non-human creature is stated in the Vaishvadevi meter: <-

**One should determine the colors in a non-human birth from the Ascendant-Navamsha, or from the conjunction or aspect of planets, whichever is strongest. One should state the colors as being equal to the number of planets viewing the Ascendant; and from planets situated in the seventh house, one should predict stripes or streaks on the back. || 4 ||**

"From the Ascendant-Navamsha" <note>Lagnanshakad</note> means: whatever planet is conjoined with the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the rising sign</term>, the color previously attributed to that planet (such as copper, white, deep red, green, etc.) should be declared as the color of the non-human creature or a lost object. "Or from the aspect": if no planet is in the Ascendant, then the color of the planet that aspects (looks at) the Ascendant should be used. If the Ascendant is neither occupied nor aspected, then one should use the color of the sign of the Navamsha <term>Navamsha: a 1/9th division of a zodiac sign</term> rising in the Ascendant, such as red or white. "Equal to the aspect": if many planets occupy or aspect the Ascendant, many colors should be noted. Even then, the color of the strongest planet will predominate, as indicated by the phrase "from the strongest." If the Navamsha in the Ascendant belongs to a sign aspected or occupied by its own lord, that color alone should be stated. Furthermore, whatever planet is situated in a specific limb of the animal will produce its own color there. This is further understood by: "from planets in the seventh house, one should predict stripes on the back of the creature according to the color of the strongest planet." As stated in the *Saravali*:

> From the rising signs or Navamshas, or from the planets conjoined or aspecting, one should know the colors; through the combination of planets and Navamshas, one may find rough or variegated colors.

# Commentary on the Language of the Stars with the Sanskrit Commentary by Bhattotpala 75

Those planets situated in the seventh house create markings on the back of the creature, matching their own color. As many planets as cast their gaze upon the Ascendant, so many colors will the non-human creature possess.
A celestial body <note>a planet</note> that is bright and powerful determines the color of the non-human birth. Jupiter makes it yellow; the Moon makes it white; Venus makes it variegated.
The Sun and Mars make it red; Saturn makes it black; and Mercury makes it a brindled or dappled color. When a planet is in its own sign, in its own division, or in its own ninth-part <term>Navamsha: a 3-degree 20-minute subdivision of a zodiac sign used for fine-tuning predictions</term> while occupying another's sign,
and that planet gazes upon the Ascendant, it bestows a color corresponding to its own nature. || 4 ||

**Vernacular Translation—** The color of the non-human birth should be told from the ninth-part <gloss>Navamsha</gloss> of the Ascendant. If there is a conjunction of any planet in the Ascendant, describe the color as being like that planet. If there are no planets in the Ascendant, but any planet gazes upon it, the color should be described as matching that planet. If more than one planet gazes upon or is joined with the Ascendant, describe the color according to the strongest planet, or describe as many colors as there are planets gazing. Furthermore, as many planets as are in the seventh house, so many lines (marks) should be said to exist on the back (exterior) of the non-human creature—specifically on the limb corresponding to the sign in the seventh house. || 4 ||

**Special Meaning—** "Those in the seventh house create markings on the back matching their color; as many as gaze [on the Ascendant], so many are the colors of the non-human."

If the rising <term>Drekkana</term> <note>A 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign; there are three in each sign.</note> at the time of birth is a "bird" Drekkana, and it is occupied by a strong planet and aspected or joined by Saturn, the birth is of a land-based bird. If it is aspected or joined by the Moon, it is a water-based bird. This is the third combination. These births occur through the conjunction or aspect of Saturn or the Moon. Thus, it is stated in the *Saravali* <note>A classical 8th-century astrological treatise by Kalyanavarman.</note>:
> "When a bird-Drekkana rises, joined by a strong planet, or in a movable <term>Navamsha</term> <note>A 3-degree 20-minute subdivision; the 9th part of a sign.</note> or a Navamsha of Mercury, birds are born—either land or water-based—depending on the aspect of Saturn or the Moon." || 5 ||

**Vernacular Commentary:** If the <term>Lagna</term> <note>The Ascendant or rising sign.</note> contains a bird-Drekkana, or a movable sign's Navamsha, or Mercury's Navamsha, and is joined by a strong planet, and is aspected or joined by Saturn, then one should predict the birth of a land bird. If aspected by the Moon, a water bird. If aspected or joined by both Saturn and the Moon, it should be understood as a bird that lives in both water and land; this is established by the sense of the text. || 5 ||

*Special Meaning:* The bird-Drekkanas are: the second of Gemini, the first of Leo, the second of Libra, and the first of Aquarius. This was described in the chapter on Drekkanas regarding their forms. || 5 ||

->Now, the birth of trees is explained in the <term>Vasantatilaka</term> <note>A specific poetic meter consisting of 14 syllables.</note> meter:<-

### When the Ascendant, Moon, Jupiter, and Sun are all devoid of strength, the birth of trees occurs.
### Whether the tree is born in water or on land is determined by the <term>Amsha</term> <note>The Navamsha or divisional portion.</note>.
### As many signs as the lord of the land or water sign is distant from the Ascendant,
### That many trees are produced, either on land or in water. || 6 ||

**Commentary:** "Hora" means the Ascendant, "Indu" is the Moon, "Suri" is Jupiter, and "Ravi" is the Sun. When these are "devoid of strength" (powerless), it should be said that the querent is asking about the birth of trees. Here is the distinction: "In water or on land." Whether the tree's birth is in water or in a dry land area is determined by the "Amsha" (the Navamsha). If a water-sign Navamsha is rising, the trees are those born near water or in marshy lands. The water signs are Cancer, the second half of Capricorn, and Pisces; through these, knowledge of marshy trees is gained. If other sign Navamshas rise, it indicates land-based trees. Regarding the number: "As many signs as the lord..." Whether it is a land-dweller or water-dweller based on the rising portion, however many signs away its lord is situated from the Ascendant, that many trees—land or water-based—should be declared. Here too, following the rules of <term>Ayurdaya</term> <note>The calculation of longevity or life-span.</note> to be mentioned later, the number should be doubled or tripled based on the lord of the portion. "If in exaltation or retrograde, triple; if in its own Vargottama, sign, or Navamsha, double." Those learned in the tradition say that when doubling or tripling is applicable, the final count should be adjusted accordingly. Thus, in the *Saravali*...

> 'If the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note>, the Sun, Jupiter, and the Moon are weak, and the remaining planets are also weak, the birth of a tree <note>mula-yoni</note> is indicated.
> The divisions of land and water signs differentiate the types of trees.
> As many signs as the lords of the land or water signs are distant from the Ascendant, so many are the trees.
> Their doubling or tripling is determined by the rules of longevity <note>Ayurdaya</note>.' ..Thus.. 6..

**Vernacular Translation—** If the Ascendant, Moon, Jupiter, and Sun are devoid of strength, one should understand it to be the birth of trees. The distinction between a water-based or land-based tree is understood through the *Navamsha* <note>a 1/9th division of a zodiac sign</note>. That is, if it is a water-dwelling *Navamsha*, the tree is near water; if it is a land-based *Navamsha*, it is a land tree. Furthermore, however many signs away from the Ascendant the lord of the water or land *Navamsha* is located, that is the number of water or land trees to be predicted. ..6..

**Special Meaning—** If the lord of the *Navamsha* is in its exaltation or is retrograde, the number should be multiplied by 3. If it is in its *Vargottama* <note>same sign in both the main chart and the 1/9th chart</note>, its own *Navamsha*, its own sign, or its own *Drekkana* <note>1/3rd division</note>, the number should be understood as doubled. ..6..

Now, he describes the specific knowledge of trees based on the lords of the land and water portions in the *Mandakranta* meter—

### The Sun produces trees with internal strength; Saturn produces wretched trees;
### The Moon produces milky trees; and Mars produces thorny ones.
### Jupiter and Mercury produce fruitful and fruitless trees respectively; Venus produces flowering trees;
### The Moon again produces oily trees, and the Son of Earth (Mars) produces bitter shrubs. ..7..

**Commentary:** Regarding "Internal strength" etc.—If the Sun is the lord of the *Navamsha*, he produces trees that are strong in the center <note>heartwood</note>, such as the *Shishapa* <note>Indian Rosewood</note>. The son of the Sun, Saturn, produces "wretched" trees that are unpleasant to the eyes and mind, such as the *Kurkusa*. The Moon <note>original: "Tuhina-kirana", the cold-rayed one</note> produces milky trees like the sugarcane. Mars produces thorny trees, abundant with spikes, such as the *Khadira* <note>Catechu</note>. Regarding "Jupiter and Mercury"—Jupiter <note>original: "Vagisha", Lord of Speech</note> and Mercury <note>original: "Jna", the Knower</note>, these two respectively produce fruitful and fruitless trees. Among them, Jupiter produces fruitful trees like the Mango. Mercury produces fruitless trees, or those whose flowers are used in the world but not the fruits. Venus produces flowering trees like the *Champaka*. The Moon again produces "oily" or glossy trees like the *Dhava* and *Devadaru* <note>Himalayan Cedar</note>. The Son of Earth, Mars, produces bitter shrubs like the *Bhallataka* <note>Marking Nut tree</note>. Because of the dual instruction here, the Moon and Mars are assigned these roles as alternatives. ..7..

->Now, the knowledge of the quality of the ground and the tree, and the quantity, is told in the Vamshastha meter:<-

**The Commentary:** "A benefic in a malefic sign" etc. If that same Lord of the terrestrial or aquatic division is a benefic planet <note>such as Jupiter or Venus</note> but is situated in a malefic sign <note>ruled by Mars or Saturn</note>, then one should say a beautiful tree is growing in bad soil. "Otherwise, the opposite" means the reverse: if the Lord of the division is a malefic but is situated in a benefic sign, one should say an unattractive tree is growing in good soil. Furthermore, if a benefic planet is in a benefic sign, it is a beautiful tree in good soil; if a malefic is in a malefic sign, it is an unattractive tree in bad soil.

Regarding "As many in another Navamsha": Count how many divisions the Lord of the terrestrial or aquatic division has moved from its own Navamsha into another. The number of trees of that specific species will be equal to that count. This provides a method for determining the quantity. As stated in the *Saravali* <note>a classic 8th-century astrological text by Kalyanavarman</note>:
> "As many as the number of divisions the planet has moved from its own Navamsha, that many trees—either terrestrial or aquatic—should be predicted." || 8 ||

**Vernacular Commentary:** If the Lord of the division is a benefic and is in a malefic sign, a beautiful tree is in bad soil; otherwise, understand the opposite (meaning: a malefic in a benefic sign means a bad tree in good soil; a benefic in a benefic sign means a beautiful tree in good soil; and a malefic in a malefic sign means a bad tree in bad soil). Additionally, however many Navamshas the Lord of the division has advanced from its own, there are that many trees of that type (terrestrial or aquatic). || 8 ||

# Chapter 4: On Conception (Nisheka)

Now, the chapter on conception <note>Sanskrit: *Nisheka*, referring to the "infusion" or the act of impregnation</note> is explained. Since conception occurs during the fertile period following menstruation, the determination of this period and the knowledge of the union between man and woman during this time is stated in the *Vamshastha* meter:

**The monthly menses of women are caused by Mars and the Moon. When the Moon is in the non-upachaya signs, and is aspected by Mars, menstruation occurs. But when the Moon is situated otherwise, in an upachaya sign of the man and aspected by a masculine benefic planet, the woman enjoys union with the man. || 1 ||**

*Regarding "caused by Mars and the Moon":* Mars <note>Sanskrit: *Kuja*</note> and the Moon <note>Sanskrit: *Indu*</note> are the causes or the instrumental reasons for the menstrual blood <note>Sanskrit: *Artava*</note>. This happens "every month" <note>Sanskrit: *Pratimasam*</note>. By mentioning "every month," the author indicates the cessation of the first flow and points to the menses capable of sustaining conception.

How does this occur? The text says: "When the Moon <note>literally: "the one with cool rays"</note> has gone to the non-upachaya signs." For women, the Moon situated in the 1st, 2nd, 4th, 5th, 7th, 8th, 9th, or 12th houses <term>Non-Upachaya: houses that are not the 3rd, 6th, 10th, or 11th</term> from the birth sign becomes the cause of menses, provided it is aspected by Mars. This applies to all except children, the elderly, the sick, and the sterile. On this, the sage Badarayana says:

> "When the Moon reaches a non-upachaya sign from the birth rashi of women and is aspected by the son of the Earth (Mars), it is said to be the menses for pregnancy. This is not intended for the sterile, the old, the sick, or those with bodily deficiencies."

Similarly, in the *Saravali*:

> "When the friend of the night-lotus (the Moon) is in a non-upachaya sign and is seen by Mars, some say the monthly menses of young women occur. The Moon is water and Mars is fire; water is blood and fire is bile <note>Pitta</note>. Thus, when the blood is agitated by bile, the menses flow in women. This flowing blood is declared the cause of pregnancy. If the Moon is in an upachaya sign, the monthly appearance is fruitless."

Having shown the menses suitable for conception, the author now shows the possibility or impossibility of the union of man and woman. "When situated otherwise" <note>Sanskrit: *ato'nyathasthe*</note> means the opposite of what was previously stated. This refers to when the Moon is in an *upachaya* sign <term>Upachaya: the 3rd, 6th, 10th, or 11th houses which signify growth</term> relative to the man's birth sign. If the Moon is there and is aspected by a "masculine benefic" <note>specifically Jupiter</note>, then it should be said that the woman "approaches union" or sexual intercourse with the man.

One might ask: why is "situated otherwise" not interpreted as the *upachaya* of the woman? That would be incorrect. It refers to the man because of his primacy in this context. As Badarayana says: "When the Moon is in the upachaya house of the male and is aspected by Jupiter..."

<summary>This page explains the astrological conditions for menstruation and sexual union, attributing the menstrual cycle to the interaction of Mars and the Moon in specific zodiacal houses. It establishes that conception requires the Moon to be in a growth-oriented position relative to the man's horoscope while being influenced by Jupiter.</summary>

# Brihat Jataka — Chapter on Conception

<page-num>80</page-num>
->Chapter on Conception<-

"One should predict the union of woman and man at that time; otherwise, not at all." Thus it is said. The author of the *Saravali* <note>A foundational 8th-century astrological text by Kalyanavarman</note> has stated this generally as follows: "When the Moon is in an *Upachaya* house <note>The 3rd, 6th, 10th, or 11th houses, associated with growth</note> and is aspected by Jupiter or by friends, it creates the yoga for union for men, especially when aspected by Venus." At what time should this be considered? It is said: on the fourth day after the woman has bathed <note>referring to the ritual bath after menstruation</note>. Likewise, Manittha <note>An ancient authority on astrology, often associated with Greco-Indian traditions</note> says:

> "When the menses have ceased and she has bathed, if the Moon is situated in an *Upachaya* house and is aspected by a strong Jupiter, then union with the husband occurs.
> If the Moon is aspected by the Sun, she meets a royal person; if by Mars, a rogue; if by Mercury, one of fickle mind; and if by Venus, a handsome man.
> If aspected by the son of the Sun (Saturn), the woman comes to union with a servant. This is the result when aspected by each one individually, and not by others like Mars and other malefic planets.
> If all planets have left their own houses <note>are poorly placed</note>, the young woman enters the state of a prostitute." 1.

**Vernacular Translation** — Every month, the menses occur in women due to Mars and the Moon. If the Moon is in a *non-Upachaya* house <note>1st, 2nd, 4th, 5th, 7th, 8th, 9th, or 12th</note> from the woman's birth sign and is aspected by Mars, it is the season fit for conception. Conversely, if the Moon is in an *Upachaya* house (3, 6, 10, 11) from the man's sign and is aspected by a benefic male planet (Jupiter), then the woman has union with the man. 1.

### Now, he describes the nature of the sexual act in the Indravajra meter—

> "In the same manner as the animal represented by the rising sign of the seventh house (the setting sign) couples, so should the nature of the union be described. If the setting sign is aspected by or joined with malefic planets, the union is with anger; if with benefics, it is with playfulness and laughter." 2.

*In the same manner as the setting sign...* — From the ascendant of conception or the ascendant of the query, the seventh house is the setting sign. The creature designated by that sign <note>e.g., a ram for Aries, a lion for Leo</note> indicates the manner in which the couple—the man and woman—enter into union or sexual intercourse; the man's application of union should be described in that very way. In that same seventh house, if it is joined with or aspected by "non-good" (malefic) planets, the union should be described as angry and quarrelsome. If joined or aspected by "desired" (benefic) planets, it is with playfulness and laughter. This implies a union accompanied by amorous gestures, laughter, and sighs of pleasure. Now, if it is not joined or aspected by any planet, it is neither angry nor playful. If joined or aspected by a mixture, it is both angry and playful. Thus, in the *Saravali*:

> "Just as the bipeds and others in the seventh house from the ascendant perform their union, so should the conception of men be understood.
> If the setting sign is joined or aspected by malefics, the rustic act <note>original: gramyam</note> involves anger and strife.
> If by benefics, the union is pleasant, as described in the manuals of Vatsyayana <note>Author of the Kama Sutra</note>." 2.

**Vernacular Translation—** One should describe the nature of the sexual act based on the animal associated with the seventh sign from the conception ascendant <term>Adhana Lagna: the astrological sign rising at the moment of conception</term> or the query ascendant. If the seventh house is occupied or aspected by malefic planets, the act is said to be accompanied by strife; if it is occupied or aspected by benefic planets, it is accompanied by laughter and playfulness. |2|

->Now, he describes the possibility or impossibility of conception using the Vanshastha meter:<-

> When the Sun, Moon, Venus, and Mars are in their own divisions <term>Navamsha: a one-ninth subdivision of a zodiac sign</term>, or when Jupiter is situated in a trine or the ascendant, offspring will certainly be born. However, for those without seed <note>impotent or sterile individuals</note>, these planetary positions are as fruitless as the rays of the moon are to the blind. |3|

**Commentary:** Regarding the verse beginning with "Ravi...": If the Sun, Moon, Venus, and Mars are in their own Navamshas in any sign, offspring is produced. This means conception occurs. If all are not in their own divisions, then conception should be predicted if the Sun and Venus are in their own Navamshas in masculine "Upachaya" signs <term>Upachaya: houses of growth, specifically the 3rd, 6th, 10th, and 11th</term>. Similarly, if Mars and the Moon are in their own Navamshas in feminine Upachaya signs at the time of conception, offspring will certainly be born. As stated in the *Svalpa Jataka*: "When the Sun and Venus are strong, in their own houses or divisions, and in Upachaya signs for men, or Mars and the Moon are likewise for women, then conception occurs."

Regarding "Jupiter in a trine or ascendant": If Jupiter is in the trines (the ninth or fifth houses) or in the ascendant (the first house), or in any of these positions, the birth of offspring is possible. "For those without seed": This means these yogas <note>astrological combinations</note> are fruitless for those who are sterile or impotent, even if the planetary positions exist. An illustration is provided: "Like the rays of the moon to the blind." Just as the rays of the cold-rayed Moon, though present, are useless to those without sight, so are these planetary influences to the sterile. |3|

**Vernacular Translation—** If the Sun, Moon, Mars, and Venus are in their own Navamshas, or if Jupiter is in a trine or the ascendant, then conception is definitely possible. These combinations are useless for impotent people, just as moonbeams are useless to a blind person. |3|

> If they are in the twelfth and second houses, they cause death;
> <span style="display: block; padding-left: 2em;">if they are conjunct with them or aspected by them alone, they are intended for death. |4|</span>
