# Brihat Jataka — Chapter on Conception

## The Sun and Others
Regarding the Sun and others: If Mars <note>original: "Kuja"</note> and Saturn <note>original: "Arkaja," son of the Sun</note> are situated in the seventh house from the Sun, they cause disease for the man. This means that at the time of conception <note>term: Adhana-kala; the moment of fertilization</note>, if Mars or Saturn is in the seventh house from the Sun's position, it brings illness to the man in his respective month. Similarly, if Mars or Saturn is in the seventh house from the Moon, it brings illness to the woman in her respective month.

If those same two planets, Mars and Saturn, are in the twelfth and second houses <note>the houses flanking a planet</note> from the Sun and Moon, they cause death for the man and woman respectively. This is to say: if one is in the twelfth and the other in the second from the Sun, whichever of the two is stronger will cause the death of the man in its month. The same applies to the Moon: if they are positioned such that one is in the twelfth and the other in the second from the Moon, the stronger one causes the death of the woman in its month.

"Joined likewise" <note>original: "Yuktau tatha"</note>: This refers to Mars and Saturn. If the Sun is joined with one of these two and aspected <note>term: Drashta; "seen" by the astrological influence of another planet</note> by the other, it is certain to cause the death of the man. Similarly, if the Moon is joined with one and aspected by the other, it causes the death of the woman. The timing is determined by the month of whichever of the two planets is stronger. || 4 ||

**Vernacular Translation:** If Saturn and Mars are in the seventh from the Sun, it is disease-producing for men; if in the seventh from the Moon, for women. Similarly, if they are in the 12th and 2nd from the Sun, they are death-inflicting for the man. If the Sun is joined with one (Mars or Saturn) and aspected by the other, it causes death for the man; if the Moon is so placed, it causes death for the woman. || 4 ||

*Now, the author explains the knowledge of good and bad fortune for the father, mother, paternal uncle, and maternal aunt of the conceived child using the Vamshastha meter:*

> During the day, the Sun and Venus are designated as Father and Mother; Saturn and the Moon are so designated at night. In the reverse case, they represent the paternal uncle and maternal aunt. If these planets are in odd or even signs respectively, it is auspicious for them. || 5

**Commentary:** Regarding "Sun and Venus during the day": For a child conceived or born during the day, the Sun and Venus are respectively designated as the Father and Mother. That is, the Sun signifies the father and Venus signifies the mother. Likewise, for one conceived or born at night, Saturn and the Moon are respectively the Father and Mother; Saturn signifies the father and the Moon signifies the mother.

"In the reverse case": By reversing the day and night designations, those same previously mentioned planets signify the paternal uncle and maternal aunt. Thus, for one born during the day, [Saturn] signifies the paternal uncle and [the Moon] signifies the maternal aunt <note>The text implies the secondary pair takes the secondary roles</note>. The purpose of these designations is to determine their welfare based on whether they occupy odd or even signs...

Those situated in appropriate signs are to be known as auspicious. Odd signs are those like Aries, while even signs are the remaining ones. Therein, if the **Sun** is in an odd sign—any one of Aries, Gemini, Leo, Libra, Sagittarius, or Aquarius—during the day, he brings auspiciousness to the father; at night, he favors the paternal uncle. Similarly, if **Venus** is in an even sign—any one of Taurus, Cancer, Virgo, Scorpio, Capricorn, or Pisces—during the day, she brings auspiciousness to the mother; at night, to the maternal aunt. **Saturn** in an odd sign at night favors the father; during the day, the paternal uncle. Likewise, the **Moon** in an even sign at night favors the mother; during the day, the maternal aunt. This is stated by implication. If these planets are placed in the opposite manner, they are inauspicious for the aforementioned relatives. For example, the Sun in an even sign during the day is inauspicious for the father, and at night for the paternal uncle. Venus in an odd sign during the day is inauspicious for the mother, and at night for the maternal aunt. Saturn in an even sign at night is inauspicious for the father, and during the day for the paternal uncle. The Moon in an odd sign at night is inauspicious for the mother, and during the day for the maternal aunt. || 5 ||

---

**Vernacular Explanation** — If conception or birth occurs during the day, the Sun is designated as the father-significator and Venus as the mother-significator. If it occurs at night, Saturn is the father-significator and the Moon is the mother-significator. The opposites represent the paternal uncle and maternal aunt. That is, during the day, Saturn represents the paternal uncle <note>Sanskrit: Pitrvya; father's brother</note> and the Moon represents the maternal aunt <note>Sanskrit: Matrsvasṛ; mother's sister</note>. At night, the Sun represents the paternal uncle and Venus the maternal aunt. Among these, if the father-significators (primary or secondary) are in odd signs, they grant auspicious results to the father and uncle. If the mother-significators are in even signs, they grant auspicious results to the mother and aunt. Otherwise, the results are inauspicious. || 5 ||

**Commentary:** "Desired by" <note>Sanskrit: Abhilasadbhih</note> refers to the rising sign <term>Lagna; the zodiac sign ascending on the eastern horizon</term> being approached by malefic planets. Some interpret this as planets in the second house from the Lagna, as they are "desiring" the rising sign by being immediately adjacent to it. Others say this refers to planets in the twelfth house, as the planet moves toward the rising sign after leaving that house. Thus, if malefic planets are in the twelfth house from the Lagna and the Lagna does not receive a "benefic aspect" <note>Sanskrit: Shubha-drsti; the gaze or influence of helpful planets like Jupiter or Mercury</note>, the pregnant woman meets her death. On this, the holy sage Garga says: "With malefics in the twelfth house, devoid of benefic aspects at the time of conception, the wise should predict the death of the woman." He then states another combination: "If Saturn is in the rising sign," etc. If Saturn...

->Now, another combination is described in the Vaitaliya meter:<-

> If both the Ascendant and the Moon are situated between two malefic planets and are not aspected by benefics, whether this occurs simultaneously or separately, one should declare that the pregnant woman will perish. || 7 ||

**Commentary:** "Ascendant and Moon" refers to the rising sign and the Moon. If these two are situated between two malefics—for instance, if the Moon is in the Ascendant and one malefic is in the 12th house while another is in the 2nd house—then the Ascendant and Moon are said to be "simultaneously" between two malefics. Now, if the Ascendant and Moon are far apart in degrees, and one malefic is positioned before them while another is positioned after them, they are still considered to be between two malefics. Or, if one malefic is in the 12th house, another in the 2nd or 3rd, and the Moon is in the 4th with a malefic beyond it, they are also considered trapped. Thus, if the Ascendant and Moon are simultaneously between malefics and are not "aspected by benefics" <note>seen by auspicious planets like Jupiter or Venus</note>, the pregnant woman perishes. "Separately" means that if the Ascendant and Moon are in different places, but even one of them is hemmed in by malefics and lacks the gaze of a benefic, the woman perishes. Alternatively, if the Moon is in the 11th from the Ascendant and malefics are in the 2nd, 3rd, and 12th, the Ascendant and Moon are still considered hemmed in. The word "simultaneously" is used for poetic meter or clarity, as the meaning is already implied by the "separate" condition. In all these cases, the general rule is that the death of the pregnant woman occurs in the month ruled by the strongest of the planets forming the combination. || 7 ||

**Vernacular Commentary —** If the Ascendant and the Moon are both—either together or individually—placed between malefic planets and are not aspected by a benefic planet, the death of the pregnant woman should be predicted. That is to say, if they are aspected by a benefic, death does not occur. || 7 ||

# The Great Compendium of Nativity: Chapter on Conception
<page-num>86</page-num>

The fourth house is the place of status. Among these—the trines <note>1st, 5th, and 9th houses</note>, the seventh, the second, the fourth, and the tenth—when benefics are situated in these positions relative to either the Moon or the Ascendant (or both), and likewise when malefic planets are situated in the third or eleventh houses from the Moon or the Ascendant, and if the Moon or the Ascendant is aspected <note>viewed</note> by the Sun, then the fetus in the womb becomes happy and well-nourished. Some read this as "aspected by Jupiter," but that is not appropriate. As stated in the *Saravali*: "With benefics joined with the Ascendant or Moon, or placed in the trines, seventh, fourth, or tenth houses, and malefics in the third and eleventh, the fetus is happy if aspected by the Sun."

**Vernacular Translation:** If auspicious planets are with the Moon or the Ascendant, or placed in the 5th, 9th, 7th, 2nd, 4th, or 10th houses from them, and malefic planets are in the 3rd or 11th houses, and the Sun aspects the Ascendant or Moon, the fetus is healthy (nourished).

*Now, the author describes the knowledge of distinguishing male and female births—whether from the time of conception, the time of birth, or the time of a query—using the Shardulavikridita meter:*

**If the Ascendant, Sun, Jupiter, and Moon are powerful and situated in odd signs and masculine divisions <note>Navamshas</note>, predict a male birth. If they are in even signs and even divisions, predict a female birth. Jupiter and the Sun in odd signs produce a male; the Moon, Venus, and Mars in even signs produce a female. If they are in dual-natured signs and aspected by Mercury, they produce twins according to their respective sides.**

**Commentary:** "In odd signs and masculine divisions" means the rising Ascendant, the Sun, Jupiter, and the Moon. When these four are situated in <term>odd signs</term> <note>Aries, Gemini, Leo, etc.</note> and not just in odd signs but also in <term>masculine divisions</term> <note>Navamshas belonging to odd signs</note> and are powerful, one should predict the birth of a male. One might ask: "The text does not explicitly mention 'odd divisions,' so why interpret it as such?" It is said "in masculine divisions," which means the divisions of masculine signs. Since odd signs are themselves masculine signs, the meaning is clear.

"In even signs and even divisions": When those same factors (Ascendant, Sun, Jupiter, and Moon) are in <term>even signs</term> <note>Taurus, Cancer, Virgo, etc.</note> and also in even divisions <note>Navamshas of even signs</note> and are powerful, one should predict the birth of a female. The determination of male or female is based on the majority of these factors. If there is an equality of factors, the determination is made by the strongest planet.

"Jupiter and the Sun": Both Jupiter and the Sun, when placed in an odd sign (regardless of the specific division), produce a male. The requirement of "strength" also applies here. The Moon, Venus, and Mars, if powerful and placed in an even sign (regardless of the division), produce a female.

"In dual-natured signs": These same planets, when in dual-natured signs <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces</note> and in dual-natured divisions...

Because of the aspect <note>drishti: a planetary gaze or influence</note> of Mercury, and by looking at Mercury, they produce twins of their own kind. "Of their own kind" means in their own category—either in a male subdivision or a female subdivision <term>navamsha: a one-ninth divisional chart used for precision</term>. This is what is being said: there are four dual signs <term>dvishvabhava: signs of a dual nature</term>, which are Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces. Among these, Gemini and Sagittarius are male subdivisions; Virgo and Pisces are female subdivisions. Therefore, as is possible, if the Sun and Jupiter are in the subdivisions of Gemini or Sagittarius and are seen by Mercury from wherever he is positioned, then two male twins should be predicted. Similarly, if the Moon, Venus, and Mars are in the subdivisions of Virgo or Pisces and are seen by Mercury from wherever he is positioned, then two female twins should be predicted. Now, if Mercury sees both categories of signs as shown, then one is a male and the second is a female.

One might ask: the word "subdivision" <note>navamsha</note> is not explicitly in the root verse, so why is it explained as "situated in dual-natured subdivisions"? This was stated in the *Svalpa Jataka* itself: "If the Sun and Jupiter are strong in odd signs, a male is born; if Mars, Moon, and Venus are in even signs, a female. In dual-natured subdivisions, under the aspect of Mercury, twins are born according to their own kind." Otherwise, there would be a redundancy, as the point would have already been covered by the phrase "in odd signs and male subdivisions." The mention of "strength" <note>bala</note> should be followed here as well. || 11 ||

**Vernacular Translation:** If the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the rising sign</term>, Sun, Jupiter, and Moon are strong and in an odd sign and odd subdivision, a male birth occurs. If these same four are in an even sign and even subdivision, a female birth should be declared. If Jupiter and the Sun are in odd signs, it is a male birth; if the Moon, Venus, and Mars are in even signs, it is a female birth. Furthermore, if these same Moon, Venus, and Mars are in dual-natured signs and are aspected by Mercury, they give birth to twins of their own kind. || 11 ||

**Special Meaning:** Regarding the birth of twins, if they are in odd dual-natured signs (Gemini, Sagittarius), it should be understood as a pair of males. If in even dual-natured signs (Virgo, Pisces), a pair of females. If they are in both odd and even, one male and one female should be understood. The birth of twins occurs only when there is an aspect from Mercury, not otherwise. || 11 ||

"Excluding the Ascendant": In the absence of the previously mentioned combinations and not otherwise, excluding the seventh house or the Ascendant at the time of conception or inquiry, if Saturn <note>Saura: son of the Sun</note> is placed in an odd sign from the Ascendant—meaning in the 3rd, 5th, 7th, 9th, or 11th houses—he causes a male birth. "Of the aforementioned planets": This refers to the planetary combinations already discussed...

# Brihat Jataka: Chapter on Conception
<page-num>88</page-num>

By observing and considering the strength and power of the causal planets, one should declare whether the birth will be a male or a female at the time of delivery. This is what is meant: where the combinations for a male birth are present, a male should be predicted. When there is a possibility of both types of combinations, the birth of a male or female should be declared based on which combination is formed by the stronger planets.

**Vernacular Commentary**—Apart from the Ascendant <note>The *Lagna* or the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note>, Saturn situated in an odd sign <note>Aries, Gemini, Leo, etc.</note> also becomes a causal factor for a male birth. In this manner, by looking at the relative strength of the previously mentioned combinations, if the male-producing planets are stronger, a male birth occurs; if the female-producing planets are stronger, a female birth should be predicted.

### Now, the combinations for the birth of a hermaphrodite are stated in the Shardulavikridita meter:

**If the Moon and the Sun mutually aspect each other, or if Saturn and Mercury do the same;**
**Or if Mars in an odd sign aspects the Sun in an even sign; or if the Moon and the Ascendant are in odd signs and are aspected by Mars in an even sign;**
**Or if the Moon and Mercury are in even and odd signs respectively and are aspected by Mars;**
**Or if Venus, the Ascendant, and the Moon are in male Navamshas <note>A 1/9th division of a zodiac sign</note>—these are the six combinations for a hermaphrodite birth.**

"Mutually" means: The Moon and the Sun, being respectively in even and odd signs, if they see each other—that is, if the Moon in an even sign sees the Sun and the Sun sees the Moon—then this is the first combination for a hermaphrodite birth. "If Saturn and Mercury also": Saturn and Mercury, being respectively in even and odd signs, if they mutually aspect each other, this is the second combination. "Or Mars in an even sign": If Mars <note>original: *Vakra*, the "crooked" or "retrograde" one, a common epithet for Mars</note> is in an odd sign and aspects the Sun <note>original: *Dinesha*, the "Lord of the Day"</note> situated in an even sign, and the Sun aspects Mars, this is the third combination. "If the Moon and the Ascendant are in odd signs": If the Moon and the Ascendant are both situated in odd signs and are aspected by Mars <note>original: *Bhumyatmaja*, "Son of the Earth"</note> situated in an even sign, this is the fourth combination. "In even and odd signs": If the Moon and Mercury <note>original: *Shashija*, "Born of the Moon"</note> are respectively in even and odd signs and are seen by Mars situated anywhere, this is the fifth combination. "In male parts": If Venus, the Ascendant, and the Moon <note>original: *Shitakirana*, "The Cold-Rayed One"</note> are all situated in male *Navamshas* <note>The 1/9th sub-division of a sign</note> within any sign, this is the sixth combination for a hermaphrodite birth. Thus says Badarayana <note>An ancient sage and authority on astrology</note>:

> "The Sun and Moon in even and odd signs respectively, looking at each other;
> Or Mercury and Saturn doing the same, produce a hermaphrodite.
> Mars in an odd sign and the Sun in an even sign, from their mutual looking;
> Mercury and the Moon aspected by Mars when in even and odd signs;
> And the Ascendant, Moon, and Venus when placed in odd Navamshas."

# Brihat Jataka — Chapter on Conception

<page-num>60</page-num>
->**Chapter on Conception**<-

One should predict two girls and one boy. Regarding the phrase "equal with unmixed": when Mercury, the other planets, and the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note> are situated in "unmixed" positions—meaning they are all in dual signs <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces</note> of the same gender—then a triplet of the same gender should be predicted. This is explained as follows: if Mercury is positioned in the Gemini Navamsha <note>a 1/9th division of a sign</note> and aspects <note>looks at</note> the other planets and the Ascendant which are also in Gemini or Sagittarius Navamshas, then one should predict three male children in the womb. However, if Mercury is in the Virgo Navamsha and aspects the planets and Ascendant situated in Virgo or Pisces Navamshas, then three female children in the womb should be predicted. So it is said in the *Saravali* <note>A classic 8th-century astrological text by Kalyanavarman</note>:

> 'When the Moon and Venus are in even signs, and Jupiter, Mars, Mercury, and the Ascendant are in odd signs, twins are born. Or, if the Moon and Ascendant are in even signs and are aspected by male planets, twins are born. Likewise, if Mercury, Mars, Jupiter, and the Ascendant are strong and in even signs, twins are predicted. When the son of the Moon <note>Mercury</note> aspects the planets and the Ascendant which are in dual-natured Navamshas: if Mercury is in a Virgo Navamsha, two girls and one boy are conceived. If Mercury is in a Gemini Navamsha, one girl and two boys are born. If Mercury is in a Gemini Navamsha and aspects planets and the Ascendant in Gemini or Sagittarius, there are three males in the womb. If the son of the Moon is in a Virgo Navamsha and aspects planets and the Ascendant in Virgo or Pisces Navamshas, then there are three females in the womb.' || 14 ||

**Vernacular Explanation—** If both the Moon and Venus are in even signs <note>Taurus, Cancer, Virgo, etc.</note> and Mercury, Mars, Jupiter, and the Ascendant are in odd signs <note>Aries, Gemini, Leo, etc.</note>; or if the Ascendant and Moon are both in even signs and are aspected by male planets; or if Mercury, Mars, Jupiter, and the Ascendant are strong and in even signs, they produce twins <term>Mithuna</term> <note>literally "a pair"</note> in the womb. Furthermore, if all planets and the Ascendant are in dual-natured Navamshas, and Mercury is in its own Navamsha (Gemini or Virgo) and aspects the dual Navamshas of the planets or Ascendant, then in such a combination, 3 children should be predicted. Among them, they should be of the same type as Mercury's Navamsha. If the Navamshas are of the same category, all three should be understood as the same (all boys or all girls).

**Specific Meaning—** If Mercury is in an odd (Gemini) Navamsha and the planets/Ascendant are in even (Virgo, Pisces) Navamshas, then 2 boys and 1 girl are born. If Mercury is in an even (Virgo) Navamsha and the planets/Ascendant are in odd (Gemini, Sagittarius) Navamshas, then 2 girls and 1 boy are born. If Mercury and the planets/Ascendant are all in odd Navamshas, understand all three to be boys. If all are in even Navamshas, all three should be understood as girls. || 14 ||

**The Bow (Sagittarius)**: When the Ascendant <term>Lagna; the rising sign on the eastern horizon</term> is in Sagittarius, or specifically in the Sagittarius subdivision <term>Navamsha; a 1/9th division of a zodiac sign</term>, and all planets are positioned in that same Sagittarius subdivision and are exceptionally strong, and if they are aspected <note>viewed by the astrological influence of</note> by a powerful Mercury and Saturn, then there are many fetuses—five, seven, or even ten—enclosed within the womb.

->Now, the author describes the Lords of the Months of pregnancy in a verse:<-

### The embryo, the mass, the limbs, bone, skin, hair, and consciousness
### Are ruled by Venus, Mars, Jupiter, the Sun, the Moon, Saturn, and Mercury.
### Thereafter, the Lords of the Ascendant, the Moon, and the Sun
### Are declared in order; the well-being or ill-fortune of the fetus
### Corresponds to the condition of the Lord of that Month. (16)

**Commentary:** The planets starting with Venus govern the development of the fetus from the first month onwards. Specifically: In the first month of pregnancy, the **embryo** <term>kalala; the jelly-like initial stage of the embryo</term> is formed. When the seed and blood mix and thicken, Venus is the Lord of that month. In the second month, **solidity** <note>the hardening of the mass</note> occurs; Mars is the Lord there. In the third month, the **sprouting of limbs** like hands occurs; Jupiter is the Lord there. In the fourth month, the **formation of bones** occurs; the Sun is the Lord there. In the fifth month, the **formation of skin** occurs; the Moon is the Lord there. In the sixth month, the **formation of hair** <insert>body hair</insert> occurs; Saturn is the Lord there. In the seventh month, **consciousness** <note>the capacity for sensation and movement</note> arises; Mercury is the Lord there.

After the month of Mercury, the remaining months involve the feeding, the movement, and the delivery of the fetus. These are ruled by the Lord of the Ascendant, the Moon, and the Sun respectively. In the eighth month, the creature in the womb **consumes food**; the essence of what is eaten and drunk by the mother passes through the umbilical cord. The planet that was the Lord of the Ascendant at the time of conception is the Lord of this month. In the ninth month, the fetus experiences **agitation** <note>readiness to move</note>; the Moon is the Lord there. In the tenth month, the **delivery** of the fetus occurs; the Sun is the Lord there. As stated in the *Svalpa Jataka*:

> "*The embryo, the mass, the limbs, bones, skin, hair, and memory arise in order*
> *In the months ruled by Venus, Mars, Jupiter, the Sun, the Moon, Saturn, and Mercury.*
> *Feeding, agitation, and delivery follow under the Lords of the Ascendant, Moon, and Sun.*"

# Brihat Jataka — Chapter on Conception
## Page 62

On this subject, there is a difference of opinion between the author and the Lord of the Yavanas <note>Yavaneshwara, an early authority on Indian-Greek astrology</note> regarding the rulers of the first and second months. His statement is as follows:

> "Mars, Venus, Jupiter, the Sun, the Moon, Saturn, and the Moon-at-birth, the Ascendant, the Moon, and the Sun—these are not said to be the lords of the months by their mere presence, but by their strength and afflictions like other planets.
> In the first month, the embryo is a liquid mass <note>original: "kalala"</note>; in the second, it becomes a fleshy mass; in the third, the limbs appear.
> In the fourth, bones, sinews, and veins are formed; in the fifth, marrow and skin.
> In the sixth, blood, hair, and nails are formed; in the seventh, consciousness <note>original: "chetasvita"</note> should be considered.
> In the eighth, there is thirst, hunger, and the sense of taste; in the ninth, there is the sensation of touch and excitement.
> With its channels opened and its body complete, the fetus is born in the tenth solar month."

The Teacher’s <note>Varahamihira's</note> preferred view is that the auspicious or inauspicious results for the fetus correspond to the condition of the planetary ruler of that specific month. This means: if the planet ruling a particular month is afflicted at the time of conception, the fetus may fall <note>miscarriage</note> during that month. If the planet is dim, lusterless, or discolored, there is suffering. If it is clear, full of rays, and powerful, there is healthy growth. So it is said in the <term>Sukshma Jataka</term> <note>The "Brief Birth Manual"</note>: "Suffering comes from dim planets, falling from afflicted ones, and nourishment from clear ones." Furthermore, other authors of the scriptures have mentioned specific details. Some of that is shown here. As stated in the <term>Saravali</term> <note>A major 8th-century astrological compendium</note>:

> "There, influenced by a mixture of good and bad past deeds, the soul enters the womb at the union of semen and blood. The mental state of the couple, their passion or lethargy, and the balance of bodily humors <note>phlegm, etc.</note> determine the qualities of the conceived.
> Whatever planet looks upon the womb, the son will possess qualities similar to that planet. Resemblance to the father or mother depends on the strength and yoga <note>alignment</note> of the Sun and the Moon."

This is easy to understand. // 16 //

**Vernacular Commentary** — In the first month of pregnancy, there is <term>Kalala</term> (the mixture of semen and ovum); in the second month, <term>Ghana</term> (a solid mass or <term>Pinda</term>); in the third month, <term>Ankura</term> (sprouts or the beginning of limbs); in the fourth month, <term>Asthi</term> (bones); in the fifth month, <term>Charma</term> (skin); in the sixth month, <term>Angaja</term> (body hair); and in the seventh month, <term>Chaitanya</term> (consciousness) occurs. The rulers of these seven months are, in order: Venus, Mars, Jupiter, the Sun, the Moon, Saturn, and Mercury. After this, the lords of the eighth, ninth, and tenth months are, in order: the <term>Lagnesha</term> (Lord of the Ascendant), the Moon, and the Sun. The well-being or ill-health of the fetus depends on the auspicious or inauspicious state of these monthly lords. That is, in the month whose lord is strong, the pregnant woman experiences comfort; in the month whose lord is weak, she experiences distress (pain). // 16 //

**Special Meaning** — In the eighth month, the fetus consumes the essence of the food eaten by the mother; in the ninth month, it feels the urge to emerge (come out) from the womb; and in the tenth month, birth occurs. As stated in the <term>Laghu Jataka</term> (see the Sanskrit commentary).

# Page 63
### [Header: Accompanied by the Sanskrit Commentary of Bhattotpala and the Hindi Language Translation]

Now, [the author] describes the combinations for the birth of those with extra limbs, the mute, and those who gain speech late, using the *Vamshastha* meter:

->If Mercury is in a trine, and the others are without strength,<-
->then one is born with double the face, feet, and hands.<-
->If the Moon is in Taurus and malefic planets are in the junctions of signs,<-
->one is mute; if aspected by benefics, one speaks after a long time. || 17 ||<-

**Regarding "If Mercury is in a trine":** If Mercury is in a trine—meaning in the ninth or fifth house from the Ascendant <note>The *Lagna* or rising sign</note>—and if all other planets, wherever they may be situated, are "without strength" (devoid of potency), then the child in the womb should be declared to have double the face, feet, and hands. This means having two heads, four feet, and four hands. Some say this applies when Mercury is in Virgo <note>Mercury's sign of exaltation</note> in a trine, but that is incorrect. For the Lord Garga says:
> "When Mercury is in the ninth or fifth house and all other planets are powerless, the child has double the feet, heads, and hands, yet shares a single torso."

**Regarding "If the Moon is in Taurus":** When the Moon is situated in Taurus and malefic planets are in the "junctions of signs" <note>The *Rashi-sandhi* or the transition points between signs, specifically the last portions of Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces</note>, the child in the womb is said to be mute. **Regarding "aspected by benefics":** The word "if" is used here in a conditional sense. In such a combination, if the Moon is aspected by <term>benefic planets</term> <note>Gentle planets like Jupiter or Venus</note>, then the newborn produces speech after a long time. However, if aspected by malefics, the person remains without speech. In this combination, if the benefics are strong while being aspected by a mix of planets, speech is gained after a long time. If the malefics are stronger, speech is never gained. On this, Lord Garga says:
> "With malefics in the ends of Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces, and the Moon in Taurus, one is mute if aspected by malefics; if aspected by benefics, one gains speech after a long time. With mixed aspects, one is either mute or gains speech late." || 17 ||

**Hindi Translation —** If Mercury is in a trine from the Ascendant and the remaining planets are weak, the person has 2 faces, 4 feet, and 4 hands. If the Moon is in Taurus and malefic planets are in the junction of signs (*Rashi-gandanta*), the person is mute. If the aspect of a benefic planet is upon them, the person speaks after many days. || 17 ||

Now, [the author] describes the combinations for being born with teeth, as a hunchback, or as mentally disabled, using the *Mandakranta* meter:

->If Saturn and Mars are in a Navamsha of Mercury, the child is born with teeth;<-
->A hunchback, if the Moon is in its own sign at the Ascendant and aspected by Saturn and Mars;<-
->A cripple, if Pisces is at the Ascendant and aspected by Saturn, the Moon, and Mars;<-
->If a malefic and the Moon are in a junction, one is mentally disabled, unless aspected by a benefic. || 18 ||<-

**Regarding "If Saturn and Mars...":** Saturn and Mars, in whichever sign they may be, if they are in a "Navamsha of Mercury"—meaning in the <term>Navamsha</term> <note>A 1/9th divisional chart used for fine detail</note> of Gemini or Virgo...

Alternatively, if the planets are situated in a sign of Mercury <note>original: "Budha-rkshe"</note>, meaning either Gemini or Virgo—the word "if" here implies a conditional state—then in this planetary combination, the fetus should be declared as being born "with teeth" <note>original: "sadanto"</note>. Some authorities suggest this occurs specifically when the planet is in the sign of Mercury and also in the corresponding sub-division <term>Navamsha (a 1/9th division of a zodiac sign used for precision)</term> of Gemini or Virgo, because the text mentions both the sign and the division together. If the word "division" were used alone, it would suffice, so the inclusion of "sign" adds specific emphasis. In such a combination, the fetus is born with teeth, or alternatively, becomes a hunchback.

Regarding the phrase "in its own sign": When the Moon <note>original: "Shashini"</note> is in its own sign (Cancer) and that sign is also the Ascendant <term>Lagna (the sign rising on the eastern horizon)</term>, and it is "aspected" <note>viewed by the gravitational/astrological influence</note> by Saturn <note>original: "Manda"</note> and Mars <note>original: "Maheya"</note>, then the fetus should be declared a hunchback <note>original: "kubja"</note>.

Regarding "Lame in Pisces": If Pisces is the Ascendant and it is aspected by Saturn <note>original: "Yama"</note>, the Moon <note>original: "Shashi"</note>, and Mars <note>original: "Kuja"</note>, the fetus should be declared "lame" <note>original: "pangu"</note>, meaning deficient in the feet.

Regarding "Malefics in the junction": If a malefic planet (Sun, Mars, or Saturn) and the Moon are in a "junction" <note>original: "sandhi" — the transition point between two signs</note>, specifically in the final sub-divisions of Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces, then the creature in the womb should be declared "dull-witted" <note>original: "jada"</note> and "devoid of the sense of hearing."

Regarding "If not aspected by benefics": These planetary combinations produce the stated effects only if they are not "aspected" (viewed) by benefic planets <note>Jupiter, Venus, or Mercury</note>. If they are viewed by strong benefics, the conditions do not manifest; if viewed by planets of medium or weak strength, the results are only partially realized. ||18||

**Vernacular Translation:** If Saturn, Mars, and Mercury are in their own signs and in the sub-division of Mercury, the child is born with teeth. If the Moon is in its own sign (Cancer) in the Ascendant and is viewed by Saturn and Mars, the child is a hunchback. If Pisces is the Ascendant and is viewed by Saturn, Moon, and Mars, the child is lame. If malefic planets and the Moon are at the junction of signs, the child is deaf/dull. These results only occur if no benefic planets view the combination. If benefics do view them, these defects do not occur. ||18||

The second decan of the fifth house is called the **Intellect-Decan** <note>original: "Dhi-Dreshkana"</note>. When this second decan is rising at the horizon and is occupied by a malefic planet, and is further aspected <note>In astrology, an "aspect" is a specific angular relationship between planets that exerts influence</note> by Saturn, the Moon, and the Sun, the child in the womb should be declared to be born without arms.

Similarly, when the third decan of the rising sign <term>Ascendant|The sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of conception</term> is rising, it is called the **Ninth-Decan** because of its relationship to the ninth sign. If this decan is rising, occupied by a malefic, and aspected by Saturn, the Moon, and the Sun, the child in the womb should be declared to be without feet.

Furthermore, because the first decan is related to the rising sign itself, it is called the **Rising-Decan**. If this decan is rising and aspected by Saturn, the Moon, and the Sun, the child in the womb should be declared to be without a head. In these combinations, the phrase "occupied by a malefic" refers to the influence of Saturn, the Moon, and the Sun. If it is occupied by Mars <note>original: "Angaraka"</note> alone, the combination also occurs.

Here, other commentators explain the possibility of being without arms, feet, or a head simply by the presence of malefics in the Intellect, Ninth, or Rising decans. They do not require the aspect of Saturn, the Moon, and the Sun. Others, regarding the birth of those without arms etc., ignore the specific order and say that in any of the three decans, any of the deformities may occur as an alternative: either without arms, or without feet, or without a head.

Others explain it thus: When the first decan is in the Ascendant, the first decan is also in the fifth and ninth signs. If these three decans are occupied by malefics, the child in the womb is said to be without arms. If the second decan is rising in the Ascendant, then the second decan is also in the fifth and ninth signs. If these three are occupied by malefics, the child is said to be without feet. If the third decan is rising in the Ascendant, then the third decan is also in the fifth and ninth signs. If these three are occupied by malefics, the child is said to be without a head. Here too, others ignore the specific order and suggest any of the three deformities may occur in any of the three combinations.

However, we say: At the time of conception <note>original: "Nisheka-kala"</note>, if the decan in the fifth sign is occupied by Mars and aspected by Saturn, the Moon, and the Sun, [the child is armless]. Similarly, the decan in the ninth house is the Ninth-Decan; if at the time of conception the decan in the ninth sign is occupied by Mars and aspected by Saturn, the Moon, and the Sun, then the child is without feet. Likewise, if the decan in the Ascendant at the time of conception is occupied by Mars and aspected by Saturn, the Moon, and the Sun, the child in the womb is said to be without a head. This is the correct explanation. As the Sage Garga says:

> -> "Mars placed in the rising decan, aspected by Saturn, the Sun, and the Moon, <-
> -> makes one headless; similarly in the fifth, it makes one armless. <-
> -> In the ninth house, it causes footlessness, if not aspected by benefics." <-

## Chapter on Conception (Nisheka)

It is stated similarly in the *Saravali* <note>A foundational 8th-century astrological text by Kalyanavarman</note>: "If the decans <term>Decan: A 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign, also called a Drekkana</term> in the trine houses (1st, 5th, and 9th) are occupied by Mars and aspected by Saturn, the Sun, and the Moon, the child is born without arms, legs, or a head respectively." || 16 ||

**Vernacular Explanation—** If the Ascendant (Lagna) is in the final decan of Capricorn and is aspected by <note>Aspected by: In astrology, this means the planets are positioned to "look at" or influence that specific point</note> Saturn, the Moon, and the Sun, the person born will be a dwarf. Furthermore, if the decans of the 5th, 9th, and 1st houses are occupied by the malefic Mars and aspected by Saturn, the Moon, and the Sun, the person will be born without arms, without legs, and without a head, respectively. This result should only be predicted if there is no influence or aspect from benefic <note>Benefic: Auspicious or "kind" planets like Jupiter or Venus</note> planets. || 16 ||

## Special Meaning— As stated by the Sage Garga:

**"Mars in the decan of the Ascendant, aspected by Saturn, the Sun, and the Moon, causes the loss of the head; similarly in the 5th house, the loss of arms; and in the 9th house, the loss of legs—provided no benefic planets aspect these positions."** || 16 ||

## Now, regarding the knowledge of births with sensory defects, he speaks in the Harini meter:

**"If the Sun and Moon are together in Leo in the Ascendant, and aspected by Mars and Saturn, the child is born blind. If aspected by both benefics and malefics, the eyes are like bubbles (cataracts). If the Moon is in the 12th house, the left eye is destroyed; if the Sun is there, the right eye. These yogas <term>Yoga: A specific planetary combination</term> described as inauspicious become manageable (less severe) if aspected by benefics."** || 20 ||

**Commentary:** Regarding "Sun and Moon together"—if the Ascendant is Leo and contains both the Sun and Moon, and is aspected by Mars and Saturn, one should predict that the fetus will be born without eyes (blind). However, if the Leo Ascendant contains only the Sun and is aspected by Saturn and Mars, the right eye is blind. If the Leo Ascendant contains only the Moon and is aspected by Saturn and Mars, the left eye is blind. 

Regarding "eyes like bubbles"—if in that same Leo Ascendant, the Sun and Moon are present and aspected by both benefic and malefic planets, the child in the womb will have "bubble-eyes" <note>Likely referring to cataracts or protruding eyes</note>. This also applies if only one of the luminaries (Sun or Moon) is present under the same conditions.

Regarding "in the 12th house"—if at the time of conception or birth, the Moon is in the 12th house from the Ascendant, it destroys the left eye. Similarly, if the Sun is in the 12th house from the Ascendant, it destroys the right eye. 

Regarding "yogas described as inauspicious"—all these combinations previously mentioned (starting from the verse "Mercury in the trines...") which give auspicious or inauspicious results, if the planets forming these combinations are aspected by benefic planets, the conditions become "manageable." This means they do not yield the full negative result described, but only a slight or partial version of it. || 20 ||

**Vernacular Translation:** If the Sun and Moon are together in the Leo Ascendant and are aspected <note>aspected: viewed by the astrological influence of another planet</note> by Mars and Saturn, the person born is blind. Now, the author describes the knowledge of the time of delivery based on the planetary combinations at the time of the query or conception, using the *Vasantatilaka* meter:

->**(1) The specific twelfth-part (dwadashamsha) occupied by the Moon at that moment,**<-
->**When the Moon in the future reaches the sign corresponding to that number,**<-
->**And when the portion of the day or night equal to the elapsed portion of the sign rises,**<-

**Commentary:** "The specific twelfth-part occupied by the Moon at that moment" refers to the twelfth-part <term>Dwadashamsha: a 2.5-degree division of a zodiac sign</term> in which the Moon is situated at the time of the query or conception. Some read this as "the twelfth-part together with the Moon of that time." Some interpret this to mean: count the number of the twelfth-part the Moon occupies (from 1 to 12), then count that same number of signs starting from Aries; when the Moon reaches that resulting sign in the tenth month, the delivery of the fetus should be predicted. As stated in the <term>Saravali: a classic 8th-century astrological text by Kalyanavarman</term>—

> "In whichever twelfth-part the Moon is situated at the time of conception,
> the wise should predict the delivery in the sign corresponding to that number."

Others explain it differently: In whichever sign the Moon is situated at the time of conception, find the number of its twelfth-part. Count that many signs forward from the sign occupied by the Moon; when the Moon reaches that sign in the tenth month, the birth should be predicted. This is the correct explanation. As the venerable <term>Garga: an ancient legendary sage and astronomer</term> says—

> "In whichever number of the twelfth-part the Moon is situated,
> count that many signs from there; when the Moon reaches that sign, the birth occurs." (2)

Here also is the method of proportion for bringing out the <term>Nakshatra: lunar mansion or star cluster</term>. If the entire lunar sign of 1800 minutes <note>original: "lipta"</note> is obtained by the measure of the Moon's twelfth-part, then by the measure of the elapsed portion of that twelfth-part, what is obtained? From that result, the Nakshatra should be inferred by calculating based on 800 minutes.

(1) "The specific twelfth-part occupied by the Moon" and "The twelfth-part together with the Moon of that time" are variant readings.
(2) An example is shown here for the understanding of beginners: Suppose conception <note>original: "nisheka"</note> occurs on the full moon of the month of Vaishakha, when Jupiter is at 11 hours of the night. The calculated Moon at that time is in Scorpio at 6 degrees, 30 minutes, 10 seconds. Here, the Moon is in the 4th twelfth-part of Scorpio. The 4th twelfth-part of Scorpio belongs to Aquarius. Therefore, counting four signs from Aquarius leads to Taurus; when the Moon is in Taurus in the tenth month (Phalguna), the birth will occur.

Here he explains the knowledge of the specific time of day or night: *As much as has risen...* The definitions of day and night [signs] were explained previously, such as Taurus, Aries, Leo, Cancer, Gemini, and so on. ## With the Sanskrit Commentary of Bhattotpala and the Hindi Language Exposition

> "Whatever portion of the zodiac sign <term>Rashi-bhaga; a specific degree within a sign</term> rises at that time, designated as day or night,
> To that same extent of the rising should the day or night be declared.
> Thus, having first determined the time of birth <term>Sutika-kala; the moment of delivery</term> from the time of conception,
> The mathematician <note>astrologer-mathematician</note> should then consider the procedures prescribed for birth horoscopy." ||21||

**Vernacular Explanation**—In the tenth month from conception, birth occurs when the Moon enters the sign that is as many signs away from the conception-sign as the number of the <term>Dvadashamsha; a 1/12th division of a sign, equal to 2.5 degrees</term> the Moon occupied at the time of conception. Alternatively, birth should be predicted to occur after as much of the day or night has passed as the degrees of the conception-sign (whether day-strong or night-strong) that had risen at that time. ||21||

**Special Meaning**—The words of Lord Garga <note>An ancient sage and authority on Indian astronomy/astrology</note>:
> "In whichever number of the twelfth-part <term>Dvadashamsha</term> the Cool-Rayed One <note>The Moon</note> is situated,
> When the Moon reaches that same number of signs from there, birth shall occur."

**As stated in the Saravali** <note>A classic 8th-century astrological treatise by Kalyanavarman</note>:
> "Whatever portion of the zodiac sign rises at that time, designated as day or night,
> To that same extent of the rising should the day or night be declared."

**Example**—Suppose the time of conception is Monday, the 3rd day of the bright fortnight of the month of Phalguna, Samvat 1661, at 7:30 ghatis into the night. If the rising sign <term>Lagna</term> is 5s 23° 15' 20" and the clear Moon is 11s 8° 14' 25". Here, the Moon is in the 4th twelfth-part (Gemini) of the sign Pisces. Therefore, birth will occur in the tenth month from conception when the Moon enters the 4th sign from Gemini, which is Virgo. 

Furthermore, to understand the degrees and minutes of the Moon, the Rule of Three <term>Trairashika; a mathematical proportion</term> is applied: If 30 degrees correspond to the 150 minutes (2° 30') of one twelfth-part, then what corresponds to the elapsed minutes of the twelfth-part at conception? Thus, the degrees of the Moon at birth are obtained as:

-> 30 x Elapsed minutes of the twelfth-part &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Elapsed minutes of the twelfth-part <-
-> ———————————————————————  =  ——————————————————————— <-
-> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; 150 &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; 5 &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <-

In other words, dividing the elapsed minutes of the twelfth-part by 5 gives the degrees and minutes. Since the elapsed minutes of the 4th twelfth-part of the conception Moon (11s 8° 14' 25") are 44' 25", dividing this by 5 yields 8° 53' 0". Thus, it is determined that birth will occur in the tenth month (Agrahayana) when the Moon reaches 8 degrees and 53 minutes of the sign Virgo.

Consequently, the Moon at birth is 5s 8° 53' 0". From this, the desired time <term>Ishtakala; the specific time elapsed since sunrise</term> should also be understood.

<header>The Chapter on Conception in the Brihat Jataka <note>The Brihat Jataka is a foundational 6th-century Sanskrit text on Vedic astrology written by Varahamihira.</note></header>

**Example—** It has been established above that the birth will occur when the Moon enters the fourth quarter of the *Uttara Phalguni* <note>The 12th lunar mansion or star cluster</note> constellation.

That occurred in the year 1662 <note>Vikram Samvat calendar, roughly 1605 CE</note>, on the 11th day of the dark fortnight of the month of Agrahayana, a Thursday. Furthermore, the *Lagna* <term>Lagna: The ascending sign on the eastern horizon</term> at conception is Virgo, which is "day-strong" <note>Signs are categorized by whether they are more influential during day or night</note>. From its elapsed degrees of 23° 15' 20", the following proportion is derived: if 30 degrees correspond to the standard length of the day at birth, what do the elapsed degrees correspond to?

->Day-length X Elapsed Degrees<-
->= ----------------------- = Elapsed time of day at birth<-
->30<-

In other words, multiplying the elapsed degrees by the day-length and dividing by 30 yields the desired time (*Ishtakala*). Similarly, for a "night-strong" ascending sign, the elapsed time of night is established using the night-length. For example, multiplying the standard day-length of 26:30 by the elapsed degrees of the ascending sign 23:15:20 results in 616:16:20; dividing this by 30 yields the elapsed time of day as 20 *ghatis* and 32 *palas* <note>Ancient Indian units of time: 1 ghati is 24 minutes</note>. || 21 ||

*Now, in the Malini meter, the author explains the knowledge of three-year and twelve-year gestations:*

> If at the time of conception the ascending sign is in a Navamsha <note>A 1/9th subdivision of a zodiac sign</note> of Saturn, and Saturn is positioned in the seventh house from the ascendant, the birth occurs after three years. If this same configuration involves the Moon, the birth occurs in the twelfth year. This rule should also be applied with logic to the time of birth. || 22 ||

->**Thus ends the Fourth Chapter, the Chapter on Conception,**<-
->**in the Brihat Jataka composed by the illustrious Acharya Varahamihira.**<-

Regarding "If at the time of rising...": If at the time of conception, the rising *Lagna* is in a *Mridu-bhansha*—meaning a *Navamsha* subdivision belonging to Saturn (either Capricorn or Aquarius)—and at that same time Saturn is in the seventh house (the house of partnership/setting), then the delivery of the carried fetus should be predicted to occur after three years. Regarding "the Moon...": If this same rule applies to the Moon—meaning the rising sign is the Cancer *Navamsha* <note>Cancer is ruled by the Moon</note> and the Moon is in the seventh house from that ascendant—then the delivery of the carried fetus should be predicted in the twelfth year.

Regarding "This rule should also be applied...": Just as the combinations at the time of conception indicate the possibility of a fetus with missing or extra limbs, similar combinations at the time of birth should be used to describe the nature of the newborn. The good or bad fortune of the father, mother, paternal uncle, and maternal aunt should also be predicted based on the *Lagna* at the time of birth. Regarding "with logic": One should not predict what is impossible, such as predicting a specific delivery time if a miscarriage has already occurred.

**Vernacular—** If the Navamsha <note>a one-ninth division of a zodiac sign</note> of Saturn's residence (Capricorn or Aquarius) is in the Ascendant and Saturn is in the seventh house, then if conception occurs in such a combination, delivery takes place in 3 years. Similarly, if it is in the Moon's [Navamsha] (meaning the Navamsha of Cancer is in the Ascendant and the Moon is in the seventh house), then if conception occurs in such a combination, delivery takes place in 12 years. Using the logic of the results stated in this chapter, one should also deliberate on the time of birth. || 22 ||

**Special Meaning—** Just as one should deliberate on the auspicious or inauspicious state of the father and mother at the time of birth from the planets designated as "Father" and "Mother," etc. || 2 ||

# Chapter 5: On the Manner of Birth

Now, the chapter named "The Manner of Birth" is explained. First, [the author] states in an Anushtubh meter whether the child is born in the presence or absence of the father—

<margin>
(1) Here the Teacher has recited the names of the twelve houses starting from the Ascendant. However, he did not define what the Ascendant is, what the houses are, or how they are calculated; therefore, for the benefit of students, I demonstrate their calculation here. First, I demonstrate the calculation of the Precession of the Equinoxes <term>Ayanamsha: the longitudinal difference between the tropical and sidereal zodiacs</term> due to its utility:

In the Shaka year measured by one, two, and four (421 Shaka Era / 499 CE), the ancient teachers found a total absence of Ayanamsha. After that, a motion of the equinox <term>Ayanagati</term> of 54 <gloss>54</gloss> seconds was found per year. Therefore, to find the Ayanamsha from a desired Shaka year, one should subtract 421 from the desired year. With the remaining years, use the proportion: if in one year a motion of 54 <gloss>54</gloss> seconds is obtained, then what is obtained by the remaining years? The resulting seconds of the Ayanamsha from the desired year are divided by the square of sixty (3600).

The resulting Ayanamsha:
  54 (Desired Year — 421)      3 (Desired Year — 421)
------------------------- = ------------------------- Therefore, here is the verse:
        1 X 3600                      200

> From the Shaka year minus 421, multiplied by three and divided by ten,
> The result divided by two hundred is known as the Ayanamsha from the years.
</margin>

> The child is born in the father's absence (1) if the Moon does not aspect the Ascendant.
> The father is in a foreign land if the Sun is in a movable sign and fallen from the meridian. || 1 ||

"Born of the father" means the birth. If the Moon does not see (aspect) the Ascendant of birth, the child is born "out of sight" of the progenitor, meaning in his absence. Regarding the knowledge of whether the father is in his own country or a foreign land during that absence, he says: "In a foreign land..." if the Sun is situated in a movable sign...

# Page 102
## Chapter on the Method of Birth from the *Brihat Jataka* <note>The *Brihat Jataka* is a foundational 6th-century Sanskrit text on Vedic astrology written by Varahamihira.</note>

If the Sun has fallen from the meridian (the 10th house) and is situated in the 11th, 12th, 9th, or 8th houses, the birth occurs while the father is in a different direction or has traveled to another land. If the Moon does not aspect <note>In astrology, "aspect" refers to the angular relationship between celestial bodies</note> the Ascendant at birth, this same rule applies.

Now, for the purpose of calculating the *Ayanamsha* <note>The "Ayanamsha" is the angular difference between the tropical and sidereal zodiacs, accounting for the precession of the equinoxes</note> related to the desired position of the Sun, the following proportion is used: If 54 minutes of arc of the precession are obtained for the 12 signs traversed by the Sun, then what is obtained for the desired signs of the Sun? The resulting minutes of arc are added.

**54 $\times$ [Desired Signs] / 12 = 9 $\times$ [Desired Signs] / 2** — By adding these to the *Ayanamsha* values existing at the start of the year, one obtains the values for the start of the desired month. Thus, there is a verse on this:

> The number of signs traversed by the Sun is multiplied by nine and divided by two; the resulting minutes of arc are added to the *Ayanamsha* at the start of the year. These become the *Ayanamsha* values for the beginning of one's desired month.

Then, to calculate the precession minutes related to the degrees traversed by the Sun: If 54 minutes of arc are obtained for a full circle (360 degrees), then what is obtained for the specific degrees traversed by the Sun? By adding the resulting minutes to the *Ayanamsha* at the start of the month, the values for the desired day are found. Thus, there is a verse:

> The degrees traversed by the Sun are multiplied by three and divided by twenty <note>original: "tri-ghna-nakha-apta" — 'tri' (3) multiplied, 'nakha' (20) divided</note>. By adding the minutes obtained in this way to the *Ayanamsha* at the start of the month, they certainly become the values for the desired day.

This is the direction for calculating the *Ayanamsha*.

***

### Method for Determining Planetary Positions at a Desired Time

Now, the method for calculating the positions of planets at a specific desired time from the data in the almanac <term>Panchanga: a five-limbed Hindu calendar/almanac</term> is shown:

On the day the planets are to be calculated, if the row in the table preceding the desired time is closer, then subtract the time in the table from the desired time. The remainder is known as the "Positive Adjustment" <term>Dhanachalana: additive correction</term>. Multiply the planetary velocity by this, divide by sixty, and add the resulting degrees and minutes to the planet's position in the almanac; that will be the planet's position at the desired time.

If the row following the desired time is closer, subtract the desired time from the table time. The remainder is the "Negative Adjustment" <term>Rinachalana: subtractive correction</term>. Multiply the planetary velocity by this, divide by sixty, and subtract the resulting degrees and minutes from the planet's position in the table; that will be the planet's position at the desired time.

As it is said:

> If the desired time is ahead of the table row, subtract the table time from the desired. That adjustment is known as positive; in the opposite case, it is the opposite (negative). Multiply the velocity by the adjustment and divide by sixty. The resulting degrees should be added or subtracted respectively to find the desired planet. In the case of Rahu <note>The North Node of the Moon, which moves "backwards"</note>, because of its retrograde motion, do the reverse. This same rule applies to any planet in retrograde motion.

In this manner, all planets are to be calculated for the desired time.

***

### Verses for Calculating the First Ascendant (Lagna)

> The degrees of the Sun (with *Ayanamsha* added) already traversed are multiplied by the rising time of the sign and divided by thirty. The resulting minutes are subtracted from the desired time (converted to minutes). Then, the rising times of the signs to be traversed should be subtracted. The sign that cannot be fully subtracted is called the "Unpurified Sign" <note>The sign currently rising on the horizon</note>. The remainder is multiplied by thirty and divided by the rising time of that unpurified sign. The resulting degrees are added to the preceding signs to find the Ascendant.

## With the Bhashya Commentary and the Sanskrit Commentary by Bhattotpala <note>Bhattotpala was a 10th-century scholar famous for his commentaries on Varahamihira's works.</note>

The combination is not otherwise. If the Moon does not aspect the Ascendant at birth, and the Sun is situated in a fixed sign but has fallen from the meridian <note>meaning the Sun is no longer at the highest point in the sky</note>, the child is born in the absence of the father, even if the father is in his own country. -> From the loss of the 12th house, the result should be calculated from the Ascendant. <-
-> The Ascendant is calculated from the desired time after sunrise using the "remaining portion" method. <-
-> Or, using the remaining ghatis <note>1 ghati = 24 minutes</note> of the night, it is calculated by the "elapsed portion" method. <-

-> At the exact time of sunrise, the Sun is always the Ascendant. <-
-> At the time of sunset, the wise should know it is equal to the Sun plus six signs. <-

-> In the absence of nighttime "natakala," it is equal to the Sun plus six signs. <-

The calculation of the Tenth House (Midheaven) arises from the *natakala* <note>the time elapsed since the Sun was at the meridian</note>; therefore, the method for determining *natakala* is shown here: If the desired time is less than half the day, subtract the desired time from the half-day duration; the remainder is the *natakala*. If the desired time is greater than half the day, subtract the half-day from the desired time; the remainder is known as the *natakala*. Similarly, for the night, the wise should calculate the nighttime *natakala* from the half-night according to their own intellect. Then, from that *natakala*, the calculation of the Tenth House should be performed using the "Lankodaya" <note>Equatorial risings/Right Ascensions</note> in the same way the Ascendant is calculated. 

How is the Tenth House calculated using Lankodaya? It is explained: The Tenth House, which is the intersection of one's meridian and the ecliptic, is the "First House" for those living on the equator <note>the "circle of no latitude"</note> because their meridian is their horizon. Therefore, the Tenth House is always calculated using equatorial risings (Lankodaya). The First House (Ascendant), however, stays on one's own horizon, so it is calculated using the rising times of one's own latitude. The verses explaining the values for equatorial and local risings can be seen in the commentary on Verse 16 of the first chapter of this book.

### Verses for calculating Natakala, the Tenth House, and the Junctions of all Houses:

> 1. Subtract the desired time from the half-day duration to find the "Eastern Natakala." If the desired time is greater than the half-day, subtract the half-day from it to find the "Western Natakala."
> 2. The wise should perform the same calculation for the night using the half-night. From the Eastern Natakala, calculate the house using the "elapsed" method with equatorial risings as previously described.
> 3. The house resulting from the Western Natakala using the "remaining" method is called the Tenth House. By adding six signs to that, the Ascendant is found, and by adding six signs to the Ascendant, the Seventh House (Setting Sign) is known.
> 4. The Ascendant subtracted from the Fourth House, divided by six and added to the Ascendant, becomes the first junction (*sandhi*). That added by another sixth part becomes the Second House. That added by another sixth part becomes its own junction, and that added by another sixth part becomes the Third House.
> 5. That house added by a sixth part becomes its own junction. By this method of adding sixth parts, the Fourth, First, and Tenth houses are connected to their junctions; the Fifth and Sixth houses are also calculated in this way.

### Now, other combinations are described in the Anushtubh meter:—

"Situated between": if the Moon is between <term>Mercury and Venus</term>—Mercury being the son of the Moon and Venus being the descendant of Bhrigu. This means one is in the twelfth house and the other in the second house from the Moon, or all three are in one sign with the Moon in the middle degrees and Mercury and Venus at the beginning and end. In such a combination, the birth is in the absence of the father.

**Translation—** If Saturn is in the Ascendant, or Mars is in the seventh house, or the Moon is between Mercury and Venus, the birth should be said to occur in the absence of the father. || 2 ||

Regarding the moon (Shashanka): If the Lord of Scorpio <note>Mars</note> is the ruler of the Moon's position, and the Moon is located in a decan <term>Drekkana; a 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign</term> belonging to Mars—these decans are the first of Aries, the second of Cancer, the third of Leo, the first of Scorpio, the second of Sagittarius, and the third of Pisces—and if the benefics <note>auspicious planets like Jupiter, Venus, or Mercury</note> are situated in the 2nd and 11th houses from that Moon, then it should be said that a serpent was born. 

Alternatively, regarding a malefic ascendant: When a decan of Mars rises in a malefic-associated ascendant <term>Lagna</term>—specifically the first of Aries, second of Cancer, third of Leo, first of Scorpio, second of Sagittarius, or third of Pisces—and if the benefics are in the 2nd and 11th houses from that ascendant, then it should be said that the creature born is "coiled" or "encircled by a serpent."

**Special Meaning—** The word of the venerable Garga: "When the Moon is in a decan of Mars and benefics are in the 11th and 2nd houses, a serpent is born; similarly, if it occurs in a malefic ascendant, one should indicate a birth encircled by such." The meaning is clear. || 3 ||

# Chapter on the Rites of Birth from the Brihat Jataka

->Now, he describes the knowledge of a birth entwined in the umbilical cord in the Anustubh meter:<-

**If the Ascendant is Aries, Leo, or Taurus, and Saturn or Mars is situated therein, the child is born with the umbilical cord entwined around the limb corresponding to the rising Navamsha.**

*Aries* refers to the Ram; *Leo* is well-known; *Taurus* is the Bull. If any of these—Aries, Leo, or Taurus—becomes the Ascendant <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</note>, and if Saturn or Mars is also situated in that same sign, the creature is born entwined by the cord. By the word "cord," the umbilical vessels are meant. To the question "On which limb is it entwined?" he says: *In the limb corresponding to the portion of the sign.* The "portion of the sign" refers to the Navamsha <note>A 1/9th division of a zodiac sign used for fine-tuning predictions</note> of the Ascendant rising at that time. Whichever sign that Navamsha belongs to, and whichever limb of the "Time-Person" <note>The *Kala-Purusha*, a concept mapping the twelve zodiac signs to specific parts of the human body</note> that sign represents—as defined in the texts beginning with "The limbs of Time"—on that very limb, it should be said the cord is entwined. Thus it is said in the *Saravali*:
> "With Leo, Aries, or Taurus rising, a creature is born entwined by the cord if Mars or Saturn is in the Ascendant; the limb corresponds to the Navamsha of the sign."

<term>Vernacular Explanation</term>— If the Ascendant is Aries, Leo, or Taurus, and Saturn or Mars is present there, the person is born with the umbilical cord wrapped around the limb that corresponds to the specific Navamsha division of the Ascendant.

->Now, he describes a birth from a paramour <note>A birth resulting from an extramarital affair, termed *Jarajata*</note> in the Vamshastha meter:<-

**If Jupiter does not aspect the Ascendant nor the Moon, nor the Moon when joined with the Sun; or if the Moon is joined with the Sun and accompanied by a malefic, the sages say it is certainly a birth by another.**

*If Jupiter does not aspect the Ascendant...* If Jupiter <note>The planet of wisdom and legitimacy</note> does not see (aspect) the rising sign or the Moon—whether the Ascendant and Moon are in the same sign or different signs—if both are not seen by Jupiter, then the sages say with certainty that the birth is by another, a paramour. Here, if the Ascendant and Moon are in a portion (Navamsha) belonging to Jupiter, then one should not say it is a birth by another. For as Yavaneshvara <note>An ancient authority on Indian astrology, often associated with Indo-Greek traditions</note> says: "If the Moon or the Ascendant are not in a portion of Jupiter, or are not aspected by Jupiter, they say the birth is from another; however, this should be declared after observing the strength of the lords of the people." *Nor the Moon...* If Jupiter does not aspect the Moon when it is joined with the Sun—that is, when the Moon and Sun are in the same sign...

### Now, the knowledge of the father's imprisonment at birth is told in the Vaitaliya meter—

> If the two malefics are in the signs of cruel planets and situated in the seventh, ninth, or fifth from the Sun, the father is imprisoned; either in a foreign land, his own land, or on a journey, according to the nature of the sign. || 7 ||

"In the signs of cruel planets" means the signs of malefic planets: Aries, Leo, Scorpio, Capricorn, and Aquarius; also Cancer when the Moon is waning in the dark fortnight, and Virgo or Gemini when Mercury is joined with malefics. If the two "unlucky ones" <note>malefics Saturn and Mars</note> are in these cruel signs and situated in the seventh, ninth, or fifth <note>Sanskrit: dyuna, nava, atmaja</note> from the Sun, then the father of the newborn is said to be bound <note>imprisoned</note>. Regarding the location of the imprisonment, he says: "In his own [land] or on the path according to the sign." If the Sun is in a movable sign, he is bound in a foreign land; if the Sun is in a fixed sign, in his own land; if in a dual-natured sign, on the path or journey. Thus is the knowledge of the place according to the sign. The particle "atho" implies an alternative. Some read "In his own [land] or according to the sign, or likewise on the path." || 7 ||

### Now, the knowledge of birth occurring on a boat is told in the Vaitaliya meter:

> **When the Moon is full and in its own sign, Mercury is in the ascendant, and a benefic is in the fourth house;**
> **Or when a water-sign is in the ascendant and the Moon is in the seventh house, the birth occurs on a boat.** || 8 ||

**Commentary:** Regarding "When the Moon is full": When the Moon is in its full orb and situated in its own sign <note>Cancer</note>, and Mercury <note>the "Gentle One"</note> is in the ascendant <note>the rising sign</note>, and Jupiter <note>the "Auspicious One"</note> is in the fourth house from the ascendant, it should be said that the birth occurs on a boat <note>at sea or on a river</note>. 

In this context, others read the text as "by benefics in the fourth." They interpret it this way, but the plural "by benefics" does not fit. If Mercury is in the ascendant, only Venus and Jupiter remain as benefics. To justify the plural "benefics," one would have to assume the full Moon is joined by both Venus and Jupiter. This would only work if Aries were the ascendant with Mercury there, and the full Moon in Cancer were joined by Venus and Jupiter. 

However, this reading is not logical in my explanation. Why? Because the Moon is only full when it is in Cancer if the Sun is in Capricorn. If the Sun is in Capricorn, Mercury cannot possibly be in Aries (the 4th house from Capricorn), nor can Venus be in Cancer (the 7th house from Capricorn) <note>Mercury and Venus always stay close to the Sun in the sky</note>. Therefore, the reading "a benefic in the fourth" (singular) is the only just reading. 

Why was Jupiter specifically interpreted as the benefic? Because if Mercury is in the ascendant, it is impossible for Venus to be in the fourth house from it <note>due to astronomical distance from the Sun</note>, so it must be Jupiter. Some, following ancient scriptures, still wish for it to be Venus. 

Now, the second combination for birth on a boat: "A water-sign in the ascendant." If a watery sign—Cancer, the second half of Capricorn, or Pisces—is the ascendant, and the Moon (whether full or not) is in the seventh house from it, the birth occurs on a boat. The word "or" indicates an alternative condition. || 8 ||

**Vernacular Translation —** If the full Moon is in Cancer, Mercury is in the ascendant, and a benefic planet is in the fourth house, birth occurs on a boat. Alternatively, if a water-sign is the ascendant and the Moon is in the seventh house, birth should also be understood to occur on a boat. || 8 ||

### Now, the knowledge of birth in the middle of water is told in the Vaitaliya meter:

> **If a watery sign is rising and the full Moon is in a watery sign or aspects the ascendant;**
> **Or if the Moon is in the tenth, fourth, or the ascendant, the birth is in water, without a doubt.** || 9 ||

### On Birth Near Water

The term "Watery Rising" refers to the rising of a watery sign—these are the second half of Capricorn, Cancer, and Pisces. If the Moon is also in a watery sign during a watery Ascendant <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</note>, then the birth undoubtedly takes place in water or near a body of water. Alternatively, if the Full Moon is in the Ascendant and aspects <note>The "gaze" or astrological influence one planet casts upon another or a house</note> a watery sign, the birth is likewise by the water.

In the Midheaven, the Fourth House, or the Ascendant: Alternatively, if a watery sign is rising and the Moon is situated in the tenth house (Midheaven), the fourth house (the home), or the first house (the Ascendant), one should predict a birth in water. As stated in the *Saravali* <note>A classical 8th-century astrological treatise by Kalyanavarman</note>:

> "When the Full Moon is in a watery sign and aspects a watery Ascendant, or when the Moon occupies the fourth, first, or tenth houses in such signs, birth occurs in water."

**Vernacular Translation:** If the Full Moon is in a watery sign and aspects a watery Ascendant, birth occurs in water. Furthermore, if the Moon is situated in a watery sign and occupies the 10th, 4th, or 1st house, birth in water should be predicted.

### Now, the knowledge of birth in a prison or a pit is described in the *Vaitaliya* meter:

> If the Ascendant and the Moon are together and Saturn is in the twelfth house aspected by malefic planets, birth is in confinement. If Saturn is in Scorpio or Cancer in the Ascendant and is aspected by the Moon, birth is in a pit.

Regarding the Ascendant and the Moon: When the Ascendant and the Moon are in the same sign, and Saturn is placed in the twelfth house from them and is aspected by malefic planets <note>Planets like Mars or Rahu that portend difficulty</note>, it should be said that the birth occurs in a prison or place of confinement. If Saturn is in either Scorpio or Cancer in the Ascendant and is aspected by the Moon, the birth is said to occur in a pit or a hollow in the earth.

**Vernacular Translation:** If the Moon is in the Ascendant, Saturn is in the 12th house from it, and it is aspected by a malefic planet, birth is in a jail. If Saturn is in Scorpio or Cancer in the Ascendant and is aspected by the Moon, birth should be understood to occur in a pit (a hole or depression in the ground).

### Now, the knowledge of birth in a pleasure house, a temple, or barren land is described in the *Vaitaliya* meter:

> If Saturn is in a watery sign in the Ascendant and is aspected respectively by Mercury, the Sun, or the Moon, the birth occurs in a pleasure house, a temple, or on barren/salty land.

Regarding Saturn: If Saturn is placed in a watery sign and is in the Ascendant, and is aspected in sequence by Mercury, the Sun, and the Moon, one should predict birth in a pleasure house, a temple, or on barren land. This means: if Saturn is in a watery sign in the Ascendant and is aspected by Mercury, birth is in a pleasure house (a room for enjoyment). If aspected by the Sun, it is in a temple (house of the gods). If aspected by the Moon, it is on barren or salty land <note>original: "sokhara-bhūmi", referring to land impregnated with salt or alkaline soil</note>.

# Chapter on the Manner of Birth

**Vernacular Commentary:** If Saturn is situated in a water-sign <note>Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces</note> in the Ascendant and is aspected by Mercury, the birth should be said to occur in a place of recreation or a pleasure house; if aspected by the Sun, in a temple; and if aspected by the Moon, in barren or saline land. ||11||

->Now, the author describes the knowledge of birth in a cemetery, a beautiful place, a fire-sanctuary, a royal or divine house, a cowshed, or an artisan's workshop using the Upajati meter:<-

**If Mars aspects Saturn in a human sign, birth is in a cemetery; if Venus and Moon aspect, in a beautiful place; if Jupiter, in a fire-ritual hall.**
**If the Sun aspects, it is in the houses of kings, gods, or cows; if Mercury aspects, birth occurs in an artisan's workshop. ||12||**

**Commentary:** "In a human sign" (*nṛlagnagam*)... From the previous verse, the word "Saturn" is carried forward due to proximity. If Saturn is placed in a human sign—the human signs being Gemini, Virgo, Libra, the first half of Sagittarius, and Aquarius—and Mars (*kuja*) aspects it, then the birth occurs in a cemetery (*śmaśāna*). Some read "the Earth-born [Mars] seeing the human sign." If Venus (*sita*) or the Moon (*indu*) aspects Saturn in a human sign, the birth is in a beautiful or pleasing location. If Jupiter (*guru*) aspects such a Saturn, it is in a place of the *Agnihotra* <note>a consecrated fire-shrine</note> or a fire-hall. If the Sun (*ravi*) aspects such a Saturn, the birth is in the houses of kings (*narendra*), gods (*amara*), or cows (*gokula*)—meaning a royal palace, a temple, or a cowshed. Similarly, if aspected by Mercury (*jña*), the birth is in an artisan's workshop (*śilpālaya*)—the home of painters, book-makers, carpenters, and other craftsmen.

As stated in the *Saravali*: "If Saturn is in a water-sign in the Ascendant and aspected by Mercury, birth is in a pleasure garden; by the Sun, in a temple; and by the Moon, in barren land. If in a forest-sign Ascendant, then in a mountain, forest, or fort; if in a human sign aspected by Mars, in a cemetery; and if by Mercury, in an artisan's house."

And so says Badarayana: "They declare birth to be in the dwellings of cows, kings, or gods when aspected by the Sun; in a beautiful place when by Venus and Moon; and in the fire-hall of the twice-born <note>the priestly class</note> when aspected by Jupiter, provided the Ascendant is a human sign." ||12||

**Vernacular Commentary:** If Mars sees Saturn situated in a two-footed <note>human</note> sign in the Ascendant, birth is in a cemetery; if both Venus and Moon see it, in a beautiful place; if Jupiter sees it, in a fire-hall; if the Sun sees it, in a royal palace, a temple, or a cowshed; and if Mercury sees it, birth occurs in a gallery of arts. ||12||

->Now, the author describes the knowledge of the birth-country/environment using the Vaitaliya meter:<-

**Birth is on the road if the sign and Navamsha are similar; in a movable sign, it is on a journey; in a fixed sign, at home.**
**If in its own sign or Navamsha, it is in one's own house; the results are determined by the strength of the signs and their divisions. ||13||**

**Commentary:** "Sign and Navamsha" (*rāśyaṃśa*)... The sign is the Ascendant sign and the *amsha* is the Navamsha <note>the 1/9th divisional chart</note>. If the Ascendant sign or its Navamsha is of a similar nature...
