If either the Sun or the Moon is rising while malefic planets occupy the trines or the eighth house, and are not joined or aspected by powerful benefics, death occurs. || 9 ||

**If joined with a malefic:** Regarding the Moon being joined with a malefic—although stated generally—it specifically refers to being joined with the malefic Saturn. In such a state, if the Moon is in the Ascendant and eclipsed (joined with Rahu, the North Node), and <term>Mars</term> <note>original: "Kuja/Angaraka"</note> is situated in the eighth house <note>the house of death</note>, then the death of both the <term>mother and the son</term> <note>original: "Janani-sutayoh"</note> occurs. **If the Sun is in the Ascendant, it is caused by a weapon:** In such a combination, if the Sun is positioned there, the death of the mother and child is "weapon-born," meaning caused by a sharp instrument or weapon. This implies that if the Sun is eclipsed in the Ascendant, joined by Saturn or Mercury <note>Mercury is considered malefic when joined with malefics</note>, and Mars is in the eighth house, one should predict death for the mother and child via weapons.

<term>Now, a doubt arises</term>: It was stated generally as "malefic." Why then is it explained as the Moon being joined specifically with Saturn? And why was it not explicitly stated as the Sun joined with Saturn or Mercury? Here it is answered: Due to impossibility. A lunar eclipse occurs on a full moon; at that time, the Moon cannot be with the Sun. Mercury, however, must always stay near the Sun. Because Mars is in the eighth house, it also cannot be with the Moon. Therefore, excluding Saturn, Mercury must be considered a benefic here. Thus, the <term>Lunar Eclipse</term> is explained this way.

In the case of a <term>Solar Eclipse</term>, if the Sun is joined with Mercury, Mercury becomes malefic due to the association with the Sun; hence the explanation of the Sun being joined with Mercury. Because of the association with the waning Moon, this is counted as a malefic combination for the Sun, as a solar eclipse must occur at the end of the New Moon phase. There, the Sun must necessarily be with the waning Moon. If that was the teacher's <note>Varahamihira's</note> intention, he would have simply said "the Sun eclipsed and Mars in the eighth."

**If the Sun or the Moon is rising:** If the Sun is in the Ascendant or the Moon is in the Ascendant, and malefic planets are in the <term>trines or the eighth house</term> <note>the 5th, 9th, or 8th houses</note>—all of them as per the possibility of the combination—and if the Sun or Moon is not joined or aspected <note>glanced at</note> by <term>powerful benefics</term> <note>original: "Subhaih Viryopetaih"</note>, one should predict the death of the newborn. However, if the Sun or Moon in said combination is joined or aspected by strong benefics, the "Arishta" (misfortune) combination is nullified. || 9 ||

# Brihat Jataka: Chapter on Misfortune (Arishta)
Page 138

Now, if the Moon is either aspected by <note>aspected: in astrology, when one planet "looks at" or influences another from a specific distance</note> or associated with any one of the powerful planets—Venus <note>original: "Bhrigusuta"</note>, Mercury <note>original: "Shashiputra"</note>, or Jupiter <note>original: "Devapujya"</note>—then the misfortune of the *Arishta Yoga* <term>Arishta Yoga: astrological combinations indicating illness or early death</term> does not occur. Here, the mention of the "waning Moon" is not explicitly made; why is that? It is explained here: because it is seen in other traditional scriptures. Thus, it is said in the *Saravali*: "If the waning Moon is in the 8th, 7th, 12th, 1st, 5th, or 9th houses, and powerful malefic planets are present without being seen by benefics, the child generally loses their life." || 11 ||

**Vernacular Commentary:** If the Moon is joined with malefic planets and situated in the 5th, 7th, 6th, 12th, 1st, or 8th houses, death occurs—provided it is not associated with or aspected by a powerful Venus, Mercury, or Jupiter. If it is associated with or aspected by these, death does not occur. || 11 ||

Now, for those *Arishta Yogas* where the specific time of death has not been mentioned, the knowledge of that timing is described in the *Bhramaravilashita* meter:

When the Moon reaches the position of the strongest planet in the yoga, or its own original position, or the Ascendant <note>original: "Tanugriha"</note>, and is powerful and aspected by malefic planets, death occurs within a year; so it is said by the Sages. || 12 ||

Regarding the verse "When the Moon reaches the position...": In whichever *Arishta Yoga* the limit for the time of death has not been stated, one must identify the strongest planet among those creating the yoga. The sign <note>Zodiac sign</note> where that strongest planet was situated at the time of birth is called the "strongest position." When the Moon, in its transit, reaches that sign, the death of the newborn should be predicted. Alternatively, when the Moon reaches its own position—meaning the sign where the Moon was situated at the time of birth—death should be predicted. Or, when the Moon reaches the Ascendant <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note> during its transit, death should be predicted. When does this happen? It is said: "Within a year" <note>original: "Varshasyantah"</note>. This means: "One born under a misfortune of unstated time does not survive beyond a year." 

Now, a question arises: since the Moon travels through all the signs every month, why is it said "within a year"? It is explained: "When it is powerful and aspected by malefics." Among these specified positions, death is predicted only when the Moon is powerful and simultaneously aspected by malefic planets as it passes through. It is not triggered by the transit alone. The word "Kila" (it is said) indicates traditional authority; this definition of misfortune is heard through a long lineage of sages. 

Other teachers have also described the *Arishta-bhanga* <term>Arishta-bhanga: the cancellation or "breaking" of a death-inflicting combination</term>, and these are true in form, as many children are seen to live despite the presence of these yogas. Therefore, we write a little on this:

> "Just as a bow to the Wielder of the Trident <note>Lord Shiva</note> performed with devotion destroys many insurmountable sins,
> -> so does a powerful Jupiter, the Minister of the King of Gods, <-
> standing in the Ascendant with a shimmering web of rays,
> -> pacify all these misfortunes." <- || 1 ||

# Chapter on the Cancellation of Misfortune

If the <term>Lord of the Ascendant</term><note>The planet ruling the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth.</note> is exceedingly powerful and is not aspected by malefic planets, but is instead viewed by benefic planets situated in the <term>Kendras</term><note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, considered the pillars of a horoscope.</note>, he drives away death and bestows a very long life, along with many virtues and abundant wealth. **|| 2 ||**

Even if the Moon is in the eighth house from the Ascendant, if it occupies a <term>Decan</term><note>A 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign.</note> belonging to Jupiter, Mercury, or Venus, it protects the person from the clutches of death without fail. **|| 3 ||**

The Moon, when full in body, situated in a sign owned by a benefic planet, and aspected by benefics—especially when aspected by Venus—brings about the destruction of misfortune. **|| 4 ||**

If even one of the planets Mercury, Venus, or Jupiter is powerful and situated in a <term>Kendra</term>, <note>The asterisk in the original text refers to the footnote below regarding the reading of this verse.</note> * even if accompanied by a malefic, it immediately causes the cancellation of misfortune. **|| 5 ||**

Even if the Moon is in the sixth house, if it is in a <term>Decan</term> of Jupiter, Venus, or Mercury, it protects the person without fail, just as medicine protects one bitten by a serpent. **|| 6 ||**

The Moon, when full, with a glistening orb, and placed between two benefic planets, destroys all misfortunes entirely, just as the mythical bird <term>Garuda</term> destroys the world of serpents. **|| 7 ||**

When the Moon is full in body, during the bright fortnight, and the birth occurs at night, no misfortune can affect the newborn even if the Moon is in the sixth or eighth house. **|| 8 ||**

When Jupiter, the <term>Minister of the Gods</term>, is in a <term>Kendra</term>, possessing strength with a glistening, pure orb and shimmering rays, all misfortunes are pacified. **|| 9 ||** <note>The original text mistakenly prints the numeral '6' for verse 9.</note>

When Jupiter, the Moon, Venus, and Mercury are in the signs of benefics, or in the <term>Navamshas</term><note>The 1/9th divisional chart used for fine-tuning strength.</note> or <term>Decans</term> of benefics, they all become destroyers of misfortune. **|| 10 ||**

If the lord of the sign occupied by the Moon is in a <term>Kendra</term>, or if a benefic planet is in a <term>Kendra</term>, the combination for misfortune is pacified, just as the remembrance of God <note>original: "Hari"</note> destroys sins. **|| 11 ||**

If malefic planets are in the divisions of benefics and are aspected by benefics situated in benefic divisions, they destroy misfortune just as a disaffected young woman leaves her husband. **|| 12 ||**

If <term>Rahu</term><note>The North Node of the Moon, often considered a shadow planet of ill omen.</note> is in the 3rd, 6th, or 11th house from the Ascendant and is fully aspected by benefics, it destroys all sins and misfortunes, just as a gale of wind destroys a heap of cotton. **|| 13 ||**

If at birth all the planets are in signs that rise with their heads first <note>original: "Shirshodaya"</note> and are in their natural states, misfortune dissolves like ghee (clarified butter) placed in fire. **|| 14 ||**

If at the time of birth a benefic planet is victorious in a planetary war and is aspected by other benefics, it certainly destroys all misfortune, just as a powerful wind uproots trees. **|| 15 ||**

The Moon, when increasing in size (waxing) and aspected by all the planets, destroys misfortune, just as a king whose orders are followed by all his subjects leads them to prosperity. **|| 16 ||**

**Vernacular Commentary:** In those planetary combinations where the specific time of death has not been mentioned, the sages have stated that death occurs within a year when the Moon, becoming strong, enters its own sign, the sign of a strong planet, or the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note>, and is aspected by malefic planets. ॥11॥

# Chapter 7: On Longevity (Ayurdaya)

Now the chapter on the determination of longevity is explained. In the previously mentioned chapter on misfortunes <note>Arishta-adhyaya</note>, the calculation of the lifespan should be performed for those who are free from such early-death combinations. At the very beginning, the author states the maximum lifespan contributed by each planet according to the opinions of Maya, Yavana, Manittha, and Parashara, using the *Pushpitagra* meter:

**The years assigned to the Sun and the other planets by Maya, Yavana, Manittha, and Parashara (the son of Shakti) are nineteen, twenty-five, fifteen, twelve, fifteen, twenty-one, and twenty, respectively, when they are in their signs of highest exaltation.** ॥1॥

**Commentary:** "Maya, Yavana," etc. Maya is the name of the Danava <note>a celestial architect/astronomer</note> who received favors from the Sun God. The Yavanas refer to the Greek authorities <note>literally "foreigners," specifically referring to the Greco-Indian astrological tradition</note> who were experts in this science. Manittha is a great teacher. Parashara is referred to as "the one preceded by Shakti," where "preceded" refers to his father <note>Parashara was the son of Shakti Maharishi</note>. By these authorities—Maya, Yavana, Manittha, and Parashara—the years (*vatsara*), which are the measures of maximum longevity, are declared for the Sun and the other planets.

Regarding the numbers "nine, fifteen, five, two," etc.: the phrase "added to ten" applies to all of them. Therefore:
* Nine added to ten is **19**: the maximum longevity years for the Sun.
* Fifteen <note>Tithi</note> added to ten is **25** for the Moon.
* Five <note>Vishaya/Elements</note> added to ten is **15** for Mars.
* Two <note>Ashvins/Twins</note> added to ten is **12** for Mercury.
* Five <note>Bhuta/Elements</note> added to ten is **15** for Jupiter.
* Eleven <note>Rudras</note> added to ten is **21** for Venus.
* Ten added to ten is **20** for Saturn.

These are the maximum years of longevity for the planets when they are situated in their highest degrees of exaltation. The Sun and others provide these specified years when in such positions. Specifically, they grant these years: 19, 25, 15, 12, 15, 21, 20. These are the numerical measures of the maximum lifespan for the Sun and the rest. ॥1॥

**Vernacular Commentary:** If the Sun and other planets are in their respective exaltations, the lifespan contributed by the Sun and the others is 19, 25, 15, 12, 15, 21, and 20 years respectively. For example, if the Sun is in its highest exaltation (10 degrees of Aries), the life contributed by the Sun is 19 years; this should be understood for all planets in sequence. ॥1॥

# 141
->Now, in the Mandakranta meter, he explains the knowledge of longevity when a planet is situated in its lowest point of depression (fall):<-

> In the lowest point <term>Nicha: the point where a planet is weakest</term>, half of the value is lost <gloss>(1)</gloss>; for those situated in between, a proportion is calculated.
> The Ascendant <term>Hora</term> gives years equal to its degrees <term>Amsha</term>, though others say it is equal to the full Signs <term>Rashi</term>.
> Excluding a planet in retrograde motion, those in an enemy’s house lose a third of their contribution.
> For those whose light is obscured by the Sun <gloss>[2]</gloss>, half is discarded, except for Venus and Saturn. ||2||

**In the lowest point:** These very planets (Sun, etc.), when in their maximum depression, take away half from the years of maximum longevity previously stated. Thus it is said: "In the lowest point, half of the previously mentioned maximum longevity decreases or is lost." If the Sun and others are in their maximum depression, they grant only half of the previously stated life-force. For example: The Sun gives 9 years and 6 months. The Moon gives 12 years and 6 months. Similarly, Mars gives 7 and a half years. Mercury gives 6. Jupiter gives 7 and a half. Venus gives 10 and a half. Saturn gives 10. <note>The author is halving the standard maximum years: Sun 19/2=9.5, Moon 25/2=12.5, etc.</note> By the Sun's calculation: Sun 9 years 6 months; Moon 12 years 6 months; Mars 7 years 6 months; Mercury 6 years; Jupiter 7 years 6 months; Venus 10 years 6 months; Saturn 10 years.

**For those situated in between, a proportion:** From that point, for a planet situated in the middle—between its exaltation <term>Uccha</term> and depression <term>Nicha</term>—a "Rule of Three" <term>Trairashika: a mathematical proportion</term> must be performed. The depression points for all are written numerically. In this system, the interval between any planet's maximum exaltation and maximum depression is six signs. Converting that into minutes of arc <term>Lipta</term>, it becomes ten thousand eight hundred (10,800). When a planet has traveled beyond its exaltation, one should subtract the exaltation point and convert the remainder into minutes. If it has traveled beyond its depression, subtract the depression point and convert the remainder into minutes. This is called the "Planet's Traveled Minutes." One must then convert the years and months stated for that planet's maximum depression into a single value. How? Multiply the years by twelve and add the months...

---

<note>(1) The maximum longevity of planets (Sun=19, Moon=25, etc.) is stated for when they are in their exaltation sign. Due to gradual decrease, only half that longevity remains at the point of depression. Therefore, it is logical that the longevity in between is calculated by proportion. Specifically: if half the stated exaltation years are lost over an interval of half a zodiac circle (180 degrees), then how much is lost for the specific distance between the planet and its exaltation? Subtracting this result from the maximum years gives the planet's "clear" longevity.</note>
<note>(2) There is also a reading "Obscured by the Sun" <note>original: "Suryachanna-dyutishu"</note>. The analysis is: those whose light is covered by the Sun are "Sun-obscured-lights." This refers to combustion.</note>

# The Chapter on Longevity in the Brihat Jataka

The values for the Sun and the other planets, converted into months, are written as follows. Specifically: 114 for the Sun. Dividing as before, 150 for the Moon. 90 for Mars. 72 for Mercury. 90 for Jupiter. 126 for Venus. 120 for Saturn. In numerical form: Sun 114; Moon 150; Mars 90; Mercury 72; Jupiter 90; Venus 126; Saturn 120. 

In this context, the <term>Rule of Three</term> <note>A mathematical method to find an unknown fourth value from three known values</note> is applied: If the total minutes in half a revolution—represented by the number 10,800—yield these maximum months of longevity at a planet's lowest point (deep fall), then how many months are yielded by the minutes actually traversed by that planet? Here is the formula:

> "In the Rule of Three, the 'Argument' and the 'Requisition' are of the same kind at the beginning and end. The 'Requisition' multiplied by the 'Fruit' and divided by the 'Argument' gives the result." <note>original: "त्रैराशिके प्रमाणं फलमिच्छाद्यन्तयोः सदृशराशी । इच्छा फलेन गुणिता प्रमाणभक्ता फलं भवति ।"</note>

For that purpose, one should multiply by the <term>months of the planet's deep fall</term> and <term>divide by the minutes of half a revolution</term> to obtain the months. The remainder of the months, multiplied by thirty (30) and divided as before, gives the days. The remainder of the days, multiplied by sixty, gives the *ghatikas* <note>A unit of time equal to 24 minutes</note>. The remainder of the *ghatikas*, multiplied by sixty, gives the *vikalas* or *palas* <note>Sub-units of time</note>. In this way, the time is calculated down to the smallest units starting from months. By dividing the months by twelve, the years are obtained, and the remainder is the months. 

By subtracting this result from the years shown for the maximum exaltation longevity, the remaining time is the longevity contributed by that planet. This calculation should be performed for a planet that has moved away from its exaltation point but has not yet reached its point of fall. For a planet that has moved away from its point of fall but has not yet reached its exaltation, one should calculate the time as before and add it to the planet's minimum longevity to find the total years and months.

Alternatively, if the years of life decrease over the 10,800 minutes of a semi-circle (six signs), then what is the decrease for the minutes traversed by the planet? Here, after reducing the middle figures to a common denominator, one should multiply the minutes traversed by the planet by that number. Then, by converting and multiplying the divisors and parts—as per the rule for common denominators—the <term>minutes of half a revolution</term> multiplied by their own divisors become <term>21,600 minutes</term> <note>original: "खखषट् चन्द्रनयनलिप्ता" - a mnemonic for 21,600</note>. Dividing by this, the years are obtained. The remainder, including fractions, is multiplied by twelve; then the lower fractional parts are divided by sixty and added to the upper figure to obtain the months. Similarly, the remainder is multiplied by thirty and sixty to bring out the days, *ghatikas*, and *vighatikas*. The rest of the process is as before.

Now, a shorter method for calculating <term>Pindayu</term> <note>Longevity based on the planetary "body" or sum</note> is shown. It is as follows: Subtract the previously mentioned <term>exaltation constant</term> <note>The fixed degree where a planet is strongest</note> from the desired planet and place the remainder on the ground (write it down). If the exaltation constant cannot be subtracted, add twelve signs to the planet's position, then subtract the exaltation point and record the remainder. If that remainder is less than six signs...

<summary>This page details the mathematical formulas and the "Rule of Three" used to calculate a person's lifespan based on planetary positions between their points of exaltation and fall. It provides specific numerical constants for each planet and explains how to convert these into years, months, and days.</summary>
<keywords>Ayurdaya, Brihat Jataka, Pindayu, Rule of Three, planetary longevity, mathematical astrology, Sanskrit astronomy</keywords>

--- Page 146 ---
<meta>This page continues the technical discussion of calculating the lifespan (Ayurdaya) of an individual based on planetary positions and the rising sign (Ascendant).</meta>

<page-num>143</page-num>
<header>With the Sanskrit commentary of Bhattotpala and the vernacular explanation</header>

If [the calculation] occurs, it should be subtracted from the twelve signs and the remainder set down. If it is greater than six signs, then that value itself should be taken. That operation should be performed on the ground <note>referring to the practice of calculating on a dust-board or slate</note> with the signs, degrees, minutes, and seconds, multiplying them by the planet's own maximum lifespan years and dividing by its specific divisor; the quotient obtained should be added above. The remainder should be set aside. From the seconds divided by sixty, the degrees by thirty, and the signs by twelve, the quotient from the signs gives the years. The remainder of that gives the months; the remainder of the degrees gives the days; the remainder of the minutes gives the ghatikas <note>a unit of time equal to 24 minutes</note>; and the remainder of the seconds gives the cashakas <note>a smaller unit of time</note>. By this process alone, the calculation becomes clear. And so it is said in the *Saravali*:

> "A planet, purified by its point of exaltation, should be subtracted from the circle of signs if it is less than six signs. Multiplied by its own specific number and divided by the measure of signs etc. (1, 12, 30, 60, 60), the result is the years."

Regarding the phrase **"The Ascendant gives years equal to the Navamshas"**: The *Hora* refers to the Ascendant (Lagna). It grants years equal to the measure of its parts; specifically, it gives as many years as there are *Navamshas* <note>a 1/9th division of a zodiac sign, equal to 3 degrees and 20 minutes</note> elapsed in the Ascendant. The method for this is as follows: Setting aside the signs of the current Ascendant, the remaining portion should be converted into minutes. Dividing that by two hundred <note>the number of minutes in one Navamsha</note>, the resulting elapsed Navamshas give the years of the Ascendant's lifespan contribution. With the remainder, a "Rule of Three" <note>a mathematical proportion</note> should be performed to place the months and so on below the years. For example: if 200 minutes yield 12 months, then how many do the remaining minutes yield? By multiplying the remaining minutes by twelve and dividing by two hundred, the resulting months are placed below the years. Multiplying the remaining months by thirty and dividing by two hundred as before, the resulting days are placed below the months. This is the Ascendant's lifespan contribution.

**Others say it is equal to the signs.** Other teachers, such as Manittha and his followers, desire the lifespan contribution of the Ascendant to be equal to the number of signs. The years of the Ascendant's life are as many signs as have elapsed in the Ascendant. To calculate the months and so on, the elapsed degrees and minutes of the Ascendant should be converted into minutes and a Rule of Three performed: If 1,800 minutes <note>the total minutes in one sign</note> yield 12 months, then how many do these elapsed minutes of the Ascendant yield? As before, the months and so on should be placed below the years. Some desire the Ascendant's lifespan in this way. And so says Manittha:

> "The years are equal to the signs of the Ascendant, with months and so on calculated by proportion. Those skilled in the science of *Hora* (Astrology) desire this for the Ascendant's lifespan."

In our opinion, that view is the most pleasing. However, others desire it thus: when the lord of the Ascendant's *Navamsha* is strong, the lifespan is equal to the *Navamshas*; when the lord of the sign is strong, it is equal to the signs. And so it is said in the *Saravali*:

> "The contribution from the Ascendant is equal to the Navamshas, and by proportion for the intervals; but it is equal to the signs if the lord of the sign is endowed with strength."

**"Excepting the retrograde"**: Whatever number of years of life is given by a planet, it becomes its own...

# Chapter on Longevity in the Brihat Jataka
<page-num>144</page-num>

Therefore, from the lifespan contributed by a planet, one must subtract a third of that value if the planet is situated in an enemy’s house <note>the zodiac sign of a hostile planet</note>, excluding the planet Mars <note>original: "Bhauma"</note> if it is in retrograde motion <note>moving backward from our perspective on Earth</note>. A planet in retrograde does not lose its contribution even if it is in an enemy's house. As it is said: "Except for retrograde motion, a planet in an enemy sign loses a third." This is the opinion of many authorities, and it is the preferred view of the Teacher <note>Varahamihira, the author</note>. Otherwise, he would have simply said "excluding Mars, those in enemy houses lose a third." It is certain that just as a retrograde planet gives triple the lifespan due to its great strength, it likewise does not suffer reduction here.

Others interpret this differently: they suggest that excluding Mars specifically, any other planet in an enemy sign loses a third, meaning Mars never loses its share even in an enemy sign. On this, the sage Badarayana says: "Excluding the Son of the Earth <note>Mars</note>, those in enemy houses destroy a third of their own contributed lifespan."

Regarding those whose "splendor is severed by the Sun" <term>astangata: combustion; when a planet is too close to the Sun to be seen</term>, half of their contribution is lost. However, this excludes Venus and Saturn <note>original: "Shukra" and "Arkaputra"</note>. Even when these two are combust, they do not lose their contribution. As Badarayana says: "All planets that have set <note>become combust</note> cause a loss of half, except for the Teacher of the Daityas <note>Venus</note> and the Son of the Sun <note>Saturn</note>."

**Vernacular Commentary:** If a planet is at its point of maximum debilitation <note>its weakest zodiacal point</note>, half of the aforementioned lifespan is destroyed—meaning only half remains. Therefore, the value of the lifespan should be understood by proportion between the points of exaltation <note>maximum strength</note> and debilitation. Excluding the lifespan contributed by the Ascendant <note>calculated by the degrees passed in the rising sign</note>, the calculated lifespan of planets residing in an enemy's house is reduced by one-third. Furthermore, excluding Venus and Saturn, if other planets are "set" due to their proximity to the Sun, half of their contributed lifespan is destroyed.

->Table for Clarification<-

| Planet | Sun | Moon | Mars | Mercury | Jupiter | Venus | Saturn | |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Exaltation | 19 | 25 | 15 | 12 | 15 | 21 | 20 | Retrograde |
| Debilitation | 9 | 12 | 7 | 6 | 7 | 10 | 10 | Retrograde |
| | 9 | 6 | 6 | 0 | 6 | 6 | 6 | Mars |

**Special Meaning:** The proportion between exaltation and debilitation is as follows: "If half is lost over the interval between exaltation and debilitation (6 signs), what is lost at the specific interval between the planet and its exaltation?" Thus, multiply the distance between the exaltation point and the planet's position by half of the standard years, divide by 6, and subtract the resulting years or months from the maximum exaltation years to find that planet's specific contribution to the lifespan.

**Regarding the Longevity of the Ascendant (Lagna-ayu)—** The Teacher's <note>referring to the original author of the verses being commented upon</note> intention is that if the sign of the Ascendant is strong, the years should be understood as equal to the number of the sign.

**Retrograde Planets (Vakri-graha)—** Even if a retrograde planet is in an enemy's house, one-third of its contribution is not lost. This is because the longevity contribution of a retrograde planet increases. Therefore, the word 'Vakra' <note>literally "crooked" or "curved"</note> here should be understood as retrograde motion. Some have interpreted 'Vakra' to mean Mars <note>original: "Mangal"</note>, but this is inconsistent and not widely accepted.

Example— A birth occurred in the year 1666 <note>Vikram Samvat, approx. 1609 CE</note>, on the first day of the bright fortnight of the month of Vaishakha, on a Thursday, at 15 ghatis and 56 palas <note>approx. 6 hours and 22 minutes</note> after sunrise. The precise planetary positions and the birth chart for that time are as follows:

->Birth Chart (Janma-lagna Chakra)<-

| Precise Sun | 0 | 6 | 46 | 40 |
|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| Moon | 0 | 12 | 15 | 57 |
| Mars | 2 | 13 | 20 | 27 |
| Mercury | 11 | 24 | 17 | 25 |
| Jupiter | 7 | 14 | 10 | 27 |
| Venus | 11 | 16 | 20 | 7 |
| Saturn | 0 | 28 | 0 | 55 |
| Ascendant (Lagna) | 0 | 21 | 21 | 6 |

The difference between the precise Sun (0s 6° 46' 40") and its point of exaltation (0s 10°) is 0s 3° 10' 20", which equals 190 minutes and 20 seconds of arc. Multiplying this by half of the Sun's maximum longevity (6 years and 6 months, or 114 months), which is 21698.0, and dividing by the half-circle minutes (108000), the result is 0.12.3.18.20. Subtracting this from the 19 years elapsed from exaltation, the Sun's longevity contribution is 18 years, 6 months, 26 days, 43 minutes, and 40 seconds. Similarly: Moon's longevity: 23y 6m 21d 40s; Mars's longevity: 6y 4m 10d 0s; Mercury's longevity: 6y 3m 21d 36s; Jupiter's longevity: 6y 7m 12d 30s; Venus's longevity: 20y 4m 16d 21s; Saturn's longevity: 10y 5m 12d 0s. 

Calculating the Ascendant's longevity: The Ascendant is at 0s 21° 21' 16". Here, the sign is Aries and the ninth-division <term>Navamsha: a 3°20' subdivision of a zodiac sign used for precision</term> is Libra. Since neither is "aspected by or joined with its lord, Jupiter, or Mercury" <note>original: "svami-guru-jna-vikshita-yuta"</note>, they are considered weak. Therefore, the longevity will be equal to the degrees of the Ascendant already passed. The passed degrees are 21° 21' 16", which equals 1281 minutes and 16 seconds. Dividing by 200 gives 6 months; multiplying the remainder by 30 and dividing by 200 gives 26 days and 22.12 ghatis. Thus, the Ascendant's longevity is 6 months, 4 days, 26 ghatis, 22 palas, and 13 vipalas.

Another simple method for determining the longevity contribution as mentioned in the *Saravali* <note>a classic 8th-century astrological text by Kalyanavarman</note> is as follows:

> "Subtract the planet's position from its exaltation point; if the result exceeds six signs, subtract it from the full circle. Multiply by the planet's specific multiplier and divide by the total measure to find the years."

## Chapter on Longevity and Misfortune

**Language—** If a planet, when subtracted from its point of exaltation <note>The position where a planet is at its maximum strength</note>, results in a value less than 6 signs, subtract that value from 12. If it is 6 signs or more, take that value as it is. Multiply this by the planet's *Pinda* <term>Pinda: The base number of years assigned to a planet at its peak exaltation</term>. Then, divide the resulting signs and degrees by their respective units (divide seconds and minutes by 60, degrees by 30, and signs by 12) to determine the lifespan in years and months.

**For example—** Subtracting the Sun from its exaltation point results in 0 signs, 3 degrees, 10 minutes, and 20 seconds. Since this is less than 6 signs, we subtract it from 12 signs, giving 11 | 26 | 49 | 40. Multiplying this by the Sun's base value of 19 gives 206 | 46 | 93 | 760. By dividing the seconds by 60 and adding the quotient to the minutes, then dividing the minutes by 60 and adding to the degrees, then dividing degrees by 30 for signs, and finally dividing signs by 12, the quotient gives the years and the remainder gives the months. Thus, the Sun's contribution to the lifespan is 18 years, 9 months, 29 days, 43 minutes, and 40 seconds.

The lifespan contributions for all planets are calculated in this same manner.

Now, if a planet is in an enemy's house, one-third of its calculated years are lost; if it is "combust" <note>Too close to the Sun to be seen</note>, half is lost. Furthermore, according to the following verses, a "half-cycle reduction" <term>Chakrardha Hani: A specific reduction in years based on a planet's placement in the twelve houses</term> is also applied. In this case, Mercury and Venus are both in the twelfth house. Because Venus is exalted, it is considered strong. Therefore, only the half-cycle reduction is applied to Venus.

| Sun's Life-years | 18 | 9 | 29 | 43 | 40 |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| Moon's Life-years | 11 | 9 | 10 | 50 | 0 |
| Mars's Life-years | 9 | 4 | 10 | 0 | 0 |
| Mercury's Life-years | 4 | 2 | 14 | 24 | 0 |
| Jupiter's Life-years | 8 | 7 | 26 | 15 | 0 |
| Venus's Life-years | 9 | 9 | 15 | 27 | 0 |
| Saturn's Life-years | 10 | 5 | 12 | 0 | 0 |
| Ascendant's Life-years | 9 | 4 | 29 | 22 | 12 |
| **Total =** | **79** | **5** | **25** | **1** | **52** |

By taking half of the previously calculated age for Venus, we get 10 | 2 | 8 | 10 | 30 | 0 years. Because it is also in an enemy's house, we then subtract one-third of that (3 | 4 | 22 | 43 | 30), resulting in 9 | 9 | 15 | 27 | 0 as the corrected lifespan for Venus. Similarly, Mercury is in an enemy's house; subtracting one-third (2 | 1 | 7 | 12) from its base value results in a corrected lifespan of 4 | 2 | 14 | 24 | 0. Jupiter is in the eighth house, so after subtracting its tenth-part reduction (0 | 11 | 19 | 15), its corrected lifespan is 8 | 7 | 26 | 15 | 0. Finally, because the Moon is combust by the Sun's rays, its corrected lifespan is half of its previously calculated value, 11 | 9 | 10 | 50. The sum of all these gives a total lifespan of 79 years, 5 months, 25 days, 1 minute, and 52 seconds.

### Method for Calculating Lifespan Based on the Ascendant (Lagna) According to Common Consensus

->"The years are equal to the signs passed by the Lagna; the degrees and further units, multiplied by two and divided by five, yield the months; the remaining degrees multiplied by six yield the days and so on."<-

The number of completed signs <note>Rashi</note> of the Lagna represents the number of years. Multiply the remaining degrees, minutes, and seconds by 2 and divide by 5; the quotient gives the months. Multiply the remainder by 6 to obtain the days and further units.

For example: If the Lagna is at 10 signs, 26 degrees, 28 minutes, and 5 seconds. Here, the years are 10 (equal to the signs). The degrees etc. (26|28|5) multiplied by 2 equals 52|56|10. Dividing this by 5 gives a quotient of 10 months. Multiplying the remainder by 6 gives 17 days, 37 minutes, 0 seconds. Thus, the Lagna-based lifespan is 10 years, 10 months, 17 days, and 37 minutes.

The logic <note>Yukti</note> behind this is: If 30 degrees equal 12 months, then what do the remaining degrees equal? $\frac{12 \times \text{remaining degrees}}{30} = \frac{2 \times \text{remaining degrees}}{5}$ = number of months. 

To find the days, the remainder is multiplied by 30 and divided by 5, which simplifies to: Remainder $\times$ 6 = days.

### Now, describing the reduction of planetary lifespan due to their placement in the visible hemisphere (Chakra-pata) in the Praharshini meter:

->"The whole, a half, a third, a fourth, a fifth, and a sixth part<-
->are reduced starting from the twelfth house for malefic planets in reverse order.<-
->For benefic planets, the reduction is half of that; if multiple planets occupy one sign,<-
->only the strongest one causes the reduction; so says Satyacharya."<-

**Commentary:** Regarding "The whole, a half...": When <term>malefic planets</term><note>Asat/Papa-graha: planets like Saturn or Mars considered to have a harsh influence</note> are situated in the houses starting from the twelfth back to the seventh from the Lagna, their contributed lifespan is reduced proportionately. A malefic in the 12th house loses its entire contribution; in the 11th, one-half; in the 10th, one-third; in the 9th, one-fourth; in the 8th, one-fifth; and in the 7th, one-sixth. 

Regarding "For benefics, half": If <term>benefic planets</term><note>Sat/Shubha-graha: planets like Jupiter or Venus considered to have a positive influence</note> are in these same houses, the reduction is half of what was stated for malefics. Thus, a benefic in the 12th house loses half its contribution; in the 11th, one-fourth; in the 10th, one-sixth; in the 9th, one-eighth; in the 8th, one-tenth; and in the 7th, one-twelfth.

Regarding "multiple planets in one sign": When two or more planets occupy the same house among those mentioned, only the one that is the strongest <note>Bali</note> causes the reduction of its portion as prescribed; the others in that same house do not lose their contribution. This is the teaching of <term>Satyacharya</term><note>An ancient authority on astrology frequently cited by Bhattotpala</note>. Regarding the calculation of portions—

<vocab>Lagnayurdaya (lifespan from the ascendant), Vyayabhavana (12th house/house of loss), Papagraha (malefic planet), Shubhagraha (benefic planet), Satyacharya (Sage Satya), Bhattotpala (the commentator), Bhuktarashi (signs traversed), Praharshini (a poetic meter)</vocab>

# Chapter on Longevity in the Brihat Jataka

The following is provided to demonstrate the distribution of portions. Thus says Satyacharya: "The reduction process is said to occur from the twelfth house back to the seventh. If multiple planets occupy the same sign, only the strongest among them reduces its portion. Malefics <note>planets with a harsh influence, such as Saturn or Mars</note> take away a full, half, third, fourth, fifth, or sixth part of the total longevity. Benefics <note>planets with a gentle influence, such as Jupiter or Venus</note> take away half of what the malefics do. A malefic in the twelfth house removes the entire portion, while a benefic removes half. I shall also explain the specific combinations that remove all longevity." If several planets are in one sign, the one with the greatest strength specifically reduces the portion as stated; no other planet in that position does so. This is also the opinion of Varahamihira. The mention of Satyacharya’s view here is to show the traditional lineage of this knowledge.

**Vernacular Commentary—** If malefic planets are placed from the twelfth house back to the seventh house, then in that order, the calculated longevity is destroyed by the whole, a half, a third, a fourth, a fifth, and a sixth part. If benefic planets are in those same positions, the loss is half of what a malefic would cause. For example:
*   **12th House:** Malefic removes all; Benefic removes 1/2.
*   **11th House:** Malefic removes 1/2; Benefic removes 1/4.
*   **10th House:** Malefic removes 1/3; Benefic removes 1/6.
*   **9th House:** Malefic removes 1/4; Benefic removes 1/8.
*   **8th House:** Malefic removes 1/5; Benefic removes 1/10.
*   **7th House:** Malefic removes 1/6; Benefic removes 1/12.
If two or more planets are in the same house, only the portion of the strongest planet is lost, not all of them. This is the opinion of Satyacharya.

->Example: See the previous verse.<-

Now, a malefic in the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the rising sign on the eastern horizon</term> destroys a portion of life according to its position in the zodiacal arc. The method for knowing the measure of that portion is stated in the *Vasantatilaka* meter:

### The total longevity is multiplied by the number of Navamshas <note>a 1/9th division of a sign, equal to 3 degrees and 20 minutes</note> that have risen, including the fraction of the current one,
### and then divided by the number 108 <note>original: "ashtyuktashata" (eight plus one hundred)</note> to find the loss.
### When a malefic is in the Ascendant, this rule applies;
### if it is aspected by a benefic, the loss is reduced by half. ||4||

**Commentary:** Regarding "including the fraction of the current one"... the risen <term>Navamshas</term> are those that have already passed the horizon. This means: take the degrees of the calculated Ascendant at the time of birth, convert them into minutes, and divide by 200 <note>the number of minutes in one Navamsha</note>. This gives the number of Navamshas of the zodiac that have risen at that time...

<page-num>146</page-num>
<header>Including the Bhashya commentary and the Sanskrit commentary by Bhattotpala</header>

The partially risen <term>Navamsha</term><note>A 1/9th division of a zodiac sign, used for fine-tuning predictions</note> should be added to the total number of risen Navamshas. By doing this, the sum of the risen and partially risen Navamshas is obtained. One should multiply the entire <term>Ayuspinda</term><note>The total "lump sum" of years of life calculated for a person</note> obtained through calculation by that sum. Thus, the total longevity mass is multiplied by the risen Navamshas. When that result is divided by one hundred and eight (108), the resulting years, months, etc., undergo "destruction"—meaning they are reduced or subtracted.

Does this apply to everyone? The text says: **"When a malefic is in the Ascendant."** When a <term>Kruragraha</term><note>A "cruel" or malefic planet, specifically the Sun, Mars, or Saturn</note> is situated in the <term>Lagna</term><note>The Ascendant; the sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note>, only then should the calculated years be subtracted from the total longevity mass. By doing this, the clear (rectified) lifespan of the being born at that time is determined. However, this procedure must be performed for each planet so that the <term>Dasha</term><note>Planetary period</note> years of all are purified.

By the rule **"If aspected by a benefic,"** if that same malefic planet in the Ascendant is seen (aspected) by a <term>Saumyagraha</term><note>A "gentle" or benefic planet, such as Jupiter, Venus, or a strong Moon</note>, then only half of the result obtained (after multiplying the longevity mass by the risen Navamshas and dividing by 108) goes to "ruin." One should halve that value and then subtract it from the longevity mass; thus the measure of life becomes clear.

Others explain it this way: The Navamshas elapsed by the specific Ascendant at that time should be taken along with the partially risen Navamsha. The meaning is: discarding the full signs of the current Ascendant, convert the remaining degrees into minutes (<term>liptas</term>), divide by two hundred, and the resulting risen portions should be treated as before. But even this is a "gross" (approximate) method. Therefore, one should convert the Ascendant degrees into minutes, multiply them by the longevity years given by each planet, divide by their respective divisors, and add them up. One should divide by the minutes in a full circle of years; the resulting years etc. should be subtracted as before. As stated in the **Saravali**<note>A classic 8th-century astrological treatise by Kalyanavarman</note>:

> "Multiply the minutes of the Ascendant's Navamsha by the longevity of each planet. Divide by the minutes of a circle (21,600); the resulting years etc. should be subtracted from one's own life. If a malefic is in the Ascendant but aspected by a benefic, subtract only half." (1)

This indeed appears correct to us.

---

(1) By this statement from the *Saravali*, when a malefic is in the Ascendant:
$\frac{\text{Ascendant Navamsha minutes} \times \text{Planet's longevity}}{21600}$
This amount should be subtracted from the planetary longevity measures. Now, to find the minutes of the Ascendant's Navamsha, the proportion is: if one Navamsha contains two hundred minutes, then how many are in the Navamshas elapsed by the Ascendant?
The resulting Ascendant Navamsha minutes = $\frac{200 \times \text{Ascendant Navamshas}}{1}$
Substituting this into the previous formula (1), the amount to be subtracted is:
$\frac{200 \times \text{Ascendant Navamshas} \times \text{Planet's longevity}}{21600} = \frac{\text{Ascendant Navamshas} \times \text{Planet's longevity}}{108}$
By this, the previous statement about "multiplying by risen Navamshas and dividing by 108" is entirely proven.

This rule applies not only here but also in the case of the "falling in the wheel" <note>original: *Chakra-pata*; a specific astronomical reduction</note>. Subtract the position of the planet from the Ascendant; if the remainder is less than six signs, then that planet is subject to the wheel-reduction, otherwise not. By that remainder, divide the total lifespan portion and subtract the quotient from the total lifespan as previously described; thus, the lifespan is purified by the wheel. Now, if the divisor is less than one, subtract the divisor from one, multiply the lifespan by the remainder, and divide by one; the result is the lifespan purified by the wheel-reduction.

As it is said: "If the Ascendant minus the planet is less than six signs, that is the divisor. Divide the lifespan by it and subtract the resulting years. If the divisor is less than one, multiply by the difference from one and divide by one; then the lifespan becomes accurate." When this calculation is performed and both a malefic and a benefic planet are in the Ascendant, only the one closest to the rising degree of the Ascendant should be considered, not the other. Here, the word "cruel" <note>malefic</note> does not include the waning Moon. Thus says Badarayana: "If the Sun, Mars, or Saturn are in the Ascendant, a loss occurs. By this method, if a benefic aspects <note>looks upon</note> them, only half of the calculated loss should be subtracted." ||4||

**Vernacular Translation**—If malefic planets are in the Ascendant, multiply the total calculated lifespan by the number of elapsed <term>Navamshas</term> <note>a 1/9th division of a zodiac sign, equal to 3 degrees and 20 minutes</note> including the currently rising (partially elapsed) Navamsha. Divide this by 108; the resulting years and months represent the "destruction" or loss, which must be subtracted from the total calculated lifespan. If the malefic planet in the Ascendant is aspected by a benefic planet, then only half of the loss calculated by the above method is subtracted. ||4||

**Special Meaning**—Here, the term "partially risen" <note>original: *ardhodita*</note> refers to a Navamsha that has not fully risen—that is, the specific minutes of the current Navamsha that have appeared above the horizon. Adding this to the number of fully elapsed Navamshas of the Ascendant gives the total risen portion. Some calculate this by converting the entire longitudinal position of the Ascendant into minutes and dividing by 200 to find the Navamsha count and remainder. Others ignore the sign and convert only the degrees and minutes into minutes, dividing by 200 to find the count.

The number of years obtained by multiplying the life by the Navamsha count and dividing by 108 is the same as multiplying the life by the minutes of the Ascendant and dividing by 21,600 (the total minutes in the zodiac circle). Therefore, in the *Saravali* <note>a classic 8th-century astrological text by Kalyanavarman</note>, it is written: "Multiply the lifespan of each planet by the minutes of the Ascendant's Navamsha and divide by the minutes of the circle; subtract the result from the lifespan if a malefic is in the Ascendant. If aspected by a benefic, subtract half."

If a malefic is in the Ascendant, the loss of lifespan is proportional to the elapsed portion of the Ascendant. That is, if the Ascendant is at the very beginning of the first Navamsha, the loss of life...

### Now, he describes the maximum lifespan of humans and other beings in the Shikharini meter:

> **Sixty years doubled and five nights for humans and elephants;**
> **Thirty-two for horses; for donkeys and camels, the square of five.**
> **One less than that is the life of bulls and buffaloes; twelve for dogs**
> **Is remembered; and for goats and the like, six added to ten is the maximum. || 5 ||**

"Sixty years doubled" and so on. By the word *sama*, a year is meant. Sixty years doubled becomes one hundred and twenty years. Thus, one hundred and twenty years and "five nights"—meaning five full days—is the maximum lifespan for *manuja* (humans) and *karin* (elephants). For *haya* (horses), thirty-two years is the maximum lifespan. *Khara* is a donkey; *karabha* is a camel; for these two, the "square of five"—the square of five being twenty-five—is the maximum lifespan. "One less than that is the life": that square of five minus one is twenty-four years, which is the maximum lifespan for *vrishabha* (bulls) and *mahisha* (buffaloes). This refers to cattle and buffaloes. For *shuna* (dogs), twelve years is the maximum lifespan. The mention of "dog" is an <term>upalakshana</term> <note>a technical term for a synecdoche or a representative illustration</note> for all clawed animals; therefore, this same lifespan is remembered for lions, cats, and similar creatures. "For goats and the like," six added to ten is sixteen years, the maximum lifespan. By the phrase "and the like," deer and similar animals are included. "Maximum" is the limit for all these.

What is the purpose of knowing this maximum lifespan? It is to determine the specific lifespan of horses and other animals at their birth. It is done as follows: Having calculated the lifespan of a newborn horse or other animal in the same manner as one would for a human, a <term>trairashika</term> <note>the "Rule of Three" or mathematical proportion</note> should be applied. If the human maximum lifespan of one hundred and twenty years and five days corresponds to the calculated proportion, then what would it be for a horse whose maximum lifespan is thirty-two years? The lifespan of the horse born at that time should be declared based on this result. In this way, for all the mentioned living beings, one should calculate the proportion using their respective maximum lifespans to determine the specific life expectancy at the time of birth.

Others say this: No one lives longer than the stated maximum lifespan. That is appropriate. However, since lifespans exceeding one hundred and twenty years can occur through mathematical calculations, one must understand that the purpose of stating these maximum lifespans is specifically for the application of the Rule of Three. || 5 ||

**Vernacular Translation—** 120 years and 5 full days is stated as the maximum lifespan for Indian humans and elephants. 32 years for horses; 25 years for donkeys and camels; 24 years for cows and buffaloes; 12 years for dogs; and 16 years for goats, sheep, deer, etc., is stated as the maximum lifespan. This is the average standard. || 5 ||

**Special Note—** The purpose of stating the lifespans of all these animals here is that kings and emperors keep domestic animals; from the time of their birth...

If a birth chart is prepared to determine the auspicious and inauspicious results and the lifespan of an animal, one should first calculate their lifespan in the same manner as prescribed for humans. Then, apply the rule of three <note>A mathematical proportion (Trairashika)</note>: if a human's maximum lifespan (120 years) yields this calculated lifespan, then what would the maximum lifespan of the desired animal yield? Thus, by multiplying the mathematically derived lifespan by the animal's specific maximum lifespan and dividing by 120, the resulting years, months, etc., constitute the clear <term>Spashta: the mathematically corrected or "true" value</term> lifespan of that animal.

**Example:** Suppose a horse is born at the same time as the previous example. The lifespan calculated by the aforementioned method was 71 years, 6 months, 10 days, 17 minutes, and 46 seconds. Multiply this by the horse's maximum lifespan of 32 years and divide the product by 120. The resulting 19 years, 0 months, 26 days, 44 minutes, and 43 seconds is the clear lifespan of that horse. The maximum lifespan limits stated here for humans and others do not mean that they cannot live longer. Here, the mathematically derived lifespans based on planetary positions approach 120, and in India, people generally do not live much longer than that. Therefore, the teachers have stated the maximum lifespan based on an average mathematical value. This is because, due to specific planetary combinations <note>Yogas</note> and the merit or demerit of the individual's past actions, the lifespan can be more or less than the mathematically derived value. The teacher himself says later: *“In this world, lifespan can be unlimited if not following the regular order.”* <note>original: "अमितमिहायुरनुक्रमाद् विना स्यात्"</note> Alternatively, in Tibet, many people live up to 240 years. Thus, 120 years is stated as the average between 0 and 240 years. ॥5॥

*Now, using the Pushpitagra meter, he describes the planetary combination under which a person attains the maximum lifespan:*

"In the final degree of Pisces" <note>original: "अनिमिषपरमांशक" (Animisha-paramansha)</note> means: Pisces is the "motionless fish" (Animisha); its final degree is the ninth Navamsha <note>A 3°20' subdivision of a sign</note>. # Page 157
## Commentary by Bhattotpala with Hindi Translation

The maximum lifespan is shown to be one hundred and twenty (120) years, 1 month, and 17 days. It is possible for a lifespan to exceed this stated measure. Therefore, the recitation of the maximum lifespan standards is explained solely for the purpose of the **Rule of Three** <note>original: "Trairashika"; a mathematical proportion used to calculate values between two known points</note>. Others, however, explain this specific combination when the ascendant <note>the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> is in the final portion of the sign of Pisces. For example, if the ascendant is in the sign of Pisces and has reached the **best division** <note>original: "Vargottama"; a state where a planet or point occupies the same sign in both the main chart and the ninth-part harmonic chart, increasing its strength</note>, and Mercury, situated in Taurus, has covered twenty-five minutes of arc, and all other planets are in their signs of exaltation—even without reaching their exact highest degree—then by the power of this planetary combination, the person born lives for the full measure of the maximum lifespan.

Now, it is asked: if the constant for Mercury’s deepest debilitation was previously shown as 1 sign, 1 degree, and 4 minutes, why is a different value shown now during the calculation process? The answer is given: after passing fourteen degrees, when the fifteenth degree is reached, it is situated in the deepest point of debilitation. Therefore, fourteen degrees are shown for the planet in deepest debilitation. The lifespan shown for a planet at that point is the minimum; thus, until the fifteenth degree has been traversed by Mercury, the **Rule of Three** calculation should not be performed. This is why fifteen degrees are shown at the time of calculation. This principle of showing the traversed degrees at the time of the Rule of Three must be applied to all planets. For the purpose of these proportions, the constants for exaltation and the constants for deepest debilitation must be used to perform the work. (6)

**Vernacular Language:** If the final portion of Pisces is the ascendant, and Mercury is at 25 minutes in the sign of Taurus, and all other planets are in their respective highest exaltations, then the measure of the maximum lifespan is determined by the mathematical method mentioned above.

What about the value 8070? In this manner, by multiplying the difference of Mercury's exaltation (8675) by 6 and dividing by 10800, the resulting years etc. are 4 years, 5 months, and 25 days. Subtracting this from Mercury's stated maximum exaltation lifespan of 12 years, Mercury's <term>Spashtayu</term><note>Corrected or calculated lifespan</note> is 7 years, 6 months, and 5 days. Mars is in its exaltation, but because it falls in the eleventh house, half of its 15-year exaltation lifespan is taken, resulting in 7 years and 6 months as the <term>Spashtayu</term> of Mars. Similarly, Saturn is in the seventh house; therefore, by reducing its exaltation lifespan by one-fifth, Saturn's <term>Spashtayu</term> is 16 years. Since all other planets are in their exaltation, their stated lifespans are respectively: Sun 19, Moon 25, Jupiter 15, and Venus 21 years. Thus, the sum of all is 120 years and 5 days.

In this configuration, if the Sun is in its exaltation <note>Aries</note>, Mercury can never be in its own exaltation <note>Virgo</note> <note>Astronomically, Mercury stays close to the Sun and cannot be several signs away</note>. If Mercury were in its exaltation, the Sun and Venus could never be in theirs. Therefore, to achieve the maximum lifespan for the <term>Lagna</term><note>Ascendant/Rising sign</note>, the final degree of Pisces is imagined as the Lagna. Furthermore, when the Sun is at its highest exaltation (10 degrees in Aries), Mercury can reach at most 4 degrees of Taurus, being near its exaltation. This is because if the Sun's maximum equation is negative and Mercury's is positive, Mercury will be 24 degrees ahead of the Sun. Thus, if the Sun is at maximum exaltation, Mercury's lifespan could occasionally be 7 years, 7 months, and 18 days—which is 1 month and 13 days more than the previously calculated age. In this way, the mathematically derived lifespan reaches 120 years, 1 month, and 18 days. However, the <term>Arsha</term><note>Sage-given or traditional</note> standard for maximum lifespan is 120 years and 5 days. This is proven only by assuming Mercury to be at 25 minutes of Taurus.

->Now, to point out the flaws in this theory of maximum longevity held by others, he speaks in the Shalini meter:<-

Regarding "Longevity" (Ayurdayam): This system of longevity was not only stated by Maya, Yavana, Manittha, and Shakti, but also by Vishnugupta—another name for Chanakya. The teacher Devasvami and Siddhasena did the same. As Vishnugupta says: "When all planets are in their highest exaltation, the Moon is in the portion of Pisces, and Mercury is in Taurus, the person born attains the maximum lifespan." So also Devasvami: "With the Sun and others in exaltation, the Lagna in the portion of Pisces, and Mercury in Taurus, the newborn reaches maximum life." And Siddhasena: "With the Lagna in the highest degree of Pisces, Mercury at five degrees in Taurus, and all others in their highest exaltation, one reaches maximum life." If so many teachers have said this, what is the flaw? The system of longevity shown in the opinion of Sage Satyacharya is the opinion of many teachers. As Varahamihira pledges: "Astrology is a revealed science; it is not proper for us to create our own alternatives when there is a dispute; rather, I shall state the opinions of many." Let the contradictions of this "other" theory be set aside for a moment. There is the flaw of potential dispute, as noted in "the flaw in their method," etc.

In the opinion of these teachers, an error arises. What kind of error? He explains: "Eight years of misfortune," and so on. Thus, after eight years there is no "misfortune," and before twenty years, according to their math, no one should die. Yet, we see people dying in that interval; this is their visible error. || 7 ||

**Vernacular—** In this same manner (as described by Maya, Yavana, etc.), the teachers Vishnugupta, Devasvami, and Siddhasena have also calculated the lifespan <term>Ayurdaya: the science of determining the length of life</term>. However, there is a visible error in their opinion because the lifespan calculated this way never falls below 20 years. Yet, even excluding the eight years of childhood misfortune <term>Balarishta: planetary combinations causing early death</term>, people are observed dying before the age of 20. || 7 ||

**Special Note—** The Author <note>Varahamihira</note> points out the flaw here: if all planets are at their highest points (exaltation) and Mercury is at its maximum distance from the Sun, the maximum lifespan is 120 years and 5 days. Conversely, if we imagine Mercury at 25 minutes of Scorpio, the Ascendant at the first degree, and all other planets in their lowest points (debilitation), the calculated lifespan still does not fall below 20 years. Therefore, theoretically, no one should die before age 20. If one argues, "They die due to a misfortune yoga <note>a specific planetary alignment</note>," that is also incorrect, because childhood misfortunes are only said to last until age 8. Many die between the ages of 8 and 20. This is a visible contradiction.

Bhattotpala writes in his commentary: "This verse is inconsistent," which suggests this might not be an original verse by Varahamihira, but an interpolation by someone else. This is because, using the aforementioned methods, values of less than 20 years can indeed be produced. For example: Ascendant at 10s 0° 1'; Sun at 0s 10°; Moon at 1s 3°; Venus at 11s 27°; Mercury at 11s 15° 0'; Jupiter at 6s 50°; Saturn at 0s 20° 0'; Mars at 10s 28° 0'. Here, because the degrees of the Ascendant are zero, the years contributed by the Ascendant are 0. The lifespans for planets in exaltation and debilitation are already established. For Mars...

# Chapter on Longevity in the Brihat Jataka
->Page 160<-

To determine the lifespan, we calculate the difference for Mars at its highest point of exaltation (6 signs, 28 degrees). By multiplying the 1800 minutes of one sign by 60 months and dividing by 10800, we obtain 15 months, which is 1 year and 3 months. Subtracting this from the 15 years assigned to Mars at its maximum exaltation results in 13 years and 6 months; this is the calculated lifespan contributed by Mars. Because Jupiter is "situated in its sign of debilitation," its lifespan contribution is 7 years and 6 months. However, because it falls in the twelfth house, according to the rule "from the house of loss for malefic planets in reverse order, and for benefics in direct order" <note>original: "व्ययभवनादसत्सु वामं सत्स्वध" — a rule for reducing lifespan based on planetary placement in the houses</note>, the reduction via the "half-circle reduction" <term>Chakrardhapata: a specific astrological calculation where lifespan is halved or reduced based on a planet's position in the visible or invisible hemisphere</term> results in a lifespan of 3 years and 6 months. 

Furthermore, the contributions are: Sun 16 years, Moon 25 years, Mercury 6 years, Venus 21 years, and Saturn 10 years. The total sum is 68 years and 6 months. Then, because a malefic (Mars) is in the Ascendant, we take the "elapsed portions" <term>Navamsha: a 1/9th division of a zodiac sign</term> of the Ascendant. Using the 61st Navamsha (the partially risen portion of the current Aquarius sign), we multiply the total lifespan. This results in 8663 years and 6 months. Dividing this by 108, we obtain 82 years, 11 months, 28 days, and 20 minutes. Subtracting this from the total lifespan leaves a final calculated lifespan of 15 years, 6 months, 1 day, and 40 minutes. This result is clearly more than eight and less than twenty. Therefore, the statement "longevity does not fall below twenty" <note>original: "नायुर्विंशते स्यादधस्तात्"</note> is proven incorrect. However, even with this inconsistency, it is also inconsistent to claim "this verse is not by Varahamihira at all," because errors can be made by any human being. ||7||

*Now, using the Shalini meter, he describes another flaw in the longevity theories of those same ancient teachers—*

> **In the same yoga where full longevity is predicted, others have proclaimed the status of a universal emperor.**
> **This is a visible flaw among them; furthermore, many live a full life even without wealth.** ||8||

"In the same yoga" etc. — In the yoga where the Ascendant is in the last portion of Pisces, a full lifespan of 120 years and 5 days is predicted. In that same yoga, six planets are at their highest exaltation. Other teachers have stated that with six planets in exaltation, one becomes a "Universal Emperor" <term>Chakravarti: a supreme world ruler</term>. As Badarayana says: "With six planets, one becomes a Chakravarti and rules the entire three worlds." And Yavaneshwara says: "One possesses the power of a king of kings, with great prosperity, strength, and honor." 

In that context, as long as there are not six planets in exaltation, one does not attain the maximum lifespan. But when they are in exaltation, the person born must be a Universal Emperor. Thus, regarding full life: many men live to 120 years without any wealth or riches. Therefore, this is another flaw in their theories. It appears that these two Shalini verses, being disconnected from the context, might not be the work of Varahamihira himself. 

Regarding the flaw mentioned in the first Shalini verse, its irrelevance is explained thus: According to the rule "multiplied by the partially risen Navamsha from the whole," the reduction of life caused by a malefic in the Ascendant cannot be fixed to a specific amount because it varies with every degree of every Ascendant. Therefore, there is no fixed limit to the remaining life after that reduction. Thus, the statement "longevity does not fall below twenty" is indeed improper.

Here is an example. Suppose at the rise of the first division of the sign Aquarius <note>Kumbha</note>, the Sun, Moon, and Venus are at their highest exaltation; Mercury, Jupiter, and Saturn are at their lowest debilitation. Mars, having traveled through 28 degrees of Aquarius, is stationed there. Then the positions of the planets at that moment, including the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note>, are as follows: (1) In this case, since the Ascendant has not progressed through any portion of the sign, there is no "Ascendant Longevity" <term>Lagnayurdaya: longevity contributed specifically by the rising sign's degree</term>. For those planets at their highest exaltation, the value is already known. For Mars, the calculation is made from its current position: 10 signs and 28 degrees. The fixed point for the highest exaltation of Mars is 6 signs and 28 degrees. Subtracting these results in 10 signs. This is converted into minutes of arc: 1800.

Now, the Rule of Three <term>Trairashika: a mathematical proportion method</term> is applied: If for half a revolution (10,800 minutes), the months for Mars at its lowest point are ninety (90), then for these minutes, how many would there be? The result is 15 months. This makes 1 year and 3 months. Subtracting this from the 15 years assigned to Mars at its highest exaltation, the result is 13 years and 6 months. This is the longevity contribution of Mars. Because Jupiter is in the twelfth house from the Ascendant, its contribution is reduced by half due to its position in the cycle, resulting in 3 years and 6 months for Jupiter. For those at highest exaltation or lowest debilitation, even if in an enemy's sign, the one-third reduction is not applied; nor is the half-reduction for combust planets <note>planets too close to the sun</note>. This is because, in the yoga <note>astrological combination</note> mentioned as "the highest degree of the Fish," if one-third were subtracted for the Moon being in Taurus, the full lifespan would not be achieved, which contradicts the opinions of other teachers. Temporary friendship and enmity are described thus:
> "The planets situated in the 2nd, 9th, 4th, 5th, and 12th houses from the Root Trine <term>Mulatrikona: a planet's preferred sign</term> are temporary friends. Also, a planet is a friend to one in whose exaltation sign it possesses great strength. Those placed in the 7th, 6th, 8th, or in the same sign as the planet, or in the 1st, 3rd, or 11th, become temporary enemies. I shall now explain these friends and enemies."

By this rule, Venus and the Moon are not temporary friends. Therefore, when Venus is in Pisces and the Moon is in Taurus, the Moon is in an enemy's house. If one-third were subtracted because it is in an enemy's field, then in the combination "highest degree of the Fish," the full lifespan would not be attained. The Teacher has demonstrated this through "grabbing the horns" <term>Shringagrahika: a logical method of direct, explicit demonstration</term>. By this, he indicates: for those at highest exaltation or lowest debilitation, the one-third reduction for enemy signs and the half-reduction for combustion are not applied. Thus, the individual years of longevity for the planets are written as shown: Sun 66 years; Moon 25 years; Mars 13 years and 6 months; Mercury 6 years; Jupiter 3 years and 6 months; Venus 21 years; Saturn 10 years. Since the Ascendant has not progressed, there is no Ascendant longevity. The sum of these is 68 years and 6 months. Now, because Mars is in the Ascendant, the "half-risen" calculation is performed. There, in the Aquarius Ascendant—

### Commentary by Bhattotpala on the Bhashya

The lifespan of Mercury was already halved previously. Thus, if the lifespan does not fall below forty-two years, then the claim that it falls below twenty is inconsistent. On this point, others say: those born when the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note> is devoid of cruel planets are seen to die after eight years but before twenty; therefore, the opinions of other teachers are inconsistent. 

To this, it is replied: Having considered the opinions of other teachers in their proper sequence, they say that the very same teachers who demonstrated the calculation of lifespan by this method also described these "Death Combinations" <note>Mrityu-yoga: specific planetary alignments predicting death</note>. That is written here. 

As **Badarayana** says:
> "If a malefic planet is situated in the sixth or eighth house, occupies a malefic sign, and is aspected by an enemy, it brings about the death of the creature during its own sub-period <note>Antardasha</note>, especially if it has been defeated in planetary war by others."

And as **Yavanesvara** <note>The "Lord of the Greeks," an influential figure in early Indian astrology</note> says:
> "A malefic in the sixth or eighth house, fierce and aspected by malefics even if in a friendly sign, causes death in its sub-period through traps, bonds, or exhaustion on the road."

And in the **Saravali**:
> "When a malefic enters a sub-period during a major malefic period, there is doubt regarding the life of men, for the planetary enmity is then great. When the sub-period of Mars occurs during the major period of Saturn, death is certain even for those destined for long life. A malefic in a cruel sign, or in the sixth or eighth house, aspected by the lord of that house, gives death in its own ripening <note>Paka: the period when a planet's influence bears fruit</note>. The teacher Satyacharya declares that the enemy of the Lord of the Ascendant, when entering the sub-period of the Ascendant, causes sudden death."

Thus, for those born when the Ascendant is devoid of cruel planets, death is indeed possible after eight years and before the time shown. They should be understood to have died due to these "Death Combinations." There is a rule as to when the sub-period related to the indicated planet occurs. Therefore, according to the opinion of other teachers, death is possible after eight years and before the indicated time; thus, the first criticism is inconsistent. 

Now, the inconsistency of the second criticism is addressed. Here, long life is possible even without the "Emperor Combination" <note>Chakravarti-yoga: a rare alignment indicating a world-ruler</note>. 

Here is an example: where the temporary planets and the Ascendant are as follows—the Sun is in Taurus having traveled ten degrees; the Moon is in Gemini at three degrees; Mars is in Aquarius at twenty-eight degrees; Mercury is in Aries at fifteen degrees; Jupiter is in Leo at five degrees; Venus is in Aries at twenty-seven degrees and one-third; Saturn is in Aquarius at twenty years <note>likely degrees</note>; and the Ascendant is in the final portion of Sagittarius. 

In such a case, the years of lifespan for the planets obtained by the previously demonstrated calculations are written: 17 years and 5 months for the Sun; 22 years and 11 months for the Moon; 13 years and 6 months for Mars; 7 years and...

Regarding the Sun: Jupiter is its friend, but otherwise it is different. Venus is an enemy, and it is situated in the ninth house from Leo, which is the Sun's "Moolatrikona" <note>a primary favorable sign</note>. Therefore, it does not become a temporary friend. Because it is situated in Taurus, which is a neutral sign for the Sun, its contribution to longevity does not decrease at all. The Moon is situated in Gemini, a friendly sign. Its years of longevity remain exactly as shown, because it is said:

> "One should know Mercury and Jupiter to be friends of the Moon." <note>original: ‘इन्दोर्बुधं देवगुरुं च विद्यात्’</note>

Mars <note>Angaraka</note> is situated in Aquarius, an enemy sign. Because it is said:

> "Venus and Mercury are the friends of Mars." <note>original: ‘भौमस्य शुक्रः शशिजश्च मित्रम्’</note>

The rest are enemies. Since Saturn is the remaining one, it is an enemy; and because they are placed in the same house, Saturn becomes a "Great Enemy" <note>Adhi-shatru</note>. However, even though Mars is in an enemy sign, there is no reduction. Because it is said:

> "Except for a planet in retrograde motion, one-third is lost when in an enemy's house." <note>original: ‘हित्वा वक्रं रिपुगृहगतैर्हीयते स्वत्रिभाग’</note>

Therefore, the longevity for Mars remains exactly as calculated.

According to the statement "Except for the Sun, the children of the Moon..." <note>original: ‘चान्द्रेरनर्का’</note>, Mars is a friend of Mercury. Therefore, because it is situated in Aries, the longevity for Mercury remains as calculated. For Jupiter, the Sun is a friend. Because it is said:

> "For Jupiter, excluding Mars, all are..." <note>original: ‘गुरोश्च भौमं परि-हृत्य सर्वे’</note>

Therefore, for Jupiter situated in Leo, the longevity remains as calculated. For Venus in Aries, it is in a friendly sign. Because it is said:

> "For the son of Bhrigu (Venus), friends are declared to be all except the Sun and Moon." <note>original: ‘भृगुनन्दनस्य त्वर्केन्दुवर्ज्याः सुहृदः प्रदिष्टाः ।’</note>

Therefore, its longevity also remains as calculated. For Saturn, because it is situated in its own sign in Aquarius, its longevity remains as calculated. For the Ascendant, since it is free from the movement of the nodes <note>Patachara</note>, its longevity remains as calculated. Thus, the years of longevity are written separately:

| Planet | Years | Months | Days | Ghatikas |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Sun | 17 | 5 | 0 | 0 |
| Moon | 16 | 1 | 5 | 0 |
| Mars | 13 | 6 | 0 | 0 |
| Mercury | 7 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Jupiter | 12 | 0 | 11 | 15 |
| Venus | 16 | 2 | 26 | 30 |
| Saturn | 13 | 4 | 0 | 0 |
| Ascendant | 6 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

In such a combination <note>Yoga</note>, a lifespan of even more than one hundred and ten years is possible. The total comes to 110 years, 0 months, 2 days, and 45 ghatikas. It can even reach 113 years and 11 months. When the Moon's years are 22 and months are 6, then the sum of all is 114 years, 8 months, 7 days, and 45 ghatikas. In such a combination, a lifespan of even one hundred and fourteen years is possible. This specific combination is called **Kemadruma**. As it will be said:

> "Leaving aside the Sun, the Sunapha, Anapha, and Dhurdhura yogas are formed by planets in the houses adjacent to the Moon; otherwise, many say it is Kemadruma." <note>original: ‘हित्वाऽर्कं सुनफानफादुरुधरा...’</note>

Therefore, one born in such a combination attains a long life. However, due to the nature of the **Kemadruma** yoga, the person becomes poor. As it will be said:

> "In Kemadruma, people are filthy, sorrowful, low-minded, and penniless; they are servants and wicked, even if born in a royal lineage." <note>original: ‘केमद्रुमे मलिनदुःखितनीचनिःस्वाः...’</note>

Only the poor are seen to have such long lives. No one has truly mastered the measure of a poor man's lifespan.
