# Chapter on Ashtakavarga in the Brihat Jataka
<page-num>230</page-num>

...From Jupiter in the 3rd, 6th, 11th, 4th, 1st, and 10th. From Mercury in the 5th, 6th, 12th, and 11th. From the Sun in the 12th, 11th, 6th, 10th, 9th, and 8th." This is the *Ashtakavarga* <note>A system of points used to predict the effects of planets based on their positions relative to eight points: the seven planets and the Ascendant.</note> of Saturn. || 7 ||

**Vernacular Commentary**—Saturn is auspicious in the 3rd, 5th, 11th, and 6th positions from its own occupied position. From Mars, it is auspicious in the 3rd, 5th, 11th, 6th, 10th, and 12th. From the Sun, in the 1st, 4th, 7th, 10th, 11th, 8th, and 12th. From the Ascendant <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the time of birth.</note>, in the 3rd, 6th, 10th, 11th, 9th, and 4th. From Mercury, in the 6th, 11th, 6th, 10th, 12th, and 8th. From the Moon, in the 3rd, 6th, and 11th. From Venus, in the 6th, 11th, and 12th. And from Jupiter, Saturn is auspicious in the 11th, 12th, 5th, and 6th positions. In the remaining positions, it is a giver of inauspicious results. || 7 ||

---

->Now, to describe the results of the Ashtakavarga, he speaks in the Malini meter:<-

->**Thus, what has been declared is favorable; the rest is unfavorable. Specifically,**<-
->**they bestow the ripening of greater results from the birth sign.**<-
->**Strength and favor are found in the houses of increase, or when in exaltation;**<-
->**but prosperity is not found in the houses of decrease, or when in fall or enemy signs. || 8 ||**<-

->Thus ends the Ninth Chapter, the Chapter on Ashtakavarga, in the Brihat Jataka composed by the Great Teacher Varahamihira. || 9 ||<-

"Thus, what has been declared..." etc. By the method stated here, that which has been declared is favorable (*ishta*), and the other is unfavorable (*anishta*). Whatever has not been mentioned is entirely inauspicious. This is what is meant: the positions mentioned in the text (such as "from the Sun in the first, eleventh, fourth, and eighth") are the best in terms of results. Specifically, the "ripening of greater results" is desired after calculating the difference between favorable and unfavorable effects. These results manifest from the "birth sign" (*janmabhat*), meaning the positions where the planets were situated at the time of birth; they do not manifest in the same way from the signs occupied by the planets at the current time <note>This distinguishes between the natal chart (static) and transits (moving).</note>.

This is what is being said: the favorable positions recited by the Teacher should be marked with <term>bindus</term> <note>Literally "dots" or "drops," representing positive units of energy.</note>. The unfavorable positions should be marked with <term>rekhas</term> <note>Literally "lines," representing negative units or gaps.</note>. By finding the difference between the favorable and unfavorable, the remaining result is determined. Where eight <term>bindus</term> are accumulated, the auspicious result is complete. Where there are six <term>bindus</term>, the result is <term>three-quarters</term>. Where there are <term>four bindus</term>, the result is half. Where there are two <term>bindus</term>, the result is one-quarter. The same calculation for inauspicious results should be made using the <term>rekhas</term>.

In the application of this, such as in the case of Mars's *Ashtakavarga* for a birth occurring in the first portion of the sign of the Fish (Pisces), the positions recited by the Teacher should be marked with dots. The unmentioned, inauspicious positions should be marked with lines. For example, the planetary arrangement: Venus is <term>situated in the Pisces Ascendant</term>...

From Saturn, it is in the ninth, eighth, and the center; from Mercury, in the sixth, third, fifth, and eleventh; from Venus, in the sixth, twelfth, eleventh, and eighth; and from Jupiter, in the tenth, twelfth, eleventh, and sixth.'

# The Chapter on Ashtakavarga in Brihat Jataka

In Sagittarius, six lines and two dots were produced. There, by subtracting two dots from two lines, four lines remain. Thus, with four out of eight parts, Mars in Sagittarius is always inauspicious. <note>In this system, "lines" (Rekhas) usually represent auspicious points and "dots" (Bindus) represent inauspicious ones, though some traditions swap these terms. The text here treats the remainder as the determining factor for the planet's influence.</note> In Capricorn, three lines and five dots were produced. By subtracting three lines from three dots, two dots remain. Therefore, Mars in Capricorn is auspicious by two out of eight parts. In Aquarius, four lines and three dots were produced. Here, because the tenth house from the Moon's position is neutral for Mars, the eighth dot was not produced; therefore, by subtracting three lines from three dots, one line remains. Thus, Mars in Aquarius is inauspicious by one out of eight parts. In Pisces, five lines and three dots were produced. By subtracting three lines from three dots, two lines remain. Therefore, Mars in Pisces is inauspicious by two out of eight parts.

These are established for purification. Thus, by combining the auspicious and inauspicious results, eight outcomes are formed; after performing their correction <note>Sodhana</note>, whatever remains should be declared as the prediction. Where there are four lines and four dots, the planet is neutral or middling. Where there are eight lines, it is exceedingly inauspicious. Where there are eight dots, it is exceedingly auspicious. In this manner, the <term>Ashtakavarga</term> <note>A system of point-counting to determine planetary strength</note> of all planets should be calculated according to the zodiac signs occupied at the time of birth. As stated by <term>Badarayana</term> <note>An ancient sage and authority on astrology</note>:

> "That which is auspicious by one part becomes a giver of sin (misfortune) in six places. That which is not desired by four parts—the calculation of all results follows this logic."

Now, it was previously stated:

> "When there is a conflict between two equal results of a single planet, one should declare their destruction; whatever is in excess is what comes to fruition."

It is said that "the desired is stated, and the undesired is otherwise due to distinction"—this is a repetition. Regarding what was said—that in the absence of the <term>Ashtakavarga</term> <note>The Eight-fold system</note>, equal opposing results of a single planet cancel each other out—one must understand that destruction occurs when results are equal. For example: if the same planet by one logic grants gold, but by another logic steals gold, then it neither grants gold nor steals it. "Whatever is in excess comes to fruition"—even there, if by two reasons it steals gold and by one reason it grants gold, it will still be a stealer of gold, not a giver. Conversely, if by two reasons it gives gold and by one reason it steals gold, then because of the majority of two reasons, it remains a giver of gold. Thus, one should declare destruction when results are equal, but not when they are unequal. Here, even when results are equal, their conflict leads to destruction. This is how it is described in the Ashtakavarga by <term>Badarayana</term>, <term>Yavanesvara</term> <note>The "Lord of the Greeks," a title for authorities who integrated Greco-Egyptian astrology into Indian systems</note>, and others. A planet situated in its own place relative to the position of another planet gives these auspicious or inauspicious results. Even if those results are dissimilar, one should declare their destruction based on the conflict between the auspicious and inauspicious. Specifically, they give the ripening of the excess result from the birth sign. For instance, if a planet for some reason is a giver of gold...

# Page 233
## Commentary by Bhattotpala with Hindi Translation

-> In another case, one might be a thief of silver <note>original: "rupyapahari"</note>; even so, when two results are dissimilar and contradictory—such as giving and taking—one should conclude that the result is neither purely auspicious nor purely inauspicious. Thus, across the eight positions, if a planet is auspicious in many places and inauspicious in a few, one should weigh the specific auspicious and inauspicious fruits and conclude a single auspicious result. In this manner, only the auspiciousness or inauspiciousness of the positions is stated by the designation of the place; there is no separate instruction of results as seen in the works of Yavanesvara and others. If the Ashtakavarga is indeed primary, why did Varahamihira provide separate instructions for results based on the Moon's position in the Samhita's section on transits? For example, "The Sun in the birth sign causes fatigue," and so on. To this, it is said: whatever remains after the specific calculations of the Ashtakavarga results is what should be declared. For the sake of conviction, because the transit system is so well-known, the opinions of others were accepted and stated first. As he himself said in the *Yatra* <note>A work on journeys/military expeditions</note>: <-

> "For one who accepts the authority of transit results, the result of 'obstruction' <term>Vedha: a concept where one planet's position cancels another's transit effect</term> is desired or not. Generally, this is not widely accepted, for the transit provides results through a broad path."

Even Yavanesvara, after giving separate instructions for results, accepted that very Ashtakavarga. His statement is as follows:

> "In the Ashtakavarga of results, when the marks for auspicious and inauspicious are equal, they are declared to be without fruit. Whichever is greater, its result should be determined for the performance of journeys and for births."

Badarayana also, after giving separate instructions for results, speaks of the Ashtakavarga:

> "If the painful and the excellent results are equal in number, then the destruction of both results should be declared (1). Whichever of the two is in excess should be declared; this calculation is prescribed for every position."

It is said that a planet is strengthened and desirable when in Upachaya houses <note>Houses of growth: 3, 6, 10, and 11</note>, in a friend's sign, or in its sign of exaltation. Those houses which are Upachaya from the Ascendant or the Moon, as well as friendly signs and the sign of exaltation—these are auspicious signs and indicators of auspicious places. By implication, one's own sign and the *Mulatrikona* <note>A specific favorable zone within a sign, second only to exaltation</note> are also included. There, a planet situated in an Upachaya house from the Ascendant or the Moon, or in its own sign or Mulatrikona, gives auspicious results. On this, Shri Devakirti says:

> "A planet situated in an Upachaya from the Ascendant or the Moon, or in its own house, Mulatrikona, or exaltation, or in a friend's sign, gives exceedingly auspicious results."

Those houses which are [not] Upachaya from the Ascendant or the Moon, as well as enemy signs and signs of debilitation, are inauspicious. A planet situated in them, even when it gives auspicious results, gives them in a very degraded manner. Now, a planet in an auspicious house gives auspicious results, and in an inauspicious house, it gives little auspiciousness. Should the position of the planet at the time of birth be investigated in such places, or should the result be calculated according to its current transit? It is said: it is indeed the birth position. This is seen through internal observation. Thus says Devakirti:

> "At birth, in an Upachaya sign, in debilitation, or in an enemy's sign..."

# Chapter on the Ashtakavarga of the Brihat Jataka

<page-num>234</page-num>

...occurs at the proper time. But that planet which is excessively malefic shall give its fruit according to the time."
And **Yavaneshwara** <note>An early authority on Indian astrology, often associated with "Yavana" or Greek-influenced wisdom</note> says: "That planet which is in its sign of depression <term>Neecha: the point where a planet is weakest</term>, in an enemy's house, defeated, aspected by enemies, small in body, or discolored; even if it was the lord of the birth at the time of delivery, if it is strong in the birth chart, it is said to be fruitless when moving through the birth sign."
"One that is in a friend's house, in its sign of exaltation <term>Uccha: the point where a planet is strongest</term>, aspected by benefics, and strong in a friendly sign or an Upachaya house <note>Houses 3, 6, 10, and 11, which represent growth and improvement</note> at birth; such a planet, when residing in the birth sign, gives auspicious results, and even if it is a malefic, it does not give undesirable results."
So also says **Satya**: "A single planet in an Upachaya house at birth gives full results in the Upachaya signs. Those situated in non-Upachaya houses lead to the decrease of strength in places of suffering."
Regarding the time of fruition: any planet other than the Moon, if strong, gives full results, whether auspicious or inauspicious.
The Moon, even if naturally auspicious, becomes malefic in result if it lacks strength. On this, **Shri Devakirti** says: "A planet gives its fruit fully or weakly depending on whether it is powerful or lacking strength. Like all planets, the Moon is also a giver of misery if it is devoid of strength."
And **Satya** says: "One devoid of 'oil' <note>Sneha: refers to the essential vigor or planetary moisture</note>, body, or rays, and aspected by enemies in an enemy's sign; such a planet cannot give its fruit, and if the Moon is thus, it is miserable."
**Varahamihira** <note>The 6th-century author of this primary text</note> also speaks of weak planets being unable to give results during journeys:
"Planets in depression, defeated in planetary war, overcome, or without rays, are like snakes paralyzed by a mantra; they are incapable of performing actions in the Ascendant."
Regarding journeys, **Yavaneshwara** also says: "Planets situated in their own divisions are particularly strong and give results as specified. Those in depression, defeated, or in an enemy's house have little vigor; they destroy the manifestation of both desired and undesired fruits."
Therefore, in the scriptures, those statements which show the manifestation of good or bad results for planets in exaltation and so on, or bad results for those in depression or enemy signs, are to be understood as applying to the time of birth. And those results of benefics or malefics which show the fullness of fruit based on the planet's power are to be understood as applying to the planet at the time of its transit <term>Gochara: the current movement of planets across the zodiac</term>. || 8 ||

**Vernacular Explanation—** In this manner, for whichever planet certain places have been designated as auspicious, those places should be understood as good, and places other than those as inauspicious. In this way, in the birth chart <term>Janma-kundali</term>, one should mark the auspicious and inauspicious spots from where each planet is located. Whichever is greater—the auspicious or inauspicious marks—that is the result the planet gives when it passes through that place during its transit. If that place is an Upachaya house (3, 6, 10, 11) from the person's birth sign, or if it is the planet's house of exaltation, or a friend's house, then the auspicious results increase and the inauspicious results decrease. If, during the transit, it is in a house of depression or an enemy's house, one should understand that the inauspicious results increase and the auspicious results decrease.

### Example—Observe the Birth Chart. The Sun is in Aries, therefore "The Sun is pleasant," etc. <note>The author is referencing a specific mnemonic or rule-set starting with these words to determine planetary strength.</note>

---

| \ |||| 20000 / oooooo 1 2 || / |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| \ | | | / | |
| \ | 1 Ascendant, Sun, Moon, Mercury, Venus | / | | 12 |
| Mars | \ Saturn |||| oooo / | | |||||||| |
| ||| | \ / | | o |
| oooooo | \ 4 ||||| ooo / | 10 | |
| | \ / | |||||| oo | |
| | \ / | | |
| 5 ||| Zodiac | \ 7 ooooo ||| / | Jupiter 6 | |
| ooooo | \ / | |||| oooo | |
| \ | 6 |||| \ / 8 ||| / | |
| \ | oooo \ | / ooooo / | |

<note>This is a North Indian style birth chart. The numbers represent the zodiac signs (1=Aries, 4=Cancer, etc.). The circles (o) and lines (/) represent the Bindus and Rekhas used to calculate planetary strength.</note>

---

According to the verse, the 1st, 2nd, 4th, 7th, 8th, 9th, 10th, and 11th positions from the Sun are auspicious. Therefore, place an auspicious mark or "line" ( | ) in these positions and an inauspicious mark or "dot" ( 0 ) in the other positions. Next, from the Moon, place a line in the 3rd, 6th, 10th, and 11th positions, and a dot in the remaining positions. From Mars, place a line in the 1st, 2nd, 4th, 7th, 8th, 9th, 10th, and 11th positions, and a dot in the rest. From Mercury, place a line in the 3rd, 5th, 6th, 9th, 10th, 11th, and 12th positions, and a dot in the rest. From Jupiter, place a line in the 5th, 6th, 9th, and 11th positions, and a dot in the rest. From Venus, place a line in the 6th, 7th, and 12th positions, and a dot in the rest. From Saturn, place a line in the 1st, 2nd, 4th, 7th, 8th, 9th, 10th, and 11th positions, and a dot in the rest. Finally, from the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the rising sign at the moment of birth</term>, place a line in the 3rd, 4th, 6th, 10th, 11th, and 12th positions, and a dot in the rest. 

By doing this, the <term>Surya-Ashtakavarga-Chakra: the eight-fold mathematical grid for the Sun</term> is completed. Here, in every house, there are a total of eight marks combined (lines and dots). Among these, the line indicates an auspicious influence and the dot indicates an inauspicious influence. The houses containing more lines are "auspicious-fruit-giving" <note>benefic</note>. Those containing more dots are "inauspicious-fruit-houses" <note>malefic</note>. 

For example, here—by applying the lines and dots in the Sun's Ashtakavarga, Aries and Taurus have 4 lines and 4 dots each. Therefore, because the difference between auspicious and inauspicious is zero, both houses are "medium" <note>neutral</note>; that is, when the Sun passes through them during its transit <insert>charavasha</insert>, it will give neutral results or no significant result at all. Gemini has 5 dots and 3 lines; by calculating the difference, 2 dots (inauspicious) remain. Therefore, whenever the Sun enters Gemini, it will give an inauspicious result of one <term>Ashtamansha: one-eighth part or one 'step' of a planetary cycle</term>. 

Furthermore, Cancer has 5 lines and 3 dots; the difference is 2 lines (auspicious). Thus, whenever the Sun transits through Cancer, it will be auspicious. However, Gemini is an <term>Upachaya: a house of 'increase' or growth (3, 6, 10, 11)</term> from the birth sign; therefore, even if the result is inauspicious, the negativity will be slight. Conversely, Cancer is an <term>Apachaya: a house of 'decrease'</term> position; therefore, even though it is auspicious there, the benefic results will be diminished. Similarly, the 8th house has more dots (inauspicious) and is an *Apachaya* position; therefore, when the Sun enters that sign, the results will be highly inauspicious.

When a planet, during its transit, enters a sign where there are more auspicious marks, it will yield good results; conversely, when it enters a sign with more inauspicious marks, that planet will yield unfavorable results. || 8 ||

*Special Meaning—* Some practitioners create the Ashtakavarga chart by marking dots in auspicious places and lines in auspicious places; in such cases, one should understand the auspicious results based on the higher number of dots.

# Now, the Chapter on Livelihood || 10 ||

Now, the chapter on livelihood <note>Karma-ajiva: literally "action for subsistence"</note> is explained. In this chapter, it is determined how a person shall earn wealth. Here, there are two ways a planet becomes a giver of wealth: from the Ascendant and from the Moon. The planet situated in the 10th house from these becomes the giver of wealth. If the 10th houses from both the Ascendant and the Moon are empty, then one must look at the lords of the 10th signs from the Ascendant, the Moon, and the Sun. One must find which Navamshas <note>The ninth divisional chart, used to see the hidden strength of planets</note> those lords were stationed in at the time of the person's birth; the lords of those Navamshas then become the givers of wealth. However, the planets in the 10th from the Ascendant and the Moon are the primary givers of wealth in this manner. This is indicated by the phrase "the lords of the portions occupied by the lords of the tenth from the Moon, the Ascendant, and the Sun" <note>original: "bhendrarkaspadapatiganshanatha"</note>.

### With the Bhashya Commentary and the Sanskrit Commentary by Bhattotpala

First, the author explains how a planet situated in the tenth house from either the Ascendant or the Moon grants wealth. Furthermore, he describes two methods of determining wealth-givers based on the lords of the Navamsha <note>A Navamsha is a 1/9th division of a zodiac sign, used for fine-tuning predictions</note> occupied by the lords of the tenth houses from the Ascendant, the Moon, and the Sun. He states this in the *Praharshini* meter:

->**Wealth is obtained from the father, the father’s wife, enemies, friends,**<-
->**brothers, women, and servants, through the Sun and the other planets**<-
->**located in the tenth from the Ascendant or the Moon; or it is determined**<-
->**by the livelihood of the lord of the Navamsha occupied by the lord of the tenth from the Ascendant, Moon, or Sun. ||1||**<-

**Wealth is obtained:** From the *Hora* (Ascendant) and *Indu* (Moon), through the Sun and other planets situated in the tenth house, the acquisition of wealth from the father and others should be considered. 

In a person's birth chart, if the Sun is in the tenth house from either the Ascendant or the Moon, wealth comes from the father. If the Moon is in the tenth, it comes from the father’s wife <note>meaning the mother</note>. If Mars is in the tenth from the Ascendant or Moon, wealth comes from enemies. If Mercury, from friends. If Jupiter, from brothers. If Venus, from women. If Saturn, from servants or laborers. 

If one planet is in the tenth from the Ascendant and another from the Moon, both will grant their respective results during their specific minor planetary periods <term>Antardasha: a sub-period within a major planetary cycle</term>. Not only that, but if many planets are in the tenth from both the Moon and the Ascendant, all of them will provide wealth in their own way during their respective sub-periods.

But what if no planet is in the tenth house from either the Ascendant or the Moon? Who then gives wealth? To this, it is said: *By the livelihood of the lord of the Navamsha occupied by the lord of the tenth from the Ascendant, Moon, and Sun.* 

*Bham* means the Ascendant, *Indu* means the Moon, and *Arka* means the Sun. For each of these, find the sign called the "tenth house" (*Aspada*). The lord of that sign is situated in a certain Navamsha. The ruler of that Navamsha determines the person's livelihood and wealth according to the traits to be described later. 

When there are planets in the tenth from both the Ascendant and the Moon, the one that is stronger determines the source of wealth. Some say that among the Ascendant, Moon, and Sun, only the strongest one's tenth-house Navamsha lord should be used. However, that is not entirely correct; since no specific "strength" requirement is mentioned here, it is understood that wealth can come from all of them. This is because a person is observed to have many different sources of income. 

As the Sage Garga says:
> "Whichever planets are situated in the tenth from the rising sign or the Moon, they are all known to be givers of wealth in their own periods as described. The lord of the tenth house from the Ascendant, the Sun, and the Lord of the Night (Moon)—whichever Navamsha that lord occupies at that time, the ruler of that Navamsha determines the livelihood. When there are many wealth-givers, they surely grant it during their own planetary periods." || 1 ||

-># Chapter on Livelihood in the Brihat Jataka<-

**Vernacular Commentary—** One should understand the acquisition of wealth according to the planets situated in the tenth house from either the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note> or the Moon, or both. For instance: if the Sun is in the tenth, wealth comes from the father; if the Moon, from the mother; if Mars, from an enemy; if Mercury, from a friend; if Jupiter, from a brother; if Venus, from a wife; and if Saturn is in the tenth house, wealth is said to be gained through servants. If there are no planets in the tenth house from either the Ascendant or the Moon, then one must look at the lords of the tenth house from the Ascendant, the Moon, and the Sun. The profession <term>Vritti: a means of subsistence or trade</term> for gaining wealth should be understood based on the lord of the <term>Navamsha: a one-ninth divisional chart used for fine-tuning predictions</term> in which those tenth-house lords are placed. This is explained in the following verse. | 1 |

**Example—** As shown in the provided example, the Ascendant, the Sun, and the Moon are all in the same sign. Therefore, there are no planets in the tenth house (Capricorn) from any of them. Consequently, the lord of the tenth house (Capricorn) from these three is Saturn (at 0s 28° 5' 55"). Saturn is placed in the Navamsha of Sagittarius <note>ruled by Jupiter</note>; thus, the Navamsha lord is Jupiter. Therefore, according to the upcoming rule—*“In Jupiter’s Navamsha, through Brahmins, gods, mines, and religious duties”*—one should understand that wealth will be gained through the grace of Brahmins and deities, minerals, gold, and other such materials, as well as various land and water-related trades and religious performances. | 1 |

Regarding the statement "by the profession of the lord of the Navamsha occupied by the lord of the tenth house," the author now describes those professions in two *Praharshini* verses:

### If in the Sun's Navamsha: through grass, gold, wool, and medicine.
### If in the Moon's Navamsha: through agriculture, water-products, and dependence on women.
### If in Mars' Navamsha: through minerals, fire, weapons, and deeds of courage.
### If in Mercury's Navamsha: through writing, mathematics, poetry, and crafts. || 2 ||

**In the Sun's Navamsha:** When the lord of the tenth house is in the Navamsha of the Sun, the person earns wealth through "grass" (fragrant grasses/hay), gold, wool (sheep's hair), and medicine. The word "etcetera" <note>original: "adi"</note> implies the practice of medicine and the nursing of the sick. **In the Moon's Navamsha:** One earns wealth through agriculture, products of the water (such as conch shells, pearls, and coral), and through women. This includes the buying and selling of aquatic goods and support from women. **In Mars' Navamsha:** When the planet is in the Navamsha of Mars, wealth is obtained through "minerals" (earthy substances or processed metals like gold, silver, and copper). Alternatively, "minerals" refers to red arsenic, orpiment, and vermilion. It also includes "fire" (working with fire/heat), "weapons" (swords, discs, spears, and bows), and "deeds of courage" (impulsive actions or independent ventures). **In Mercury's Navamsha:** When in the Navamsha of Mercury, wealth is gained through writing, mathematics, poetry, and crafts. "Writing" refers to the arrangement of letters, "mathematics" includes interpretation <note>original: "vyakhyanena"</note> and the use of mechanical instruments.

# Commentary on the Language of the Stars with the Sanskrit Commentary of Bhattotpala
<page-num>236</page-num>

Through the creation of poetry and various crafts: such as painting, book-making, leaf-cutting <note>an ancient art of cutting decorative patterns into leaves</note>, making arrows and garlands, and the preparation of perfumes and incenses, one obtains wealth. || 2 ||

**Vernacular Translation —** If the lord of the tenth house from the previously mentioned Ascendant, Moon, or Sun is located in the Navamsha <note>a sub-divisional chart representing one-ninth of a sign</note> of the **Sun**, wealth is gained through grass (scents, etc.), gold, wool, woolen clothes, and medicines. If the tenth lord is in the Navamsha of the **Moon**, wealth comes from agriculture, products of the water (conch shells, pearls, etc.), and through the patronage or support of women. If in the Navamsha of **Mars**, wealth is gained through metals (copper, brass, gold, or minerals like orpiment), through work involving fire, weapons (striking with arrows, swords, etc.), and through courageous deeds (engaging in difficult or daring tasks). If in the Navamsha of **Mercury**, wealth is obtained through writing, mathematics, poetry, and painting. || 2 ||

->Now, he speaks of the Navamsha of Jupiter in the second Praharshini meter:<-

> **In Jupiter's Navamsha, wealth comes through Brahmins, gods, mines, and religious duties;**
> **In Venus's Navamsha, through gems, silver, cows, and buffaloes; (1)**
> **In Saturn's Navamsha, through labor, execution, carrying loads, and low-status crafts;**
> **Success in one's profession is determined by the Navamsha occupied by the Lord of Action. || 3 ||**

**In Jupiter's Navamsha:** This means when the tenth lord is in the Navamsha of Jupiter, one gains wealth through "twice-born" <term>Dvija: referring here to Brahmins or the priestly class</term>, through "the wise" <term>Vibudha: referring to gods or learned scholars</term>, and from "mines" <note>original: akara</note> which are the places of origin for gold, salt, antimony, or even elephants. By the word "and so forth," it includes alchemy <note>original: kriyavada</note>. Through "religious duties," it refers to sacrifices, charity, fasting, pilgrimages, and service to a Guru. 

Now, when it is in the **Navamsha of Venus**, wealth is gained through gems such as diamonds, emeralds, rubies, and sapphires; through silver; and by the word "and so forth," all other metals; through cows and buffaloes, or specifically through the products of fine buffaloes. 

Now, when it is in the **Navamsha of Saturn**, wealth is gained through "labor" such as traveling long distances, through "execution" <note>original: vadha</note> meaning either acting as an executioner or through self-mortification, by carrying heavy loads, and through "low-status crafts" which are occupations considered beneath one's family lineage. 

Thus, having understood the arrival of wealth for a person based on their birth chart, he now describes the success of these actions based on the current movement <note>transit</note> of the planets: "Success in one's profession is determined by the Navamsha occupied by the Lord of Action." The "Lord of Action" <term>Karmesha</term> is the ruler of the tenth sign from the Ascendant; whichever Navamsha that ruler occupies during its transit...

Whichever planet is the lord of the <term>Navamsha</term><note>A sub-divisional chart where a sign is divided into nine parts; used here to pinpoint specific professional influences.</note> in which the lord of the tenth house is situated, the success of the works associated with that planet—such as dealing in grass, gold, wool, or medicines for the Sun—will come to fruition. These undertaken tasks will be successful. Some commentators read this as the "attainment of success in works equal to those of the lord of the tenth house." Here, the mention of the <term>Navamsha</term> is understood through context from previous verses. As the venerable Sage Garga says: "In whichever <term>Navamsha</term> the lord of the tenth house from the Ascendant resides, one should predict the success of works corresponding to that planet's nature through the course of its transit." For a person whose birth chart is known, this refers to the practical application of work; one should declare the timely success of those specific labors indicated by the lord of the <term>Navamsha</term> occupied by the tenth lord, and not others. || 3 ||

**Vernacular Commentary—** If the lord of the tenth house is in the <term>Navamsha</term> of Jupiter, wealth is gained through Brahmins, deities, or scholars, as well as from mines (gold, salt, coal, etc.), and by the word "etc.," through elephants, horses, sacrifices, and acts of charity. If in the <term>Navamsha</term> of Venus, wealth comes from gems (emeralds, rubies, etc.), silver, and cattle like cows and buffaloes. If in the <term>Navamsha</term> of Saturn, wealth is gained through hard labor, acts of violence, carrying loads, menial work, or deeds despised by one's own lineage. Among the three starting points mentioned earlier (the Ascendant, the Moon, and the Sun), the success of the work is specifically determined by the <term>Navamsha</term> occupied by the lord of the tenth house from the Ascendant. || 3 ||

### Now, the knowledge of the arrival of wealth is described in the Praharshini meter—

-> From planets situated in the houses of friends, enemies, or their own homes, wealth comes; <-
-> If the Sun is exalted and strong, wealth comes from one's own valor. <-
-> From benefic planets situated in the eleventh, first, or second houses, <-
-> And if they are endowed with strength, wealth should be considered in many ways. || 4 || <-

Regarding "situated in the houses of friends, enemies, or their own homes": Those planets which occupy the tenth house from the Moon or the Ascendant—or in their absence, the lords of the <term>Navamshas</term> occupied by the lords of the tenth house from the Moon, Sun, or Ascendant—if they are in a friend's house at the time of birth, they grant wealth through friends during their sub-periods (<term>Antardasha</term>). If they are in an enemy's house, wealth comes from enemies. If in their own house, they provide wealth from their own resources. Regarding "the Sun being exalted and strong": If the Sun is identified as the wealth-giver by the previous rules and is exalted (occupying Aries) and possessed of temporal strength (<term>Kala-bala</term>), then that person earns wealth through his own prowess. This means he becomes one whose wealth is conquered by his own courage. Regarding "situated in the eleventh": Benefic planets (<term>Saumya</term>) situated in the eleventh house (the house of gains), the first house (the Ascendant), or the second house (the house of wealth), if they are endowed with strength and vigor...

The native born <note>the person whose birth chart is being read</note> obtains his own wealth in many ways and through various means. A certain conclusion should be made: by whatever means one desires to earn wealth, one obtains it without effort. And so says the Lord Garga:

> "The givers of wealth—at the time of birth, if planets are situated in the houses of friends, enemies, or their own signs, they grant wealth derived from friends, enemies, or oneself respectively.

> If benefic planets are in the eleventh, second, or the ascendant, by whatever profession one seeks to earn wealth, one attains it effortlessly."

Thus ends the verse. (4)

**Vernacular Language—** If the lords of the tenth house from the previously mentioned Ascendant, Moon, and Sun are in a friend's house, wealth is gained through friends; if in an enemy's house, through enemies; and if in their own house, through one's own self. If the powerful Sun is in its exaltation (Aries), wealth is gained through the strength of one's own arms. Furthermore, if powerful benefic planets are in the eleventh, the ascendant, or the second house, one gains wealth in many ways. See the words of Lord Garga in the Sanskrit commentary for further detail. (4)

# Chapter 11: On Royal Combinations (Rajayoga)

->Now begins the explanation of the chapter on Royal Combinations. First, the author states the opinions of the Greeks <term>Yavanas</term> <note>original: "Yavana"; historically referring to Greeks or foreigners who contributed to Indian astrology</note> and Jivasharma using the Vitaliya meter:<-

### The Greeks say that if cruel planets <term>malefics</term> are in their signs of exaltation, the person becomes a king of a cruel disposition.
### However, in the opinion of Jivasharma, a lord of the earth <note>a king</note> is not born from cruel planets alone. (1)

"They say" refers to the famous principle in all natal astrology that "those born with three or more planets in exaltation become kings, provided they are born into a royal lineage." Herein lies the difference of opinion among the Greeks. They say that at the time of birth, if one is born with "cruel" (malefic) planets in their exaltation, they become a "lord of the earth" (king), but are of a cruel mind or sinful intellect. By implication, if the planets in exaltation are "gentle" (benefics), the king is of a virtuous nature. This same meaning was stated by Manittha. His statement is as follows:

> "With malefics in exaltation, a man becomes a lord of the earth with a sinful mind; likewise, with benefics, he is righteous. With a mixture of both, he is of a mixed nature."

"However, with cruel planets..." refers to the school of Jivasharma. In his opinion, one is not born a king simply because malefic planets are in exaltation. Rather, such a person becomes wealthy and equal to a king, but not a monarch. His statement is as follows:

> "Men born with malefic planets in exaltation do not become kings. Instead, they become endowed with wealth, but are prone to anger and fond of quarrels."

So it is said.

# The Chapter on Royal Yogas in the Brihat Jataka

Varahamihira <note>A 6th-century Indian astronomer and astrologer</note> here intends to follow the opinion of Yavaneshwara <note>Literally "Lord of the Greeks," referring to the school of Indo-Greek astrology</note>. It is stated generally in the *Svalpa Jataka*: "Those born in royal dynasties become kings if three or more planets are in their signs of exaltation <term>Exaltation: The zodiac sign where a planet is at its maximum strength</term>. Similarly, those born in other families become kings if five or more planets are exalted or placed in their trines." — 1

**Vernacular Commentary —** If even malefic planets <note>Planets like Mars or Saturn that generally portend difficulty</note> are in their exalted positions, a king with a cruel intellect is born; such is the saying of the Yavana teachers. However, Jeevasharma <note>An earlier authority on astrology often cited by Varahamihira</note> contends that one does not become a king simply by having malefic planets in exaltation. — 1

**Special Meaning —** The opinion of the Yavanas is that even if malefic planets are in their exaltation, if there are more than three, a king is produced. However, he will be "cruel-minded." If more than three benefic planets <note>Gentle planets like Jupiter or Venus</note> are exalted, he is a wise king, and if more than two mixed planets are exalted, he is a king of mixed temperament. But Jeevasharma’s view is that malefic planets in exaltation only make one wealthy, not a king. — 1

->Now, he describes thirty-two Royal Yogas in the Vasantatilaka meter:<-

<insert>(Important)</insert> **When Mars, Saturn, the Sun, and Jupiter are all four, or any three of them,**
->**in their respective exaltations, and one of them is in the Ascendant, sixteen kings are declared.**<-
->**When two or one of these are exalted while one of them is in the Ascendant,**<-
->**and the Moon is in its own sign, sixteen more lords of the earth are born. — 2**<-

**Mars, Saturn, etc. —** "Vakra" refers to Mars, "Arkaja" to Saturn, "Arka" to the Sun, and "Guru" to Jupiter. When all four of these—Mars, Saturn, the Sun, and Jupiter—are in their signs of exaltation, and any one of these four exalted planets is in the Ascendant <term>Ascendant/Lagna: The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term>, four Royal Yogas are formed. Furthermore, when any three of these are exalted, and one of those three is in the Ascendant, twelve Royal Yogas are formed. This makes the first sixteen.

**When two or one... —** Among these same planets, when two are exalted and one of them is in the Ascendant, while the Moon is in its own sign (Cancer), twelve Royal Yogas are formed. When only one of them is exalted and is also in the Ascendant, while the Moon is in its own sign, four Royal Yogas are formed. This makes sixteen, which when added to the sixteen mentioned in the first half of the verse, totals thirty-two. For example:

The Sun in Aries, Jupiter in Cancer, Saturn in Libra, and Mars in Capricorn; the remaining planets may be anywhere. In such a planetary arrangement, if Aries is the Ascendant, that is one yoga. If Cancer is the second, Libra the third, and Capricorn the fourth. Thus, with Mars, Saturn, the Sun, and Jupiter all exalted and one of them as the Ascendant, four Royal Yogas are established.

<note>original: "राजयोग" (Raja Yoga: Royal Union/Combination), "वराहमिहिर" (Varahamihira), "यवनेश्वर" (Yavaneshwara), "जीवशर्मा" (Jeevasharma), "वसन्ततिलका" (Vasantatilaka: a poetic meter), "स्वोच्च" (Svoccha: own exaltation), "लग्न" (Lagna: Ascendant), "ग्रह" (Graha: Planet), "मेष" (Mesha: Aries), "कर्कट" (Karkata: Cancer), "तुला" (Tula: Libra), "मकर" (Makara: Capricorn)</note>

Now, regarding the combinations of three planets—for example: the Sun in Aries, Jupiter in Cancer, and Saturn in Libra, with the remaining planets placed anywhere. In such a planetary arrangement, if Aries is the Ascendant <note>The "Lagna" or rising sign</note>, that is one yoga. If Cancer is the Ascendant, that is a second; if Libra, a third. Including the previous ones, this makes seven. Now, if the Sun is in Aries, Jupiter in Cancer, and Mars in Capricorn, with the rest as desired: with Aries as the Ascendant, that is one; Cancer, a second; Capricorn, a third. Including the previous, this makes ten. Now, if the Sun is in Aries, Saturn in Libra, and Mars in Capricorn, with the rest as desired: with Aries as the Ascendant, one; Libra, a second; Capricorn, a third—thus thirteen. Now, if Jupiter is in Cancer, Saturn in Libra, and Mars in Capricorn, with the rest as desired: with Cancer as the Ascendant, one; Libra, a second; Capricorn, a third—thus sixteen Royal Yogas <term>Rajayogas: planetary combinations indicating power or high status</term>. This concludes the section on four or three planets in their signs of exaltation with one of them in the Ascendant.

In the yogas involving two or one planet, as long as the Moon is not in Cancer, the yogas do not form. For instance: in the combinations of two planets where the Moon is in its own sign <note>Cancer</note>, twelve Royal Yogas are explained. For example: [if the Sun is in Aries and the Moon in Cancer], that is one yoga. With Cancer as the Ascendant, it is a second. Now, if the Sun is in Aries, the Moon in Cancer, and Saturn in Libra, with the rest as desired: then Aries as Ascendant is the third; Libra as Ascendant is the fourth. Now, if the Sun is in Aries, the Moon in Cancer, and Mars in Capricorn, with the rest as desired: then Aries as Ascendant is the fifth; Capricorn as Ascendant is the sixth. Now, if the Moon and Jupiter are in Cancer and Saturn is in Libra, with the rest as desired: then Cancer as Ascendant is the seventh; Libra as Ascendant is the eighth. Now, if the Moon and Jupiter are in Cancer and Mars is in Capricorn, with the rest as desired: then Cancer as Ascendant is the ninth; Capricorn as Ascendant is the tenth. Now, if Saturn is in Libra, Mars in Capricorn, and the Moon in Cancer, with the rest as desired: then Libra as Ascendant is the eleventh; Capricorn as Ascendant is the twelfth. This concludes the section on two planets. Now, for single planets: with the Moon in Cancer and the Sun in Aries, Aries as Ascendant is one. With the Moon and Jupiter in Cancer, Cancer as Ascendant is the second. With the Moon in Cancer and Saturn in Libra, Libra as Ascendant is the third. With the Moon in Cancer and Mars in Capricorn, Capricorn as Ascendant is the fourth. Thus, adding these to the previous twelve makes sixteen. Combined with the sixteen mentioned in the first half of the verse, thirty-two Royal Yogas have been explained. | 2 |

**Vernacular Translation—** If Mars, Saturn, the Sun, and Jupiter—these four, or three of them—are in their respective exaltations and one of them is in the Ascendant, 16 types of Royal Yogas are formed. Additionally, if two or one of these are in exaltation and one is in the Ascendant while the Moon is in its own sign (Cancer), another 16 types of Royal Yogas are formed. | 2 |

->Now, he describes forty-four Royal Yogas in the Anustubh meter:<-

> When the Ascendant is in the best division <term>Vargottama: a planet occupying the same sign in both the main chart and the ninth divisional chart</term>, and is aspected <note>Glanced at by the influence of other planets</note> by four or more planets (excluding the Moon), twenty-two kings are said to be born. | 3 |

<summary>This page details the mathematical permutations of Rajayogas (Royal Yogas) based on planets like the Sun, Jupiter, and Mars being in their exaltation signs. It concludes that there are 32 such primary yogas and introduces a new set of 22 yogas based on the Vargottama Ascendant.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discussion on Royal Combinations (Rajayogas) from the Brihat Jataka, specifically focusing on the mathematical permutations of planetary aspects on the Ascendant or the Moon.</meta>

<page-num>244</page-num>
<header>Chapter on Royal Combinations in the Brihat Jataka</header>

**When the Ascendant is in the Vargottama...** <note>Vargottama refers to a planet or point occupying the same sign in both the main birth chart and the 9th divisional chart (Navamsha), which greatly enhances its strength.</note> This means when the Ascendant at the time of birth is placed in its own Navamsha. When that Ascendant is aspected <note>aspected: "looked at" by the gravitational/astrological influence of other planets</note> by four or more planets, excluding the Moon—specifically by four, five, or six planets—twenty-two **Royal Combinations** (*Rajayogas*) are said to occur. In this context, if the Moon aspects the Ascendant, it does not break the combination, but it is simply not counted among the required number of aspecting planets. Whether the Moon aspects it or not, if four or more other planets aspect the Ascendant, Royal Combinations are formed. Thus, there are twenty-two combinations when the Ascendant is in *Vargottama*. Similarly, when the Moon is in a *Vargottama* position and is aspected by four or more planets, another twenty-two combinations occur. This makes a total of forty-four.

Regarding these, when the Ascendant or the Moon is aspected by four planets, there are fifteen possible variations. When aspected by five planets, there are six variations. When aspected by six planets, there is one variation. This totals twenty-two. For example:

# The Chapter on Royal Yogas in the Brihat Jataka

### Now, five yogas are described in the Shikharini meter:

> If Saturn is in Aquarius, the Sun in Aries, and the Moon in Taurus, and one of these is in the Ascendant, while Mercury, Jupiter, and Mars are in Gemini, Leo, and Scorpio respectively, kings are born. If Saturn and the Moon are in their exaltation and in the Ascendant, while the Sun and Mercury are in the sixth house, and Venus, Mars, and Jupiter are in Libra, Aries, and Cancer, two types of kings are born. ||4||

**Commentary:** Regarding "Saturn etc." — When Saturn <note>original: "Yama"</note> is in Aquarius, the Sun is in Aries, and the Moon is in Taurus, and one of these planets is in the Ascendant <note>the "Lagna" or the rising sign at the time of birth</note>; and not only that, but Mercury, Jupiter, and Mars <note>original: "Shashija-Guru-Vakra"</note> are situated in Gemini, Leo, and Scorpio; then those born are kings. A "and" should be seen as implied here. Thus, this occurs: Saturn in Aquarius, Sun in Aries, Moon in Taurus, Mercury in Gemini, Jupiter in Leo, and Mars in Scorpio. In such a planetary arrangement, one yoga <term>Yoga: a specific planetary combination or "union" in a horoscope</term> occurs if Aquarius is the Ascendant, a second if Aries is, and a third if Taurus is.

Regarding "Saturn and the Moon" — Saturn and the Moon are in their exaltation <note>Saturn is exalted in Libra, the Moon in Taurus</note> and also in the Ascendant. The Sun and Mercury are in the sixth house (Virgo). Venus, Mars, and Jupiter are in Libra, Aries, and Cancer <note>original: "Indu-kshetra" or the Moon's domain</note> respectively. These result in two royal yogas. Thus: Saturn in Libra, Moon in Taurus, Sun and Mercury in Virgo, Venus in Libra, Mars in Aries, and Jupiter in Cancer. In this arrangement, one yoga occurs with Libra as the Ascendant, and a second with Taurus. Together with the previous three, there are five. Here, some interpret "sixth house" as the sixth sign from the Ascendant. This is incorrect, because if Venus is in Libra, it is impossible for the Sun to be in Pisces <note>The Sun and Venus are never that far apart in the sky</note>. As Badarayana <note>An ancient sage and authority on astrology</note> says:

> "With Libra as the Ascendant containing Venus and Saturn, Mars in Aries, Jupiter in Cancer, and the Sun and Mercury in Virgo—or with Taurus as the Ascendant containing the Moon—a king is born." ||4||

**Vernacular Translation**—If Saturn is in Aquarius, the Sun in Aries, and the Moon in Taurus, and any one of these three is in the Ascendant, while Mercury is in Gemini, Jupiter in Leo, and Mars in Scorpio, then 3 types of Royal Yogas occur based on these three Ascendants. Furthermore, if Saturn and the Moon are in their respective exaltations and one of them is in the Ascendant, with the Sun and Mercury in the sixth house, Venus in Libra, Mars in Aries, and Jupiter in Cancer, then 2 types of Royal Yogas occur based on these two Ascendants. ||4||

### Now, three other Royal Yogas are described in the Shikharini meter:

> When Mars is exalted, the Sun and Moon are in Sagittarius, and Saturn is in the Ascendant, one becomes a lord of the earth. Another becomes a lord of the earth when Mars is in the Ascendant along with the Moon. When Saturn is in the seventh house <note>original: "Asta" or the setting point</note> with the Moon, Jupiter is in Sagittarius, and the Sun is in its exaltation (Aries) in the Ascendant, a lord of the earth is born. ||5||

### With the Sanskrit Commentary of Bhattotpala and the Hindi Vernacular Translation

Regarding the verse "When Mars is exalted and the Sun and Moon...": When Mars is in its sign of exaltation, meaning it is situated in Capricorn; and the Sun and Moon are both located in Sagittarius; and Saturn is in the Ascendant <note>The "Lagna" or rising sign</note>, specifically in Capricorn. In such a combination, the person born becomes a lord of the earth, a ruler, a King. Regarding the phrase "In the Ascendant of Yama": this is explained as the Ascendant being either Capricorn or Aquarius <note>Signs ruled by Saturn/Yama</note>. Some explain this as Saturn being in the Ascendant regardless of the sign, but that is incorrect. For Badarayana <note>An ancient authority on astrology</note> says: "Saturn in the Ascendant, Mars exalted, and the Moon and Sun reaching Sagittarius." Our first explanation seems the most sound. As Mandavya states: "When the Sun and Moon are in the sign of the Lord of Speech (Sagittarius), and Mars is in Capricorn with full strength, then a virtuous man becomes the crest-jewel of kings, from whom enemies flee in battle as if from Death itself."

"Or another lord of the earth": In this same combination, if Mars is in its exaltation joined with the Moon, and the Sun is in Sagittarius, it is a Royal Yoga. In that case: with Capricorn as the Ascendant containing the Moon and Mars, and the Sun in Sagittarius, another type of King is born. On this, Badarayana says: "The Sun in Sagittarius with the Moon, or Mars reaching exaltation in the Ascendant."

"With Saturn and the Moon in the seventh...": When Saturn is joined with the Moon in the seventh house <note>The "setting" house opposite the Ascendant</note>, and Jupiter is in Sagittarius, and the Sun is in its exaltation (Aries) in the Ascendant, the person born becomes a lord of the earth, a King. To summarize: Aries is the Ascendant containing the Sun, Jupiter is in Sagittarius, and the Moon and Saturn are in Libra. In such a combination, a King is born. Thus, these are three Royal Yogas. (5)

**Vernacular Translation:** If Mars is in its exaltation (Capricorn) in the Ascendant along with Saturn, and the Sun and Jupiter are both in Sagittarius, the person born in such a combination becomes a King. Also, if the Ascendant is Capricorn and Mars is there with the Moon, he becomes a King. And if the Sun is in its exaltation (Aries) in the Ascendant, while Saturn and the Moon are in the seventh house and Jupiter is in Sagittarius, the person born also becomes a King. (5)

->Now, he describes two more Royal Yogas in the Shikharini meter:<-

If the Moon is in Taurus in the Ascendant, and the Sun, Jupiter, and Saturn are in the fourth, seventh, and tenth houses respectively, a man certainly becomes a lord of men. If Saturn is in Capricorn in the Ascendant, and the Moon and other planets are in the third, sixth, ninth, and twelfth houses, he becomes a famous ruler of great virtue and renown. (6)

# The Chapter on Royal Yogas in the Brihat Jataka

**If the Moon is in Taurus at the Ascendant** <note>The 'Ascendant' or 'Lagna' is the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth.</note> and the Sun, Jupiter, and Saturn are respectively in the 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, a person certainly becomes a lord of men—a King. This is the specific configuration: Taurus is the Ascendant with the Moon inside it; the Sun is in Leo; Jupiter is in Scorpio; and Saturn is in Aquarius. One born under such a yoga will surely be a ruler.

**If Saturn is in Capricorn at the Ascendant**, and the Moon, Mars, Mercury, and Jupiter are situated in the 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th houses respectively, the person born is famous everywhere. Such a person possesses "broad virtues and fame" <note>original: "Prithu-guna-yasha"</note>—meaning their bravery and reputation are widespread—and they become a leader of men. 

Now, one might ask: "It was said 'the Moon and the others,' so where does Venus go?" It is explained that because there is no fifth position in the sequence provided, and since Venus is often near the Sun, it is not assigned a specific house here. The resulting chart is: Capricorn as the Ascendant with Saturn there; the Moon in Pisces; Mars in Gemini; Mercury in Virgo; and Jupiter in Sagittarius. The Sun and Venus may be anywhere. One born in this yoga becomes a king of great virtue. Thus, two Royal Yogas are described here. 

As the sage Mandavya says:
*“When Saturn is in the Ascendant in Capricorn, the Moon in Pisces, Mars in Gemini, Mercury in Virgo, and Jupiter in Sagittarius; while Venus and the Sun move according to their orbits—he in whose birth this occurs becomes a ruler of men equal to Indra.”*

***

**Vernacular Translation:** If the Moon is in the Taurus Ascendant, the Sun in the 4th house (Leo), Jupiter in the 7th, and Saturn in the 10th (Aquarius), that person certainly becomes a king. Likewise, if Saturn is in the Capricorn Ascendant, the Moon in the 3rd (Pisces), Mars in the 6th, Mercury in the 9th, and Jupiter in the 12th—with the Sun and Venus anywhere—the person born in such a yoga is extremely virtuous and successful.

### Now, three Royal Yogas are described in the Shikharini meter:

->**If Jupiter and the Moon are in Sagittarius, and Mars is in the first half of Capricorn;**<-
->**Or if Venus and Mercury are in their signs of exaltation at the Ascendant, kings are born.**<-
->**If Mars and the Sun are in the 5th house, and Jupiter, Moon, and Venus are in the 4th;**<-
->**Or if Mercury is in the Virgo Ascendant, another virtuous king is produced.**<-

**Regarding "Jupiter and the Moon in Sagittarius":** When Jupiter <term>Guru: the heavy/spiritual teacher</term> is with the Moon in Sagittarius, and Mars <term>Bhumitanaya: son of the Earth</term> is in the "mouth of the deer" (the first half of Capricorn), as it is said: "The first half of the deer is Capricorn." 

**Regarding "Venus and Mercury":** If Venus <term>Bhruguja: descendant of Bhrigu</term> and Mercury <term>Shashija: son of the Moon</term> are in their respective exaltation signs <note>Venus is exalted in Pisces; Mercury is exalted in Virgo</note> while at the Ascendant, then in these two yogas, those born become kings. These are two distinct Royal Yogas.

**By the aforementioned Royal Yogas; how much more so those of royal birth!**
**But by the yogas to be described, only those of royal descent become kings;**
**In those same yogas, one not born of a king becomes merely equal to a king.** ||12||

*Commentary:* The word "even" implies possibility. By the "aforementioned Royal Yogas"—the previously stated combinations—even men born of "low families" <note>original: "khala-kula-jata"; born of wicked or base lineages</note> become possessors of kingdoms, i.e., kings. How much more so those "born of royal families"—those of royal descent—they certainly become kings. However, by the "yogas to be described" hereafter, only those "born of royal families" become kings. Among those future yogas, one "not born of a royal family" becomes "equal to a king." This means they are like a king, but not the actual ruler. The phrase "how much more so" indicates a strong probability. ||12||

*Vernacular translation—* In the yogas mentioned previously, even a man born in a low or poor family becomes a king, so what need is there to speak of those born in royal families? Furthermore, in the yogas to be mentioned hereafter, only those born in a royal lineage can be kings; a person born in another lineage becomes equal to a king, but not the ruler (sovereign). ||12||

->Now, he describes a Royal Yoga in the Aupacchandasika meter:<-

**By three or more planets in their exaltation or own trines and possessing strength, those of royal descent become lords of men.**
**By five or more such planets, those born of other families become kings; if they lack strength, they possess wealth but are not rulers of the earth.** ||13||

*Commentary:* "By three or more"—meaning three or more planets—situated in their "exaltation" <term>ucca; the sign where a planet is at its highest strength</term> or in their "own trines" <term>mula-trikona; specific favorable signs for planets</term> and "possessing strength" <note>possessing temporal and other forms of planetary strength (shadbala)</note>, those born of royal families become "lords of men" or kings. By the word "more," it includes four planets. "By five or more, those born of other families"—by five or more planets in exaltation or trines, even those born of "low families" become kings. By the word "more," it includes six or seven planets. "If they lack strength, they possess wealth"—if three planets are in exaltation or trines but "lack strength" <note>devoid of temporal and other strengths</note>, even those of royal birth do not become kings, though they may be wealthy.

<summary>This page distinguishes between planetary combinations that grant kingship to anyone regardless of birth and those that only grant full sovereignty to those of royal blood. It emphasizes that planetary strength (exaltation and trines) is the deciding factor in achieving political power.</summary>

# Chapter on Royal Yogas in the Brihat Jataka

But they become equal to kings <note>meaning they possess great influence but not the formal title</note>. If the planets are fewer than the required number, they become endowed with wealth—rich men—but not lords of the earth or kings. This is what is meant: even if born into a royal family, a person does not become a king with only one or two planets in their sign of exaltation <term>Exaltation (ucca): the specific zodiac sign where a planet reaches its maximum strength</term> or their root-trine <term>Root-trine (mula-trikona): a sign where a planet is very strong, second only to exaltation</term>; they only become wealthy. Similarly, if three or four such planets are present in the charts of those born in other families, they become wealthy but not kings. Here, if the planets are not in their exaltation signs in the specified number, but the count is completed by including those in root-trines, they still grant the stated results. This applies whether they are only in exaltation or only in their trines. || 13 ||

**Vernacular Translation—** If 3 or 4 planets, endowed with strength (temporal strength or directional strength), are in their exaltation or root-trine, a person born in a royal lineage becomes a king. One born in another lineage becomes merely wealthy. If 5 or 6 planets are in their exaltation or trine, then in such a yoga <note>Yoga: a specific planetary combination</note>, even one born in another lineage becomes a king. If fewer (2 or 1) planets are in exaltation or root-trine, the person is only wealthy, not a king. || 13 ||

->Now, another Royal Yoga is described in the Vidyunmala meter:<-

### When the Sun is on the horizon, the Moon is in Aries in the Ascendant, Mars is in its exaltation, Saturn is in Aquarius,
### and Jupiter is in Sagittarius, one should know the son of a king will become a Lord of the Earth. || 14 ||

**On the horizon** <note>original: "lekhastha"</note> means staying on the line; the word "line" refers to the rising horizon. When the Sun is "on the line," it is half-risen above the earth's circle. Not only that, but when the Moon is in Aries and that same Aries is the Ascendant <term>Ascendant (Lagna): the sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</term>, Mars is in its exaltation (Capricorn), Saturn is in Aquarius, and Jupiter has reached Sagittarius—in such a combination, if the one born is the son of a king, he should be known as a Lord of the Earth. One born in another family becomes wealthy. Here, some read "the Sun in the Ascendant and the Moon in Aries in the Ascendant." If the Sun is "on the line" in Leo and the Moon is in the Aries Ascendant, there is no contradiction; it remains a Royal Yoga. || 14 ||

**Vernacular Translation—** If the Sun is on the rising horizon, the Moon is in Aries in the Ascendant, Mars is in its exaltation (Capricorn), Saturn is in Aquarius, and Jupiter is in Sagittarius, then the son of a king born in this yoga should be understood to be a king. || 14 ||

**Special Meaning—** Some interpret the word "line" <note>lekha</note> here to mean the "Sign of Leo." Even with that meaning, a Royal Yoga can occur. However, in that case, the reading should be "the Moon in Aries in the Ascendant while the Sun is in Leo." || 14 ||

## Chapter on Royal Yogas in the Brihat Jataka

If the planets are situated in the <term>Ascendant</term><note>Lagna: the sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note>, the second, the sixth, and the eleventh houses, the person born is a king. -> Commentary by Bhattotpala with Hindi Translation <-

Now, he explains in the *Swagata* meter the knowledge of when a person born with a Royal Yoga <note>A planetary combination indicating kingship or high status</note> will attain their kingdom:

**The attainment of sovereignty occurs during the planetary period (Dasha) of the planet occupying the tenth house or the ascendant; or otherwise, of the strongest planet. During the period of a planet situated in an enemy's sign or its sign of debilitation, a "vulnerable period" (Chidra-dasha) should be expected, requiring the seeking of shelter.** || 16 ||

*During the planetary period of the planet occupying the tenth house or the ascendant:* Among the planets causing the Royal Yoga, whichever planet is situated in the "Karma" <note>The 10th house, representing profession and status</note> or the tenth house from the ascendant, or whichever planet among the Royal Yoga-makers is "Ascendant-joined" (situated in the first house at birth)—during its *Paka-dasha* <note>The major planetary period</note> or its *Antardasha* <note>The sub-period</note>, the attainment of sovereignty occurs. 

Now, if there are planets in both the ascendant and the tenth house, then the attainment of sovereignty happens during the sub-period of whichever of the two is stronger. If there are many planets there, then it occurs during the sub-period of the "Strongest"—the one possessing the highest strength. 

If both the ascendant and the tenth house are empty, then the planet which is the strongest in the entire birth chart grants the kingdom during its sub-period. Among many sub-periods, the kingdom is granted specifically during that sub-period where the planet gains extreme strength through its current transit (Chara).

*Regarding the enemy's sign or debilitation:* Even for one who has attained a kingdom, if a sub-period is given by a planet situated in an enemy's field or a sign of debilitation at the time of birth, then loss of the kingdom should be predicted during that time if that planet is strong <note>original: "balavati"</note>. Because that is a "vulnerable period" (Chidra-dasha); even if that planet is weak, misfortune occurs. That should be considered a "period for seeking shelter" (Samshraya-dasha). Therefore, during that sub-period, one must seek the protection of others. Through the merit of seeking shelter with a king favored by destiny, one may be liberated from that misfortune. As will be said in the section on Journeys (Yatra):

> "During the period of loss caused by the anger of enemies, and during the period of the enemy of the lord of the birth ascendant, the periods of the significators of one's own country's lords: a King should seek shelter."

On this matter, the venerable Garga says:

> **"Whether a planet is in the ascendant or in the tenth house, or whichever is the strongest; that planet, when powerful, grants a kingdom during its own sub-period.**
> **During the period of a strong planet situated in a debilitated or enemy sign, there is a fall from power; for one lacking strength, liberation from that fall comes through seeking shelter with another."** || 16 ||

**Vernacular Translation—** At the time of birth, the attainment of the kingdom occurs during the period of the planet situated in the tenth house or the ascendant. If there are many planets in the tenth or the ascendant, then it should be understood to occur in the major or sub-period of the one who is more powerful. If there is no planet in the tenth house or the ascendant, then the gain of the kingdom should be understood to occur in the period of the planet that is strongest among all planets. If the planet in the tenth or the ascendant is in an enemy's sign or a sign of debilitation, then during its major or sub-period, one should anticipate the loss of the kingdom or the attainment of a kingdom through the shelter of other kings. || 16 ||

->Now, using the *Malini* meter, the author describes the birth of those who enjoy pleasures and those who become leaders of forest tribes and bandits:<-

**Regarding "Jupiter, Venus, or Mercury in the Ascendant":** If any one of Jupiter, Venus, or Mercury is in the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note>, Saturn is in the seventh house, and the Sun is in the tenth house, one should know that a person born under such a combination <note>Yoga</note> will be a "pleasure-seeker" <note>Bhogi</note>; they will always enjoy comforts. Even if such a person is initially without means, they will obtain pleasures from somewhere or other. Some commentators explain the phrase "Sun, Mercury, and Venus in the Ascendant" as referring to the signs belonging to them—namely Leo, Taurus, Libra, Gemini, and Virgo. This is because it is astronomically impossible for Mercury and Venus to be in the Ascendant while the Sun is in the tenth house <note>due to their proximity to the Sun</note>. The Teacher Varahamihira has recorded this combination according to ancient scriptures. On this matter, the venerable Sage Garga says: "When Jupiter, Mercury, or Venus is in the Ascendant, Saturn is in the seventh, and the Sun is in the tenth, the person born becomes a man of pleasure." Regarding "strong benefic cardinal houses": If the signs belonging to benefic planets are in the cardinal houses and are strong, and the malefic planets are in cruel signs, the person born becomes the leader of the *Shabaras* (mountain tribes), *Pulindas* (forest dwellers), and *Dasyus* (bandits). He becomes a sharer of wealth and fortunate. Some explain "strong benefic cardinal houses" as meaning benefic planets themselves being strong in the cardinal houses, but this is incorrect. As the venerable Sage Garga states:

> "When malefic planets are in malefic signs and the cardinal houses consist of strong benefic signs, the person born shall be a leader of bandits." ||20||

Furthermore, if benefic signs are in the cardinal houses and malefic planets are in cruel signs in any house, the person born becomes a leader of thieves, bandits, etc., and is also wealthy. ||20||

# Chapter 12: On the Nabhasa Yogas

Now, the chapter on the Nabhasa <note>original: "Nabhasa" refers to the sky or celestial heavens</note> Yogas <note>term: Yoga (planetary combinations that produce specific results)</note> is explained. There are four categories of Nabhasa Yogas. Among them, the "Pattern" Yogas are one category. The three categories are Pattern Yogas, Numerical Yogas, and Positional Yogas. Or, as a fourfold classification: Pattern Yogas, Numerical Yogas, Positional Yogas, and Group Yogas. Within these, there are twenty Pattern Yogas, seven Numerical Yogas, three Positional Yogas, and two Group Yogas. Regarding the knowledge of the total number of these yogas arising from two, three, or four combinations, the author speaks in the *Aupachhandasika* meter:

->Nine, ten, and eight, multiplied by<-
->three, three, and four,<-
->give the combinations of two, three, and four.<-
->The Greeks <note>original: "Yavanas"</note> say these tripled make eighteen hundred;<-
->here, they are stated in brief. || 1 ||<-

Regarding "Nine, ten, etc.": The number nine is well-known; by the word "directions" <note>original: "Dik"</note>, ten is meant; by "Vasus," eight is meant. These are multiplied respectively by "three, fire, and Vedas." By the word "three" <note>original: "Trika"</note>, three is meant; by "fire" <note>original: "Agni"</note>, three; and by "Vedas," four. These are the multipliers. Thus: Nine, ten, and eight (9, 10, 8) multiplied respectively by three, three, and four (3, 3, 4) result in (27, 30, 32). These are the results of the two, three, and fourfold combinations respectively. 

This is what is being said: There are twenty Pattern Yogas and seven Numerical Yogas; thus, by the dual combination of Pattern and Numerical, there are twenty-seven yogas. There are three Positional Yogas; with the triple combination of Pattern, Numerical, and Positional, there are thirty (30). There are two Group Yogas; with the fourfold combination of Pattern, Numerical, Positional, and Group, there are thirty-two (32). Thus, the combinations of two, three, and four are produced. 

Regarding "The Greeks say these tripled make eighteen hundred": The ancient Greeks <note>original: "Purana-Yavanas"</note> have stated that these tripled result in eighteen hundred (1800) yogas. Now, what was said by Sphujidhvaja? It is said that the Nabhasa Yogas are infinite. As his statement goes:
> "The similarity of patterns is infinite, seeing that substances are of diverse natures."

If so, how did the ancient Greeks state there are eighteen hundred? It is explained: they described twenty-three Pattern Yogas and one hundred and twenty-seven Numerical Yogas. Thus, there are one hundred and fifty in total. Each of these was stated in relation to a single sign being the Ascendant <note>term: Lagna (the rising sign or Ascendant)</note>. Therefore, by the twelve signs of the zodiac, there are eighteen hundred yogas, because one hundred and fifty multiplied by twelve equals eighteen hundred. The origin of these—

# Chapter on Nabhasa Yogas in the Brihat Jataka

We shall demonstrate [these variations] at the end of the chapter. This is because the meaning of the chapter is easily understood once the core concepts are known. In this manner, the Yavana <note>Ancient Greek or Ionian astronomers/astrologers influential in early Indian astrology</note> masters have described six hundred tripled <note>original: "tri-guna shat-shati" meaning 1800</note> variations in great detail. In this treatise, a summary or condensation of those is being made. It is said that the essence of that expansion is being stated here. Only the thirty-two previously shown are mentioned because the results of the others are similar to these. All eighteen hundred yogas are included within these thirty-two combinations. | 1 |

**Vernacular Translation—** (In this twelfth chapter, regarding the four categories of yogas) two categories combined make 27 (3x9); three categories combined make 30 (3x10); and all four categories combined result in only 32 yogas. The ancient Yavanas spoke of 1800 variations of these. We have stated them here in brief. || 1 ||

**Special Meaning—** There are 20 Configuration Yogas (*Akriti*), 7 Numerical Yogas (*Sankhya*), 3 Positional Yogas (*Ashraya*), and 2 Partial Yogas (*Dala*). Among these, combining two categories results in 27, three results in 30, and all four result in 32, which are described hereafter.

According to the ancient Yavana teachers, there are 23 Configuration Yogas. By applying the permutations of the 7 planets in groups of one, two, three, etc., using the methods of <term>Arithmetic (Patiganita)</term>—such as "place the numbers in increasing order, divide the last by the first, and multiply sequentially"—or by the methods of calculating variations mentioned in the <term>Varaha Samhita</term> <note>A foundational encyclopedic text by Varahamihira</note>, there are a total of 127 variations from one to seven. Thus, combining Numerical and Configuration yogas, there are 150 variations. If there are 150 in one Ascendant (*Lagna*), how many are there in twelve? By this ratio, 150 x 12 = 1800 variations of yogas occur. However, all of these are subsumed within the 32 yogas described by <term>Varahamihira</term> <note>The 6th-century author of this text</note>. Therefore, the Teacher mentions only the 32 primary yogas here.

In the twelve-sign zodiac of the sky (within the twelve houses starting from the Ascendant), the results are produced according to the specific shape or configuration formed by the placement of the planets. Therefore, 20 yogas are named "Configuration" (*Akriti*) yogas.

Furthermore, because they are formed based on the refuge of Moveable, Fixed, and Dual signs, 3 yogas are named "Positional" (*Ashraya*). Additionally, 2 yogas are formed by the presence of benefics or malifics in the Angles (*Kendras*). Therefore, each of these two is called a "Partial" (*Dala*) yoga. Finally, 7 yogas are designated as "Numerical" (*Sankhya*) based on the number of signs (from 1 onwards) occupied by the planets.

**Note—** To avoid making the book excessively long, the visual diagrams of all yogas are not shown; only the diagrams of a few yogas are shown in their respective places. || 1 ||

# Page 256
## Commentary by Bhattotpala with Hindi Translation

**The Rope, the Pestle, and the Reed:** By the movable and other signs—meaning the combinations of planets situated in movable, fixed, and dual signs respectively—three yogas known as **Rope** (<term>Rajju: a rope or cord</term>), **Pestle** (<term>Mushala: a wooden pestle used for grinding</term>), and **Reed** (<term>Nala: a hollow reed or tube</term>) are formed. 

Specifically, when all planets are situated in one, two, three, or four movable signs, and the fixed and dual signs are entirely empty of planets, the yoga called **Rope** occurs. Similarly, when all planets are in one, two, three, or four fixed signs, and the movable and dual signs are empty, the yoga called **Pestle** occurs. Likewise, when all planets are in one, two, three, or four dual signs, and the movable and fixed signs are empty, the yoga called **Reed** occurs. These three "Support-based" (<term>Ashraya</term>) yogas were declared by the teacher Satyacharya. Some read the text as "Satya spoke of the Support-based yogas in this chapter." 

Thus says Satya:
> "When all planets are in movable signs, he called that yoga **Rope**. One born under this is constantly fond of wandering and earns wealth in foreign lands. When all planets are in fixed signs, he called that yoga **Pestle**. It is the birth-sign of workers who are endowed with wealth and honor. In dual signs, the yoga is **Reed**; it belongs to those with deficient or extra limbs <note>This may refer to physical disabilities or perhaps metaphorical 'reach'</note>, who are clever and enjoy accumulated wealth."

Some have interpreted this to mean all planets must occupy all four signs of a category simultaneously. This is incorrect. As the venerable Garga says:
> "When one, two, three, or all four movable signs are occupied by planets, the movable yoga is **Rope**, giving birth to those who are travelers. If fixed, it is **Pestle**, creating prideful men. If dual, it is **Reed**, celebrated for creating wealthy men."

Thus the three Support-based yogas are explained according to the school of Satya. As Satya further states:
> "With the lords of the planets in movable signs, it is Rope; in fixed signs, Pestle; and in dual signs, the yoga is named Reed by the sages."

### The Two Branch Yogas
Now the two **Branch Yogas** (<term>Dala Yogas</term>) are described. By the "centers" (<term>Kendras: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</term>) being joined by "good" or "bad" planets respectively, the Branch Yogas named **Garland** (<term>Sragmala</term>) and **Serpent** (<term>Sarpa</term>) occur. 

This means: when the benefic planets—Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus—occupy any three of the centers, and no malefic planet is in any center, the yoga is **Garland**. Conversely, when the malefic planets—the Sun, Mars, and Saturn—occupy the centers and no benefic planet is in any center, the yoga is **Serpent**. 

One might ask: why is it interpreted that these occur in "three" centers when the text simply says "centers joined by good or bad"? <note>The commentator is addressing a technical debate on whether all four centers must be occupied or just three.</note>
