# The Chapter on the Nature of the Moon in the Zodiac Signs in the *Brihat Jataka* <note>The *Brihat Jataka* is a foundational 6th-century Sanskrit text on Vedic astrology written by Varahamihira.</note>

**The neck of a young camel...** <note>original: "karabhagala"</note> He whose neck is like that of a camel, whose veins are prominent <note>original: "shiralu"</note>, and whose body is covered in coarse, rough hair. He possesses a tall, elongated frame with broad feet, thighs, back, buttocks, face, and waist. Such a person is stubborn or foolish <note>original: "jaratha"</note> and is constantly engaged with the wives of others, the wealth of others, and sinful deeds. His fortune is subject to constant rise and fall. He is a lover of flowers, fragrant ointments <note>original: "anulepana"</note>, and friends. He has the endurance for long journeys. These are the traits of one born when the Moon is in the sign of the Water-bearer <note>Aquarius/Kumbha</note>. ||11||

**Vernacular Translation—** A person born in the sign of Aquarius has a neck like a camel, visible veins, a rough and hairy body, and long legs. They have a broad waist, face, and back. They are foolish, attracted to other men's wives and wealth, prone to sinful acts, experience fluctuations in wealth, love flowers and perfumes, and enjoy traveling. ||11||

### Now, the author describes the nature of one born with the Moon in Pisces using the *Malini* meter:

->**He enjoys wealth from water and others, loves his wife and fine clothes,**<-
->**Possesses a well-proportioned, radiant body, a prominent nose, and a large head.**<-
->**He overcomes his enemies, is conquered by women, has beautiful eyes,**<-
->**Enjoys hidden treasures and wealth, and is learned—this is one born in the final sign.**<- ||12||

**He enjoys wealth from water and others...** This means he is the master or consumer of wealth derived from water—such as pearls or profits from maritime trade—as well as the wealth of others. He is devoted to his wife <note>original: "dara"</note> and fond of fine clothing. His body is symmetrical, complete in all its parts, and possesses a healthy glow. He has a high, prominent nose and a broad forehead <note>original: "brihatka"</note>. He defeats or overcomes his rivals and enemies. He is "conquered by women" <note>meaning he is deeply influenced or led by them</note>. He is a consumer of "treasures" <note>original: "nidhi"</note>—referring to wealth hidden beneath the earth—and is a scholar <note>original: "pandita"</note> well-versed in the meaning of the scriptures. Such are the qualities of one born in the final sign <note>Pisces/Meena</note> when the Moon resides there. ||12||

**Vernacular Translation—** One born in the sign of Pisces enjoys wealth produced from water (like pearls) and the wealth of others. He is fond of women and clothes, has a medium-sized beautiful body, a high nose, and a large head...

<page-num>317</page-num>
<header>With the Sanskrit commentary of Bhattotpala and the Hindi vernacular explanation</header>

...he becomes a conqueror of enemies, is submissive to women, possesses beautiful eyes, enjoys splendor and wealth derived from treasures <note>original: "nidhi" - refers to mineral wealth or hidden treasures</note>, and is a learned scholar. || 12 ||

Now, he describes the nature of the aforementioned signs and the exceptions using the *Bhramaravilasita* meter—

->**When the sign is powerful, and its lord is also strong,**<-
->**and if the Moon <note>original: "tuhināṃśu" - literally 'the cold-rayed one'</note> is endowed with its own strength,**<-
->**then it is the full giver of the stated results;**<-
->**other planets should also be considered in the same manner as the Moon.**<- || 13 ||

*Thus ends the seventeenth chapter, titled "The Character of the Moon's Signs," in the Brihat Jataka composed by the venerable teacher Varahamihira.* || 17 ||

**Commentary:** Regarding "When the sign is powerful"—at the time of a person's birth, if the zodiac sign in which the Moon is situated is strong, and the lord of that sign is also strong, and the Moon itself is endowed with its own inherent strength <note>referring to positional or temporal strength mentioned previously</note>, then the person born will fully manifest the characteristics of that sign as described. As it is said: "the full giver of the stated results." With this combination of factors, the Moon provides the complete and undiminished results of the described nature. If only two of these three factors are strong, a moderate degree of the nature is obtained. If only one is strong, the result is minimal, and if none are strong, the described nature does not manifest at all. Regarding "In the same manner as the Moon"—just as with the Moon, the remaining planets (Sun, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn) should be evaluated. They will grant results based on the signs they occupy, just like the Moon. This means: when the sign is strong, its lord is strong, and the planet whose sign-results are being read is also strong, the full nature of that sign is realized. If strength is lacking, the results are diminished accordingly. This concludes the nature of the Moon's signs. || 13 ||

*Thus ends the seventeenth chapter, titled "The Character of the Moon's Signs," in the Commentary on the Brihat Jataka composed by the venerable Bhattotpala.* || 17 ||

**Vernacular Language <note>Hindi</note>** — If at the time of birth the sign in which the Moon is placed, its lord, and the Moon itself are all three endowed with strength, then the stated results should be understood to manifest in full. It follows that if two of these are strong, the result is somewhat less; if only one is strong, it is half; and if all are weak, the result is very slight. In this same way (similar to the Moon), one should issue predictions for other planets by adjusting the proportions of their effects. || 13 ||

<term>Moon's Sign</term>: The zodiac sign (Rashi) occupied by the Moon at birth, central to Indian astrology.
<term>Strength (Bala)</term>: A technical calculation in astrology to determine how effectively a planet can deliver its results.

It also notes that these rules for the Moon apply to all other planets.</summary>

# Now begins the Chapter on the Nature of the Signs (Chapter 18)

*Now, the author describes the nature of a person born when the Sun is in Aries or Taurus, using the Aupachhandasika meter:*

**Famous, clever, wandering, and of modest means; if in Aries, he bears arms, provided it is not in the degree of exaltation.**
**In Taurus, he earns through clothing, perfumes, and trade; he is a hater of women and skilled in song and instrumental music. ||1||**

"Famous" etc. — A person born when the Sun is in Aries is famous (renowned), clever (dexterous), a wanderer (inclined to travel), possesses little wealth (limited means), and is a bearer of weapons (earning a living through arms). This specific result applies "provided it is not in the degree of exaltation" <note>The Sun is most powerful at 10 degrees of Aries</note>. If the Sun is in Aries but not at that highest point of exaltation, these results follow. However, if it is at the peak exaltation, the negative traits do not apply. For instance, instead of having little wealth, he becomes very wealthy; he is not a mere wanderer, and he does not carry weapons himself—rather, others who carry weapons follow him as his attendants. The other qualities, like being famous and clever, remain. "In Taurus" etc. — He lives by trading in garments (clothes), fragrant substances (perfumes), and merchandise. He is a "hater of women" (dislikes or is disliked by women) and is "skilled" (trained) in singing and the methods of playing musical instruments. Such is the person born with the Sun in Taurus. ||1||

<gloss>Translation: If at the time of birth the Sun is in Aries, but away from its highest point of exaltation (10 degrees), the person is famous, clever, a traveler, has little money, and carries weapons. This implies that if the Sun is exactly at the highest exaltation (the 10th degree), the "inferior" results (like low wealth or being a common soldier) do not occur; instead, in the highest exaltation, the person is very rich and has armed followers. If the Sun is in Taurus, the person trades in clothes and perfumes (attar, etc.), dislikes women, and is an expert in singing and music. ||1||</gloss>

*Now, the nature of one born with the Sun in Gemini, Cancer, Leo, and Virgo is described*
->using the Shardulavikridita meter:<-

**With the Sun in Gemini, one is learned, an astrologer, and wealthy. When in Cancer,**
**one is harsh, poor, does the work of others, and is joined with the fatigue and pain of the road.**
**In Leo, one delights in forests, mountains, and cattle-sheds, is full of valor, but ignorant. In Virgo,**
**one is endowed with knowledge of scripts, writing, poetry, and mathematics, and possesses a feminine body. ||2||**

"Knowledge" etc. — One born with the Sun in Gemini is "learned" (a scholar), an "astrologer" (knower of the science of the stars), and "wealthy" (rich). "Harsh" (fierce), "poor" (destitute), "doing the work of others" (a servant to others), and joined with labor...

# Commentary on the Sun’s Transit through the Zodiac
## Page 316

-> [The Sun in Cancer, Leo, and Virgo] <-

By the hardships of the road, by exertion, and by exhaustion—just as one is joined with the pains and sorrows of travel at all times—such is the person born when the Sun is in **Cancer** <note>Sanskrit: *Kulira* or *Karkata*</note>.

Regarding the Sun in **Leo**: One who delights in the forest, the mountains, and the cow-pen <note>Sanskrit: *Gokula*</note>; one who is inclined to reside in these places and is attached to them. Such a person born with the Sun in Leo is endowed with strength but is ignorant <note>Sanskrit: *Ajna*, meaning unlearned or foolish</note>.

One who is endowed with the skills of writing <note>Sanskrit: *Lipi*, the arrangement of letters</note>, painting <note>Sanskrit: *Lekhyam*</note>, poetry <note>the work of a poet</note>, mathematics <note>including the calculation of planetary movements</note>, and scientific knowledge; one who possesses a body like that of a woman—such is the person born when the Sun is in **Virgo**. **2**

**Vernacular Translation—**
If the Sun is in **Gemini**, the native is a scholar, an astrologer, and wealthy. If the Sun is in **Cancer**, they are of a fierce temperament, poor, a servant to others' work, and a partaker of distress from labor and travel. If the Sun is in **Leo**, they love forests, mountains, and cattle-rearing, and are strong but foolish. If the Sun is in **Virgo**, they are knowledgeable in painting, writing, poetry, and mathematics, and have a physical form resembling a woman. **2**

### Now, the nature of one born with the Sun in Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, and Capricorn is told in the *Shardulavikridita* meter:

> **Born in Libra, one is a vintner, fond of travel, a goldsmith, and a doer of base deeds;**
> **In Scorpio, one is cruel, reckless, earning wealth through poison (1), and skilled in weapons.**
> **In Sagittarius, one is honored by the good, wealthy, sharp, a physician, and a craftsman;**
> **In Capricorn, one is of low character, ignorant, a petty merchant, of little wealth, greedy, and intent on the fortune of others. 3**

**Commentary:**
*A Vintner:* One who sells liquor, or according to some, one who manufactures it. *Fond of travel:* Attached to the road. *A Goldsmith:* A worker in gold. *A doer of base deeds:* One who performs improper actions. Such is the person born when the Sun is in **Libra**.

*Cruel:* Of a fierce nature. *Reckless:* One who acts without deliberation. As it is said: "One who performs actions without foresight is remembered as reckless." *Wealth earned through poison:* One who has accumulated wealth through the use of poisons. In another reading, *Wealth earned in vain:* Whatever wealth he earns becomes useless to him, as thieves and others take it away. *Skilled in weapons:* One who has reached the end <note>mastery</note> of the science of weapons and tools. Such is the person born when the Sun is in **Scorpio**.

*Honored by the good:* Worthy of worship by virtuous people. *Wealthy:* Possessed of riches. *Sharp:* Of fierce actions. *A Physician:* Knowledgeable in medical practice. *A Craftsman:* Skilled in the manual arts. Such is the person born when the Sun is in **Sagittarius**.

*Low:* One who performs unrighteous deeds unsuited to their family. *Ignorant:* Foolish. *A petty merchant:* <note>The text breaks off here</note>

(1) There is also a reading "Wealth earned in vain," meaning wealth that is acquired fruitlessly.

For instance, if in Aries, on the head; if in Taurus, on the face, and so forth. || 4 ||

## Now, he describes the nature of one born when Mars is in Aries, Scorpio, Taurus, or Libra, using the *Trotaka* meter:

> Honored by kings, a wanderer, a commander, a merchant, wealthy,
> With a scarred body, a thief, and having many sensory pursuits—thus is Mars in its own house.
> Conquered by women, treacherous to friends, devoted to others' wives,
> Deceitful, well-dressed, timid, and harsh—thus Mars in the signs of Venus. ||5||

**Honored by kings** etc. **Honored by kings** means respected by royalty; **a wanderer** means having a habit of traveling; **a commander** means a leader of an army; **a merchant** means one skilled in buying and selling; **wealthy** means endowed with riches; **scarred body** means a wounded or scarred physique; **a thief** means a robber; **having many sensory pursuits** <note>original: bhūri-viṣaya</note> means one whose senses are scattered or intensely engaged with worldly objects. Mars <note>Kuja/Bhauma</note> produces such individuals when situated in its own houses, Aries and Scorpio. **Conquered by women** means submissive to women; **to friends** means among companions; **treacherous** <note>original: viṣama</note> means difficult to deal with or having a cruel nature; **devoted to others' wives** means attached to the wives of others; **deceitful** <note>original: kuhakajña</note> means a magician or illusionist; **well-dressed** means wearing beautiful ornaments; **timid** means a fearful person; **harsh** <note>original: karkaśa</note> means lacking in affection or rough. Mars situated in the signs of Venus <note>Sita-bha</note>, namely Taurus and Libra, would produce such men. ||5||

**Vernacular Translation**—If Mars is in Aries or Scorpio, the person born receives honors from the king, is fond of wandering, becomes an army commander, a businessman, and a wealthy man. If Mars is in Taurus or Libra, it produces a man who is under the control of women, deceives his friends, is attached to other men's wives, knows the art of illusion <note>magic</note>, wears beautiful clothes, is cowardly, and is harsh in speech. ||5||

## Now, he describes the nature of one born when Mars is in Gemini, Virgo, or Cancer, using the *Vasantatilaka* meter:

**In the signs of Mercury** etc. **Powerful** <note>original: asaha</note> means energetic/splendid; **having sons** means endowed with children; **friendless** means devoid of friends; **grateful** means having a nature that remembers favors; **skilled in music and war** means skilled in <term>Gandharva</term> <note>the traditional science of music and celestial arts</note> and in battle, such as in the tactics of entering, exiting, and forming military arrays; **stingy** means one who does not give; **fearless** means brave; **a beggar** <note>original: arthī</note> means one given to requesting or seeking—such is one born when Mars is in the signs of Mercury, Gemini and Virgo. Now he describes the nature of one born when Mars is in Cancer. **In the sign of the Moon** etc. **Wealthy** means possessed of riches; **earning money through water-travel** means wealth well-earned by means of water-craft such as boats, or by traveling via water routes...

### Afflicted by grief, penniless, a wanderer, devoted to falsehood, and sharp/harsh when in Aquarius;
### In Capricorn, Mars makes one possessor of great wealth and many children, a king, or equal to a king. ||7||

**Poor** means destitute; **enduring distress** means courageous in calamity or able to withstand hardship; **wandering in forests** means one who moves through the middle of the wilderness; some read this as "fearless forest-dweller." **Fearless** means without fear; **wandering in forests** means a forest-goer; **few wives and children** means having a small family—such is one born with Mars in Leo. **Many enemies** means having numerous foes; **royal minister** means a counselor; **famous** means of known reputation; **fearless** means undaunted; **few children** means having little progeny—such is one born with Mars in the signs of Sagittarius or Pisces. **Afflicted by grief** means constantly tormented by sorrow; **penniless** means poor; **wanderer** means having a roaming nature; **devoted to falsehood** means a liar; **sharp** means indifferent or cruel—such is one born with Mars in Aquarius. **Great wealth and children** means abundant riches and many sons; **a king** or **equal to a king** means a ruler or someone of similar status—such is one born when Mars has entered Capricorn. This concludes the nature of Mars in the signs. ||7||

**Vernacular Translation—** If at the time of birth Mars is in the sign of Leo, the person is poor, endures suffering, wanders in the jungle, and has few wives and few sons. If Mars is in Sagittarius or Pisces, he has many enemies, is a minister to a king, is famous, fearless, and has few sons. If Mars is in Aquarius, he is troubled by sorrow, wealthless, a wanderer, a liar, and of a fierce temperament. If Mars is in Capricorn, he has much wealth and many sons, and is a king or like a king. ||7||

## Now, he describes the nature of one born with Mercury in Aries, Scorpio, Libra, or Taurus, using the Vasantatilaka meter—

->Devoted to gambling, debt, and drinking; atheistic, a thief, and destitute;<-
->Having a wicked wife, a deceiver, and devoted to falsehood—these are the traits in the signs of Mars.<-
->A teacher, with many children and wives, desiring the acquisition of wealth;<-
->Generous and devoted to the service of elders—these are the traits in the signs of Venus when occupied by Mercury. || 8 ||<-

**Regarding "Devoted to gambling" etc.**—One who is devoted to gambling (knowledge of dice), debt (taking others' property), and drinking; an atheist (one who has strayed from the meaning of the scriptures, a sophist who believes there is no afterlife); a thief; destitute (poor); having a wicked wife (a contemptible spouse); a deceiver (a hypocrite or forger); and devoted to falsehood (a speaker of untruths). Such are those born when Mercury <note>Sanskrit: *Saumya*, the son of the Moon</note> is in the signs of Mars <note>Sanskrit: *Bhaumarksha*</note>, namely Aries or Scorpio. **Regarding "A teacher" etc.**—A teacher (one who gives instruction); having many children; having many wives; one for whom the acquisition of wealth is desired, or who is constantly striving for gain; generous (a giver); and devoted to the service of elders (devoted to mother, father, and teachers). Such men are born when Mercury is in the signs of Venus <note>Sanskrit: *Shaukra*</note>, namely Taurus or Libra. || 8 ||

**Vernacular Translation—** If at the time of birth Mercury is in the sign of Aries or Scorpio, the native is a gambler, a debtor, a drinker, an atheist, a thief, poor, possesses a wicked wife, is a forger, and a liar. If Mercury is in Taurus or Libra, the native is a teacher, has many sons, many wives, earns much wealth, is large-hearted, and is a devotee of elders (parents, etc.). || 8 ||

## Now, he describes the nature of one born with Mercury in Gemini or Cancer, using the Upendravajra meter—

->A boaster, skilled in scriptures and arts, speaking kindly, and devoted to pleasure in the third sign.<-
->Earning wealth through water, and an enemy to his own kin, when the son of the Moon is joined with the sign of the Moon. || 9 ||<-

**Regarding "A boaster" etc.**—A boaster (talkative or one who speaks untruths); skilled in scriptures and arts (educated in the scriptures and the arts such as singing, instrumental music, dance, sports, and painting); a speaker of pleasant things (one who speaks what is liked); and devoted to pleasure. Such a person is born when the son of the Moon <note>Mercury</note> is in the third sign, Gemini. **Regarding "Earning wealth through water" etc.**—One who has earned wealth through water (aquatic products or maritime trade). Some read this as "earned wealth through strength" <note>Sanskrit: *balārjitasva*</note>, meaning wealth acquired through power or heroism. An enemy to his own people (a foe to his kinsmen and relatives). Such a person is born when the son of the Moon is in the sign of the Moon <note>Sanskrit: *Shitakararksha*</note>, which is Cancer. || 9 ||

**Vernacular Translation—** If Mercury is in the sign of Gemini, the native is a great talker (loquacious), a knower of scriptures and arts, speaks pleasantly, and is happy.

...is. If Mercury is in Cancer, the person earns wealth from water-born goods <note>such as pearls, shells, or salt</note> and becomes an enemy to his own kinsmen. ||9||

*Now, the author describes the nature of one born with Mercury in Leo or Virgo using the Praharshini meter:*

->**Hated by women, lacking wealth, happiness, and children; a wanderer, ignorant,**<-
->**Lustful, and disgraced by his own people when Mercury is in the Sun's sign (Leo).**<-
->**Generous, learned, possessing many virtues, happy, patient,**<-

**Commentary:** *Hated by women* means disliked by females. *Lacking wealth, happiness, and children* indicates one who is poor, devoid of joy, and without offspring. *A wanderer* is one prone to roaming. *Ignorant* means foolish. *Lustful* indicates a desire for women. *Disgraced by his own* means suffering insults from his own relatives. These traits occur when Mercury is in the Sun's sign, Leo. 

Conversely, *Generous* means a giver. *Learned* means a scholar. *Possessing many virtues* refers to qualities like education and bravery. *Happy* means contented. *Patient* means enduring. *Skillful in means* <note>original: "Yuktijna"</note> means one who knows how to apply methods or logic. *Fearless* means brave. These traits occur when Mercury is in the sixth sign, Virgo. ||10||

**Vernacular Translation—** If Mercury is in the sign of Leo, the person is an enemy to women, devoid of wealth, happiness, and children, a wanderer, a fool, lecherous (desiring others' wives), and is disregarded by his own people. If Mercury is in the sign of Virgo, he is a donor, a scholar, endowed with many virtues, happy, forgiving, knowledgeable in tactics, and fearless. ||10||

*Now, the author describes the nature of one born with Mercury in Capricorn, Aquarius, Sagittarius, or Pisces using the Aupachchandasika meter:*

->**A servant to others, poor, having a craftsman's mind,**<-
->**Indebted, and a laborer when Mercury is in Saturn's signs.**<-
->**Honored by kings, a scholar, trusted in speech in the ninth sign (Sagittarius);**<-
->**In the last sign (Pisces), he is a master of servants but a lowly craftsman. ||11||**<-

**Commentary:** *A servant to others* means one who performs tasks for others. *Poor* means indigent. *Having a craftsman's mind* means an intellect inclined toward manual arts or trades. *Indebted* means one prone to taking others' money. *A laborer* <note>original: "Vishtikara"</note> means a menial worker. These traits occur when Mercury is in Saturn's signs, Capricorn or Aquarius. 

*Honored by kings* means respected by royalty or a royal favorite. *Scholar* means learned. *Trusted in speech* means one whose words are reliable in business or law. These traits occur when Mercury is in the ninth sign, Sagittarius. 

*Master of servants* <note>original: "Jitasevaka"</note> means one who has conquered or effectively manages servants, or one skilled in understanding the intentions of others. *Lowly craftsman* means one engaged in inferior trades. These traits occur when Mercury is in the last sign, Pisces. Thus ends the section on the nature of Mercury in the various signs. ||11||

### Now, the nature of a person born with Jupiter in Aries, Scorpio, Taurus, Libra, Gemini, or Virgo is described in the Shardulavikridita meter:

**A leader of armies, possessing much wealth, wives, and sons; a giver, having good servants, and patient;**
**Endowed with brilliance and the virtues of a wife; a famous man is born when the Teacher of the Gods is in the signs of Mars.**
**With a healthy body, possessing wealth, friends, and sons; a renouncer and beloved when in the signs of Venus.**
**In the signs of Mercury, one possesses many possessions, children, and friends; engaged in ministry and happy. ||12||**

**The Commentary:** *A leader of armies* means a general. *Much wealth* means abundant riches. *Many wives* means many spouses. *Many sons* means abundant progeny. *A giver* means charitable by nature. *Good servants* means excellent attendants. *Patient* means possessing forgiveness. *Endowed with brilliance* means with luster, and *virtues of a wife* refers to the happiness derived from a spouse. *Famous* means of celebrated renown. Such a person is born when the Teacher of the Gods <term>Suraguru: a title for Jupiter, the preceptor of the deities</term>, is in the signs of Mars <note>original: "kaujbe"</note>, namely Aries or Scorpio.

*With a healthy body* means a sound physique. *Possessing wealth* means wealthy. *With friends* means having companions. *With sons* means endowed with children. Thus, one is joined with happiness, wealth, friends, and sons. *A renouncer* means a donor. *Beloved* means dear to all people. Such a person is born when Jupiter is in the signs of Venus <note>original: "shaukrabhe"</note>, namely Taurus or Libra.

*In the signs of Mercury* etc.: *Many possessions* means many clothes, houses, and family members. *Many children* means many sons. *Many friends* means abundant companions. *Engaged in ministry* means appointed to the post of a counselor or minister <note>sachivya: the state or office of a minister</note>. *Happy* means one who is joyful. Such a person is born when Jupiter is in the signs of Mercury <note>original: "baudhe"</note>, namely Gemini or Virgo. ||12||

**Vernacular Translation:** If Jupiter is in Aries or Scorpio, the person is a commander, possessing much wealth, many wives, and many sons; a donor, having good servants, patient, endowed with luster and marital happiness, and a famous man. If Jupiter is in Taurus or Libra, the person has a strong body, is wealthy, endowed with happiness, friends, and sons, a donor, and beloved by all. If Jupiter is in Gemini or Virgo, the person possesses many clothes, many sons and friends, is a royal minister, and is happy. ||12||

### Now, the nature of a person born with Jupiter in Cancer, Leo, Sagittarius, Pisces, Aquarius, or Capricorn is described in the Shardulavikridita meter:

**In the sign of the Moon, one is endowed with gems, sons, wealth, a wife, power, wisdom, and happiness.**
**In Leo, one becomes a leader of forces, and possesses those qualities mentioned for the Moon's sign.**

# Brihat Jataka: Chapter on the Nature of the Signs
<page-num>326</page-num>

**In its own sign, one becomes a provincial ruler, a royal minister, a general, or wealthy.**
**In Aquarius, the results are like Cancer; in Capricorn, one is base, has little wealth, and is unhappy. ||13||**

Regarding the Moon's sign: "Gems" refers to jewels; "sons" to male offspring; "own" to wealth; "wives" to spouses; "glory" to power; "wisdom" to intelligence; "happiness" to a state of comfort. One born when Jupiter is in the Moon’s sign (Cancer) is endowed with these. A "leader of forces" is a commander-in-chief. Furthermore, the qualities mentioned for Cancer—being endowed with gems, sons, wealth, wives, glory, wisdom, and happiness—also apply when Jupiter is in Leo. A "provincial ruler" <term>Mandallika: a governor or ruler of a specific territory</term>, a commander of an army, or a wealthy person is born when Jupiter is in its own signs (Sagittarius or Pisces). "In Aquarius, like Cancer" means that the results declared for Jupiter in Cancer—being endowed with gems, sons, wealth, wives, glory, wisdom, and happiness—also occur when Jupiter is in Aquarius. <note>The commentator notes a disagreement here with other authorities who might suggest unfavorable results for Aquarius.</note> Thus, it is said: "In Aquarius, it produces one attached to works related to water." One who is "base" performs unrighteous deeds unsuited to their lineage; "little wealth" means having meager means; "unhappy" means distressed. Such is a person born with Jupiter in Capricorn. This concludes the nature of Jupiter in the signs. ||13||

**Vernacular Translation—** If Jupiter is in Cancer, the native is endowed with gems, sons, wealth, women, glory, intellect, and all comforts. If Jupiter is in Leo, all the results mentioned for Cancer apply, and the person becomes a general. If Jupiter is in Sagittarius or Pisces, the person becomes a provincial ruler (governor), a royal minister, a general, or wealthy. If Jupiter is in Aquarius, understand all results to be the same as Cancer. If Jupiter is in Capricorn, the person is base, penniless, and miserable. ||13||

Now, the author describes the nature of one born with Venus in Aries, Scorpio, Taurus, or Libra in the *Pushpitagra* meter:

->**Devoted to the wives of others, losing wealth through**<-
->**disputes over them, a disgrace to the family in Mars' signs.**<-
**Wealthy through own strength and mind, honored by kings,**
**chief among kin, famous, and fearless when Venus is in its own signs. ||14||**

"Devoted to the wives of others" means attached to other men's wives. "Losing wealth through disputes over them" means their riches are taken away due to legal accusations or speech regarding those women. "A disgrace to the family" means being a blot on one's lineage. Such is a person born when Venus (Shukra) is in the signs of Mars (Aries or Scorpio). "Wealthy through own strength etc.": one whose wealth comes from their own power and their own intelligence or purity of mind; "honored by kings" means a favorite of the sovereign; "chief among kin" means the leader of their relatives; "famous" means well-known; "fearless" means without dread. Such is a person born when Venus is in its own signs (Taurus or Libra). ||14||

If the planet **Venus** <note>Sanskrit: Śukra</note> is situated in the sign of **Sagittarius** <note>Sanskrit: Dhanu</note>, which is associated with the horse, the person born is of such a nature. If Venus is in **Pisces** <note>Sanskrit: Jhaṣa/Mīna</note>, the person becomes **learned** (a scholar), **wealthy** (a lord), and **honored by kings** <note>original: nṛpajanitapūjaḥ; meaning worship or respect produced by the ruler</note>. # Page 326
## Commentary by Bhattotpala with Hindi Translation

Regarding forbidden women... If **Saturn** (the son of the Sun) is positioned in **Taurus**, the person born will be fond of "unapproachable" women <note>original: "agamyasu" - referring to women with whom relations are socially or morally prohibited</note>, will not possess great wealth (having only modest means), but will have many wives. 

If Saturn is in its sign of exaltation, **Libra**, the person is famous (of well-known reputation), honored and respected by groups, cities, armies, and villages, and is wealthy. 

If Saturn is in **Cancer**, the person is poor, has defective or few teeth, is motherless (separated from the mother), childless, and ignorant (foolish). 

Regarding **Leo**: If Saturn is in Leo, the person is "un-Aryan" <note>original: "anarya" - here meaning ignoble, uncivilized, or foolish</note>, dejected (sorrowful), childless, and a laborer or carrier of burdens (a "vistikrit"). ||18||

**Vernacular Translation:** If Saturn is in the sign of Taurus, the native is a lover of forbidden women, possesses little wealth, and is the husband of many women. If Saturn is in Libra, the native is famous among the masses, and is a leader and wealthy man in the city, army, or village. If Saturn is in Cancer, he is penniless, has few teeth or dental disease, is motherless, childless, and a fool. If Saturn is in Leo, he is thoughtless, unhappy, childless, and a carrier of loads. ||18||

Now, the author describes the nature of one born when Saturn is in Sagittarius, Pisces, Capricorn, or Aquarius, using the *Shardulavikridita* meter:

->**If the son of the Sun (Saturn) is in the domain of Jupiter, the man has a good end, is trusted in the royal palace, and possesses good children, a good wife, and wealth; or he is a leader of cities, armies, and villages.**<-
->**If born in his own signs, he is surrounded by the wealth and women of others, is a leader of cities, armies, and villages, but has poor eyesight, is unclean, and possesses stable wealth and enjoyments.**<- ||19||

**Commentary:** "A good end" (*svantah*) means one whose end or death comes through auspicious deeds, or one who has happiness and comfort at the end of life. "Trusted in the royal palace" means he has gained the confidence of the king. He has "good children" (virtuous offspring), a "good wife," and "good wealth." He is a "leader of cities, armies, and villages"—the chief or commander of towns, military forces, and rural settlements. Such is the person born when Saturn is in the "domain of Jupiter" <note>original: "jivakshetra" - referring to the signs ruled by Jupiter: Sagittarius and Pisces</note>.

"Surrounded by the wealth and women of others" means he is associated with or supported by the resources and wives of other men. He is a "leader of cities, armies, and villages" (a primary commander). "Poor eyesight" (*mandadrik*) means having weak eyes. "Unclean" (*malinah*) refers to being covered in dirt or being lazy regarding bathing. "Stable wealth" means his riches and power are enduring...

# The Chapter on the Nature of the Signs

A man born when Saturn is in its own signs <note>Saturn rules Capricorn and Aquarius</note> possesses enduring wealth and power; he is one who enjoys life's pleasures but is not inclined toward hoarding or accumulation. Such is the nature of Saturn’s influence in its own domains. In all these descriptions of planetary signs, the predicted traits manifest fully only if the sign, its ruler, and the planet itself are all strong. If only two or one of these factors are strong, the results are moderate. If none are strong, the results will not manifest at all.

**Vernacular Translation** — If Saturn is positioned in Sagittarius or Pisces, the person will find happiness toward the end of their life. They will be a trusted confidant in royal circles, blessed with virtuous sons and a beautiful wife, and will possess abundant wealth. They may also serve as a leader of a city, an army, or a village. If Saturn is in Capricorn or Aquarius, the person may be associated with the wives or wealth of others, yet will be a leader of a city, army, or village. They may have weak eyesight, a somewhat unkempt appearance, but will possess stable wealth, majesty, and a capacity for enjoyment.

---

Now, using the *Pushpitagra* meter, the author describes how the traits previously mentioned for the Moon in various signs also apply to the Rising Signs (Lagnas) starting from Aries:

->The results described for the Moon’s presence in the signs<-
->are said by the sages to apply equally to the Rising Sign.<-
->However, additional results must be considered here<-
->based on the specific "Houses" and the qualities of their lords.<-

Thus ends the eighteenth chapter, titled "The Nature of the Signs," in the *Brihat Jataka* composed by the Great Teacher Varahamihira.

**Commentary:** Regarding the verse "The results...": The physical and temperamental traits described when the "Cool-Rayed One" <note>The Moon</note> occupies a sign—such as "round, copper-colored eyes" for Aries—should also be predicted for an individual who has that sign as their Rising Sign (Ascendant). This applies to Taurus and all other signs. Sages say the results are similar because the essential nature of the sign does not change. As the sage Satyacharya says:

> "One born with Aries as the Rising Sign may have diseased nails, a quick temper, and a tendency to create divisions or speak with a stammer. They are dominated by the humors of bile and wind <term>Pitta and Vata: two of the three biological energies in Ayurveda</term>, may be stingy, and suffer much physical pain. In childhood, they may be separated from their elders or teachers. They have few children and are helpful to their kinsmen and siblings. They may travel to foreign lands for religious purposes but find their labors bear little fruit. They might marry a woman who is low-born, deceitful, or previously married. Their friends and siblings treat them with the closeness of family. Their end may come through weapons, poison, biliary disorders, fire, rain, or a fall from a difficult height."

When **Taurus** <note>Sanskrit: *Vrishabha*</note> is the rising sign, the person has thick lips, cheeks, and nose, and a large forehead. They are always longing for a spouse, are a destroyer of scriptures <note>or one who goes against traditional learning</note>, and often seize the property of their own kinsmen. Death comes through weapons, nooses, or wild animals in foreign lands.

They have modest intelligence and a small frame, yet are honored by the virtuous and by teachers. They have few siblings, show little effort in physical tasks, are oppressive to others, yet are endowed with good qualities.

Engaged in many types of work, they pursue their goals but not necessarily through righteous means. They acquire various gains but lose them through various faults.

They obtain many wives and suffer from severe diseases. Death comes through serpents, poison, wild animals, or water.

When **Cancer** <note>Sanskrit: *Karka*</note> is the rising sign at the beginning, the person is not driven by a single desire, suffers from private diseases, and is timid. They have a distinctive mark or birthmark on the chest and a temperament of phlegm and wind; they are firm in their grasp.

They associate with wicked and unfriendly people and may lose others' wealth entrusted to them through spending. Though respected by their kin, they are also reproached by them; their offspring are unstable <note>possibly referring to health or longevity of children</note>.

They perform harsh work in foreign lands, are perpetually half-risen <note>struggling for full success</note>, and serve others. They have an unsuitable spouse, are defeated by enemies, yet are honored by assemblies.

Death comes from constriction of the throat, ropes, an excess of phlegm, the breaking of bones, or piercing. Alternatively, death occurs through the cutting of the body or from dropsy <note>Sanskrit: *jalodara*, an accumulation of fluid in the abdomen</note>.

When **Leo** <note>Sanskrit: *Simha*</note> is the rising sign, the person is harsh, fond of meat, of a bilious temperament <note>Sanskrit: *paittika* or Pitta dosha</note>, and has a broad nose. They have a large family to support, are miserly, yet are respected and famous.

They are despondent regarding their siblings, are a destroyer of their own kinsmen, yet are endowed with their own prowess. They are tireless in work and use various means, though they may be unrighteous.

<page-num>334</page-num>
<header>Brihat Jataka: Chapter on the Nature of the Signs</header>

Death [occurs] through men honored by groups or assemblies, or by diseases of the private parts <note>original: "guhyajair-vikarair"; likely referring to hemorrhoids or reproductive ailments</note>, or through the application of knowledge and medicine, or from fasting, or from the perils of the road.

In this way, the results produced by the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at birth</term> are similar to those arising from the Moon's conjunction. Furthermore, the results of the aspects <note>Drishti: planetary "glances" or influences</note> on the sign occupied by the Moon <note>original: "shishirakara"; literally "the cool-rayed one," a poetic name for the Moon</note>, which will be described hereafter, should also be stated for the person born with that same Ascendant. This refers to verses such as "When the Moon is [aspected by] the King or Mercury," etc. 

However, what is the specific result regarding the Ascendant? Whatever "House" <term>Bhava: the twelve astrological houses representing areas of life like body, wealth, etc.</term> is considered here, starting from the Moon-sign, the results in the houses starting from the Ascendant are more significant. These should be contemplated and investigated through the qualities of the signs and the qualities of the lords of those signs. The "quality" of the house and its lord refers to their strength.

This is what is meant: if the Ascendant is strong and the Lord of the Ascendant is strong, the physical nourishment and health of the person born should be declared. If the second sign from the Ascendant is strong and its lord is strong, the person's abundance of wealth should be declared. In the same way, if the remaining signs and their lords are strong, the prosperity of brothers and other relatives should be declared. 

Nevertheless, he mentions a slight distinction: "The opposite is true in the twelfth, sixth, and eighth houses," etc. <note>These are the 'Dusthanas' or difficult houses in Vedic astrology</note>. Thus, if the signs situated in the houses starting from the body (the 1st) are weak, and their lords are weak, the loss or destruction of that house's significance should be declared. If one of the two—the house or the house-lord—is strong, then a middling increase of the house should be stated. As Yavanesvara <note>An ancient authority on Greek-influenced Indian astrology</note> says:

> "Through the nature, superior, middling, or inferior, of the Lord of the House and the planet situated in the House, and by their aspects, the success or calamity of that house reaches its final fruition for men." || 20 ||

->Thus ends the commentary on the Brihat Jataka<-
->composed by the venerable Bhattotpala,<-
->being the eighteenth chapter, titled "The Nature of the Signs." || 18 ||<-

**Vernacular Translation—** Whatever results have been stated for the Moon's conjunctions and aspects in Aries and the other signs, the results for Aries and the other Ascendants are the same. However, there is this specialty regarding the Ascendant: the results of the houses <gloss>Bhavas</gloss> occur according to the qualities of the sign and the sign-lord of the houses starting from the Ascendant.

For example—the results of the Moon in Aries previously mentioned in the verse "Round eyes, copper-colored," etc., as well as the results of aspects mentioned later in "When the Moon is [aspected by] the King or Mercury," etc., should also be understood for the Aries Ascendant. The specialty in house-results is this: if both the sign of a house and the lord of that sign are strong, there is full prosperity of that house; if only one is strong, it is middling; if both are weak, there is loss of the house; and in the 6th, 8th, and 12th houses, the results are reversed. || 20 ||

# Chapter 18: On the Results of Planetary Aspects

Now begins the explanation of the chapter regarding the results of planetary aspects <note>Sanskrit: *Drishti-phala-adhyaya*; 'Drishti' refers to the 'glance' or aspect one planet casts upon another, influencing its effects</note>. In this section, the author describes the nature of a person born when the Moon is situated in Aries, Taurus, Gemini, or Cancer and is aspected by Mars and the other planets, using the *Shardulavikridita* meter:

**When the Moon is in Aries, the results of aspects from Mars and the others are: a king, a scholar, one equal to a king, a virtuous man, a thief, and a pauper.**
**In Taurus: one without wealth, a thief, one honored by men, a king, a wealthy man, and a servant.**
**In Gemini: a dealer in iron, a ruler, a scholar, one who is fearless, a weaver, and a pauper.**
**In its own sign (Cancer): a warrior, a poet, a learned man, a king, one who lives by iron, and one with eye disease. ॥ 1 ॥**

Regarding "When the Moon is in Aries...": The "Mars and the others" refers to the sequence of Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, and the Sun. 

When the Moon is in **Aries** <note>original: *Ajage* or *Mesha*</note>:
- Aspected by Mars: The person becomes a king.
- Aspected by Mercury: A scholar <note>original: *Pandita*</note>.
- Aspected by Jupiter: Equal to a king (such as a high official).
- Aspected by Venus: A virtuous man <note>Some manuscripts read *Vanik*, meaning a merchant</note>.
- Aspected by Saturn: A thief.
- Aspected by the Sun: A pauper.
These results also apply if Aries is the Ascendant <note>Rising sign</note> and is aspected by these planets.

When the Moon is in **Taurus** <note>original: *Gavi* or *Vrisha*</note>:
- Aspected by Mars: One without wealth.
- Aspected by Mercury: A thief.
- Aspected by Jupiter: Honored by men <note>Some read *Nripadhya*, meaning a wealthy lord</note>.
- Aspected by Venus: A king.
- Aspected by Saturn: A wealthy person.
- Aspected by the Sun: A servant or slave.
The same applies to the Taurus Ascendant.

When the Moon is in **Gemini** <note>original: *Nrinsthe* or *Mithuna*</note>:
- Aspected by Mars: A dealer in iron <note>specifically a seller of weapons</note>.
- Aspected by Mercury: A ruler or king.
- Aspected by Jupiter: A scholar.
- Aspected by Venus: Fearless and brave.
- Aspected by Saturn: A weaver <note>term: *Tantuvaya* — a traditional cloth-maker</note>.
- Aspected by the Sun: A pauper.
The same applies to the Gemini Ascendant.

When the Moon is in its **own sign (Cancer)** <note>original: *Swarkshe* or *Karkata*</note>:
- Aspected by Mars: A warrior skilled in combat.
- Aspected by Mercury: A poet.
- Aspected by Jupiter: A learned man.
- Aspected by Venus: A king.
- Aspected by Saturn: One who lives by iron <note>term: *Ayojivi* — one who earns a living through weapons or iron tools</note>.
- Aspected by the Sun: One suffering from eye disease <note>term: *Drig-rogi*</note>.
The same applies to the Cancer Ascendant. ॥ 1 ॥

**Vernacular Explanation:** If the Moon is in Aries and is seen by Mars and the other planets, the person born is respectively a king, a scholar, equal to a king, virtuous, a thief, and poor. That is, by the aspect of Mars—a king; Mercury—a scholar; Jupiter—equal to a king (minister, etc.); Venus—virtuous; Saturn—a thief; and the Sun—poor. The same sequence of planets should be understood for the following signs. In Taurus, the Moon aspected by Mars etc. results in being poor, a thief, respected in the world, a king, wealthy, and a servant. For the Moon in Gemini...

If the Moon is aspected <note>aspected: in astrology, this refers to the angular relationship between planets that "glance" at or influence one another</note> by other planets, the results are, in order: a blacksmith, a king, a scholar, one who is fearless, a weaver, and a poor person. If the Moon is in Cancer and aspected by Mars and the other planets, the person born is, in order: a warrior, a poet, a scholar, a king, a dealer in iron, and one with eye disease. ॥1॥

*Special Meaning—* These same results should also be understood for the Ascendants <term>Lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the time of birth</term> starting from Aries, when aspected by Mars and the others. ॥1॥

---

->Now, the nature of a person born with the Moon in Leo, Virgo, Libra, and Scorpio, aspected by Mercury and others, is described in the Shardulavikridita meter:<-

## **An astrologer, a wealthy man, a king, a barber, and a king again are produced by Mercury and the others in Leo;**
## **Similarly, in the sixth sign (Virgo), a king, a commander, and one with skill; if by the malefic planets, one dependent on women.**
## **In Libra, a king, a goldsmith, and a merchant; if aspected by the remaining, a cruel person.**
## **In Scorpio, a father of twins, one who is humble, a washerman, one with a missing limb, a poor man, and a king. ॥2॥**

*Commentary:* "An astrologer" etc. — The planets Mercury and the others are: Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, the Sun, and Mars. When the Moon is in "Hari" (the sign of Leo) and aspected by Mercury, the person is an astrologer (one who knows the meaning of the science of the stars). If aspected by Jupiter, they are wealthy (a lord). If aspected by Venus, they are a ruler of men (a king). If aspected by Saturn, they are a barber. If aspected by the Sun, they are a sovereign (a king). If aspected by Mars, they are a lord of the earth (a king). This also applies to the Leo Ascendant. "Similarly" etc. — the phrase "aspected by Mercury and the others" follows throughout.

In the sixth sign (Virgo), if the Moon is aspected by Mercury, the person is a king. If aspected by Jupiter, a commander of an army. If aspected by Venus, they are endowed with skill (a subtle vision in all tasks). If aspected by the "malefics" (Saturn, Sun, and Mars), they are "dependent on women"—meaning they live by relying on a woman. This also applies to the Virgo Ascendant.

In "Juka" (Libra), if the Moon is aspected by Mercury, the person becomes a king. If aspected by Jupiter, a goldsmith. If aspected by Venus, a merchant (one who knows buying and selling). If aspected by the "remaining" (Saturn, Sun, and Mars), they are "cruel" (a destroyer of living beings). This also applies to the Libra Ascendant.

In "Kita" (Scorpio), if the Moon is aspected by Mercury, the person is a "father of twins" (the progenitor of a pair). <note>original: "dvipitṛka" - some read this as 'having two fathers'</note>. If aspected by Jupiter, they are humble (bowing). If aspected by Venus, a washerman (one who dyes or cleans clothes). If aspected by Saturn, they are "missing a limb" (physically disabled). If aspected by the Sun, they are "without wealth" (destitute). If aspected by Mars, they are a lord of the earth (a king). This also applies to Scorpio when aspected by these same planets. ॥ 2 ॥

***Vernacular Translation—*** If the Moon is in Leo and aspected by Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, the Sun, and Mars, the person born is, in order: an astrologer, wealthy, a king, a barber, a king, and a lord. If the Moon is in Virgo and aspected by Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus, they are, in order: a king, a minister, and skillful (possessing a subtle intellect in all work). If aspected by the remaining malefic planets—Saturn, Sun, and Mars—they live as a dependent of a woman.

If the Moon is situated in **Libra** and is aspected <note>viewed by a planetary alignment</note> by the benefic planets **Mercury**, **Jupiter**, and **Venus**, the person becomes, respectively, a king, a goldsmith, and a merchant. If aspected by the remaining malefic planets, the person becomes a killer of living beings. If the Moon is in **Scorpio** and is aspected by **Mercury**, **Jupiter**, **Venus**, **Saturn**, the **Sun**, or **Mars**, the person becomes, respectively, a father of two children, humble, a washerman, physically disabled, poor, or a king. These results should be understood according to the sequence of each planet. || 2 ||

---

-> Now, the author describes the nature of a person born with the Moon in **Sagittarius**, **Capricorn**, **Aquarius**, or **Pisces**, aspected by Mercury and others, using the *Shardulavikridita* meter: <-

> If in **Sagittarius**, the person is a protector of kin, a lord of the earth, or a shelter for people; if by malefics, they are hypocritical and wicked. In **Capricorn**, they are a great king, a ruler, a scholar, wealthy, poor, or a king. In **Aquarius**, they are a king, like a king, or devoted to others' wives; the same for the remaining planets. In **Pisces**, they are a humorist, a king, or a scholar; if aspected by malefics, they are sinful. || 3 ||

**Commentary:** Regarding "If in Sagittarius" etc.: If the Moon is in **Sagittarius** <note>original: *turaga*, literally "horse"</note> and aspected by **Mercury**, the person is a <term>protector of kin</term> <note>original: *jñāturīśaḥ*</note>; if aspected by **Jupiter**, they are a <term>lord of the earth (king)</term>; if aspected by **Venus**, they are a <term>shelter for people</term>; if aspected by **malefics** (Saturn, Sun, Mars), they are <term>hypocritical</term> (a false practitioner of religion) and <term>wicked</term> (averse to helping others). This also applies to the **Sagittarius Ascendant**.

If the Moon is in **Capricorn** <note>original: *mṛga*, literally "deer"</note> and aspected by **Mercury**, they become a <term>great king</term> (emperor); if aspected by **Jupiter**, a <term>ruler</term>; if aspected by **Venus**, a <term>scholar</term>; if aspected by **Saturn**, <term>wealthy</term>; if aspected by the **Sun**, <term>poor</term>; and if aspected by **Mars**, a <term>king</term>. This also applies to the **Capricorn Ascendant**.

When the Moon is in **Aquarius** and aspected by **Mercury**, the person is a <term>king</term>. If aspected by **Jupiter**, they are <term>like a king</term>. If aspected by **Venus**, they are <term>devoted to others' wives</term>. Because of the word "and" <note>original: *ca*</note>, the remaining three (Saturn, Sun, Mars) also make one devoted to others' wives. This also applies to the **Aquarius Ascendant**.

When the Moon is in **Pisces** <note>original: *jhaṣage*, literally "fish-dwelling"</note> and aspected by **Mercury**, the person is a <term>humorist</term> (knows how to joke). If aspected by **Jupiter**, they are a <term>king</term>. If aspected by **Venus**, they are a <term>scholar</term> <note>original: *budhaḥ*</note>. The malefics are **Saturn, Sun, and Mars**; if aspected by these, the person is simply <term>sinful</term>. This also applies to the **Pisces Ascendant**.

The results for the Ascendant (Lagna) are stated by extending the results of the Moon: <term>"The results for the birth Ascendant are said to be similar to those of the aspects on the Moon."</term> <note>original: *śiśirakara-samāgamekṣaṇānāṃ...*</note>. In that context, the result of the Moon aspecting the Ascendant was not mentioned. Therefore, it is stated here: <term>"An Ascendant aspected or joined by its own lord, Jupiter, or Mercury, and not by others, is full of strength."</term> Except for **Cancer**, any other Ascendant aspected by the Moon is <term>weak</term>. Being weak, it is unfavorable. As it is said: <term>"Except for the house of the Moon (Cancer), an Ascendant aspected by the Moon is designated as having inauspicious results, whether at the time of a query or at birth."</term> || 3 ||

**Vernacular Translation:** If the Moon in Sagittarius is aspected by Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus, then respectively, the person supports their relatives, is a king, and a shelter for many people...

...becomes a person of refuge. If there is an aspect from malefic planets <note>original: "papagrahas"</note> (Saturn, Sun, Mars), the person becomes a hypocrite (one who falsely displays the banner of religion) and a rogue. When the Moon is in Capricorn and aspected by the six planets starting with Mercury, the results are: a king of kings, a king, a scholar, a wealthy person, a poor person, and a king, respectively. When the Moon is in Aquarius, an aspect from Mercury makes one a king; from Jupiter, one becomes like a king; and from the remaining planets, one becomes an adulterer. When the Moon is in Pisces, an aspect from Mercury makes one fond of humor; from Jupiter, a king; from Venus, a scholar; and from the remaining malefic planets, a sinner. ||3||

### Now, he describes the results of planetary aspects on the Moon when situated in a Hora or Drekkana using the Shardulavikridita meter—

> **The Moon is auspicious when aspected by planets occupying the same half of a sign (Hora) as the Moon itself. It is also praised when aspected by the lords of the decanates (Drekkana) it occupies, or by planets placed in friendly signs. The results previously mentioned for aspects in each sign should also be applied to the twelfth-parts (Dwadashamsha); similarly, the results of the Sun and other planets looking at the Moon should be understood for the ninth-parts (Navamsha). ||4||**

*Explanation of the verse:* By the word "Hora," a half of a zodiac sign is meant. This is based on the statement: "Hora refers to the Ascendant and also to the half of a sign." The phrase "occupying the same half of a sign as the Hora lord" means that the Moon, situated in a particular Hora, becomes auspicious if it is aspected by planets that are also situated in that same Hora. This implies the following: in whichever sign and in whichever Hora the Moon is placed, if it is seen by all planets situated in that same Hora, it becomes auspicious for the birth. Therefore, the Moon in the Sun's Hora, aspected by planets in any sign that are also in the Sun's Hora, is auspicious. Conversely, if it is aspected by those in the Moon's Hora, it is inauspicious. Similarly, the Moon in its own Hora (the Moon's Hora), aspected by planets in the Moon's Hora regardless of their sign, is auspicious; but if aspected by those in the Sun's Hora, it is inauspicious. The same logic regarding the Hora lord should be applied to the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note> as well.

Regarding the phrase "by the lords of those divisions": In whichever sign and in whichever <term>Drekkana</term> <note>a 10-degree division or "decanate" of a sign</note> the Moon is situated, if it is aspected by the lord of that Drekkana, the Moon is "praised," meaning it produces auspicious results. The use of the plural "lords" <note>original: "patibhir"</note> implies that the lords of the <term>Navamsha</term> <note>1/9th division</note>, <term>Dwadashamsha</term> <note>1/12th division</note>, and <term>Trimshamsha</term> <note>1/30th division</note> are also included. The Moon becomes auspicious when aspected by these lords as well. This also applies to the Ascendant. Although stated generally, it is praised specifically when aspected by the lords of these divisions if they are benefic planets; if they are malefic, the result is mediocre. As stated in the author's own *Svalpa Jataka*: "If the Moon is aspected by the lord of the sign, the person is a king; if by the lord's friends, the person is wealthy. Auspicious results generally come from the lords of the Drekkanas and Amshas if they are benefics, but not from others." Regarding "placed in friendly houses": the Moon is praised and auspicious when aspected by planets situated in friendly signs <note>original: "mitra-kshetra"</note>. Likewise, the Moon is praised when aspected by planets situated in their own houses.

# Commentary with Hindi Translation and Sanskrit Notes by Bhattotpala

If the Moon is viewed by planets located in houses belonging to its enemies, it is not praised and yields inauspicious results. The same should be applied to the Ascendant (<term>Lagna</term> - the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon). Whatever results were stated for the aspects in each sign are also remembered to apply to the <term>Dvadasamsa</term> <note>original: "द्वादशांश" - a 1/12th division of a zodiac sign, equaling 2.5 degrees</note>. In every single sign, from Aries onwards, the results described for the Moon being aspected (viewed) by other planets apply equally when the Moon occupies the corresponding 1/12th division of that sign. This is what must be declared. This refers to the previous statements regarding the King, Mercury, and others. This applies to the Ascendant as well. However, excluding the 1/12th division of Cancer, the sight of the Moon by the Sun and others is considered auspicious. Therefore, hereafter, the results of the Moon being aspected by the Sun and other planets while in the <term>Navamsa</term> <note>original: "नवांश" - the 1/9th division of a sign, crucial for determining a planet's true strength</note> divisions should be understood. 4

**Vernacular Translation—** If the Moon is in the <term>Hora</term> <note>original: "होरा" - a 1/2 division of a sign (15 degrees), ruled by either the Sun or the Moon</note> of the Sun, it becomes a giver of auspiciousness when aspected by planets situated in the Sun's Hora. Similarly, if the Moon is in its own Hora (the Moon's Hora), it is auspicious when aspected by planets situated in the Moon's Hora. Otherwise, it is inauspicious. Furthermore, in whichever <term>Drekkana</term> <note>original: "द्रेष्काण" - a 1/3rd division of a sign (10 degrees)</note> or other division the Moon is placed, it is auspicious if aspected by the lord of that division or by planets situated in a friend's sign. The results of aspects mentioned for each sign also apply to the <term>Dvadasamsa</term> of that sign. And whatever results were mentioned for the Moon being aspected by the Sun and other planets should also be understood to apply in the <term>Navamsa</term>. 4

**Special Meaning—** Although it is said that the Moon yields auspicious results when aspected by the lords of the Hora and other divisions it occupies, one should understand that a "benefic" lord gives full auspiciousness, while a "malefic" or "enemy" lord gives diminished results. If the lord of the division is both a malefic planet and an enemy, auspicious results cannot occur. Other such nuances should be inferred even if not explicitly stated. As the Master himself said in the <term>Laghu Jataka</term> <note>original: "लघुजातक" - a concise foundational text on astrology by Varahamihira</note>:

> "When the Moon is aspected by the lord of the sign it occupies, the person becomes a King; if aspected by the lord's friends, they become wealthy. If aspected by the lords of the <term>Drekkana</term> or <term>Navamsa</term>, results are generally auspicious if those lords are benefics, and not otherwise." This is the clear meaning. 4

Now, the author describes the results of the Moon being aspected by the Sun and others while situated in the Navamsas of Aries, Scorpio, Taurus, or Libra, using the *Vasantatilaka* meter:

->If in a Navamsa of Mars, the Moon is aspected by the Sun, one becomes a protector; by Mars, a lover of violence; by Mercury, skilled in close combat;<-
->by Jupiter, a King; by Venus, wealthy; by Saturn, a creator of quarrels.<-
->If in a Navamsa of Venus, the Moon is aspected by the Sun, one is a fool; by Mars, devoted to others' wives; by Mercury, a fine poet;<-
->by Jupiter, a creator of excellent literature; by Venus, intent on pleasure; by Saturn, one who consorts with the wives of others. 5<-

Regarding "Protector" (<term>Arakshika</term>): "Son of the Earth" refers to Mars. When the Moon is in a Navamsa belonging to Mars (Aries or Scorpio) and is aspected by the Sun, the person becomes a protector. A protector is an official in charge of city security. If aspected by Mars, one is a lover of slaughter (a killer of living beings). If aspected by Mercury, one is skilled in <term>Niyuddha</term> <note>original: "नियुद्ध" - hand-to-hand combat or wrestling</note>; skilled means trained and proficient in wrestling. If aspected by Jupiter, one is a King. If aspected by Venus...

...if aspected by the Sun, he becomes wealthy and a leader; if aspected by Saturn, he is a creator of strife. Regarding the "Foolish" etc.: When the Moon is situated in a **white-rayed** <note>original: "sitāmśuke" - referring to the Navamshas of Venus</note> portion—that is, in the Navamsha of Taurus or Libra—and is aspected by the Sun, the person becomes a fool. Furthermore, if the Moon is in the Navamsha of Taurus or Libra and the Sun aspects it, the native is a fool; if Mars aspects, he follows the wives of others; if Mercury aspects, he is a poet; if Jupiter aspects, he is a creator of good poetry; if Venus aspects, he is happy; and if Saturn aspects, he follows the wives of others. || 5 ||

*Now, he describes the results for the Moon situated in the Navamshas of Mercury (Gemini/Virgo) and Cancer using the Vasantatilaka meter:*

-> **When the Moon is in the portion of Mercury, he becomes an actor, a thief, a lord of poets, or a minister;** <-

**Commentary:** "In the portion of Mercury": When the Moon is situated in a Navamsha of Mercury—either Gemini or Virgo—and is aspected [by the Sun], he becomes a performer <note>original: "raṅgacara" - literally 'one who moves on a stage', such as a wrestler or actor</note>. If aspected by Mars, he is a thief; if by Mercury, a lord of poets; if by Jupiter, a minister or secretary; if by Venus, a knower of songs; and if by Saturn, skilled in crafts. "In its own portion": When the Moon is in its own Navamsha—the Navamsha of Cancer—and is aspected by the Sun, he has a small or lean body. If aspected by Mars, he is greedy for wealth, a miser, or possesses little wealth; if by Mercury, he is an ascetic; if by Jupiter, he is a leader or chief; if by Venus, he is supported by women <note>original: "strīpoṣyaḥ" - one whose livelihood is provided by women</note>; and if by Saturn, he is devoted to his duties <note>The vernacular suggests "always ready for work," though some readings imply "devoted to his wife"</note>. || 6 ||

**Vernacular Translation—** If the Moon is in the Navamsha of Gemini or Virgo and is aspected by the Sun, the native is a dancer or a wrestler. By the aspect of Mars, a thief; by the aspect of Mercury, a poet; by the aspect of Jupiter, a minister of state; by the aspect of Venus, a musician; and by the aspect of Saturn, skilled in crafts (such as painting). If the Moon is in the Cancer Navamsha and the Sun aspects, the native has a small body; by the aspect of Mars, he is greedy for money; by the aspect of Mercury, an ascetic; by the aspect of Jupiter, a leader (chief); by the aspect of Venus, one who lives through women; and by the aspect of Saturn, he is always ready to perform his tasks. || 6 ||

### Now, the results of the Moon being in the Navamshas of Leo, Sagittarius, or Pisces, while being aspected by the Sun and other planets, are described in the Praharshini meter:

->**One becomes wrathful, honored by kings, or a master of treasures;**<-
->**In the Leo Navamsha, one is a lord, childless, or performs very violent deeds.**<-
->**In Jupiter’s Navamsha, one has celebrated strength, is a teacher of war,**<-
->**A knower of humor, a minister, or one with passionless or aged character. || 7 ||**<-

**One becomes wrathful, etc.:** When the Moon is in the <term>Navamsha</term><note>A 1/9th division of a zodiac sign, used for fine-tuning predictions</note> of Leo and is aspected by the Sun, the person is wrathful (filled with anger). If aspected by Mars, they are honored by kings (a favorite of royalty). If aspected by Mercury, they are a master of treasures (obtaining wealth from hidden stores). If aspected by Jupiter, they are a lord (one whose commands are unopposed). If aspected by Venus, they are childless (without sons). If aspected by Saturn, they perform very violent deeds (engaged in cruel actions).

**In Jupiter’s Navamsha, etc.:** When the Moon is in a Navamsha belonging to Jupiter—meaning either Sagittarius or Pisces—and is aspected by the Sun, the person possesses celebrated strength (famous for their valor). If aspected by Mars, they are a teacher of war (knowledgeable in the timing, location, and formations of battle). If aspected by Mercury, they are a knower of humor (skilled in wit). If aspected by Jupiter, they are a minister (a counselor). If aspected by Venus, they are passionless (lacking sexual desire or potency). If aspected by Saturn, they have an aged character (a religious or serious disposition). || 7 ||

**Vernacular Translation—** If the Moon is in the Leo Navamsha: aspected by the Sun, the native is angry; by Mars, respected by royalty; by Mercury, owner of treasures (wealth from mines); by Jupiter, a lord (with absolute authority); by Venus, sonless; and by Saturn, a performer of extremely cruel (violent) deeds. If the Moon is in the Sagittarius or Pisces Navamsha: aspected by the Sun, famously strong; by Mars, a teacher of the science of war; by Mercury, fond of humor; by Jupiter, a state minister; by Venus, devoid of passion (impotent); and by Saturn, possessing the nature of an elder. || 7 ||

### Now, the results of the Moon being in the Navamsha of Capricorn or Aquarius, aspected by the Sun and others, are described in the Shalini meter:

->**Having few children, miserable despite wealth, attached to pride, devoted to one's work;**<-
->**Liked by wicked women, and a miser—such is the Moon in Saturn's portion aspected by the Sun and others. || 8 ||**<-

**Having few children, etc.:** "Saturn's portion" refers to the Navamshas of Capricorn or Aquarius. When the Moon is situated there and aspected by the Sun, the person has few children (limited offspring). If aspected by Mars, they are miserable despite wealth (unhappy even when riches are present). If aspected by Mercury, they are attached to pride (arrogant)...

When the Moon is aspected <note>aspected: in astrology, this refers to the angular relationship between planets that "glance" at one another, influencing their effects</note> by Jupiter, the person is devoted to their own duties and performs work suited to their family lineage. When aspected by Venus, they are fond of wicked women but remain a favorite of others. When aspected by Saturn, they are miserable and ungenerous. These results should also be applied to the Ascendant based on the specific Navamsha <note term="Navamsha">A one-ninth subdivision of a zodiac sign, used for fine-tuned predictions</note> at the time of birth. However, in that case, the Moon’s aspect is considered inauspicious except when in the Cancer Navamsha. Regarding the Sun, when it is aspected by the Moon and other planets, the results are similar to those described for the Moon. Specifically, whatever results were stated for the Moon being aspected by the Sun in various Navamshas, the same should be declared for the Sun being aspected by the Moon. This means the results of the "star-planets" <note>original: "tara-graha" (Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn)</note> aspecting the Sun or Moon are equal. However, the specific result mentioned for the Sun aspecting the Moon must be applied when the Moon aspects the Sun. For example: if the Sun is in the Aries Navamsha and aspected by the Moon, the person becomes a protector or police officer. In Taurus or Libra Navamshas, a fool; in Gemini or Virgo, a traveler or beggar; in Leo, full of anger; in Sagittarius or Pisces, of renowned strength; in Capricorn or Aquarius, having few children; and in the Cancer Navamsha, having a small body. Thus, the results for the Sun in various Navamshas aspected by the Moon are identical to the reverse. || 8 ||

**Language—** If the Moon is in a Capricorn or Aquarius Navamsha: aspected by the Sun, the person has few children; by Mars, they are unhappy despite having wealth; by Mercury, they are arrogant; by Jupiter, they are devoted to their work; by Venus, they are the husband of a wicked woman; and by Saturn, they are miserly. Just as the results of the Sun and other planets aspecting the Moon in Aries and other Navamshas have been told, the same applies to the Sun in those Navamshas when aspected by the Moon and others. || 8 ||

**Special Meaning—** The distinction is that the results of aspects from Mars and the other planets are the same for both the Moon and the Sun. However, the specific results attributed to the Sun's aspect on the Moon are the same results that occur when the Moon aspects the Sun. || 8 ||

> ->**A powerful Lord of the Navamsha obstructs the previous**<-
> ->**Result of the sign-aspect and gives the result of the Navamsha.**<- || 16 ||

Regarding "Vargottama" etc.: When the Moon is situated in a Navamsha, the results of the aspects are of two types—auspicious and inauspicious. For example, "a protector" is auspicious, while "fond of a hunter's life" <note>original: "vadhuruchi"</note> is inauspicious.

# Page 343
## Commentary by Bhattotpala with Hindi Translation

In this context, when the Moon is situated in a **Vargottama** <note>The "best division," where a planet occupies the same sign in both the main birth chart and the ninth divisional chart (Navamsha), greatly increasing its strength.</note> portion, any auspicious results arising from the aspects <note>The "glance" or influence of one planet upon another.</note> of other planets are extremely powerful and beneficial. However, if the Moon is in its own **Navamsha** <note>The ninth part of a zodiac sign, used for fine-tuned analysis of a planet's strength.</note>, the auspicious results are moderate. There is a hierarchy of full strength, moderate strength, and slight strength. Conversely, regarding inauspicious results: if the Moon is in a **Vargottama** portion, the ill effects are slight; if in its own **Navamsha**, they are moderate; and if in another's portion, they are extremely inauspicious. This same logic for the results of aspects should also be applied to the Ascendant and the Sun. It is understood that all these results manifest in a birth chart. As the Lord of the Greeks <note>original: "Yavanesvara," an influential early authority in Indian astrology often associated with Indo-Greek traditions.</note> stated: "Through the combinations of different signs and portions, through their mutual aspects and conjunctions, and through the various permutations of their union, this science is as immeasurable as the waters of the ocean." Therefore, one always obtains a sequence of results from both the sign-aspects and the **Navamsha**-aspects. 

To determine when the **Navamsha** lord is powerful enough to override the results of the sign-aspect, the text says: **Endowed with strength.** Whichever **Navamsha** the Moon or the Ascendant occupies, if the lord of that **Navamsha** is powerful, it first obstructs or prevents—what? Not everything, but specifically the result of the sign-aspect. It does not obstruct the results of the aspects on the Hour, Decan, or Twelfth-part <note>Technical divisions of a sign: Hora, Drekkana, and Dwadashamsha.</note>; rather, it gives the result of the aspect on that specific portion. However, if the lord of the portion is not powerful, then the results of both the sign-aspect and the portion-aspect must be declared. This applies to both the Moon and the Ascendant. For the Sun, however, only the results of the portion-aspects should be stated, as the results for its sign-aspects have not been mentioned here. || 6 ||

---

->Thus ends the Nineteenth Chapter, titled "Results of Aspects,"<-
->in the Commentary on the Brihat Jataka composed by the illustrious Bhattotpala.<-

---

**Vernacular Translation—** If the Moon is in a **Vargottama Navamsha**, all stated auspicious results occur in full; if in its own **Navamsha**, all auspicious results are of moderate measure; and if in another **Navamsha**, all auspicious results are of slight measure. Inauspicious results are the opposite: if the Moon is in **Vargottama**, the stated inauspicious results are slight; if in its own **Navamsha**, they are moderate; and if in another, they are full. If the lord of the **Navamsha** is endowed with strength, it prevents the sign-aspect result and gives the **Navamsha** aspect result first. || 6 ||

**Special Meaning—** The significance is that the **Navamsha** is more subtle than the sign; therefore, if the lord of the **Navamsha** is strong, the **Navamsha** result occurs first. All results described for the Moon should be understood in the same way for the Ascendant. For the Sun, only the **Navamsha** results should be understood (like the Moon's), because the results for the Sun's sign-aspects have not been described. || 6 ||

<summary>This page concludes the chapter on planetary aspects, explaining how the strength of an astrological prediction varies based on whether a planet is in a Vargottama or its own Navamsha division. It establishes that the lord of the Navamsha, if strong, takes precedence over the general sign-based influences.</summary>

# Chapter 20: On the Houses (Bhavas)

Now, the chapter on the houses is explained. Therein, the author describes the results of the Sun being situated in the first house <note>the Ascendant or 'Lagna'</note> and the second house using the *Mandakranta* meter:

> **The person is brave, stiff-necked, has impaired vision, and is pitiless when the Sun is in the first house. If in Aries, he is wealthy but has eye disease; in Leo, he is night-blind. In its sign of debilitation <note>Libra</note>, he is blind and poor; in the house of the Moon <note>Cancer</note>, his eyes are like bubbles. In the second house, he has much wealth, though it is seized by the king, and he suffers from diseases of the mouth. ||1||**

**Commentary:** "Brave" means fond of battle. "Stiff-necked" means one who performs tasks slowly <note>procrastinating</note>. "Impaired vision" means weak eyesight. "Pitiless" means cruel. Such are the traits when the Sun is in the first house. This is the general result for all Ascendants. However, if the Sun is in one of the specific signs—Aries, Leo, Libra, or Cancer—the general result is modified by the specific sign-based results that follow.

Specifically: "In Aries, wealthy." If Aries is the Ascendant and the Sun is there, the person is wealthy but has "darkness in the eyes," meaning a specific eye disease <note>likely cataracts or glaucoma</note>. If Leo is the Ascendant and the Sun is there, he is "night-blind" <note>nyctalopia</note>. The Sun's sign of debilitation is Libra; if that is the Ascendant and the Sun is there, the person is blind and "without wealth" (impoverished). In the "house of the Moon," which is the Cancer Ascendant, if the Sun is there, he has "bubble-eyes" <note>eyes with white spots or a protruding appearance</note>. "Much wealth" etc.: If the Sun is in the second house from the Ascendant, the person possesses great riches, but his wealth is "seized by the king" <note>confiscated by the state or government</note>, and he is "afflicted in the face," meaning he suffers from oral diseases. || 1 ||

**Vernacular Translation:** If the Sun is in the Ascendant, the individual loves combat, is a procrastinator, has weak eyes, and is cruel. If the Sun is in Aries in the Ascendant, he is rich but has eye disease. In Leo Ascendant, he is rich but blind at night. In Libra, he is blind and poor. In Cancer, he has a film or "flower" in the eye. If the Sun is in the second house, he is very wealthy, but his wealth is seized by the ruler from time to time, and he suffers from mouth diseases. || 1 ||

->Now, the results of the Sun in the third, fourth, fifth, and sixth<-
->houses from the Ascendant are stated in the *Aupachhandasika* meter:<-

> **With the Sun in the third, one is intelligent and powerful; in the fourth, one is unhappy and mentally distressed. In the fifth <note>the trine</note>, one is childless and devoid of wealth; in the sixth, one is strong and overcomes his enemies. ||2||**
