...possessing [these qualities]. "Intelligence and Valour": Intelligence refers to the intellect, and Valour refers to prowess; one who possesses both of these is born when the Sun is in the **third house**. "Unhappy": One who is sorrowful, with a pained mind and a constantly anxious heart; such is one born when the Sun is in the **fourth house**. "Childless": Without sons, and "void of wealth": poor; such is one born when the Sun is in the **fifth house** (the trine). "Powerful": Endowed with strength, and "conqueror of enemies": one who has overcome his foes; such is one born when the Sun has gone to the **sixth house**. Some read the text for the sixth house as "powerful and with destroyed enemies." Accordingly, Satyacharya says: <note>Satyacharya was an ancient authority on astrology often cited by Varahamihira.</note> "In the sixth, the Sun destroys enemies, disease, and grief." The Teacher <note>Referring to Varahamihira, the author of the original verses.</note> has here accepted the opinion of Yavanesvara <note>Literally "Lord of the Greeks," a title for early Greco-Indian astrological authorities.</note>, because Yavanesvara described the malefic effects of cruel planets situated in the sixth house. Thus says Sphujidhvaja: "The Sun in the sixth makes men afflicted by poison, weapons, fire, minor diseases, enemies, and vices; or with teeth shattered by falls from wood or stone, or wounded by young animals, fangs, or claws. Mars there makes the body scarred, the eyes diseased, and the person wasted by insults. Saturn there causes injury from falls of stones on the head, or from wind, or blows from fists." By this very comparison, the Teacher will later apply the effects of other malefic planets as being similar to the Sun. || 2 ||

> **Vernacular Summary:** If the Sun is in the third house, the person is intelligent and brave. In the fourth house, they are devoid of happiness and have an anxious heart. In the fifth house, they are without sons and wealth. If the Sun is in the sixth house, they are strong and a conqueror of enemies. || 2 ||

---

### Now, the nature of one born with the Sun in the seventh, eighth, ninth, tenth, eleventh, and twelfth houses from the Ascendant is told in the Vasantatilaka meter:

->**Humiliated by women if the Sun is in the house of passion (7th),**<-
->**Few children and impaired vision if in the house of death (8th);**<-
->**In the house of virtue (9th), possessing sons, wealth, and happiness; in the sky (10th), possessing happiness and heroism;**<-
->**In the house of gain (11th), extremely wealthy; but fallen if in the last house (12th). || 3 ||**<-

"Humiliated by women" etc.: When the <term>Sun</term><note>original: "Patanga," literally "the flyer/bird," a poetic name for the Sun.</note> is in the **seventh house**, the person suffers humiliation from women. Some read "greatly" instead of "Sun." When the Sun is in the **eighth house**, the person has "few children" (limited offspring) and "impaired vision"—meaning one whose eyes are weak or whose sight is not firm. In the **ninth house**, one possesses "sons, wealth, and happiness." Some read this as "devoid of sons and wealth" in the ninth. Accordingly, Satyacharya says: "In the ninth, the Sun causes opposition to virtuous conduct, bestows disease, and creates wretchedness." In the **tenth house** (the "sky"), one is "happy and heroic"—joyful and strong. In the **eleventh house** (gain), one is "extremely wealthy" with much gold. In the **twelfth house**, one is "fallen"—meaning one who has strayed from their duties. Thus ends the movement of the Sun. || 3 ||

Such a person is born when the Moon is in the sixth house from the Ascendant. || 4 ||

Thus ends the movement of the Moon. ||5||

If the Moon is in the tenth house, he attains success in all works and is endowed with religion, wealth, intelligence, and prowess. If the Moon is in the eleventh house, he is famous and possesses gains. If the Moon is in the twelfth house <note>the house of expenditure</note>, the native is mean and physically deformed. ||5||

# Chapter on the Houses of the Horoscope
## Now, the nature of a person born with Mars and Mercury in the Ascendant and other houses is described in the Vasantatilaka meter:

> If Mars is in the Ascendant, the body is scarred; in the second house, one eats poor food;
> In the ninth house, one is sinful; in other positions, he is like the Sun.
> Mercury makes one learned, wealthy, very wicked, scholarly, a minister, or without enemies;
> A knower of dharma, or of famous virtues; in subsequent houses, he is like the Sun. ||6||

**Commentary:**
Regarding the Ascendant: If Mars <note>original: "Kuja"</note> is situated in the Ascendant <term>Lagna; the first house representing the self and physical body</term>, the person has a scarred body <note>original: "kshata-tanu"</note> due to wounds or injuries. If in the second house <note>the house of wealth and food</note>, he eats "bad food" <note>original: "kadanna"; coarse or inferior nourishment</note>. In the ninth house <note>the house of religion and fortune</note>, he is sinful or inclined toward evil deeds.

In other positions, he is like the Sun: In the remaining houses—the third, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth, tenth, eleventh, and twelfth—the results for Mars are the same as those stated for the Sun. Specifically: in the third, he is intelligent and courageous; in the fourth, unhappy and mentally distressed; in the fifth, devoid of children and wealth; in the sixth, powerful and a conqueror of enemies; in the seventh, humiliated by women; in the eighth, having few children and impaired vision; in the ninth, possessing children, wealth, and happiness; in the tenth, happy and brave; in the eleventh, possessing abundant wealth; and in the twelfth, fallen or degraded. This concludes the movement of Mars.

Now for the movement of Mercury <note>original: "Budha-chara"</note>: "Learned, wealthy, etc." If Mercury <note>original: "Jna"</note> is in the Ascendant, the person is learned or a scholar. In the second, he is wealthy. In the third, he is "very wicked" <note>original: "prakhala"; an intense scoundrel</note>. In the fourth, he is a scholar. In the fifth, he is a minister. In the sixth, he is "without enemies" <note>original: "ashatru"</note>. In the seventh, he is a knower of righteousness <term>Dharma</term>. In the eighth, he is of "famous virtues" <note>original: "vishruta-guna"</note>. In the subsequent houses, he is like the Sun: In the ninth, tenth, eleventh, and twelfth houses, the results for Mercury are the same as those stated for the Sun. Specifically: in the ninth, he enjoys children, wealth, and happiness; in the tenth, he possesses happiness and valor; in the eleventh, he has great wealth; and in the twelfth, he is fallen. This concludes the movement of Mercury. ||6||

**Vernacular Translation (Hindi):**
If Mars is in the Ascendant, the person has a scarred body (a wound on some limb); if in the house of wealth (2nd), he consumes poor food; if in the ninth house, he is a sinner; and in the remaining houses, the results of Mars are like those of the Sun. If Mercury is in the Ascendant, the person is learned; in the second house, wealthy; in the third house, wicked; in the fourth house, a scholar; in the fifth house, a royal minister; in the sixth house, free of enemies; in the seventh house, a knower of dharma; and in the eighth house, he possesses celebrated virtues. In the remaining 9th, 10th, 11th, and 12th houses, the results of Mercury are similar to the results of the Sun. ||6||

## Now, the results of Jupiter being in the Ascendant and other houses are stated in the Indravajra meter:

**A scholar, well-spoken, a miser, and happy; wise, without enemies, and surpassing one's father;**
**Lowly, an ascetic, wealthy, gaining profit, and wicked—these are the results of Jupiter in order from the Ascendant. || 7 ||**

*Scholar, etc.* — When Jupiter <note>original: "Guru"</note> is situated in the twelve houses starting from the Ascendant <note>The first house or rising sign</note>, these results occur in sequence. They are as follows:
If Jupiter is in the **First House** (Ascendant), one becomes a scholar or a learned man.
In the **Second**, one is well-spoken <note>possessing pleasing speech</note>.
In the **Third**, one is a miser <note>one who does not give</note>.
In the **Fourth**, one is happy.
In the **Fifth**, one is wise <note>intelligent</note>.
In the **Sixth**, one is without enemies <note>one whose foes have disappeared</note>.
In the **Seventh**, one surpasses their father <note>possessing more virtues than the father</note>.
In the **Eighth**, one is lowly <note>performing actions unsuitable for one's family lineage</note>.
In the **奠Ninth**, one is an ascetic <note>engaged in penance</note>.
In the **Tenth**, one is wealthy <note>possessing riches</note>.
In the **Eleventh**, one is gainful <note>endowed with profits</note>.
In the **Twelfth**, one is wicked <note>cruel in their actions</note>.
Thus ends the movement of Jupiter. || 7 ||

**Hindi Translation:**
If Jupiter is in the Ascendant, the person is a scholar; in the second house, a pleasant speaker; in the third, a miser; in the fourth, happy; in the fifth, a scholar; in the sixth, without enemies; in the seventh, more virtuous than his father; in the eighth, a doer of improper deeds; in the ninth, an ascetic; in the tenth, wealthy; in the eleventh, gaining profit; and in the twelfth, the person is wicked. || 7 ||

---

## Now, the results of Venus being in the Ascendant and other houses are stated in the Chitra meter:

**Skilled in love and happy in the Ascendant; fond of quarrels and desiring sex in the seventh;**
**Happy when in the house of children; elsewhere like Jupiter; and wealthy in the last. || 8 ||**

*Skilled in love, etc.* — One becomes skilled in the arts of love <note>original: "Smara-nipuna"</note> and endowed with happiness when Venus <note>the son of Bhrigu</note> is in the **First House** (Ascendant).
One becomes fond of quarrels and desirous of sexual union when Venus is in the **Seventh House** <note>the house of setting</note>.
One is happy when Venus is in the **Fifth House** <note>the house of children/sons</note>.
*Elsewhere like Jupiter* — In the houses other than these three, the results should be stated as being the same as those for Jupiter <note>Guru</note>.
Specifically, in the **Second, Third, Fourth, Sixth, Eighth, Ninth, Tenth, Eleventh, and Twelfth houses**, the results declared for Jupiter are to be applied to Venus.
To illustrate: In the second, one is well-spoken; in the third, a miser; in the fourth, happy; in the sixth, without enemies; in the eighth, lowly; in the ninth, an ascetic; in the tenth, wealthy; in the eleventh, gainful; and in the twelfth, wicked.
*Wealthy in the last* — In the "last" sign, which is Pisces <note>the 12th sign of the zodiac, where Venus is exalted</note>, regardless of which house it occupies, the person becomes wealthy. In that case, the general house-result does not apply.
Some read the text as "But in Pisces, one becomes wealthy" instead of "elsewhere like Jupiter." Therefore, in the remaining houses, the results are like Jupiter, but in Pisces <note>original: "Jhasha"</note>, one becomes wealthy.
Thus ends the movement of Venus. || 8 ||

Page 350
### Chapter on the Houses in the Brihat Jataka
<note>The Brihat Jataka is a foundational 6th-century Sanskrit text on Hindu astrology written by Varahamihira.</note>

**Vernacular Commentary:** If **Venus** <note>Sanskrit: Shukra</note> is in the Ascendant <note>The first house or "Lagna," representing the self and physical body</note>, the native is skilled in the arts of love and is happy. If it is in the seventh house <note>The house of partnerships and marriage</note>, they are fond of quarrels and lustful. If Venus is in the fifth house <note>The house of children and intelligence</note>, they are happy. In the other houses (2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 10, 11), the results should be understood as being similar to those of **Jupiter**. However, if Venus is in the twelfth house <note>The house of loss and liberation</note>, the native becomes wealthy. ||8||

---

->Now, the effects of **Saturn** being in the Ascendant and other houses are described in the *Shikharini* meter:<-

# Lacking wealth, sickly, enslaved by lust, and extremely filthy;
# Suffering in childhood, slow of speech is one with Saturn in the Ascendant.
# But if in Jupiter’s signs, its own sign, or its exaltation, one is like a king or a leader of cities;
# Learned and handsome; elsewhere, the effects are said to be like the Sun. ||9||

**Lacking wealth and sickly:** "Lacking wealth" means constantly poor; "sickly" means afflicted by disease; "enslaved by lust" means dominated by carnal desires; "extremely filthy" means possessing much bodily impurity; "suffering in childhood" means tormented by illness in early life; "slow of speech" means speaking indistinctly. Such is the person born when the son of the Sun (**Saturn**) is in the Ascendant. This specific negative result occurs only if the Ascendant is not one of the following signs: Libra, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, or Pisces. 

The author then describes the effects if one of these specific signs is in the Ascendant: **"In Jupiter’s signs, its own sign, or its exaltation."** Jupiter’s signs are Sagittarius and Pisces; Saturn’s own signs are Capricorn and Aquarius; its sign of exaltation <note>The sign where a planet reaches its maximum strength</note> is Libra. If any of these signs are in the Ascendant and Saturn is situated there, the native becomes **"like a king,"** equal to royalty. They are a **"leader of cities,"** the lord of villages or towns; **"learned,"** a scholar; and **"handsome,"** possessing beautiful limbs. Some read the text as "in a friend's sign, its own sign, or exaltation," but the current reading is preferred because it is stated in the *Saravali* <note>A classic 8th-century astrological treatise by Kalyanavarman</note>:

> "In its exaltation or in the houses of Jupiter, the son of the Sun in the Ascendant makes one equal to a protector of the earth (a king) or a ruler of a country. In the remaining signs, the child is surely afflicted by misery and disease, impoverished, lustful, filthy, and lazy."

**"Elsewhere, the effects are said to be like the Sun":** In the other houses (from the second onwards), the effects of Saturn are said to be equal to those of the Sun. Whatever results were stated for the Sun should be applied to Saturn. Specifically:
* **In the second house:** Possessing much wealth, but having it seized by the king, and suffering from diseases of the mouth.
* **In the third house:** Possessing intelligence and valor.
* **In the fourth house:** Unhappy and mentally distressed.
* **In the fifth house:** Childless and devoid of wealth.
* **In the sixth house:** Powerful but defeated by enemies.
* **In the seventh house:** Suffering humiliation at the hands of women.
* **In the eighth house:** Having few children and impaired vision.
* **In the ninth house:** Endowed with children, wealth, and happiness.
* **In the tenth house:** Endowed with happiness and heroism.
* **In the eleventh house:** Possessing abundant wealth.
* **In the twelfth house:** Fallen <note>Degraded in status or sinful</note>.

Thus ends the movement of Saturn. ||9||

<header>Including the Sanskrit commentary by Bhattotpala and the vernacular explanation</header>

**Vernacular Commentary—** If Saturn is positioned in the Ascendant <note>the first house or 'Lagna'</note> in any sign other than Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, Pisces, or Libra, the person born will be poor, sickly, lustful, very untidy, miserable in childhood, and have indistinct speech. However, if Saturn is in the Ascendant specifically in Sagittarius, Pisces, Capricorn, Aquarius, or Libra, the person will be like a king, the head of a village or city, learned, and possess a handsome body. For the second and subsequent houses, the effects of Saturn should be understood as being similar to those described for the Sun. ||6||

Now, the author describes the specific effects of all planets situated in the houses starting from the Ascendant (the body, etc.) using the *Malini* meter:

->**The effects of planets situated in friendly, inimical, neutral, or their own signs, or in exaltation,**<-
->**should be carefully considered in relation to the houses such as the Ascendant and the body.**<-
->**Satyacharya says that benefic planets bring growth and malefic planets bring calamity;**<-
->**however, this is reversed in the twelfth, sixth, and eighth houses. ||10||**<-

**Friendly, inimical, etc. ||** The effects must be carefully considered for each house, starting from the Ascendant through the twelve positions. The "houses" refer to the body, family, siblings, and so on. Regarding the phrase "houses such as the Ascendant and the body": the Ascendant is to be conceived as the body/physical self. Starting from the Ascendant, the houses of body, family, siblings, etc., are to be arranged. What confusion could there be here? It is addressed thus: there is indeed a possibility of confusion, because the Master of the Greeks <note>original: "Yavanesvara," a famous early authority in Indian astrology influenced by Greco-Egyptian traditions</note> says: "One should know the form from the Ascendant and the Moon's sign." Here, one should not calculate from the Moon's sign, but rather from the Ascendant. A planet situated in those houses (body, etc.) causes either the flourishing or the wasting of that house.

How so? He says: "The effects of planets situated in friendly, inimical, neutral, or their own signs, or in exaltation should be carefully considered." A "friendly field" is a friend's sign; an "inimical field" is an enemy's sign; "another's" refers to a neutral sign; "own sign" is one's own field; and "exalted" is the sign of highest strength. The effects of planets situated in these places must be calculated. A planet in a house gives results according to the type of sign it occupies. 

Now, a list of friendly and other signs has been made, but the division of auspicious and inauspicious results was not explicitly stated there. It is answered: This is understood from the context itself. For instance, a planet in a friend's sign causes the growth of that house, while one in an enemy's sign causes its loss. Furthermore, although the "Trine" <note>Trikona</note> and "Debilitation" <note>Nicha</note> signs were not mentioned, they should also be included. The mention of "friendly signs, etc." is intended to represent all types of planetary dignities. What is the difference between "inimical" and "another's"? "Another" here means neutral. "Inimical" is the enemy, "another" is the neutral party. The meaning is this: whether a planet is malefic or benefic, if it is in its sign of debilitation or an enemy's sign, it causes the destruction of the house in which it is situated.

It emphasizes that the Ascendant, not the Moon, is the primary starting point for these house calculations according to this tradition.</summary>

<header>The Chapter on Houses in the Brihat Jataka</header>

# The Chapter on Houses in the Brihat Jataka

When a planet is situated in a neutral sign <note>original: "udāsīna-kshetra"; a sign belonging to a planet that is neither a friend nor an enemy</note>, it causes neither loss nor increase to the house. When situated in a friend's sign, its own sign, its root-trine <term>mūlatrikoṇa: a specific favorable position for a planet, stronger than its own sign but weaker than its exaltation</term>, or its exaltation, it causes the increase of that house. This is the opinion of some authorities. Thus says the Sage Garga:
> "A planet situated in its sign of fall <note>original: "nīcha-ṛkṣa"</note> or in the house of an enemy causes the destruction of the house. In a neutral house, the effect is middling. When in a friend's sign, its root-trine, or its exaltation, the planet is remembered as surely causing the increase of the house."

However, Satyacharya <note>An influential early authority on astrology often cited by Varahamihira</note> speaks regarding the increase or ruin caused by benefics <term>saumya: "gentle" or "benefic" planets like Jupiter, Venus, and Mercury</term> and malefics <term>pāpa: "cruel" or "malefic" planets like Saturn and Mars</term>. In whichever house benefics are placed, they cause the increase of that house; in whichever house malefics are placed, they cause the ruin or loss of that house. But they say this is reversed in the twelfth, sixth, and eighth houses. In the twelfth house <note>original: "riḥpha"</note>, benefics cause the loss of expenditure <note>meaning they reduce wasteful spending</note>, while malefics cause the increase of expenditure. In the sixth house, benefics cause the destruction of enemies, while malefics cause the increase of enemies. In the eighth house, benefics cause the destruction of death <note>meaning they promote longevity</note>, while malefics cause the increase of death. Thus says Satya:
> "Benefics cause nourishment and malefics cause loss to the houses they occupy. In the houses starting from the first <note>the Ascendant</note>, this is true; but in the eighth, the twelfth, and the sixth, the results are reversed."

Now, a question arises: previously it was explained that both benefics and malefics situated in the "Upachaya" <note>houses of growth: 3, 6, 10, and 11</note> houses give auspicious results; so how can it be said that malefics in the sixth house increase enemies? To this it is replied: the previous statement was a general rule. Where there is a specific scriptural contradiction, one should set aside the general house-effect and state the specific result as taught. If so, why is it said in the *Svalpa Jataka* <note>The "Short Birth Manual," a condensed work by the same author</note>:
> "Benefics nourish the houses from the body <note>the 1st house</note> onwards; malefics situated there destroy them. Benefics in the sixth destroy enemies; all planets are undesirable in the eighth and twelfth."

To this it is replied: In the *Brihat Jataka* <note>The "Great Birth Manual"</note>, the Teacher <note>Varahamihira</note> spoke his own view, but in the *Svalpa Jataka*, he acknowledged the views of other teachers. As the Teacher himself promised:
> "Astrology is a traditional science; where there is disagreement, it is not proper for us to simply choose for ourselves; rather, I shall state the opinions of many."

Where there is an equal weight of differing opinions among the teachers, Varahamihira shows both views. Thus, in the *Brihat Yatra* <note>Great Work on Journeys</note> he describes one form of planetary chart, while in the *Svalpa Yatra* <note>Short Work on Journeys</note> he reads a common form. The same applies to his two works on marriage <note>the Vivaha-patalas</note>. || 10 ||

<insert>
**Vernacular Explanation**—Starting from the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note>, there are twelve houses known as Body, Wealth, etc. One must consider the results based on whether a planet is in a friendly sign, enemy sign, neutral sign, its own sign, or its exaltation. For example, a planet said to give physical comfort in the first house will increase that comfort if in a friendly sign; if in an enemy's house, the comfort will be slight; in a neutral sign, it will be middling; in its own sign, the comfort will be full; and if in its exaltation, the physical comfort will be excellent.
</insert>

It should be stated that a house <note>bhava: an astrological house or life-domain</note> is strengthened when joined by a benefic planet, while it suffers loss when joined by a malefic planet. However, the opposite is true for the 6th, 8th, and 12th houses <note>these are the 'Dusthanas' or difficult houses</note>: in these three, a benefic planet causes the loss of that house's (negative) effects, such as enemies, while a malefic planet increases them. ||10||

### Now, the specific results based on the planetary chart are stated in the Anustubh meter:

> Full, three-quarters, half, one-quarter, slight, or nil results are given
> By planets situated in exaltation, Moolatrikona, own, friend's, enemy's, or debilitation signs respectively. ||11||

->Thus ends the twentieth chapter, the Chapter on the Houses, in the Brihat Jataka composed by the illustrious Acharya Varahamihira.<-

**Regarding the verse:** In the planetary chart, two types of results are mentioned: auspicious and inauspicious. Among these, the auspicious results given by planets situated in exaltation, Moolatrikona <note>a specific favorable sign position</note>, their own sign, a friend's sign, an enemy's sign, or a debilitation sign are, in order: full, three-quarters, half, one-quarter, slight, and nil. Therefore, a planet in its exaltation gives full results. One in Moolatrikona gives three-quarters; in its own sign, half; in a friend's sign, a quarter; in an enemy's sign, less than a quarter; and in debilitation or when combust <note>astamita: hidden by the sun's light</note>, it gives nothing at all. This applies to auspicious results. By understanding the auspicious, the reverse should be interpreted for inauspicious planets. In that case, a planet that is combust or in debilitation gives full inauspicious results. In an enemy's sign, it gives three-quarters; in a friend's sign, half; in its own sign, a quarter; in Moolatrikona, less than a quarter; and in exaltation, nothing at all. Thus, the results should be declared based on the planet's position at the time of birth. During the periods of the Dasha or Ashtakavarga <note>systems for timing events</note>, the planet provides the full auspicious or inauspicious result. This has been explained previously. As it is said:

> "If the lord of the Dasha period is strong at that time,
> Its result, whether auspicious or inauspicious, must always be declared as full." ||11||

->Thus ends the twentieth chapter, the Chapter on the Houses, in the commentary on the Brihat Jataka composed by the illustrious Bhattotpala.<-

---

**Vernacular Translation—** Regarding the auspicious house results mentioned previously: if a planet is in its highest exaltation, the result is full; in Moolatrikona, 3 parts (75%); in its own house, 2 parts (50%); in a friend's house, 1 part (25%); in an enemy's house, very little; and if in debilitation or combust, there is a total lack of result. From this, it is established that inauspicious results are the opposite: if a planet is combust or in debilitation, the inauspicious result is full; in an enemy's house, 3 parts; in a friend's house, 2 parts; in its own house, 1 part; in Moolatrikona, very little; and if the planet is in exaltation, there is an absence of inauspicious house results. ||11||

# Now, the Chapter on Dependent Combinations || 21 ||

Now, the chapter on Dependent Combinations <note>Sanskrit: *Asraya Yoga*; these are planetary configurations that depend on the nature of the zodiac signs the planets occupy</note> is explained. At the very beginning, the author describes the results of planets occupying their own signs or friendly signs, increasing in number from one upwards, using the *Pushpitagra* meter:

> ->Those born with planets in their own signs, increasing by one, become:<-
> ->equal to their family, leaders of the family, honored by kin, wealthy,<-
> ->happy, enjoyers, and kings.<-
> ->In friendly signs, they are: supported by others' wealth, by friends,<-
> ->by themselves, by kin; or they become leaders of groups, army chiefs, and kings. || 1 ||<-

**Equal to the family, etc.:** With planets situated in their <term>own signs</term> <note>Sanskrit: *Svabha*; the specific zodiac sign ruled by that planet</note> increasing by one, men are born who are equal to their family, leaders of the family, honored by kin, wealthy, happy, enjoyers, and kings. If one planet is in its own sign, the person is equal to his family (attaining the same status as his parents). With two planets in their own signs, he is the leader of the family, superior to his kin. With three, he is honored by his kinsmen. With four, he is wealthy. With five, he is happy. With six, he is an "enjoyer" or like a king—some read this as "ruler of the earth." Because it is a comparison, "like a king" implies equality with a sovereign. It is also said in the *Svalpa Jataka*: "Men are equal to family, superior to family, respected by kin, wealthy, enjoyers, like kings, and lords of men." Thus, with six, one is like a king; with seven, one is a king.

**Supported by others' wealth, etc.:** The rule of "increasing by one" continues here. When planets are situated in <term>friendly signs</term> <note>Sanskrit: *Mitrabha*; signs ruled by planets that are natural or temporary friends to the occupying planet</note> increasing by one, those born are supported by others' wealth, by friends, by themselves, or by kin; or they become group leaders, army chiefs, and kings. Therefore, with one planet in a friendly sign, the person is supported by others' wealth—meaning he is a dependent. With two, he is supported by friends. With three, he supports himself or is supported by his community. With four, he is supported by his kinsmen (brothers). With five, he is a <term>leader of a group</term> <note>Sanskrit: *Ganapa*; a head of a community or guild</note>. With six, he is a <term>commander of an army</term> <note>Sanskrit: *Balesha*</note>. With seven, he is a king. || 1 ||

**Vernacular Translation:** If at the time of birth one planet is in its own house, the person is like his father; 2 planets in their own house, he is the chief of the family; 3 planets, he is honored among kin; 4 planets, wealthy; 5 planets, happy; 6 planets, an enjoyer; if all seven planets are in their own houses, he is a king. Similarly, if one planet is in a friendly sign, he is nourished by another's wealth; 2 planets in friendly houses, by friends; 3 planets, by his own caste; 4 planets, by kinsmen. 5 planets in friendly signs, he is a leader of many; 6 planets, an army chief; if all seven planets are in friendly signs, he is a king. || 1 ||

The results range from being a simple dependent to becoming a powerful king or military commander.</summary>

Now, the author describes the result of even a single planet being in its exaltation <note>The highest point of a planet's strength</note> and aspected by a friend, increasing by one for each additional planet; and the wretchedness caused by planets in debilitation or enemy signs:

> Even a single planet in exaltation, aspected by a friend, produces a king
> endowed with abundant wealth and success through the association of friends.
> Conversely, planets in enemy signs or debilitation produce those who are
> penniless, joyless, foolish, diseased, tormented by bondage,
> and afflicted by execution or sin. ||2||

**Commentary:** Even a single planet in its exaltation, aspected by a friend—meaning looked upon by a friendly planet—produces or creates a king. Similarly, even one planet in exaltation, due to association with a friend—meaning being joined with a friendly planet—produces one endowed with abundant wealth and success. "Endowed with abundant wealth" means possessing sufficient riches, and "success" means attaining honor everywhere. Regarding "penniless, joyless, foolish," etc.: by an increase of one, those born with planets in enemy signs or debilitation signs become penniless, joyless, foolish, diseased, tormented by bondage, and afflicted by execution or sin. Thus, one in whose birth one planet is in an enemy sign or debilitation becomes "penniless"—devoid of wealth, a pauper. One who has two such planets is "joyless"—miserable. One who has three is "foolish"—senseless. One who has four is "diseased"—afflicted. One who has five is "tormented by bondage." One who has six is "tormented"—greatly scorched by many sorrows. One who has seven is "afflicted by execution and sin"—liable to be killed or joined with wickedness. Although it is not possible for seven planets to be in debilitation simultaneously <note>Astronomically, certain planets like the Sun and Venus cannot be in opposite signs at the same time</note>, the instruction of such results is given according to ancient scriptures, similar to the *Vajra* yoga. ||2||

### Vernacular Translation—
If even one planet is in its exaltation and is aspected by its friend, the native becomes a king endowed with great wealth. If it is joined with a friend, he becomes a wealthy king who receives honor everywhere. If two or more planets are in exaltation, then what more need be said? Similarly, if one planet is in an enemy or debilitation sign, the person is devoid of wealth; if 2 planets, devoid of happiness; if 3 planets, a fool; if 4 planets, afflicted by disease; if 5 planets are in debilitation, suffering from imprisonment; and if 6 planets are in debilitation, or 6 or 7 are in enemy houses, the person is afflicted by death (execution) and sin (wickedness). ||2||

### Special Meaning—
All seven planets cannot be in debilitation at the same time. However, seven planets can be in enemy houses; therefore, the result for 6 and 7 planets is stated as the same: "afflicted by sin and execution." ||2||

Now, the author speaks of the inauspicious results for those born with Aquarius as the Ascendant <term>Kumbha Lagna: The rising sign of Aquarius</term> in the Upajati meter:

> Satyacharya says the Aquarius Ascendant is not auspicious; the Yavanas <note>The "Greeks" or Western astrologers</note> say this is not so because of the division of the signs into degrees. Vishnugupta <note>An alias for Chanakya or a later astronomical authority</note> says: "To which sign does the division of degrees not apply?"—for such an argument would lead to an absurdity. ||3||

# Brihat Jataka: Chapter on Dependent Combinations

### Page 356

"Not the Aquarius Ascendant" — Satyacharya <note>A celebrated ancient authority on astrology often cited by Varahamihira</note> says that Aquarius as the rising sign at birth is not auspicious; he stated it is not good. Thus Satyacharya says: **"The Moon is best at birth except when in the house of a fierce enemy or the house of death. The Ascendant is also desired among the human signs, excluding Aquarius. A man born in the Aquarius Ascendant becomes afflicted by sorrow and grief."**

"Not due to the division of portions" — The ancient Yavana <note>The "Yavanas" refers to the Greeks or Westerners whose astrological systems influenced early Indian texts</note> teachers believe that the Aquarius Ascendant is inauspicious due to the "division of portions" (the twelfth-part or *dwadashamsha*). Their opinion is that birth is not auspicious specifically when the twelfth-part of the rising sign is Aquarius, rather than the entire sign of Aquarius itself. Thus, following that opinion, Shrutakirti says: **"When the twelfth-part of Aquarius occurs within any rising sign, the person will not be happy and will eat the food of others."**

On this point, Vishnugupta <note>Another name for Chanakya, the famous strategist and scholar</note> and Chanakya say: "Of which sign is this division?" It was said that the Aquarius portion makes a birth inauspicious. But to which rising sign does this apply? The twelfth-part of Aquarius does not belong to just one, but exists within all signs. Therefore, if the twelfth-part of Aquarius were inauspicious, then all the results predicted for every rising sign would become meaningless. This leads to an "over-extension" <term>Atiprasanga: a logical fallacy where a definition is too broad</term>. Therefore, it is the Aquarius Ascendant itself that is inauspicious, not merely that specific division of portions. Thus their statement:

> "The twelfth-part of Aquarius in the Ascendant is not praised by the Yavanas.
> If this were so, then all rising signs would yield undesirable results.
> That opinion is not held by all the authors of the Shastras <note>Sacred scriptures/treatises</note>.
> Therefore, the Aquarius Ascendant is inauspicious at birth, not its division." ||3||

**Vernacular Translation** — Satyacharya says: "The Aquarius Ascendant is not auspicious at the time of birth." However, the ancient Yavana teachers hold the opinion that the twelfth-part (*dwadashamsha*) of Aquarius in any Ascendant is inauspicious. But Vishnugupta says: "Which sign is there that does not contain a twelfth-part of Aquarius?" That is to say, since the twelfth-part of Aquarius is in every sign, then every sign would become inauspicious as an Ascendant; therefore, to believe this is a logical over-extension. Thus, only the Aquarius Ascendant itself is inauspicious at birth. ||3||

->Now, he describes the results of planets situated in the solar and lunar halves of the signs (Horas) in the Vasantatilaka meter:<-

> If the cruel planets are in odd signs and have entered the Solar Hora,
> the person born is famous, possesses great effort, strength, and wealth, and is very majestic.
> If the gentle planets are in even signs and in the Lunar Hora,
> the person born possesses softness, beauty, happiness,
> good fortune, intelligence, and sweet speech. ||4||

"If they have entered" — The "bad planets" are the malefics. When these malefics are situated in odd signs and have not only entered those signs but have specifically entered the Solar Hora (the half of the sign ruled by the Sun)...

# Page 357
### With the Sanskrit Commentary of Bhattotpala and the Hindi Translation

When malefic planets <note>original: "pāpāḥ"; referring to planets like Mars or Saturn</note> are situated in the first half of **odd-numbered signs** <note>Aries, Gemini, Leo, etc.</note>, the person born is famous and renowned everywhere, endowed with great effort, strength, and wealth—meaning they are engaged in great works, powerful, and rich—and possesses great brilliance. 

Regarding the phrase "benefics in the lunar [division]": when benefic planets <note>original: "saumya-graheṣu"; gentle planets like Jupiter or Venus</note> occupy the lunar <term>Hora<gloss>a 15-degree division of a zodiac sign</gloss></term> in **even-numbered signs** <note>Taurus, Cancer, Virgo, etc.</note>, the person born is endowed with gentleness of nature, luster, happiness, and good fortune—meaning they are beloved by all—as well as wisdom and sweet speech. The person is born possessed of these qualities. || 4 ||

**Vernacular Translation—** If malefic planets are in an odd sign and in the Sun's Hora, the native is famous everywhere, highly industrious, wealthy, and extremely brilliant. Likewise, if benefic planets are in an even sign and in the Moon's Hora, the native is soft-natured, lustrous, and endowed with happiness, fortune, intellect, and pleasant speech. || 4 ||

**Special Meaning—** If malefic planets are in an odd sign and the Sun's Hora, and benefic planets are in an even sign and the Moon's Hora, one should understand through their own intelligence that the native will possess both types of qualities mentioned above. || 4 ||

->Now, the author describes the results of planetary positions in the Horas again using the *Indravajra* meter:<-

**If the planets are in the same Horas but in the opposite signs, men are known to have the aforementioned qualities only to a middling degree.**
**If the planets are situated in both the opposite Horas and opposite signs, mortals are devoid of the stated qualities. || 5 ||**

"In those very [Horas]": If born when planets are in those same previously mentioned Horas but in the "other signs" <note>meaning malefics in the Sun's Hora but in an even sign, or benefics in the Moon's Hora but in an odd sign</note>, the qualities previously described are "middling" or moderate. 

This is what is being said: When malefic planets are placed in the Sun's Hora within **even signs**, the previously mentioned qualities are moderate. Similarly, when benefic planets are placed in the Moon's Hora within **odd signs**, the previously mentioned qualities are moderate. 

Regarding "situated in opposite Horas and signs": When planets are in the reverse Horas and reverse signs, the mortals born are "devoid of"—meaning lacking—the qualities previously specified. 

This is what is being said: When malefic planets are placed in the Moon's Hora within **even signs**, those born are devoid of great effort, strength, and wealth, and lack brilliance. Likewise, when benefic planets are placed in the Sun's Hora within **odd signs**, those born are devoid of gentleness, luster, fortune, wisdom, and sweet speech. In these planetary positions shown here, the abundance of qualities should be predicted according to the number of planets involved. || 5 ||

**From the Brihat Jataka: Chapter on Dependent Yogas** <note>original: "बृहज्जातके अथाश्रययोगाध्यायः"; Yogas are planetary combinations that "depend" on specific signs or divisions.</note>

**Vernacular Commentary —** If malefic planets <note>planets with a harsh influence, like Mars or Saturn</note> are in the Sun's *Hora* <note>a 15-degree division of a sign</note> but in an even-numbered sign, and if benefic planets <note>gentle planets like Jupiter or Venus</note> are in the Moon's *Hora* but in an odd-numbered sign, the person born will possess the previously mentioned qualities to a moderate degree. If the situation is entirely reversed (meaning malefic planets are in the Moon's *Hora* and an even sign, while benefics are in the Sun's *Hora* and an odd sign), the person will be devoid of those positive qualities. || 5 ||

->Now, the effects of the Moon based on its position in the *Drekkana* <note>a 10-degree division, also known as a decan</note> are described in the *Vasantatilaka* meter:<-

### Beautiful in form and character when in its own or a friend's decan;
### Elsewhere, the Moon bestows the qualities of that decan's lord.
### In the Serpent, Armed, Quadruped, or Bird decans,
### One is sharp, extremely violent, a defiler of the teacher's bed, or a wanderer. || 6 ||

**Beautiful in form and character:** When the Moon is situated in its own *Drekkana* or in the *Drekkana* of a friendly planet, the person born is "beautiful in form and character"—meaning they possess an excellent appearance and excellent virtues. Regarding the Moon's placement in decans other than its own or a friend's: the text says "Elsewhere, it bestows the qualities of that decan's lord." If the lord of the decan where the Moon is placed is neutral toward the Moon at that time, the person's appearance and character will be mediocre. However, if the lord of the decan is a temporary enemy to the Moon, the person will lack beauty and good character.

**Serpent, Armed, etc.:** In a "Serpent decan" <note>original: "Vyala-drekkana"</note>, if the Moon is present, the person born is "sharp" or fierce. In an "Armed decan" <note>original: "Udyatayudha-drekkana"; depicting a raised weapon</note>, the person is "extremely violent," meaning they have a murderous nature or take pleasure in killing living beings. In a "Quadruped decan" <note>four-legged animals</note>, the person becomes a "defiler of the teacher's bed," meaning one who has illicit relations with the wife of a superior or teacher. In a "Bird decan" <note>original: "Andaja" or "Khaga"</note>, the person is a "wanderer," possessing a roaming nature. If the Moon is simultaneously in its own decan and a Serpent decan, both sets of results should be predicted.

The Serpent decans are: the 2nd and 3rd of Cancer, the 1st and 2nd of Scorpio, and the 3rd of Pisces.
The Armed decans are: the 1st and 3rd of Aries, the 2nd and 3rd of Gemini, the 3rd of Leo, the 2nd of Virgo, the 3rd of Libra, the 1st and 3rd of Sagittarius, and the 3rd of Capricorn.
The Quadruped decans are: the 2nd of Aries, the 2nd and 3rd of Taurus, the 1st of Cancer, the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd of Leo, the 3rd of Libra, the 3rd of Scorpio, the 1st of Sagittarius, and <margin>Note (1)</margin> the 1st of Capricorn.
Now, the Bird decans...

*Armed Decans—* The first and third of Aries, the second and third of Gemini, the second and third of Leo, the second of Virgo, the third of Libra, and the third of Capricorn.

In the **Capricorn subdivision**, one is a sinner. In the **Aquarius subdivision**, one is a hunter or cruel. In the **Pisces subdivision**, one is fearless. **Special Meaning —** Whichever sign is rising, if its own Navamsha is also rising, it is called Vargottama. For example, in an Aries ascendant, if the Navamsha is also Aries, the person is a "king of thieves"; in a Taurus ascendant, if the Navamsha is Taurus, he is the "best among enjoyers," and so on for the other signs. || 7 ||

->Accompanied by the performance of deeds <note>original: "ksitikaaryakaranena"; likely referring to earthly or bold actions</note>, such a person is born when Mars is in its own portion, situated in its own <term>Trimsamsha</term> <note>A 1/30th division of a zodiac sign used in Vedic astrology to determine specific character traits</note>. Intelligence; the arts such as singing, instrumental music, dance, books, painting, etc.; cunning (deceitfulness); poetry (the work of a poet); debate (eloquence); craftsmanship such as carpentry; the meaning of the scriptures (the practice of the conduct of the virtuous); courage (the tendency to perform deeds without hesitation); and being highly honored (highly venerable)—such people are born when the son of the Moon (Mercury) is in its own Trimsamsha. Some prefer the singular number throughout this section, but even so, there is no fault. || 9 ||

**Vernacular Translation:** If Jupiter is in its own Trimsamsha, the native is endowed with wealth, fame, happiness, and intellect, and is radiant, respected by the world, free from disease, industrious, and an enjoyer of pleasures. If Mercury is in its own Trimsamsha, the native is intelligent, a knower of arts, cunning, a composer of poetry, a knower of the meaning of the scriptures, courageous, and respectable in the world. || 9 ||

## Brihat Jataka: The Chapter on Support Yogas <note>Sanskrit: Ashraya-yoga-adhyaya. These are planetary combinations that provide a "support" or foundation for the horoscope.</note>

Now, using the *Mandakranta* meter, the author describes the nature of a person born when Venus is in its own degree-division, and when the Moon and Sun are in the degree-divisions of Mars and the other planets—

> If Venus is in its own degree-division, the person has many sons, much happiness, health, fortune, wealth, and beauty; they are sharp, have a very graceful body, and their senses are widely dispersed <note>This implies a sensual nature or one who seeks many pleasures.</note>. When the Sun and Moon are in the divisions starting with Mars, they make one: brave or sluggish; wicked or a murderer; endowed with good qualities or wealthy; happy or learned; and handsome or well-liked. || 10 ||

->Thus ends the twenty-first chapter, the Chapter on Support Yogas, in the Brihat Jataka composed by the Great Teacher Varahamihira. || 21 ||<-

**Regarding "In its own degree-division":** One born with Venus in its own degree-division <note>A Trimsamsha is a 1-degree division used in Vedic astrology to fine-tune character traits.</note> has many sons, immense happiness, health (freedom from disease), fortune (being loved by people), wealth, and beauty. Some read the text as "wealth and beauty through a wife." Furthermore, such a person is "sharp" (cruel or intense), has a "very graceful body," and "widely dispersed senses"—meaning their senses are scattered toward many objects, often indicating one who frequents many women.

**Regarding "Brave, sluggish, etc.":** These are the results when the Sun and Moon are in the divisions starting with Mars <note>The text follows a specific sequence: Mars, Saturn, Jupiter, Mercury, and Venus.</note> respectively. Specifically:
*   **In the degree of Mars:** If the Sun is there, one is brave (fond of battle); if the Moon, one is sluggish (a procrastinator).
*   **In the degree of Saturn:** If the Sun is there, one is wicked (cruel); if the Moon, one is a murderer.
*   **In the degree of Jupiter:** If the Sun is there, one has good qualities; if the Moon, one is wealthy (a lord).
*   **In the degree of Mercury:** If the Sun is there, one is happy; if the Moon, one is learned (a scholar).
*   **In the degree of Venus:** If the Sun is there, one has a handsome body; if the Moon, one is "desired" (beloved by all).
This is the sequence for the divisions beginning with Mars. || 10 ||

->Thus ends the commentary on the twenty-first chapter, the Chapter on Support Yogas,<-
->in the Explanation of Brihat Jataka composed by Bhattotpala.<-

**Vernacular Translation—** If Venus is in its own degree-division, the subject possesses many sons, happiness, health, fortune, wealth, and beauty, but is also cruel, has a beautiful body, and is prone to many women. If the Sun is in the degree of Mars, the person is brave; if the Moon is there, they are sluggish. If the Sun is in the degree of Saturn, they are wicked; if the Moon, they are violent. If the Sun is in the degree of Jupiter, they are virtuous; if the Moon, they are wealthy. If the Sun is in the degree of Mercury, they are happy; if the Moon, they are a scholar. If the Sun is in the degree of Venus, they have a beautiful body; if the Moon, they are loved by everyone. || 10 ||

# Chapter 22: On Miscellaneous Topics

Now, the chapter on miscellaneous topics is explained. "Miscellaneous" <note>Sanskrit: *Prakīrṇaka*</note> refers to a mixture of various subjects.
->In this regard, the author describes the mutual "Significator" <term>Karaka: a planet that acts as a functional producer of results</term> relationship of the planets using the *Vaitālīya* meter:<-

> Planets situated in their own signs, their signs of exaltation, or their "root-trine" <note>Sanskrit: *Mūlatrikoṇa*; a specific favorable zodiacal position</note> signs, as long as they occupy the "angles" <term>Kaṇṭaka: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, also called Kendras</term>, are all mutual significators of one another. However, the one situated in the tenth house from another is especially significant. || 1 ||

**Commentary:** If a planet is in its own sign (*Svarkṣa*), in its exaltation (*Tuṅga*), or in its root-trine (*Mūlatrikoṇa*), and is situated in the angles or centers starting from the Ascendant, and if there is another such planet also in an angle, then those two planets are called mutual "Significators" (*Kāraka*) to each other. Among these, the one situated in the tenth house (*Karmaga*) from another planet is particularly designated as a Significator. Thus it is said: "the one in the tenth is especially so." || 1 ||

**Vernacular Translation:** As many planets as are in their own signs, exaltation, or root-trine and are in mutual angles to each other, all those planets are called mutual significators. Among them, the one that resides in the tenth house from another is a significator in a special sense. || 1 ||

->Now, to demonstrate an example of this, the author speaks in the *Rathoddhatā* meter:<-

> When the Moon is in the rising sign of Cancer, and Mars, Saturn, the Sun, and Jupiter are in their respective signs of exaltation, they are declared mutual significators. For a planet in the Ascendant, any planet in the tenth or fourth house is a significator. || 2 ||

**Commentary:** For example, if the Moon (*Uḍupa*) is in the rising sign of Cancer (*Karkaṭa*), and Mars (*Kuja*), Saturn (*Yama*), the Sun (*Arka*), and Jupiter (*Sūri*) are in their exaltation signs—Mars in Capricorn, Saturn in Libra, the Sun in Aries, and Jupiter in Cancer—then they are called mutual significators. In this manner, however many such planets there are, they are mutually named significators. By this example, it is demonstrated that even if planets are in their own signs, exaltations, or trines outside the birth Ascendant, if they are in mutual angles, they still obtain the name of significator. Regarding "For a planet in the Ascendant": for a planet situated in the first house, any planet situated in the sky (the 10th house) or in the water (the 4th house) is designated a significator. This means that even if a planet in the Ascendant is in its own sign, exaltation, or trine, the one in the tenth from it...

Or if that planet is in the fourth house and is situated in its own sign of exaltation, its "moolatrikona" <note>a specific favorable position in a zodiac sign</note>, or its own home sign, it becomes a "Karaka" <note>a significator or 'doer' planet</note> for the planet in the ascendant, but the planet in the ascendant is not a Karaka for it. Thus it is said: for the planet in the ascendant, those in the tenth and fourth houses are fully effective. || 2 ||

**Vernacular Explanation:** For example, if the Moon is in the ascendant in Cancer, Mars is in Capricorn, Saturn is in Libra, the Sun is in Aries, and Jupiter is in Cancer—since these four planets are in their own signs or signs of exaltation and fall in mutual angles (Kendras), they become mutual Karakas. Those planets situated in exaltation in the fourth and tenth houses from the ascendant-occupying planet are especially significant Karakas.

<insert>
[North Indian style Astrological Chart containing the numbers 5, 3, 6, 8, 7, 4, 2, 1, 10, 9, 11, 12 and the planetary names Saturn, Moon, Jupiter, Sun, Mars]
</insert>

As in this example: from Saturn, the Moon and Jupiter are in the 10th house in their own signs and exaltation, making them both special Karakas. Similarly, from Mars, Saturn is in the tenth house in its sign of exaltation, making it a special Karaka. Planets that provide happiness, kingdom, and prosperity to the native are called Karakas.
When Karaka planets fall in mutual angles, they assist each other in giving auspicious results. They provide favorable outcomes during their mutual major and minor planetary periods (Dasha-Antardasha).

### Now, another characteristic is described in the Anushtubh meter:

> **If a planet in its moolatrikona or exaltation is in the tenth house (Karma) from another,**
> **and is a friend endowed with those qualities, it is also known as a Karaka. || 3 ||**

"In its own trine or exaltation..." means that being in its own moolatrikona or exaltation is the cause for a planet's Karaka status, not merely being in an angle. Thus, even without considering the ascendant's center, if any planet is situated in the tenth house (the house of action) from another planet, and that planet is in its own sign, exaltation, or moolatrikona, it qualifies. Furthermore, it must be a natural friend to the planet from which it is tenth, and not just a natural friend, but also a "temporary friend" according to the rules of planetary friendship, thereby achieving the status of a "Great Friend" (Adhimitra). Such a planet is called a Karaka. However, the planet from which it is tenth does not become its Karaka. This designation of Karaka is particularly useful in "Yatra" <note>Astrology related to journeys or military expeditions</note>. As it is said there: "A king should set out during the period of a Karaka planet of his native country, avoiding empty or afflicted planetary periods." Similarly, the Moon in a Karaka sign, joined with auspicious houses, bestows victory, happiness, and wealth. || 3 ||

**Vernacular Explanation:** A planet being in its exaltation, home, or moolatrikona is the reason for its Karaka status, not just being in an angle from the ascendant. Therefore, if a planet situated in its exaltation etc., is in the tenth house from another planet also in exaltation, and is a natural friend, it also becomes a Karaka. || 3 ||

<page-num>365</page-num>
<header>Page 365, including the Sanskrit commentary by Bhattotpala and the Hindi translation</header>

**Special Meaning—** The mention of the tenth and fourth houses is a specific qualification because planets situated in the tenth and fourth houses from each other possess "temporary friendship" <note>original: "Tatkalika Maitri"</note>. If these planets also possess "natural friendship" <note>original: "Naisargika Maitri"</note>, they become "great friends" <note>Adhimitra</note>, which results in a specialized power to produce effects (Karaka-status) || 3 ||

->Now, he describes the purpose of the "Significator" (Karaka) designation in the Anushtubh meter:<-

> A birth is auspicious when it occurs in a *Vargottama* <note>The best division; when a planet occupies the same sign in both the main chart and the 9th divisional chart</note>, when a benefic planet occupies the *Veshi* position <note>The 2nd house from the Sun</note>, when the *Kendras* <note>The angular houses: 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th</note> are not empty, and when "Significator" planets are present. || 4 ||

**Auspiciousness:** If a person's birth occurs when the rising sign's 9th division <note>Navamsha</note> is a *Vargottama*, or if the Moon is in a *Vargottama* division, that birth is auspicious. The second sign from the sign where the Sun is located at the time of birth is called the *Veshi* position. If a "good planet" <note>a benefic, such as Mercury, Jupiter, or Venus</note> is in that *Veshi* position, the birth is also auspicious. If even one of the four *Kendras* (angles) is not empty <note>contains a planet</note>, the birth is auspicious. Here, a *Kendra* occupied by a benefic planet is especially auspicious. As the author himself has said: "If there is not even one benefic planet in the *Kendras* during a journey, at birth, or at the time of an action, the teachers say it is not auspicious." If there are planets designated as "Significators" <note>Karakas</note> in the birth chart, that birth is also auspicious. The greater the number of these qualities, the more auspicious the birth will be. 4

**Vernacular Translation—** If the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note> or the Moon is in a *Vargottama Navamsha*, the birth is auspicious. Alternatively, if there is a benefic planet in the second house from the Sun, the birth is auspicious. Or, if the *Kendra* positions from the Ascendant are not empty—meaning there is a planet in any of the angles—the birth is auspicious. Furthermore, if there are "Significator" <note>Karaka</note> planets in the birth chart, the birth is auspicious. This means a person born under such a configuration becomes successful, famous, and happy. 4.

->Now, he describes the yoga (combination) by which one becomes happy in their youth, and the timing of the fruits of the "Period Lord" <note>Dashapati</note> in the Vaitaliya meter:<-

> Jupiter, the Lord of the Moon-sign, and the Lord of the Ascendant provide happiness in the middle of life when situated in the *Kendras*. Planets in "Rear-rising," "Both-rising," and "Head-rising" signs give their fruits at the end, the middle, and the beginning of their periods, respectively. || 5 ||

**In the middle of life:** Jupiter, the Lord of the sign where the Moon is placed <note>Janmapa</note>, and the Lord of the Ascendant <note>Lagnapa</note>—if any of these are in the *Kendras* (angles) of the chart, they provide happiness in the middle of one's life; this means the person becomes happy in their youth. On this, Yavaneshwara <note>An ancient authority on Greco-Indian astrology</note> says: "For those whose Lord of the Moon-sign, Lord of the Ascendant, or powerful Jupiter is in a quadrant, they shall receive the fruits of that time in the four stages of life." Regarding "Rear-rising" <note>Prishtodaya</note> etc.: If the Period Lord <note>Dasha-pati</note>, at the start of its period, is in a "Rear-rising" sign (Aries, Taurus, Cancer, Sagittarius, or Capricorn), it gives its results at the *end* of its period. If it is in the "Both-rising" sign (Pisces), it gives results in the *middle* of the period. If it is in a "Head-rising" <note>Shirshodaya</note> sign (Gemini, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, or Aquarius)...

# Page 366
## Brihat Jataka: Miscellaneous Chapter

...it happens that at the time of entering the first phase of the planetary period <term>Dasha</term>, it becomes the giver of results. In this way, the ripening of both auspicious and inauspicious effects should be declared. Having divided the duration of the period into three parts, the time when the ripening of its fruit is known—whether at the beginning, middle, or end—the Moon provides the indications of good results, and the malefic planets do otherwise. This should be understood by dividing the period into three parts. All previously mentioned results of the periods should be applied. How is it known that the lord of the period gives its fruit while situated at the moment of entry? It has been stated generally by the Lords of the Yavanas <note>Yavaneshwara refers to the "Lord of the Greeks," indicating the influence of Greco-Indian astrology</note> and others; it is also stated by the words of the venerable Garga. Thus says the venerable Garga:

> "The lord of the period, situated at the time of the entry into the period, should be declared as giving results at the beginning, end, or middle, depending on whether the sign rises by the head, the back, or both." || 5 ||

**Vernacular Translation —** If Jupiter, the lord of the birth sign <term>Janma Rashi</term>, and the lord of the ascendant <term>Lagna</term> are in quadrants <term>Kendras</term>, they provide happiness in the middle of life (youth). A planet situated in a sign that rises from the back <term>Prishthodaya</term> (Aries, Taurus, Cancer, Sagittarius—first half, Capricorn) gives its results at the end of its period. One in a sign rising both ways <term>Ubhayodaya</term> (Pisces) gives results in the middle of the period. One in a sign rising by the head <term>Shirshodaya</term> (Gemini, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Sagittarius—latter half, Scorpio, Aquarius) gives its results at the very beginning of its period. || 5 ||

->Now, he describes the timing of the results of the Eight-fold Chart <term>Ashtakavarga</term> in the Pushpitagra meter:<-

**The Sun and Mars give results at the time of entry; Jupiter and Venus when they have reached the middle of the house.**
**Saturn and the Moon give results when they are departing; but the son of the Moon (Mercury) gives results at all times.** || 6 ||

->Thus ends the twenty-second chapter, the Miscellaneous Chapter, in the Brihat Jataka composed by the illustrious teacher Varahamihira. || 22 ||<-

Regarding "The Sun etc.": During the time of ripening according to the transits, in whichever sign the Sun (Aditya) bestows the results of the Eight-fold Chart—whether auspicious or inauspicious—it bestows that fruit while situated in the first third (the entry) of that sign. The same applies to Mars (Rudhir). Jupiter (Jiva) and Venus (the son of Bhrigu)—these two, Jupiter and Venus, become givers of results when they have reached the middle of the house or sign, meaning the middle third. Saturn (the son of the Sun) and the Moon—these two give results when they are departing, meaning situated in the final third of the sign. Mercury (the son of the Moon) is a giver of results at all times; situated in any part, he provides the fruit. For as long as he stays in the entire sign, he gives the auspicious or inauspicious fruit as it has been earned. || 6 ||

->Thus ends the twenty-second chapter, the Miscellaneous Chapter, in the commentary on the Brihat Jataka composed by the illustrious Bhattotpala. || 22 ||<-

**Vernacular Translation —** The Sun and Mars, both of these give their respective results according to the Eight-fold Chart at the very time of entering a sign. Jupiter and Venus give results in the middle of the sign, Saturn and the Moon at the end of the sign, and Mercury gives his results always.

**Special Note —** There are 30 degrees in one sign; therefore, up to 10 degrees should be understood as the beginning of the sign, up to 20 degrees as the middle, and up to 30 degrees as the end. || 6 ||

# Chapter 23: On Unfavorable Combinations

Now, the chapter on unfavorable combinations is being explained. At the very beginning, the knowledge of births devoid of wife and children is stated in the *Shardulavikridita* <note>A specific classical Sanskrit poetic meter consisting of 19 syllables per line</note> meter:

->If the houses of children and wife, relative to the Ascendant or the Moon, are occupied or aspected by benefics or their own lords, then there is prosperity in those areas; otherwise, their absence is known. When the Sun is in the rising sign of Virgo, and Saturn is in Pisces, it destroys the wife; and when Mars is in the fifth house, it causes the death of the child. (1)<-

**Relative to the Ascendant...** In anyone's birth, if the "child-house" <term>Putra-bhava</term> <note>The 5th house in a horoscope</note> is joined with or aspected by a benefic planet or its own lord, it should be said that there is prosperity regarding children. Similarly, if the 5th house from the Moon is joined or aspected by a benefic or its own lord, there is prosperity of children. If the 5th house from both the Ascendant and the Moon is neither joined nor aspected by a benefic or its own lord, then the impossibility of children—childlessness—should be declared.

In this context, some describe twelve types of sons:
1. **Legitimate** <note>born of a legal wife</note>
2. **Appointed** <note>born of a wife by a kinsman</note>
3. **Adopted**
4. **Artificial** <note>made a son through mutual agreement</note>
5. **Low-born**
6. **Secretly born**
7. **Cast-off** <note>abandoned by parents and taken in</note>
8. **Son of a remarried woman**
9. **Son of an unmarried girl**
10. **Son of a pregnant bride**
11. **Purchased**
12. **Son of a female slave**

Thus, it is said in the *Saravali* <note>A classic 8th-century astrological text by Kalyanavarman</note>:

> "If the house of children is a benefic sign, or joined by a benefic, or aspected by a benefic, the birth of a son certainly occurs for men, and not the opposite. If the house is in a division of Jupiter or a benefic sign, and aspected by benefics from the Ascendant or the Moon (whichever is stronger), a **Legitimate** son is born. The number of children is equal to the number of *Navamshas* <note>The 1/9th divisional chart</note>; if in a benefic division, that many are seen. If aspected by a benefic, the number is doubled; if in a malefic division or aspected by a malefic, it is distressed. If the house is in a sign of Saturn, having Saturn's qualities, and aspected by Mercury but devoid of the aspect of Jupiter, Mars, or the Sun, it produces an **Appointed** son; the same applies to Mercury's influence when aspected by Saturn. If the child-house and the Moon are in Saturn's sign and joined or aspected by Saturn, the birth of an **Adopted** son occurs; the same applies to Mercury for a **Purchased** son. If Mars is in the 7th portion and Saturn is in the 5th house, and it is free from the aspect of other planets, one should know it as an **Artificial** son. If the 5th house is in a division of Saturn and the Sun is placed there, aspected by Mars, the son born is said to be **Low-born**. If the Moon is in a division of Mars in the 5th house and aspected by Saturn, a **Secretly born** son occurs, provided no other planets aspect. If Mars is in the same position but in a division of Saturn and aspected by the Sun, the son is **Cast-off**, according to the words of the Sage Charaka. If the Moon is in a division of Saturn, joined with Saturn in the 5th house, and aspected by Venus and the Sun, the son is one of a **Remarried woman**..."

# 368 Brihat Jataka: Chapter on Misfortunes

If the Sun aspects or is conjoined <note>original: "sahite"</note> with the fifth house, a son born to an unmarried woman <term>kanina: a son born to a maiden</term> is possible. If the Sun and Moon are in their own divisions <term>varga: divisional charts used to determine planetary strength</term> in the fifth house, and are aspected only by Venus, the son is said to be "brought along" <term>sahodha: a son born to a woman who was pregnant at the time of her marriage</term>.

When the fifth house is a sign owned by a malefic planet and is occupied by powerful malefics, and lacks any aspect from a benefic planet, the person born will be childless. However, if that house is in the Navamsha <note>a one-ninth sub-division of a sign</note> of Venus and is aspected by Venus, one should say the children are born of a female slave; some teachers say this also applies to the Moon. If the divisions of Venus and the Moon are in the fifth house and are aspected by or conjoined with them, there will generally be daughters; otherwise, if the divisions belong to other planets, there will be sons.

Thus, from the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the rising sign</term> or from the Moon, if the seventh house (the house of the spouse) is occupied or aspected by a benefic or by its own lord, it should be said that the person possesses the wealth of a spouse. Conversely, if the seventh house from the Ascendant or the Moon is not occupied or aspected by a benefic or its own lord, it should be said that the person lacks the wealth of a spouse—meaning, he will have no wife.

As it is said: "Otherwise, the impossibility should be known." This means the absence <note>original: "abhava"</note> of children and spouse is to be understood. Here, the mention of "children and spouse" is illustrative; the status of all houses, such as the body (first house) and others, must be investigated from both the Ascendant and the Moon, as both are designated as "the self" <note>original: "murti"</note>. As Yavanesvara <note>An ancient authority on Greco-Indian astrology</note> says: "One should know the self through both the Horoscope (Ascendant) and the Moon."

Regarding the house of the spouse, some describe specific details: "If Venus, Moon, Jupiter, and Mercury—all four, or three, or two, or even one—are in the seventh house, or if the house belongs to them or is aspected by them, there will be wives corresponding to the nature of those signs and divisions. Similarly, destruction of the spouse occurs through malefics from the Ascendant or Moon depending on their strength. In the seventh house of Saturn and Mars, the wife of a man may be a remarried woman <term>punarbhu: a woman who takes a second husband</term>. The number of wives corresponds to the number of divisions of the house-lord, or by the aspects. Only one wife is predicted if the seventh house is in the divisions of the Sun or Mars, or if Jupiter and Mercury are there. Generally, if the Moon and Venus are strong or in the seventh house, or aspecting it, there are many wives, especially so with Venus. With Jupiter and Venus, the wives are of one's own caste; with the Sun, Mars, and Saturn, they are of lower status. If Venus is involved, they are like prostitutes; the school of Ketumala says this also applies to the Moon."

"Pathona" etc.: <term>Pathona</term> refers to the sign Virgo. If Virgo is the Ascendant and the Sun is placed there, and the son of the Sun (Saturn) is in Pisces, then he becomes a "wife-killer" <note>original: "daraha"</note>, meaning he destroys his spouse. One must predict the death of the wife during the man's lifetime. In this same combination, if Virgo is the Ascendant with the Sun in it, and the son of the Earth (Mars) goes to the house of children (the fifth house) and stays in Capricorn, then he gives the death of a son. One must predict the death of the son during the man's lifetime.

**Vernacular Translation—** If the 5th house from the Ascendant or the Moon is conjoined with or aspected by a benefic planet and its own lord, then he has the wealth of sons (many good sons). Similarly, the seventh...

If the house <note>the 7th house of marriage</note> is joined or aspected by beneficial planets and its own lord, one should understand it as "wife-wealth" (having many wives or full happiness from a wife). Otherwise (if there is no connection with benefits or the lord, and instead there is connection or aspect from malefic planets), one should understand it as a lack of sons and a wife. ->Now, he describes three combinations for the death of a wife while the husband is still living, using the Praharshini meter:<-

### If malefic planets are placed in the squares (4th and 8th) from Venus,
### or if the Son of Bhrigu <note>Venus</note> is situated between two malefics,
### and is neither joined with nor aspected by benefic planets,
### the death of the wife occurs by fire, a fall, or a noose. ||2||

**Regarding "By malefic planets":** Malefic planets are the Sun, Mars, and Saturn. If these are placed in the squares—meaning the fourth and eighth positions—from Venus in a person's birth chart, the <term>death of the wife (jayavadha)</term> occurs by <term>fire (dahana)</term>. While the man is still living, his wife destroys herself by fire. Alternatively, if Venus (the Son of Bhrigu) is situated between two malefics—one in the twelfth house and the other in the second house from it—the <term>death of the wife occurs by a fall (nipata)</term> from a great height. While the man is living, his wife dies from falling. This also applies if Venus is in the same sign but placed between two malefics (one at a lower degree and one at a higher degree). Furthermore, if in a birth chart Venus is not joined with any of the benefic planets, nor is it aspected (seen) by them, the <term>death of the wife occurs by the noose (pasha)</term>. While the man is living, his wife destroys herself by hanging. Some have explained this as only two combinations: one where malefics are in the 4th/8th from Venus, and a second where Venus is between malefics and lacks benefic influence. They view the results (fire, fall, noose) as options for both. But that is incorrect; as the Lord Garga says:

> "If Saturn, Mars, or the Sun are in the 4th or 8th from Venus, death is by fire.
> If Venus is situated between two of them, death is by a fall.
> If Venus is devoid of the aspect or company of benefics, death of the wife is by the noose." ||2||

**Vernacular Translation**—If malefic planets (Saturn, Sun, Mars) are in the 4th or 8th house from Venus, or if Venus is between two malefic planets, and if Venus is [not] joined or aspected by benefics...

*Now, the author describes the birth combinations for impaired vision and physical defects in the wife using the Vasantatilaka meter:*

->**If the Moon and the Sun are situated in the twelfth and sixth houses from the Ascendant,**<-

Regarding "In the seventh": If Venus and the Sun are both in the seventh house from the Ascendant, or both in the ninth or both in the fifth, they say the native has a "deformed wife." This means the wife will have a missing or impaired limb. Here, some interpret the combination of Venus and the Sun in the seventh, ninth, or fifth as occurring "wherever possible" <note>referring to the astronomical proximity of the Sun and Venus</note>. > "If Venus and the Sun are together in the fifth, ninth, or seventh house,
> the one who has this will have a wife who is deprived of one limb." ||3||

**Vernacular Translation:** If the Moon and the Sun are in the 12th and 6th houses from the Ascendant, a person is born who, along with his wife, has only one eye. If Venus and Mars <note>The vernacular text here says Mars, though the Sanskrit verse and commentary specify the Sun (Arka)</note> are in the seventh, ninth, or fifth house from the Ascendant, the native's wife is physically deformed. ||3||

<meta>This page continues the astrological discussion on planetary combinations (yogas) that determine the nature of a person's marriage and offspring, specifically focusing on infertility and infidelity.</meta>

This occurs in the signs of the Virgin <note>Virgo</note>. By using the term "husband of a barren woman" instead of simply saying "sonless," the author indicates that while he may have a wife from his youth and follow lawful desires, no children are produced. Regarding "malefic planets": if malefic planets are situated in the twelfth house <term>Vyaya-sthana; the house of loss</term>, the seventh house <term>Mada-sthana; the house of passion/marriage</term>, or the rising sign <term>Lagna; the ascendant</term>—either in two of these or just one—and if the Moon is waning and placed in the fifth house <term>Dhi-stha; the house of intellect and children</term>, then a person is born without a son and without a wife. **Vernacular Translation:** If Saturn is in the Ascendant, Venus is in a "sign-junction" <note>Rashi-sandhi; the very end of Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces</note> while occupying the seventh house, and if the fifth house is not occupied by a benefic planet or the lord of the fifth house, the subject becomes the husband of a barren woman. If malefic planets are in the 12th, 7th, and 1st houses, and a waning Moon is in the 5th house, a person is born devoid of both son and wife. ||4||

### Now, the knowledge of relations with other women is told in the Harini meter:

**If Venus is in a division <term>Varga; a sub-divisional map</term> of Saturn or Mars and is placed in the seventh house and aspected by them, the man frequents other women. If Saturn and Mars are in the seventh house along with the Moon, both the man and his wife become unchaste. If Venus and the Moon are in the seventh, the man is wifeless or childless. If these two <insert>Venus and Moon</insert> are in the seventh and aspected by benefics, the couple becomes aged.** ||5||

**Commentary:** "Of Saturn and Mars": If Venus is in a division belonging to either Saturn or Mars and is situated in the seventh house from the Ascendant, and is "aspected by them"—meaning seen by either Saturn or Mars—the person born becomes a "frequenter of other women" <note>original: "parayuvatiga"</note>, meaning an adulterer. "If those two...": If those two, Saturn and Mars, are in the seventh house in the same sign along with the Moon, and Venus is in their division and aspected by them, then the person born is "unchaste along with his wife" <note>original: "pumshchalah"</note>. This means the man goes to other men's wives, and his wife goes to other men. "Of the son of Bhrigu and the Moon": Venus <note>Bhriguja</note> and the Moon <note>Shashi</note>. If these two are in the same sign in the seventh house, the man born is "wifeless" <note>abharyo</note> or "childless" <note>visuto</note>. The word "or" here functions as "and," not as an alternative; he is both wifeless and childless. "Aged bodies": If the male and female planets <note>Venus and Moon</note> are in the seventh house and are "seen by benefics"—aspected by any auspicious planet—then the "husband and wife have aged bodies." This means that in his old age, he is joined by an elderly wife. ||5||

**Vernacular Commentary—** If Venus is situated in the divisions <note>Varga: sub-divisions like Navamsha used for fine-tuning strength</note> of Saturn or Mars, occupies the seventh house, and is aspected by <note>viewed by</note> Saturn and Mars, the person born will seek the company of others' wives.
