->Now, other unfavorable combinations are stated in the Mandakranta meter:<-

## **The destroyer of the lineage is formed by the Moon, Venus, and malefics in the 10th, 7th, and 4th houses;**
## **One becomes an artisan if Mercury is in a decanate aspected by Saturn from a cardinal house;**
## **One is born of a slave-woman if Venus is in the twelfth house in a division of Saturn;**
## **One is base-born if the Sun and Moon are in the seventh house and aspected by Saturn. ||6||**

**The destroyer of the lineage etc.** The Moon, Venus <note>original: "Daityejya" - the teacher of the demons</note>, and the malefic planets <note>original: "Papa" - the Sun, Mars, and Saturn</note> are located in the 10th <note>Kha</note>, 7th <note>Mada</note>, and 4th <note>Sukha</note> houses. When a birth occurs with these planets in these specific places, the person becomes a "destroyer of the lineage" <note>Vanshachhetta</note>. This means: if in a birth chart the Moon is in the 10th, Venus is in the 7th, and the malefics are in the 4th, the lineage is destroyed; the family line comes to an end, much like the fate of Duryodhana <note>The antagonist of the Mahabharata whose entire line was killed in war</note>.

**An artisan in a decanate etc.** If the decanate <note>original: "Tryamsha" or "Drekkana" - a 10-degree division of a sign</note> occupied by Mercury <note>original: "Shashisuta" - son of the Moon</note> is aspected by Saturn <note>original: "Arki" - son of the Sun</note> who is situated in a cardinal house <note>Kendra</note>, the person becomes an artisan <note>Shilpi</note>. This means they earn their living through crafts like painting and similar arts. 

On this point, some commentators describe the aspect of Saturn on the sign occupied by Mercury. They argue that if the sign is aspected, the decanate within it is also aspected. However, if this view were intended by the Great Teacher <note>Varahamihira, the author</note>, he would have simply said "Mercury aspected by Saturn in a cardinal house makes one an artisan." He would not have specifically mentioned the "decanate." Because he did mention it, we conclude that the specific decanate division is vital to the calculation. Therefore, the consideration of the aspect on the decanate-sign is not merely general, but must be calculated precisely.

**Born of a slave-woman etc.** If Venus <note>original: "Ditisutaguru"</note> is in the twelfth house <note>original: "Riphpha"</note> from the Ascendant, and specifically in a Navamsha <note>9th-part division</note> belonging to Saturn, the person is said to be born of a slave-woman. 

**Base-born etc.** If the Sun and Moon...

**Vernacular Translation:** If Venus and Mars are in the seventh house and are aspected by malefic planets, the person suffers from disease (a visible, manifest illness). If the Moon is joined with a <term>Malefic Planet</term> and is in the Navamsha of Cancer or Scorpio, the person suffers from a secret disease—that is, a disease that cannot be easily identified or is hidden. If malefic planets are in the 12th and 2nd houses, the Moon is in the ascendant, and the Sun is in the 7th house, the person has white leprosy. If the Moon is in the 10th house, Mars is in the 7th, and Saturn is in the second place from the Sun, the person is <term>Deformed</term> (missing a limb). || 7 ||

# Brihat Jataka: Chapter on Inauspicious Combinations
<page-num>374</page-num>

->Now, he describes other inauspicious combinations in the *Vasantatilaka* meter:<-

> If the Moon is situated between two malefic planets <note>specifically Saturn and Mars</note> and the Sun is in Capricorn, the person born will suffer from asthma, consumption, enlargement of the spleen, internal abscesses, or chronic enlargement of the spleen (gulma). One becomes emaciated (consumptive) if the Sun and Moon are in each other's signs or navamsas <note>a 1/9th division of a sign</note>, or if they are both together in either of those two signs. || 8 ||

**Commentary:** Regarding the phrase "between": whenever the Moon is placed between two malefics—Saturn and Mars—and the Sun is in Capricorn, those born under this alignment suffer from asthma, consumption, spleen disorders, abscesses, and *gulma* <note>a term for abdominal tumors or chronic dyspepsia</note>. "Asthma" is well-known; "consumption" refers to the wasting away of the body; "spleen" is the well-known mass of flesh on the left side of the abdomen; "abscess" and "*gulma*" are well-known diseases. The meaning is that they will be afflicted by one of these ailments. Some read this in the singular: "one becomes a sufferer of asthma, consumption..." etc.

Regarding "emaciated": if the Sun and Moon are in each other's signs or divisions—meaning the Sun is in Cancer and the Moon is in Leo, or if in any sign the Moon is in the Leo-division and the Sun is in the Cancer-division—then the person born becomes consumptive. Here, some interpret "in each other's signs and divisions" to mean the Moon is in Leo in a Leo-division and the Sun is in Cancer in a Cancer-division; they say such a person becomes consumptive. But that is incorrect. For the Lord Garga says: <note>original: "परस्परगृहे यातौ यदि वापि तदंशगौ । भवेतामर्कशीतांशु तदा शोषी प्रजायते ।।"</note> "If the Sun and Moon have gone to each other's houses, or even to those respective divisions, then one is born consumptive." 

Regarding "or in the sign": when both are simultaneously in the sign of the other—meaning both the Sun and Moon are together in Leo, or both are in Cancer—then the person born becomes consumptive or "lean." "Lean" means physically weak. || 8 ||

**Vernacular Translation:** If the Moon is between two malefic planets and the Sun is in Capricorn, the native suffers from asthma, consumption, spleen disease, abscesses, or *gulma*. If the Sun is in Cancer and the Moon is in Leo, or the Sun is in the Cancer-division and the Moon is in the Leo-division, or if both are together in either Cancer or Leo, the native will have consumption or a weak body. || 8 ||

->Now, he describes other inauspicious combinations in the *Vasantatilaka* meter:<-

> If the Moon is in the last part of Pisces, Cancer, Capricorn, or Aries, and is joined with or aspected <note>viewed by a planetary 'glance'</note> by Saturn and Mars, the person becomes a leper. If Scorpio, Cancer, Taurus, or Capricorn fall in the fifth or ninth houses and are occupied or aspected by malefics, the person also becomes a leper. || 9 ||

**The Moon...** If the Moon is situated in the middle of Sagittarius <note>specifically in the fifth ninth-part or 'Navamsha'</note> and is joined with or aspected by <note>aspected: a term in astrology where one planet 'looks at' or influences another from a specific distance</note> Saturn or Mars, the person born will suffer from leprosy <term>Kushtha: a broad term in ancient texts for various skin diseases, including leprosy</term>. Alternatively, if the Moon is in any zodiac sign but falls within the ninth-part <term>Navamsha: a 3°20' subdivision of a sign used for fine-tuning predictions</term> of Pisces, Cancer, Capricorn, or Aries, and is joined or aspected by Saturn or Mars, the person will likewise have leprosy. However, if the Moon is aspected by a beneficial planet, the person will only suffer from a skin itch or rash rather than leprosy. As the Lord of the Greeks <note>original: "Yavaneshwara" - referring to an influential early authority in Indian astrology who preserved Greco-Egyptian traditions</note> says: "If the Moon is in the ninth-part of Pisces, Aries, or Capricorn and is aspected by a malefic, the body is destroyed by white leprosy; if aspected by a benefic, it causes an itching disorder."

Regarding the trines: If the signs Scorpio, Cancer, Taurus, or Capricorn fall in the trine positions <note>the 1st, 5th, or 9th houses of a birth chart</note> and are joined or aspected by malefic planets, the person born will suffer from leprosy. || 6 ||

**Vernacular Translation:** If the Moon is in the middle of Sagittarius (the 5th Navamsha) or in the Navamsha of Pisces, Cancer, Capricorn, or Aries in any sign, and is joined or aspected by Saturn or Mars, the native suffers from leprosy. Alternatively, if Scorpio, Cancer, Taurus, or Capricorn are in a trine (1, 5, 9) from the ascendant and are joined or aspected by malefic planets, the native also suffers from leprosy. || 6 ||

->Now he describes other unfavorable combinations in the Vasantatilaka meter:<-

> **The Sun, Moon, Mars, and Saturn, situated in the eighth, sixth, second, or twelfth houses in any manner,**
> **cause blindness in humans through the humor associated with the strongest planet.** || 10 ||

**The Sun, etc...** The Sun, the Moon, Mars, and Saturn—these four—if they are placed in any manner in the eighth, sixth, second, or twelfth houses, they produce blindness in the humans born under such a configuration. The phrase "in any manner" is used to indicate that there is no specific required order for these planets. This blindness is caused by the "humor" <term>Dosha: the three bodily humors—Vata (air), Pitta (bile), and Kapha (phlegm)</term> of whichever of these four planets is the strongest. The destruction of the eyes occurs due to the aggravation of that specific humor. || 10 ||

**Vernacular Translation:** If the Sun, Moon, Mars, and Saturn are somehow located in the 8th, 6th, 2th, or 12th houses, then the native's eyes are destroyed by the humor (phlegm, wind, or bile) associated with the strongest of these four planets. || 10 ||

### Now, he describes other unfavorable combinations in the Vaitaliya meter—

> **If malefic planets occupy the ninth, eleventh, third, or fifth houses and are not aspected by benefics,**
> **they certainly cause hearing impairment; if they are in the seventh house, they cause dental deformities. ||11||**

**Commentary:** Regarding "Nava..." (the ninth, etc.): If malefic planets—namely the Sun, Moon <note>The Moon is considered malefic here if it is waning or "dark"</note>, Mars, and Saturn—are positioned in the ninth, eleventh, third, or fifth houses as applicable, and are not "aspected" (viewed) by benefic planets, then due to the strength of the planetary affliction, they will certainly cause hearing impairment or <term>deafness</term> (badhirya). Regarding the term "malefics," the Sun, Moon, Mars, and Saturn mentioned previously should be understood. "And dental deformities in the seventh": If those same planets (Sun, Moon, Mars, and Saturn) are in the seventh house from the Ascendant and are not viewed by benefics, they cause deformities of the teeth. ||11||

**Vernacular Translation**— If <term>malefic planets</term> (ashubha-graha) are in the 9th, 11th, 3rd, or 5th houses and are not aspected by <term>benefic planets</term> (shubha-graha), they definitely cause <term>ear diseases</term> (karna-roga). If <term>sinful planets</term> (papa-graha) are in the seventh house and unseen by benefics, they produce disorders in the native's teeth. ||11||

> **When the Moon is rising while eclipsed by Rahu, and malefics are in the trines, the person is possessed;**

**Commentary:** Regarding "Udayati..." (rising, etc.): When the <term>Moon</term> (udupa) is in the Ascendant (rising) and is "in the mouth of the demon" <note>original: "asurasya-ge" — meaning eclipsed by Rahu</note>, and from that Ascendant, the malefics Saturn and Mars are in the trines (the ninth and fifth houses), the native becomes "possessed by spirits" (sapishacha). This means they are afflicted by spirits. Similarly, if the solar orb is eclipsed by Rahu and is in the Ascendant, and the malefics Saturn and Mars are in the trines from the Ascendant, the person born is "deprived of eyes" (nayana-pavarjita). This means they are blind. ||12||

**Vernacular Translation**— If <term>Rahu</term> eclipses the Moon in the Ascendant and <term>malefic planets</term> (Saturn and Mars) are in the ninth or fifth houses from it, the native is possessed by spirits. If the Sun is eclipsed by Rahu in the Ascendant and Saturn and Mars are in the trines, the native is blind. ||12||

**Touched** [by wind] etc. — He in whose birth the slow-moving planet Saturn is situated in the seventh house (the house of partnerships/descendant) and Jupiter is in the ascendant (the first house) is "touched" by wind. **By the lords of the sign and Navamsha** etc. — The lord of the <term>Navamsha</term> <note>a 1/9th division of a zodiac sign used for fine-tuning astrological strength</note> in which the Moon is situated is the "lord of the sign-portion." Those born under these conditions become slaves respectively. He who has one such planet becomes a slave by **agreement** <note>voluntary servitude, often for survival or to pay a debt</note>. He who has two is **purchased**; he becomes the slave of whoever buys him. He who has three or four is a **slave by birth**—the son of a slave man or woman, commonly known in the world as a "house-born slave." || 14 ||

# Brihat Jataka: Chapter on Unfavorable Combinations
<page-num>378</page-num>

**Vernacular Commentary—** If any one among the lord of the Navamsha <note>a 1/9th divisional chart used for fine-tuning predictions</note> of the birth sign, the Sun, the Moon, or Jupiter is in a debilitated or enemy's Navamsha, the native becomes an <term>Abhyupagama-dasa</term> (one who voluntarily approaches someone to serve as a servant). If two of these planets are in debilitated or enemy Navamshas, he becomes a <term>Kraya-dasa</term> (a servant purchased by another for life). If three or four of these planets are in debilitated or enemy Navamshas, he becomes a <term>Garbha-dasa</term> (a servant from the womb, i.e., the son of a servant, born into servitude). ||14||

->Now, the author speaks in the Harini meter to explain other unfavorable combinations:<-

**If Taurus, Aries, or Sagittarius is the Ascendant and is aspected by malefic planets, the person has deformed teeth.**
**If the Ascendant is a malefic sign, or Sagittarius, or Taurus, and is aspected by malefics, the person is bald.**
**If the Sun is in the ninth or fifth house and aspected by malefics, the person has weak eyesight.**
**If Saturn is so placed, he has many diseases; if Mars is so placed, the man is deformed. ||15||**

The commentary explains: If the Ascendant is Taurus, Aries, or Sagittarius and is aspected (looked upon) by malefic planets, the person has "Vikrita-dashana" or misshapen teeth. Malefic signs are the signs of malefic planets: Aries, Leo, Scorpio, Capricorn, and Aquarius. If any of these, or Sagittarius or Taurus, is the Ascendant and is aspected by malefics, the person born is <term>Khalati</term> (bald-headed). If the Sun is in the ninth or fifth house from the Ascendant and is aspected by malefic planets, the person has "Adridhekshana" (unsteady or weak eyes). Similarly, if Saturn is in the ninth or fifth house and aspected by malefics, the person suffers from "Naika-vyadhi" (many diseases). In the same way, if Mars is in the ninth or fifth house and aspected by malefics, the man born is "Vikala" (deformed or missing a limb). ||15||

**Vernacular Commentary—** If Taurus, Aries, or Sagittarius is the Ascendant and is aspected by a malefic planet, the native has deformed teeth. If a malefic sign (Aries, Scorpio, Leo, Capricorn, Aquarius), Sagittarius, or Taurus is the Ascendant, the native is <term>Khalvata</term> (a bald-headed person). If the Sun is in the 9th or 5th house and aspected by a malefic, the native has poor vision; if Mars is in the 9th or 5th and aspected by a malefic, he is afflicted with many diseases; if Saturn is in the 9th or 5th house and aspected by a malefic, the native is deformed. ||15|| <note>Note: The commentary slightly swaps the effects of Mars and Saturn compared to the Sanskrit verse above, a common variation in manuscript traditions.</note>

->**On Imprisonment**<-

**Regarding "Vyasuta..." [Verse 16]:** If malefic planets <note>non-benefic planets like Mars or Saturn</note> are situated in the 12th, 5th, 2nd, or 9th houses—or any combination thereof—the person born under such a configuration faces "confinement" <term>Nibandhanam: imprisonment or being bound</term>. This means the individual is captured or restrained. The nature of that confinement is "equal to the house" <note>Bhavana-samana</note>, meaning it corresponds to the characteristics of the zodiac sign <term>Rashi</term> involved.

Specifically:
*   If the Ascendant <term>Lagna</term> is **Aries, Taurus, or Sagittarius**, the person is bound with ropes <note>these are "quadruped" or four-legged signs</note>.
*   If the Ascendant is **Gemini, Virgo, Libra, or Aquarius**, the person is bound with chains or shackles <note>these are "human" or two-legged signs</note>.
*   If the Ascendant is **Cancer, Capricorn, or Pisces**, the person is kept guarded in a fortress or stronghold without physical bonds <note>these are "watery" signs</note>.
*   If the Ascendant is **Scorpio**, the person is confined in an underground vault or cellar.

**Regarding "The Bearer of the Serpent, Fetters, or Noose":** If the person is born in a Decan <term>Drekkana: a 10-degree subdivision of a sign</term> that is classified as a "Serpent," "Fetter," or "Noose" Decan, and if that sign is aspected <note>viewed</note> by a powerful malefic planet, then the confinement will be of the nature associated with that specific Decan.

The **Serpent Decans** <note>Bhujaga-drekkana</note> are:
*   The 2nd and 3rd parts of Cancer.
*   The 1st and 2nd parts of Scorpio.
*   The 3rd part of Pisces.

The **Fetter Decan** <note>Nigada-drekkana</note> is:
*   The 1st part of Capricorn.

Some commentators explain "Bearer of the Serpent, Fetters, and Noose" together. Therefore, if these specific degrees are aspected by strong malefics, the person will be "touched" by such fate. This is what is read in Verse 16.

---

### Vernacular Translation
If malefic planets are in the 12th, 5th, 2nd, or 9th houses from the Ascendant, the imprisonment of the native should be understood to match the nature of the sign containing the strongest malefic. If the Ascendant falls in a Serpent or Fetter Decan and is aspected by a powerful malefic, the native will be bound in a manner corresponding to that Decan.

---

### Special Meaning
The core idea is that in both aforementioned combinations, the native suffers imprisonment. The "nature of the sign" implies:
*   **Quadruped Signs:** Binding by rope.
*   **Biped (Human) Signs:** Binding by shackles/chains.
*   **Aquatic Signs:** Confinement without physical bonds (house arrest or fortress).
*   **Scorpio:** Confinement in a cave or underground pit.

---

### Serpent Decans
Cancer (2nd and 3rd); Scorpio (1st and 2nd); Pisces (3rd).
**Fetter Decan:** Capricorn (1st). See the Chapter on Decans for further detail.

# Page 380
## Brihat Jataka: Chapter on Inauspicious Results

Now, the author describes further inauspicious combinations using the Harini meter:

### If the Lord of the Night (the Moon) is joined with the son of the Sun (Saturn), is aspected by Mars, and is situated within a halo (Parivesha), the person born will be harsh-voiced, suffer from epilepsy, and consumption.
### If the Sun, Saturn, and Mars occupy the tenth house (the sky) without being aspected by benefics, the person becomes a servant; according to the number of these planets mentioned, they are of the best, lowest, or middle grade. || 17 ||

->Thus ends the twenty-third chapter on Inauspicious Results<-
->in the Brihat Jataka composed by the Great Teacher Varahamihira.<-

**Commentary:** Regarding "harsh-voiced" etc.: When the Lord of the Night (the Moon) is with the son of the Sun (Saturn), aspected by Mars <note>original: "vakra-aloka-gate"</note>, and joined with a halo <note>a celestial phenomenon where a circle of light appears around a luminary</note> at that time, the person born speaks harshly, always saying unpleasant things, suffers from <term>Apasmara</term> <note>epilepsy or falling sickness</note>, and <term>Kshayi</term> <note>consumption or tuberculosis</note>. 

Here, three conditions of the Moon are explained, and three afflictions. If the Moon meets one condition, the person has one affliction. If the Moon is with Saturn, they are harsh-voiced and always speak unpleasantly. If with Saturn and aspected by Mars, they suffer from epilepsy. If with Saturn, aspected by Mars, and in a halo, they suffer from consumption. 

Regarding "Sun, Saturn, and Mars": If the Sun, Saturn (Yama), and Mars (the son of Earth) occupy the tenth house <note>the "sky" or mid-heaven</note> and are not aspected by any of the benefic planets, the person born becomes a servant <note>original: "bhritaka"</note>. Based on these previously mentioned planets—Sun, Saturn, and Mars—the servant is of the best, lowest, or middle grade. With one such planet, the servant is "best" or superior, performing work that is not despised. With two, they are "middle." With three, they are "lowest," performing despised or menial labor. || 17 ||

->Thus ends the twenty-third chapter on Inauspicious Results<-
->in the Commentary on Brihat Jataka composed by Bhattotpala.<-

**Vernacular Translation—** If the Moon is joined with Saturn, aspected by Mars, and joined with a halo, the native is harsh-speaking, suffers from <term>Apasmara</term> (epilepsy), and is a consumptive patient. Furthermore, if one among the Sun, Saturn, or Mars is in the tenth house, they perform high-class service; if two planets are in the tenth, they perform middle-class service; if all three are in the tenth, they perform low-class service. || 17 ||

**Special Meaning—** If one of these conditions (Moon with Saturn, aspected by Mars, or in a halo) exists, the person is bitter-tongued; if two conditions exist, they have epilepsy; if all three exist, they suffer from consumption. || 17 ||

# Chapter 24: On the Horoscopes of Women

Now begins the explanation of the chapter regarding the horoscopes of women. At the very outset, the author <note>Varahamihira</note> describes the application of results previously mentioned for male births, as well as specific additions for women, using the *Vasantatilaka* meter:

> Whatever results are declared for the birth of men that are impossible for women,
> those should be applied to their husbands; all else should be assigned to the women themselves.
> Their husband’s death is seen from the eighth house, while their physical constitution
> is determined from the Ascendant and the Moon; their charm and their husband are seen from the seventh house. || 1 ||

**Whatever results:** In a male birth, whatever results are impossible or inapplicable to women should be declared as affecting their husbands. Regarding the results mentioned for male births—such as "having round, copper-colored eyes" and so on—those which are suitable for women should be attributed to them directly. Those which are impossible, such as "attaining a kingdom" <note>referring to traditional ruling roles</note>, should be predicted for the husband after examining the woman's birth chart. However, results that are possible for both, such as the fruits of the *Sunapha* yoga <term>Sunapha Yoga: A planetary combination signifying wealth and status</term>, should be declared for both.

These results are of three kinds: some are to be told of the women, some of their husbands, and some of both. Descriptions of physical appearance, like "round copper eyes," apply to the women themselves. Results like "Royal Yogas" <note>combinations for power</note> apply to their husbands. The results of yogas like *Sunapha*, which indicate happiness or sorrow, apply to both. Alternatively, the entirety of the woman's horoscope results may be applied to the husband.

**Regarding them:** For these women, the death of the husband is to be predicted from the eighth house <note>the house of longevity and transformation</note>, as will be explained later. The **body** (physicality and health) is determined by the Ascendant <term>Lagna: The rising sign on the eastern horizon at birth</term> and the Moon. Their **charm** (good fortune/grace) and the nature of the husband are to be told from the seventh house <note>the house of partnerships</note>. This too will be explained further. || 1 ||

**Vernacular Commentary:** Among the results previously stated for male horoscopes, those which are impossible in a female horoscope should be understood to apply to the woman's master (husband). That is, results possible for a woman should be stated for her just as for a man. All previously mentioned results should be applied to her husband according to the woman's Ascendant. A woman's husband's death should be told from the eighth house, physical results from the Ascendant and the Moon, and good fortune from the seventh house. || 1 ||

Regarding the statement "the body is determined from the Ascendant and the Moon," the author shows this using the *Vasantatilaka* meter:

> If the Ascendant and the Moon are in even signs,
> the woman is naturally feminine and endowed with good character and ornaments, especially if aspected by benefics.
> If both are in odd signs, she possesses a masculine appearance and character;
> if they are associated with or aspected by malefics, she is wicked and devoid of virtues. || 2 ||

# The Great Birth-Chart: Chapter on Female Horoscopy

->**On the Even Signs**<-

**In the even signs:** If both the Ascendant <note>Lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note> and the Moon are situated in even signs <note>Even signs are feminine: Taurus, Cancer, Virgo, Scorpio, Capricorn, and Pisces</note>, the woman is firmly established in her true nature; she possesses a feminine disposition. If these two (the Ascendant and the Moon) are also aspected <note>viewed by the astrological "glance" of a planet</note> by benefic planets, she is endowed with the ornament of good character. This means her virtuous conduct is her finery, or she is blessed with both good character and physical jewelry.

**In the odd signs:** If these same two are in odd signs <note>Odd signs are masculine: Aries, Gemini, Leo, Libra, Sagittarius, and Aquarius</note>, she possesses a masculine appearance and character. If the Ascendant and Moon are joined with or aspected by malefic planets <note>planets with a harsh influence, like Mars or Saturn</note>, she is sinful, of wicked character, and devoid of all virtues.

Now, if one is in an even sign and the other is in an odd sign, she will have a form and nature that is a mixture of male and female. Similarly, if one is joined with a benefic planet and the other with a malefic, she will be of mixed character—partly virtuous and partly not. The same applies if one is aspected by a benefic and the other by a malefic, or if both are influenced by a mix of benefics and malefics. One should use this logic to determine the remaining possibilities. || 2 ||

**Vernacular Translation —** If both the Ascendant and the Moon are in even signs, the woman is endowed with a feminine nature (soft luster, modesty, pleasant speech, etc.). If the Ascendant and Moon are aspected by benefic planets, she possesses an excellent disposition and is accompanied by fine clothes and ornaments. If both the Ascendant and Moon are in odd signs, that girl will have a masculine appearance and nature. If there is an aspect or conjunction of malefic planets upon them, she will be prone to sin and lacking in virtues. || 2 ||

**Special Meaning —** From this, it is established that if one of the two (Ascendant or Moon) is in an odd sign and the other in an even sign, and they are influenced by both malefic and benefic planets, she will be of a mixed nature. || 2 ||

---

Now, using the *Indravajra* meter, the author describes the nature of a woman born when the Ascendant or the Moon is in a sign of Mars, specifically according to the <term>Trishansha</term> <note>A 30th part of a zodiac sign, used to determine specific character traits</note> of Mars and others:

### A girl becomes wicked, enters servitude, is virtuous, deceptive, or of bad character;
### In the sign of the Earth’s Son (Mars), respectively, in the divisions (Trishanshas)
### Of Mars, Saturn, Jupiter, Mercury, and Venus. || 3 ||

**A girl becomes wicked:** In a sign of the Earth’s Son <note>Mars</note>—meaning if either Aries or Scorpio is the Ascendant or contains the Moon—the results should be stated according to the *Trishanshas* (30-degree divisions) of Mars, Saturn, Jupiter, Mercury, and Venus in sequence.

Specifically: If the Ascendant or Moon is in a sign of Mars and falls in the **Mars** *Trishansha*, the girl becomes wicked; even before marriage, she seeks the company of men. If born in the **Saturn** *Trishansha*, she enters into servitude or a state of slavery. In this same Martian sign, if she is in the **Jupiter** *Trishansha*, she is virtuous and of good character. If born in the **Mercury** *Trishansha*, she is deceptive...

Now, regarding what was said about the husband at the time of setting (the 7th house), he explains that knowledge through a verse in the <term>Shardulavikridita</term><note>A specific classical Sanskrit poetic meter</note> meter:

> If the seventh house is empty and weak, and not aspected by benefic planets, the husband is a contemptible man. If Mercury and Saturn are in the seventh, the husband is a eunuch. If the seventh house is a movable sign, he is always traveling. If the Sun is there, she is abandoned; if Mars is there and aspected by malefic planets, she becomes a widow in her youth. If Saturn is in the seventh and aspected by malefics, she reaches old age as a virgin. || 8 ||

**Commentary:** Regarding "Empty": If the seventh sign from the Ascendant or the Moon is empty (devoid of all planets) and weak (lacking strength), and in that empty, weak seventh house there is no aspect from <term>benefic planets</term><note>Sanskrit: Saumya-graha; planets like Jupiter, Venus, or Mercury that bring positive influence</note>—meaning it is neither seen nor joined by any auspicious planet—the husband of the woman born then is a "contemptible man" (a base or cowardly man). 

Alternatively, if either Mercury or Saturn is situated in the seventh sign from the Ascendant or the Moon, the husband of the woman born then is a eunuch (lacking virility). For one who has a "movable sign" in the seventh, her husband is "always traveling," meaning he is constantly away on journeys. Conversely, if the seventh is a fixed sign, he remains always at home; if it is a dual-natured sign, he is sometimes traveling and sometimes at home. 

Regarding "Abandoned by the Sun, a widow by Mars": If the Sun is in the seventh house, the woman is abandoned or cast off by her husband. If Mars is in the seventh and is aspected by <term>malefic planets</term><note>Sanskrit: Ashubha-graha; planets like Saturn or Mars that bring challenges</note>, she becomes a widow in her youth. If the son of the Sun (Saturn) is in the seventh house and is aspected by malefic planets...

"The maiden herself approaches old age," meaning she becomes an old woman while still a virgin. The implication is that she does not marry. This should be predicted based on the relative strength of the Moon and the Ascendant <note>The 'Lagna' or rising sign</note>. || 8 ||

**Vernacular Translation—** If the seventh house from the Ascendant and the Moon is devoid of planets, is weak, and is not aspected <note>seen</note> by benefic planets, then the husband of the girl born under this yoga <note>planetary combination</note> will be a base man (lacking in effort or status). If Mercury and Saturn are in the seventh house, the girl's husband will be impotent. If the seventh house contains a movable sign <term>Chara Rashi: signs like Aries or Cancer that indicate movement</term>, the husband will be a foreigner or traveler. If the Sun is in the seventh house, she is abandoned by her husband. If Mars is in the seventh house, she becomes a child-widow. If Saturn is in the seventh house, she reaches old age while still in her maidenhood. || 8 ||

**Special Meaning—** A movable sign in the seventh house makes the husband a traveler. From this, it is established that if a fixed sign <term>Sthira Rashi: signs like Taurus or Leo indicating stability</term> is in the seventh, her husband will always remain with her (at home). If it is a dual-natured sign <term>Dvisvabhava Rashi: signs like Gemini or Pisces</term>, he may be sometimes at home and sometimes abroad. || 8 ||

Now, how is this result understood from the seventh house from the Moon as well? It is said that because the results of the Moon in the seventh house have not been fully seen, the author explains what the woman's nature will be like using the *Shardulavikridita* meter:

> **If malefic planets are in the setting sign (7th house), she becomes a widow; if there is a mixture of planets, she becomes a remarried woman.**
> **If a malefic is weak in the 7th house but aspected by a benefic, she is abandoned by her own husband.**
> **If Venus and Mars are in each other's Navamsha (divisional signs), she is a woman attached to other men;**
> **Or if those two are with the Moon in the 7th house, then she acts so with her husband's permission. || 9 ||**

"By the fiery ones" <note>original: *Agneyair*, referring to malefic/fiery planets</note>... The results for individual malefic planets in the seventh have been stated. If many fiery/malefic planets are in the seventh house, then disregarding the individual results, she certainly becomes a widow. With a "mixture" of both malefics and benefics in the seventh, she becomes a *Punarbhu* <note>a woman who marries a second time</note>. This means she leaves her first husband and becomes the wife of another; she is "twice-consecrated." Thus, the definition of a *Punarbhu* is given in another text: "A self-willed woman who leaves her husband of the same caste out of desire and seeks another; if she is still a virgin <note>original: *akshata*, 'unscarred'</note>, she is a remarried woman consecrated again." Regarding "Malefic": if one of the malefics—Sun, Mars, or Saturn—is in the setting sign (7th from the Ascendant) and is "weak" (devoid of all strength) but "aspected by a benefic" (seen by Mercury, Jupiter, or Venus), the woman born is "abandoned" or rejected by her own husband. Regarding "In each other's Navamsha": Venus and Mars <note>original: *Sita-Avanijayoh*</note> being in each other's divisional signs—wherever they are, if Mars is in a Navamsha of Venus and Venus is in a Navamsha of Mars—then that woman is "attached to others," meaning she seeks other men. Alternatively, if those same two (Mars and Venus) are in the "Dyuna" (7th house) from the Ascendant...

**Old and Foolish**... If at a woman's birth, the seventh house from the ascendant <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> is a sign of Saturn (either Capricorn or Aquarius) or if a Navamsha <note>a one-ninth division of a zodiac sign used for precision</note> of Saturn is in the seventh house, her husband will be old and foolish. ### Now, the knowledge regarding the Moon's sign, Jupiter's sign, or the Sun's sign (or their Navamshas) being in the seventh house is told in the Pushpitagra meter—

->**Controlled by passion and soft-hearted if in the Moon's; if in the Teacher of the Gods' <note>Jupiter</note>, virtuous and self-controlled.**<-
->**Very mild and a great worker if in the Sun's; this occurs when the sign or Navamsha is situated in the setting house <note>the seventh house</note>. 12**<-

**Controlled by passion**... For a woman born when the Moon's sign (Cancer) or its Navamsha is in the seventh house, her husband will be under the sway of passion <note>lustful</note> and will be soft or gentle. If the sign of the Teacher of the Gods (Jupiter)—either Sagittarius or Pisces—or his Navamsha is in the seventh house, the husband will be virtuous, endowed with qualities like bravery, and self-controlled <note>original: "jitendriya," one who has conquered his senses</note>. If the Sun's sign (Leo) or its Navamsha is in the seventh house, the husband will be very mild and a "great worker" <note>original: "atikarmakrit"</note>, meaning one who is very industrious in business. Some interpret "atikarmakrit" as being excessively passionate or attached to sexual desires. Thus, the results are declared for the sign or Navamsha situated in the "setting" or seventh house. Where the sign in the seventh belongs to one planet and the Navamsha to another, the result should be predicted based on whichever of the two (the sign-lord or the Navamsha-lord) is stronger. 12.

**Vernacular Translation**—If at the time of birth the Moon's sign (Cancer) or Navamsha is in the seventh house, that woman's lord is passionate and soft-hearted. If it is Jupiter's sign or Navamsha, her lord is virtuous and has conquered his senses. If it is the Sun's sign or Navamsha, her husband is of a very mild nature and a great worker. 12.

# The Brihat Jataka: Chapter on Female Horoscopy

**Special Meaning—** If both the sign <term>Rashi; the 30-degree zodiac sign</term> and the <term>Navamsha; the ninth part of a sign used for divisional strength</term> of the seventh house belong to the same planet, the aforementioned results should be understood to apply fully. If they belong to different planets, the results should be predicted according to whichever ruler is stronger. If both the ruler of the sign and the ruler of the Navamsha are of equal strength, then a mixture of both results should be understood. <note>This refers to the characteristics of the husband based on the 7th house.</note>

Now, the author describes the nature of a woman when two or three planets—the Moon, Venus, and Mercury—are situated in the Ascendant <term>Lagna; the rising sign</term>, using the *Vasantatilaka* meter:

->**If the Moon and Venus are in the Ascendant, she is envious and devoted to pleasure.**<-
->**With Mercury and the Moon, she is skilled in the arts, happy, and virtuous.**<-
->**With Venus and Mercury, she is beautiful, fortunate, and knowledgeable in arts.**<-
->**If all three benefics are present, she possesses many riches, happiness, and virtues.**<-

**Commentary:** For a woman whose birth Ascendant contains both the Moon and Venus, she will be envious <note>original: "irshyanvita" - filled with jealousy or malice</note> and deeply attached to physical comforts. If Mercury and the Moon are in the Ascendant, she is an expert in the arts <note>original: "kalasu nipuna" - skilled in the 64 traditional arts</note>, lives a happy life, and is endowed with many good qualities. If Venus and Mercury are in the Ascendant, she is lovely to look at, possesses great charm, is beloved by her husband, and knows the arts. Regarding "all three": if the Moon, Mercury, and Venus are all in the Ascendant, she will be endowed with various types of wealth <note>original: "vasu" - riches</note>, happiness, and many virtues. By the word "also," it is implied that if the three natural benefics—Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus—are in the Ascendant, she likewise possesses great wealth, happiness, and virtue.

**Vernacular Translation—** If the Moon and Venus are in the birth Ascendant, the woman is envious and happy. If Mercury and the Moon are present, she is a connoisseur of the arts, happy, and virtuous. If Mercury and Venus are in the birth Ascendant, she is beautiful, fortunate, and knows the arts. If three benefic planets (Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus) are in the birth Ascendant, she possesses many kinds of wealth, happiness, and qualities.

Next, regarding the previous mention of the husband's death, the author explains how to determine the timing using the *Vasantatilaka* meter:

->**A malefic in the eighth house brings widowhood; the timing is told**<-
->**By the age associated with the lord of the Navamsha occupied by the eighth lord.**<-
->**If benefics are in the second house, she dies before her husband.**<-
->**With the Moon in Virgo, Scorpio, Taurus, or Leo, there are few children.**<-

**Commentary:** If a malefic planet <term>Krura-graha; "cruel" planets like Mars or Saturn</term> is in the eighth house <note>The house of longevity and the husband's life in a female chart</note>, widowhood occurs. At what time? The author says: look at the lord of the eighth house <note>original: "Nidhaneshvara"</note>. Find which planet's Navamsha that lord occupies. The "age" or period assigned to that Navamsha lord determines when, after marriage, her widowhood will occur. <note>The text refers to specific year-assignments for planets like one, two, nine, or twenty years used in traditional timing.</note>

The age of the planets. Some say this refers to physical age. We, however, use the word "age" to refer to the period of the *Dasha* <note>major planetary period</note> and *Antardasha* <note>sub-period</note>. When the lord of the eighth house <note>the house of longevity and widowhood</note> is in a Navamsha <note>ninth-part division of a sign</note> belonging to either the Moon or Mars, the "age" or duration is three years. In such cases, marriage often occurs for young girls, and widowhood is predicted during the sub-period of the lord of the Navamsha in which the eighth house ruler is situated. 

**Regarding the presence of benefics:** If a malefic planet is in the eighth house at birth, but a benefic planet <note>a "good" planet like Jupiter or Venus</note> is in the second house <note>the house of wealth and family</note>, then the woman herself will die before her husband. 

If at the time of birth, the Moon is situated in Virgo, Scorpio, Taurus, or Leo, it should be said that she will have few children. A woman whose Moon sign is any of these—Virgo, Scorpio, Leo—will have limited offspring. ||14||

**Vernacular Translation:** If a malefic planet is in the eighth house from the Ascendant at birth, that woman becomes a widow. In this yoga <note>planetary combination</note> for widowhood, the woman becomes a widow during the "state" (infancy, youth, or old age) or the period/sub-period of the planet in whose Navamsha the lord of the eighth house resides. If a benefic planet is in the second house, the woman’s own death occurs in the presence of her husband. She who has the Moon in Virgo, Scorpio, Taurus, or Leo at birth will have few children. 14.

### Now, with a verse in the Shardulavikridita meter, he describes two combinations: one where a woman becomes "masculine" in nature, and another where she becomes a "Brahmavadini" (a female philosopher or seeker of sacred knowledge)—

> If Saturn is of moderate strength, while the Moon, Venus, and Mercury are devoid of strength, and the remaining planets <note>Sun, Mars, and Jupiter</note> are endowed with power, and if the rising sign is an odd sign, the woman becomes "masculine" in nature. 
> 
> If Jupiter, Mars, Venus, and Mercury are strong, and the rising sign is an even sign, the woman becomes famous on earth, skilled in many sciences, and a "Brahmavadini" <note>one who discourses on the Vedas or Supreme Truth</note>. 15.

**Commentary:** Regarding "Saturn": When Saturn is of moderate strength—neither very strong nor very weak—and the Moon, Venus, and Mercury are devoid of strength, while the remaining planets (Sun, Mars, and Jupiter) are powerful wherever they may be situated, and if an odd sign <note>Aries, Gemini, Leo, Libra, Sagittarius, or Aquarius</note> is rising at the Ascendant—meaning she is born in an odd sign—then she becomes "masculine" <term>Purushini: a woman with masculine traits or one who associates with many men</term>. 

Regarding "Jupiter, Mars, Venus, and Mercury": When Jupiter, Mars, Venus, and Mercury are strong wherever they are placed, and if the Ascendant is an even sign <note>Taurus, Cancer, Virgo, Scorpio, Capricorn, or Pisces</note>, then the woman born becomes famous on earth, renowned everywhere, skilled in many sciences (knowledgeable in various fields of study), and also a *Brahmavadini* <note>original: "Brahmavadini"</note>, meaning she is skilled in the science of liberation <note>Moksha-shastra</note>. 15.

# The Brihat Jataka: Chapter on Female Horoscopy
<page-num>362</page-num>
<header>Chapter on Female Horoscopy in the Brihat Jataka</header>

**Vernacular Commentary—** If at the time of a woman's birth, Saturn is moderately strong, while the Moon, Venus, and Mercury are weak, and the Sun, Mars, and Jupiter are endowed with strength, and the <term>Ascendant (Lagna)</term> falls in an odd sign (such as Aries, Gemini, etc.), then that woman becomes "masculine" in nature <note>The term 'Purushini' suggests a woman who either possesses masculine traits, frequents the company of many men, or takes a dominant role</note>. If the Ascendant is in an even sign (Taurus, Cancer, etc.) and Jupiter, Mars, Venus, and Mercury are powerful, then that woman becomes famous in the world, skilled in various sciences <note>Shastras</note>, and a knower of <term>Brahmavidya</term> <note>The supreme knowledge of the Absolute or spiritual philosophy</note>. ||15||

*Now, the author describes the planetary combinations through which a woman takes up the life of an ascetic (renunciation) in the Praharshini meter—*

**If a malefic planet is in the seventh house, the woman will undoubtedly enter that specific type of ascetic order belonging to the planet situated in the ninth house. This entire system of interpretation should be applied at the time of marriage, during the selection of the bride, at the time of giving the girl away, and even during a horary inquiry.** ||16||

->Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter, titled "Female Horoscopy," in the Brihat Jataka composed by the illustrious teacher Varahamihira.<-

**Scholarly Commentary (by Bhattotpala)—** Regarding the verse "If a malefic...": Previously, the specific effects of planets in the seventh house were described individually. Here, if a malefic (cruel) planet is in the seventh house from the Ascendant, and if any other planet is situated in the ninth house from the Ascendant, then the woman does not receive the previously mentioned results <note>referring to marital results</note>. Instead, the young woman undoubtedly attains the <term>Pravrajya</term> <note>ascetic order or renunciation</note> associated with that planet in the ninth house. Thus is the female horoscope explained. 

Regarding "In marriage...": The combinations explained here should also be applied if they occur at the time of the wedding. Similarly, this entire system should be applied during the "selection of the bride" (the formal seeking of the girl), at the "time of giving" (the actual donation of the bride), and during "inquiry" (the time a question is posed to an astrologer). In female horoscopy, the auspicious and inauspicious combinations mentioned here are the ones to be declared, not necessarily everything mentioned in the general horoscopy of men. These should be understood according to the timing demonstrated. Furthermore, those combinations which are contradicted by the rules in the upcoming chapter on marriage <note>Vivaha-patala</note> should not be applied here. This chapter on marriage has been stated with logical reasoning. ||16||

->Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter, titled "Female Horoscopy,"<-
->in the commentary on Brihat Jataka composed by Sri Bhattotpala.<-

**Vernacular Commentary—** If at the time of a woman's birth, there is a malefic planet in the seventh house and any planet in the ninth house, then the woman enters an ascetic order (such as the Buddhist <term>Shakya</term> order, etc.) corresponding to that planet in the ninth house. If there is no planet in the ninth house, renunciation does not occur. All the results mentioned in this chapter should be considered from the marriage-ascendant, the selection of the bride (Tilak), the giving of the bride, and the horary ascendant. That is to say, marriage and other rites should be performed during the auspicious ascendants mentioned, and not in the inauspicious ones. ||16||

# Chapter 25: On the Exit from Life (Nairyāṇika)

*Now, the chapter regarding the exit from life is explained. First, the author describes how a person dies when the eighth house is either occupied or aspected <note>aspected: in astrology, when a planet "looks at" or influences another sign from a distance</note> by planets, using the Śārdūlavikrīḍita meter:*

**Death occurs in an instant through the eighth house; if planets are strong, it arises from the provocation of their respective humors.**
**If many strong planets are involved, death springs from multiple causes in the limb associated with that sign.**
**By Sun and the others in the eighth, death is caused by fire, water, weapons, fever, chronic disease, thirst, or hunger.**
**In movable and other signs, death occurs in foreign lands, at home, or on a journey respectively. ||1||**

"Death occurs..." etc. Death happens in an instant through the eighth house when planets are powerful. If the eighth house from the birth ascendant <term>Lagna: the rising sign at the moment of birth</term> is empty, but a strong planet aspects it, the person dies from the provocation of the "humor" <term>Dhatu: the biological substances or humors in Ayurvedic medicine</term> associated with that planet. For example: the Sun rules bile; the Moon rules wind and phlegm; Mars rules bile; Mercury rules all three (wind, bile, and phlegm); Jupiter rules phlegm; Venus rules wind and phlegm; and Saturn rules wind.

"In the limb associated with that sign": This refers to the eighth house from the ascendant. Death arises in the specific part of the body represented by the eighth sign in the "Time-Person" <note>Kāla-puruṣa: the personification of Time as a human body, where each zodiac sign corresponds to a body part</note> due to the provocation of the humors of the aspecting planet. If many planets are powerful and aspect the empty eighth house, death has multiple causes. The various humors of all those aspecting planets will provoke an ailment in the limb of the Time-Person corresponding to the eighth sign, leading to death.

"By fire, water, weapons...": If the Sun and other planets are actually situated *within* the eighth house, death occurs through fire and so on. Specifically: if the Sun is in the eighth, death is by fire; if the Moon, by water; if Mars, by weapons; if Mercury, by fever; if Jupiter, by chronic disease <note>original: "āmaya-kṛta," often interpreted as an internal or undiagnosed ailment</note>; if Venus, by thirst; and if Saturn, by hunger. If these planets are strong, death occurs through "good" or natural circumstances; if weak, through "bad" or painful circumstances; and if of middling strength, through middling circumstances.

To know the place of death, he says: "In movable and other signs." If the eighth house is a movable sign <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn</note>, the person dies in a foreign land. If it is a fixed sign <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius</note>, they die in their own home. If it is a dual-natured sign <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces</note>, they die on the road while traveling. ||1||

**Vernacular Translation—** If there is no planet in the eighth house but a strong planet aspects the eighth house, the person's death occurs due to the provocation of that planet's humor (phlegm, wind, or bile). The sign of the eighth house represents a limb of the Time-Person <meta>text ends abruptly at edge of page</meta>

<page-num>364</page-num>
-># The Chapter on Death in the Bṛhajjātaka<-

Death occurs due to the aggravation of the specific bodily humor <term>Dhatu; the primary elements or humors of the body</term> associated with the planet situated in the eighth house. If multiple powerful planets cast their gaze upon the eighth house, death results from a complication of all those planetary humors. If the Sun is in the eighth house, death is by fire; if the Moon, by water; if Mars, by weapons; if Mercury, by fever; if Jupiter, by an undiagnosed or mysterious disease; if Venus, by thirst; and if Saturn, by starvation. Furthermore, if the eighth house falls in a movable sign <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn</note>, death occurs in a foreign land; if in a fixed sign <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius</note>, it occurs in one's own home; and if in a dual sign <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces</note>, death occurs while traveling on a path. ||1||

*Special Meaning—* The planetary humors mentioned previously are as follows: the Sun rules bile <note>Pitta</note>; the Moon rules wind and phlegm <note>Vata and Kapha</note>; Mars rules bile; Mercury rules phlegm, wind, and bile; Jupiter rules phlegm; Venus rules phlegm and wind; and Saturn rules wind. ||1||

Now, the author describes death by falling from a mountain peak and other such accidents in the *Shardulavikridita* meter:

### Death occurs by being struck by a mountain peak if the Sun and Mars are in the tenth and fourth houses;
### By falling into a well if Saturn, the Moon, and Mars are in the fourth, seventh, and tenth houses respectively;
### In the sign of Virgo, death is caused by one's own kinsmen if the Moon and Sun are aspected by malefic planets;
### If the Sun and Moon are in a dual-natured rising sign, then death occurs by drowning in water. ||2||

<note>original Sanskrit: "Śailāgrābhihatasya..."</note> This means: If the Sun and Mars <note>Ravi and Bhauma</note> are simultaneously in the tenth and fourth houses, the person dies by being struck by a rock or falling from a cliff. Regarding the well: if Saturn, the Moon, and Mars are respectively in the fourth, seventh, and tenth houses—specifically, Saturn in the 4th, Moon in the 7th, and Mars in the 10th—the person dies by falling into a well. Regarding Virgo: if the Moon and Sun <note>Himoṣṇakarayoḥ; the cold and hot-rayed ones</note> are in Virgo and are seen by malefic planets, the person is killed by their own relatives. If the Sun and Moon are in a dual-natured sign <note>Dvisvabhāva</note> at the time of the rising sign <term>Lagna; the ascendant</term>, the person dies by drowning in water. ||2||

**Vernacular Translation—** If at the time of birth both the Sun and Mars are in the fourth or tenth house, the person dies from a stone injury. If Saturn is in the fourth, the Moon in the seventh, and Mars in the tenth house, he dies by falling into a well. If both the Sun and the Moon are in the sign of Virgo and are aspected by malefic planets, death occurs at the hands of one's own family members (kinsmen). If the Sun and Moon are in the sign of Pisces <note>interpreted here from the context of 'watery' dual signs</note>, death occurs by drowning in water. ||2||

*Special Meaning—* Here, regarding the term 'Ubhayodaya' <note>rising of both/dual</note>, many commentators have interpreted this to mean the dual-natured signs. ||2||

If the Moon is between two malefic planets in Virgo, death occurs from blood defects or swelling/wasting diseases. The "soft" <term>Decans</term> <note>A Decan or Drekkana is a 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign; there are three in each sign.</note> are the second of Cancer, the third of Cancer, the first of Scorpio, the second of Scorpio, and the last of Pisces. This means that if these planets are not anywhere else except these three positions, then the person dies by a spear. "And if in the house of relatives": when the Sun is in the fourth house from the Ascendant and Mars is in the tenth house and is seen by the waning Moon, the person dies by a spear. # Brihat Jataka: Chapter on Fatalities
## Page 368

If at a person's birth, Saturn is in the second house, the Moon is in the fourth, and Mars is in the tenth, death occurs due to **worms in a wound**. <note>Sanskrit: *kṣata-kṛmi*; literally, insects or larvae developing within an open sore or injury</note>. The body perishes as a result of the decay caused by these organisms. |7|

**Vernacular Translation:** If Mars, the Sun, and Saturn are respectively in the 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, the person dies by weapons, fire, or the wrath of a king. If Saturn, the Moon, and Mars are in the 2nd, 4th, and 10th houses, death occurs due to worms infecting a wound. |7|

Now, other yogas <note>astrological combinations</note> regarding death are described in the *Śārdūlavikrīḍita* meter:

->**If the Sun is in the tenth and Mars in the fourth, death is caused by falling from a vehicle.**<-
->**If Mars is in the seventh and Saturn, the Moon, and the Sun are in the ascendant, death is caused by being crushed by machinery.**<-
->**If Mars, Saturn, and the Moon are in Libra, Aries, and the signs of Saturn (Capricorn/Aquarius) respectively, or if the waning Moon, Sun, and Mars are in the tenth, seventh, and fourth houses, death occurs amidst excrement.**<- |8|

**Commentary:** Regarding "Sun in the sky": When the Sun is in the tenth house and Mars is in the fourth house <note>the "abyss" or *rasātala*</note>, the person dies by falling from a vehicle <note>originally *yāna*, meaning a carriage, litter, or mount</note>. 

Regarding "crushed by machinery": If Mars is in the seventh house and Saturn, the Moon, and the Sun are in the ascendant <note>the *Lagna*</note>, the person dies being crushed by a machine <note>*yantra*</note>. Some read "waning Moon" instead of "Moon and Sun" in the ascendant; in that case, the waning Moon, the Sun, and Saturn in the ascendant with Mars in the seventh also causes death by machinery. 

Regarding "amidst excrement": If Mars, Saturn, and the Moon are respectively in Libra <note>*Jūka*</note>, Aries <note>*Aja*</note>, and the signs of Saturn <note>Capricorn or Aquarius</note>—meaning Mars in Libra, Saturn in Aries, and the Moon in either Capricorn or Aquarius—the person dies in the midst of filth or excrement. 

Alternatively: If the waning Moon, the Sun, and Mars occupy the tenth <note>Sky</note>, seventh <note>Setting</note>, and fourth <note>Relative/Home</note> houses respectively—that is, the waning Moon in the 10th, the Sun in the 7th, and Mars in the 4th—the person also dies in the midst of excrement. |8|

**Vernacular Translation:** If the Sun is in the 10th house and Mars is in the 4th, the person dies falling from a ride. If Mars is in the 7th and Saturn and the Moon are in the 1st (ascendant), death occurs by being crushed in a machine. If Mars, Saturn, and the Moon are in Libra, Aries, and Capricorn/Aquarius; or if the waning Moon, Sun, and Mars are in the 10th, 7th, and 4th houses respectively, in both these cases, the person dies in the middle of feces. |8|

### Now, he describes other unfavorable combinations for death in the Vaitaliya meter:

> **If the Moon is waning and Saturn is situated in the eighth house, while being aspected by a powerful Mars, death occurs due to diseases arising in the private parts, or from worms, weapons, or fire. || 6 ||**

**Commentary:** *If the Moon is waning* <note>original: "kshīṇendau"</note> and is aspected or seen by a powerful *Mars* <note>original: "vakra," literally 'the crooked one,' a common name for Mars</note>, and *Saturn* <note>original: "arkaje," son of the Sun</note> is situated in the *eighth house* <note>the house of death and longevity</note>, the person born will suffer from *diseases arising in the private parts* <note>original: "guhyodbhava-roga"</note>. # Page 400
## Brihat Jataka: Chapter on Departure

*Now, if in a person's birth none of the previously mentioned planetary combinations <note>yogas</note> exist, and there is no planet in the eighth house, nor does any planet aspect the eighth house, the cause of death is explained through the following verse in the Vataliya meter:*

> The twenty-second decan <note>term: Drekkana; a 10-degree division of a zodiac sign</note> is said by the wise to be the cause of death.
> Its lord, or the lord of the sign where it resides, grants departure through its own inherent qualities. ||11||

**The Twenty-Second...** From whichever decan a person is born, the twenty-second decan from that point is declared by the learned scholars to be the cause or instrument of death. How so? It is said: "Its lord," and so on. The planet that is the lord of that twenty-second decan grants death through its own qualities—such as fire, water, weapons, etc.—which were previously listed as causes. Alternatively, the lord of the zodiac sign in which that twenty-second decan falls grants death through its own specific nature. 

How is this twenty-second decan identified? It is found in the eighth sign from the ascendant <note>term: Lagna; the rising sign</note>. It is explained thus: if the birth is in the first decan of the ascendant, then the twenty-second is the first decan of the eighth house. If it is the second decan of the ascendant, then it is the second of the eighth. If it is the third of the ascendant, then it is the third of the eighth. This system applies to all signs. By this method, the decan of the eighth sign is indeed the twenty-second decan. It should be understood that when the aforementioned combinations are absent and the eighth house is neither occupied nor aspected by planets, death occurs due to the afflictions associated with whichever is stronger: the lord of the twenty-second decan or the lord of the eighth sign. ||11||

**Vernacular Translation—** For one whose eighth house from the birth ascendant lacks the aspect or presence of any planet, the twenty-second decan from the decan present at birth is the cause of death, as stated by the pundits. The lord of the twenty-second decan, or the lord of the sign in the eighth house, causes the death of the subject through its previously mentioned qualities (fire, water, weapons, etc., as stated in the first verse). ||11||

**Special Meaning—** There are 7 signs between the ascendant and the eighth house, and each sign contains 3 decans. Therefore, if the first decan is in the ascendant, the 22nd decan will be the first decan of the eighth house. If the second decan is in the ascendant, the 22nd will be the second of the eighth. If the third decan is in the ascendant, the 22nd will be the third decan of the eighth house. ||11||

*Now, the knowledge of the type of ground/place where one dies is stated in the Vasantatilaka meter:*

->The death occurs on ground similar to that indicated by the Navamsha <note>term: Navamsha; a 1/9th division of a sign</note> of the ascendant;<-
->beyond this, it should be determined through planetary combinations and aspects.<-

<note>original: "द्वाविंश द्रेष्काण" (Twenty-second decan), "अष्टम भाव" (Eighth house), "निर्याण" (Departure/Death), "बृहज्जातक" (Brihat Jataka), "वसन्ततिलक" (Vasantatilaka meter)</note>

> The state of unconsciousness <note>original: "moha"</note> at the time of death is equal to the portion of the rising sign <note>the Ascendant or 'Lagna'</note> that has not yet risen.
> This duration is doubled if the Ascendant is aspected <note>viewed by a planetary influence</note> by its own lord, and tripled if aspected by benefic planets. ।।12।।

Regarding the subdivision of the rising sign <note>the Navamsha of the Lagna</note>: At the time of a person's birth, one must look to the lord <note>ruling planet</note> of the specific ninth-part subdivision <term>Navamsha|A 3°20' division of a zodiac sign</term> of the rising sign. The location where that lord is situated indicates the type of ground where the person will die. For example: If that sign is a "dual" sign, death occurs in a place of frequent travel. If the sign is Aries, it is in a place where goats and sheep roam. If Taurus, a place where bulls graze. If Gemini, inside a house; if Cancer, near a well; if Leo, in a forest; if Virgo, near a well <note>or water-source</note>; if Libra, in a marketplace or shop; if Scorpio, in a hole or cavity; if Sagittarius, in a place where horses roam; if Capricorn, in a marshy or watery place; if Aquarius, inside a house; and if Pisces, in a marshy place. 

However, for those whose death-combination specifically indicates death by water or other means, that specific rule takes precedence. The location should not be determined solely by the sign, but also by planetary conjunctions and aspects. Whichever planet occupies or aspects the sign where the lord of the rising subdivision is placed—or the nature of the ground associated with the subdivision itself—that is where the person dies. When multiple locations are possible, one must judge based on the strongest planet. 

If one asks: "What is the specific ground associated with each planet?" The answer is: the ground associated with the planet's own zodiac sign. If a planet rules two signs, the ground associated with its "Moolatrikona" <note>primary or preferred</note> sign is used. For example: For the Sun (Leo), it is the forest. For the Moon (Cancer), it is marshy land. For Mars (Aries), it is the grazing land of goats and sheep. For Mercury (Virgo), it is marshy land. For Jupiter (Sagittarius), it is where horses roam. For Venus (Libra), it is the marketplace. For Saturn (Aquarius), it is the house. 

Some authorities suggest other locations such as temples, fire-rooms, treasuries, bedrooms, or rubbish heaps. This is also acceptable, as people are observed dying in such places. Other possibilities should be considered similarly. 

Regarding unconsciousness <note>original: "moha"</note>: The duration of the state of unconsciousness at the time of death is equal to the time represented by the remaining (unrisen) degrees of the rising sign. In other words, the time it would take for the remainder of the rising sign to pass the horizon at birth equals the duration of the final unconsciousness. If the rising sign is aspected by its own lord, this time is doubled. If it is aspected by both its lord and a benefic planet, the time is said to be sixfold. ।।12।।

**Vernacular Translation—** The ground corresponding to the sign occupied by the lord of the rising subdivision (as described in the verses beginning with "All moving in their own...") is where—

# Chapter on the Signs of Death

Death should be predicted accordingly. Furthermore, one should determine the location of death based on the environment associated with the planet that either joins or aspects the Lord of the Navamsha <note>The Navamsha is a 1/9th division of a zodiac sign, used for fine-tuning predictions</note>. The duration of unconsciousness at the time of death should be calculated based on the remaining degrees of the rising sign (Lagna) at birth. If the rising sign is aspected by its own Lord, this duration is doubled; if aspected by a benefic planet, it is tripled; and if aspected by both its Lord and a benefic planet, the duration of unconsciousness is sixfold. This is the established conclusion. ॥12॥

*Special Meaning—* The essence is that death occurs in a place corresponding to the nature of the planet residing with the Lord of the Navamsha. If multiple planets are present, the strongest one determines the location. If no planets are present, look to the planet aspecting it; if many aspect it, choose the strongest. If there is neither association nor aspect, the location is determined by the zodiac sign in which the Navamsha Lord is situated. Regarding the calculation of time: if 30 degrees represent the total rising time of the sign, what do the remaining degrees represent? Multiply the remaining degrees by the rising time and divide by 30 to find the duration of unconsciousness. ॥12॥

->Now, the author describes the fate of the corpse in the Malini meter:<-

> By fire, water, or a mixture; by turning to ash, decomposition, or drying;
> Or by being mangled by scavengers if the Eighth House contains the Serpent-divisions;
> Thus the fate of the corpse must be contemplated as stated;
> Further details should be sought from the extensive scriptures of the ancestors. ॥ 13 ॥

*By fire, etc.* The fate of the corpse is to be contemplated based on the <term>Drekkana</term> <note>A 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign, also known as a decan</note> situated in the eighth house (the house of death). By calculation, this is the 22nd Drekkana from the rising sign. If it is a "Fire Drekkana," the body turns to ash, meaning it is cremated. A Fire Drekkana is typically a division associated with a malefic planet. If it is a "Water Drekkana," the body decomposes or is cast into water. A Water Drekkana is associated with a benefic planet. If it is a "Mixed Drekkana," the body dries up; this occurs when a benefic division is joined by a malefic planet, or vice versa. Furthermore, if the eighth house contains <term>Serpent-divisions</term> <note>Specific decans associated with snakes or bondage</note>, the body is "mangled," meaning it is eaten by dogs, jackals, crows, and other scavengers. Here, the <term>Serpent-divisions</term> are defined as the first and second decans of Cancer, the first and second of Scorpio, and the last of Pisces. As it is said: "The first and second parts of the Moon's house (Cancer), the same for the Scorpion (Scorpio), and the final part of the Fish (Pisces)."

# The Brihat Jataka: Chapter on Exit from Life
<page-num>404</page-num>

It should be stated as follows: If the <term>Drekkana</term><note>A decan, or a 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign.</note> belongs to Jupiter, it should be said that the person has come from the world of the gods <note>original: "vibudha-loka"</note>. If it belongs to either the Moon or Venus, they have come from the world of the ancestors <note>original: "pitru-loka"</note>. If it belongs to either the Sun or Mars, they have come from the world of animals <note>original: "tiryag-loka"</note>. If it belongs to either Saturn or Mercury <insert>the Sanskrit text mentions Mars here, but the Hindi commentary correctly identifies Mercury as the alternative</insert>, they have come from the world of hell <note>original: "naraka-loka"</note>. 

Regarding the status—superior, middle, or inferior—within that world from which they came, the text says: If the planet representing that world is in its sign of exaltation <note>its highest point of strength</note>, the person was a leader or prominent figure there. If it is between its exaltation and debilitation, they were of middle status. If it is in its sign of debilitation <note>its weakest point</note>, they were of a low or wretched status in that previous life. || 14 ||

**Vernacular Commentary—** Between the Sun and the Moon, whichever is stronger: look at the <term>Drekkana</term> it occupies. If the lord of that decan is Jupiter, the native has come from the realm of the gods. If the Moon or Venus is the lord, they come from the realm of the ancestors. If the Sun or Mars is the lord, they come from the world of mortals or animals. If Saturn or Mercury is the lord, they come from hell. To know their quality in that past life: if the lord is near its exaltation, they were superior; if between exaltation and debilitation, they were average; and if near debilitation, they were of a low class in that realm. || 14 ||

->Now, the knowledge of what the destination of the deceased will be is told in the Malini meter:<-

> **The destination is determined by the lord of the decan of the 6th or 8th house, or the planet in the 7th.**
> **If Jupiter is in the 6th, a center <note>1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th house</note>, or the 8th house, and is in its exaltation;**
> **Or if the sign of Pisces is on the ascendant and contains a benefic planet, then Liberation <note>Moksha</note>**
> **Occurs, provided the remaining planets are devoid of strength. || 15 ||**

Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter, titled "The Chapter on Exit," in the *Brihat Jataka* composed by the Great Teacher Varahamihira. | 25 |

**Commentary:** Regarding "The destination" <note>original: "gati"</note>—If the 6th, 7th, and 8th houses from the birth ascendant are empty, then look at the <term>Drekkana</term> of the 6th house and the <term>Drekkana</term> of the 8th house. Between the lords of these two decans, whichever is stronger represents the world the soul will travel to. This is the meaning of "lord of the decan of the 6th or 8th." The deceased must go there. Or, if there is a planet situated in the 7th house, the soul goes to the world represented by that planet. If there are planets in two or three of these houses (6th, 7th, or 8th)...

->Language Commentary and Bhattotpala's Sanskrit Commentary 405<-

There are summary verses regarding this. Now, if there are two or more planets in a single house, the person goes to the world associated with whichever planet is the strongest among them. One might ask: the text previously mentioned "situated in the descendant" <note>the 7th house</note> as a single location; why then is it explained that planets in the 6th or 8th houses also lead one to their respective paths? It is said that in the phrase "situated in the descendant or," the word "or" should be understood to mean "and." It is not only the one in the descendant; by the inclusion of "and," some read it as "the enemy house <note>6th</note> and the hole <note>8th</note>." Thus, it is stated in the *Svalpa Jataka*:

> "Jupiter, the Moon and Venus, Mars and the Sun, and Saturn lead one to the worlds of the Gods, Ancestors, Animals, or Hell-beings respectively, when they are lords of the decans <term>Drekkana: a 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign</term> of the 6th or 8th houses, or are themselves placed in the 7th, 6th, or 8th houses."

Regarding the phrase "If Jupiter is present": The word "now" is used to complete the meter. If, in a person's birth chart, Jupiter is in the 6th house (the house of enemies), or in the centers <note>houses 1, 4, 7, or 10</note>, or in the 8th house (the "hole"), and is simultaneously in its sign of exaltation (Cancer), this constitutes one Yoga <term>Yoga: a specific planetary combination</term>. Alternatively, if the sign Pisces is rising at the ascendant and, with the exception of Jupiter, all other planets are devoid of strength, this constitutes the second Yoga. It should be declared that one born under either of these two Yogas will attain liberation <term>Moksha: release from the cycle of rebirth</term>. In the phrase "rising in the final house and in a benefic subdivision," the word "and" carries the meaning of "or." Just as the destination is described based on the planets at the time of birth, the destination should also be described based on the ascendant at the time of death. As stated in the *Svalpa Jataka*:

> "If Jupiter is in the 6th, 8th, or a center house, or if Pisces is the ascendant, and the remaining planets are weak at the time of birth or death, they say the soul attains the path of liberation." ||15||

### Thus ends the 25th Chapter, the Chapter on Death,
### in the Commentary on Brihat Jataka composed by Shri Bhattotpala. || 25 ||

**Vernacular Translation—** Whichever planet is strongest in the 6th, 7th, or 8th houses from the birth ascendant, the soul goes to the world associated with that planet (as mentioned in the previous verse) after death. If there are no planets in these 6th, 7th, or 8th houses, the soul goes to the world associated with the lord of the decan of the 6th or 8th house, whichever is stronger. Now, the combinations for liberation (Moksha Yoga) are described: If Jupiter is in Cancer and situated in the 6th, 1st, 4th, 7th, 9th, 10th, or 8th houses from the ascendant; or if the ascendant is Pisces with a subdivision <term>Navamsha: a 1/9th division of a sign</term> of a benefic planet, and in both these combinations all other planets are weak, the native attains liberation. || 15 ||

**Special Meaning—** Here, the word "or" in "situated in the descendant or" also implies planets situated in the 6th and 8th houses. As the Teacher <note>Varahamihira</note> himself says in the *Laghu Jataka*:

> "The lords of the decans of the 6th and 8th houses, and those situated in the 7th, 6th, or 8th houses, lead the soul." (Meaning is clear).

Furthermore, just as the knowledge of the soul's path is gained from the birth ascendant, it should be understood similarly from the ascendant at the time of death. As in the *Laghu Jataka*:

> "If Jupiter is in the 6th, 8th, or a center, or if Pisces is the ascendant, and the remaining planets are powerless at birth or death, they say the soul attains the path of liberation." (Meaning is clear). || 15 ||

# Chapter 26: On Lost Horoscopes (Nashta-Jataka)

Now the chapter on Lost Horoscopes is explained. At the very beginning, the author describes the method for determining the time of birth using the *Indravajra* meter:

->**When the times of conception and birth are unknown, one should declare the birth from the Ascendant of the person asking the question.**<-
->**From the first or second half of the sign, one should know if the birth occurred during the Sun's northern or southern course.**<-

**Commentary:** Regarding "Conception," etc.—for a person whose time of conception is known, the birth has already been explained previously through the time of conception (using the rule "the time when the Moon is associated with..." etc.). The time of birth has also been explained. However, when there is a lack of knowledge <note>original: "aparibodha"</note> regarding both the time of conception and birth, one should declare the birth from the *Vilagna*—the Ascendant <term>Ascendant: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the query</term> of the querent. If the first half of the Ascendant (the first *Hora* or 15 degrees) is rising when the querent asks, then the birth should be said to have occurred when the Sun was in its northern course <term>Uttarayana: the six months when the sun moves north, starting from Capricorn</term>. This means the person was born when the Sun was in the six signs starting from Capricorn. If the second half of the Ascendant (the second *Hora*) is rising, then the birth occurred during the Sun's southern course <term>Dakshinayana: the six months when the sun moves south, starting from Cancer</term>. This means the person was born when the Sun was in the six signs starting from Cancer. Thus, for a living being whose conception and birth are unknown, one should indicate the birth from the query-ascendant. ॥ 1 ॥

**Vernacular Translation:** For a person whose time of conception or birth is not known, the time of birth should be understood from the Ascendant at the time of the query. For example, if the query-ascendant is within the first 15 degrees of the sign (i.e., the first *Hora*), the birth is in the Northern Course (Sun in the 6 signs from Capricorn). If the Ascendant is above 15 degrees (i.e., the second *Hora*), the birth should be understood to be in the Southern Course (Sun in the 6 signs from Cancer). ॥ 1 ॥

**Example:** Suppose in Kashi <note>Modern-day Varanasi</note>, in the year 2001 of the Vikrama Era <note>approx. 1944 CE</note>, on the 7th lunar day of the bright half of the month of Vaishakha, Saturday, at 11:10 *Ghati-Pala* <term>Ghati-Pala: traditional Indian units of time; 1 Ghati is 24 minutes</term> after sunrise, someone asks to create a lost horoscope because their birth time is unknown. Look at the calculated planets and the Ascendant chart for that time. The length of the day is 32:20. Here, the query-ascendant is above 15 degrees; therefore, the birth occurred during the Southern Course of the sun. ॥ 1 ॥

->The Chart of the Query-Time<-
