# Chapter on the Drekkanas in the Brihat Jataka

**The Second Drekkana of Leo**

<note>original: "हयाकृतिरिति" - Referring to the horse-shaped form</note> Horse-shaped; having a pale or slightly white garland <note>original: "माल्यं"</note> of flowers upon his head; wearing a black antelope skin <note>original: "कृष्णाजिनं"</note> and a woolen blanket. Some read this as "wearing a tattered garment of antelope skin." This man is difficult to overcome or approach, like a lion; he holds a bow <note>original: "आत्तकार्मुकः"</note> and has a nose that is hooked or curved at the tip. This is the second Drekkana of the King of Beasts (Leo), which is horse-shaped. This is a masculine, quadruped <term>Drekkana (a 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign)</term>, armed, and associated with the soul <note>original: "जीवसक्तश्च" - likely referring to the influence of Jupiter or the vital breath</note>.

**Vernacular Translation:** Having a form like a horse, with a pale yellow-white garland on the head, wearing black deer skin and a blanket, unconquerable like a lion, holding a bow, and having a downward-curved nose—such is the second Drekkana of Leo. ||14||

### Now, the form of the third Drekkana of Leo is described in the Upajati meter:

**With the face of a bear and the movements of a monkey, he carries a staff, fruit, and meat.**
**A man with a long beard and curly hair; such is the final third of the Lord of Beasts (Leo). ||15||**

<note>original: "ॠक्षानन इति"</note> Having the face of a bear; his actions and nature are similar to those of a monkey or ape. He carries a staff as a weapon, fruit (such as a mango), and meat. He is "Kurchi," meaning he has a long beard, and is a man with curly hair on his head. This is the final third part of the Lord of Beasts (Leo). This is a human Drekkana, yet also a quadruped Drekkana, armed, and associated with Mars <note>original: "भौमसत्तश्च" - indicating the influence of the planet Mars</note>. ||15||

**Vernacular Translation:** Having a face like a bear, acting like a monkey, carrying a stick, fruit, and meat, with a long beard and curly hair—this is the third Drekkana of Leo. ||15||

### Now, the form of the first Drekkana of Virgo is described in the Upajati meter:

**A maiden with a pot filled with flowers, her body covered in soiled garments,**
**Desiring the acquisition of clothes and wealth, she seeks the house of her teacher; this is the first of Virgo. ||16||**

<note>original: "पुष्पप्रपूर्णेनेति"</note> A maiden or young girl, characterized by a jar filled with flowers; her limbs are covered in clothes that are very dirty or stained with impurities. Desiring the union of clothes and wealth (money), she goes to the house of her teacher <note>original: "गुरोः कुलं"</note>. This is the first Drekkana of the Maiden (Virgo). This is a feminine Drekkana and is associated with Mercury <note>original: "बुधसत्तश्च"</note>. ||16||

**Vernacular Translation:** A girl holding a pot full of flowers, wearing dirty clothes, wishing to collect clothes and wealth, and going to the teacher's house—this is said to be the first Drekkana of Virgo. ||16||

### *Now, he describes the form of the second decan of Virgo in the Vaitaliya meter—*

**A man holding a pen, dark-complexioned, with a cloth wrapped around his head, calculating income and expenditure;**
**He carries a large bow, his body is covered in hair, and he is of middle stature. ||17||**

A man... [The commentary explains]: A man, holding a pen <note>original: "lekhani" — a reed pen or stylus used for writing</note> with which letters are written; dark-complexioned <note>original: "shyama" — a dusky or dark-brown hue</note>; with a cloth-covered head, meaning his head is bound with a cloth <insert>some read "baddha-shira," meaning a bound head</insert>. He calculates "expenditure" (outflow) and "income" (inflow). He carries or holds a "large" (wide) bow. His body is "covered in hair" <note>original: "romavyaptatanu"</note>. This is the middle or second decan. This is a human decan, armed, and associated with Saturn <note>original: "saurasakta" — influenced by the planet Saturn</note>. ||17||

Hindi translation: A man with a pen in hand, dark-complexioned, with a turban tied on his head, considering income and expenses, his body covered in hair, and carrying a very large bow—this is the form of the second decan of Virgo. ||17||

---

### *Now, he describes the knowledge of the form of the third decan of Virgo in the Upajatika meter—*

**A fair-skinned woman, covered by a clean white silken garment, tall, holding a pot and a ladle;**
**Pure and headed toward a temple—this, they say, is the final third of Virgo. ||18||**

Fair-skinned... [The commentary explains]: Fair-complexioned; "covered" or hidden by a "silken garment" <note>original: "dukula" — fine linen or silk</note> whose ends are well-washed <insert>some read "holding a silken cloth in her hand"</insert>. She is "tall" (very high in stature); she has a "pot" (water jar) and a "ladle" <note>original: "katchu" — a famous iron household utensil or spoon</note> in her hand. A "woman" (young lady), "pure" (composed/devout), "headed" (ready to go) to a "temple" (house of the gods). So say the Sages. This is the final third or third decan of Virgo. This is a female decan and is associated with Venus <note>original: "shukrasakta"</note>. ||18||

Hindi translation: Fair-complexioned, wearing washed clothes, of tall stature, holding a pot and a ladle in her hand, very holy, and proceeding to go to a temple—such is the form of the third decan of the sign Virgo as described by the Sages. ||18||

### *Now, he describes the form of the first decan of Libra in the Vasantatilaka meter—*

**A man in a shop within a marketplace, holding scales,**
**Skilled in weighing and measuring, with weights in his hand;**
**He thinks of the goods and their price—this form**
**The Greeks say is the first of Libra. ||19||**

In a marketplace... [The commentary explains]: Situated in the middle of a street where a merchant's shop is located. A man holding "scales" <note>original: "tula" — a balance scale</note> in his hand...

He is skilled in weighing <note>original: "unmane"</note> and measuring—both in upward weighing like scales and in volumetric measures like the *kudava* <note>a traditional unit of dry measure</note>. He is an expert in these matters. In his hand, he holds the counter-weights used to determine the value of goods such as gold and gems. He contemplates the merchandise in his vessel and calculates its price, thinking, "This is the value of this item." The Yavana <note>Greek or foreign</note> masters say this is the form of the first decan of Libra. This is a human decan and is associated with Venus. || 19 ||

**Vernacular:** A man keeping a shop in a city street, holding scales in his hand, skilled in weighing gold etc., or measuring with a grain-measure, holding a touchstone <note>a stone used to test the purity of gold</note> in his hand, knowing how to buy and determine the price of goods—such is the nature of the first decan of Libra as described by the Yavanas. || 19 ||

### Now, the form of the second decan of Libra is described in the Trotaka meter:

**A man with the face of a vulture, holding a water-pot, desires to fall or fly away. Hungry and thirsty, he travels in his mind toward his wife and children; such is the middle of the Balance-bearer.** || 20 ||

Regarding the water-pot: A man with the face of a vulture <note>original: "gridhra-mukha"</note> takes a pot and desires to fly out or fall down. Because he is hungry and thirsty, he goes toward his wife and sons with his mind—meaning he longs for them or remembers them. Such is the middle decan of Libra. This is a human decan, a bird decan, and is associated with Saturn. || 20 ||

**Vernacular:** A man with a face like a vulture, holding a pot in his hand and wishing to fall, distressed by hunger and thirst, remembering his wife and son in his heart—such is said to be the second decan of Libra. || 20 ||

### Now, the form of the third decan of Libra is described in the Vamshastha meter:

**Adorned with gems, he stands scaring the deer in the forest, wearing golden armor and carrying a quiver. A man bearing the form of a monkey, carrying fruit and meat; this is declared by the Yavanas at the end of Libra.** || 21 ||

Regarding scaring: Adorned with various jewels, he stands in the forest scaring the deer. What is he like? He carries a golden quiver for arrows and wears armor. He carries fruits and meat. He is a man who bears the form of a monkey <note>original: "vanara-rupa-bhrit"</note>. Some read this as "a man holding a bow with the form of a Kinnara" <note>a celestial being with a human body and a horse's head, or vice versa</note>. The ancient Yavanas have described this in the third decan of Libra. This man with a monkey-like appearance is a quadruped decan and is associated with Mercury. || 21 ||

*Commentary—* "Home": A woman desires the comforts of her place for the sake of her husband. Her body is "entwined by a serpent," meaning covered by snakes. **Skilled in the arts, with eyes as long as lotus petals, dark-complexioned and seeking various things;**

"Skilled in the arts..." etc. Skilled in the arts means she has thorough knowledge of them. With eyes as long as lotus petals <note>Sanskrit: *Abja-dala*</note> means her eyes are long and wide like the leaf of a lotus. Adorned with ornaments, and with "iron ears"—meaning she has iron ornaments in her ears. This woman is described in the middle or second decan of Capricorn. This is a female decan and is associated with Venus. // 29 //

# The Chapter on Decans in the Brihat Jataka

**Vernacular Translation:** A woman skilled in all types of arts, with eyes like lotus petals, of dark complexion, a seeker of various kinds of objects, adorned with ornaments, and wearing iron in her ears—such is said to be the form of the [second] Decan of Capricorn. || 29 ||

### Now, the form of the third Decan of Capricorn is described in the Rathoddhata meter:

**With a body like a Kinnara, carrying a blanket, equipped with a quiver, a bow, and armor;**
**He carries a gem-studded pot upon his shoulder—this is the final part of the sign of Capricorn.** || 30 ||

*Commentary:* "With a body like a Kinnara"—Kinnaras are a class of celestial beings with the faces of horses and bodies of men. He possesses a body like theirs. "Carrying a blanket"—accompanied by a woolen wrap. "Equipped with a quiver, bow, and armor"—joined with a case for arrows, a bow, and protective mail. He carries or holds a "pot"—a water jar—"studded with gems"—fashioned with jewels—resting "upon his shoulder"—attached to his upper back. This is the "final" or third Decan of the sign of Capricorn. This is a male Decan, armed, and ruled by Saturn <note>The text mentions 'Budhasattascha' likely referring to the planetary influence or nature, though traditionally the third decan of Capricorn is ruled by Mercury/Budha</note>. || 30 ||

**Vernacular Translation:** Having a body like a Kinnara <note>original: "Kinnara" - a celestial being often depicted as a centaur-like figure or a human with a horse's head</note>, provided with a blanket, a quiver, a bow, and armor, carrying a gem-encrusted pot on his shoulder—such is the form of the third Decan of Capricorn. || 30 ||

### Now, the form of the first Decan of Aquarius is described in the Dodhaka meter:

**His mind is agitated by the arrival of oil, liquor, water, and food; he wears a blanket,**
**Silk garments, and a deer skin; with a face like a vulture—this is the beginning of the Pot.** || 31 ||

*Commentary:* "Oil, liquor, water, and food"—oil refers to substances like sesame oil; liquor is a specific drink; water and food. His "mind" or consciousness is "agitated by the arrival" or acquisition of these things. "Wearing a blanket"—accompanied by a woolen wrap. "Silk garments"—clothed in silk. "With a deer skin"—joined with the hide of a black antelope. "With a face like a vulture"—his countenance resembles that of the vulture bird. "The beginning of the Pot"—the first Decan of Aquarius. This is a male Decan, bird-like in face, and ruled by Saturn. || 31 ||

**Vernacular Translation:** One whose mind is anxious regarding the income of oil, ghee, wine, water, and food; wearing a blanket, silk clothes, and a deer skin, with a face like a vulture—such is the form of the first Decan of the sign of Aquarius <note>original: "Kumbha" - the Water-bearer</note>. || 31 ||

### Now, the form of the second Decan of Aquarius is described in the Vaitaliya meter:

**In a burnt cart along with Silk-cotton trees, a woman gathers iron in the forest;**
**Covered by a soiled cloth, with pots placed upon her head—this is the middle one.** || 32 ||

*Commentary:* "In a burnt cart"—in a vehicle consumed and turned to ash by fire. "Along with Silk-cotton trees"—together with Shalmali trees. A "woman" gathers or collects "iron" in the "forest" or wilderness. She is "covered" or wrapped in a "soiled cloth"—a garment that is dirty. With "pots"—vessels—placed upon her head...

# The Great Book of Nativity: Chapter on the Decans
<page-num>442</page-num>

Now, the author describes the nature of the second decan of Pisces in the *Vasantatilaka* meter:

> A woman with a complexion like the Champaka flower, accompanied by her attendants, boards a ship adorned with very high flags and banners, and sails toward the shore of the ocean. This is declared by the Sages to be the second division of Pisces. ||35||

**Commentary:** "With very high flags"—she boards a ship where the flags and banners are extremely elevated. She travels toward the shore or coast of the great ocean. She is a "young woman," and of what kind? "Accompanied by her attendants," meaning surrounded by her circle of friends. Her complexion is like the "Champaka," a specific yellow flower; the meaning is that her facial radiance rivals the beauty of the Champaka. This second third-part of Pisces has been spoken of by the Sages. This is a female decan and is associated with the Moon. ||35||

**Vernacular Translation:** A woman with a face radiant like the Champaka flower, with her family/attendants, boarding a ship with very high banners and going to the seashore—such is the form of the second decan of Pisces as told by the Sages. ||35||

Now, the author describes the nature of the third decan of Pisces in the *Indravajra* meter:

> Near a pit in the forest, a man whose limbs are encircled by snakes, destitute of clothes, his soul agitated by thieves and fire, stands weeping. This is the final portion of the Fish (Pisces). ||36||

->Thus ends the Twenty-Seventh Chapter, the Chapter on the Nature of the Decans,<-
->in the *Brihat Jataka* composed by the Great Teacher Varahamihira.<-

**Commentary:** "Near a pit"—close to a hole or cavern. "Limbs encircled by snakes"—his body parts are wrapped by serpents. "Destitute of clothes"—lacking garments. A man in the "forest" or wilderness, whose "inner soul is agitated" or disturbed by "thieves" (robbers) and "fire." He "weeps" or cries out. This is the "final portion," the third decan of the "Fish" (Pisces). This is a "Serpent Decan" <note>original: "Vyala-dreshkana"</note> and is associated with Mars. 

The purpose of knowing the forms of the decans has been explained in various places. As will be said regarding journeys: "One should apply the results according to the <term>form and gestures of the decan</term> <note>The physical appearance of the decan helps the astrologer predict the physical characteristics of a thief or the nature of a lost object.</note> for the sake of prosperity. If the decan is of a gentle form, joined with flowers, fruits, or vessels of gems, and is aspected by benefic planets, there will be victory. If it resembles a weapon or is aspected by malefic planets, there will be defeat, delusion, or imprisonment; if joined with serpents or fetters and malefic planets, one suffers from thirst." 

Furthermore, another use for this is the knowledge of the thief's appearance, location, and so on. As stated in the *Shatpanchashika* by Prithuyashas: "The object is known from the degree-division, the thieves are known from the decans; the time, direction, and place are known from the zodiac signs, and the age and caste from the lord of the Ascendant." Thus are the verses. ||36||

**Vernacular Translation:** In the forest near a pit, a man with a body joined with snakes, without clothes, weeping with a mind agitated by fear of thieves and fire—such is the form of the third decan of Pisces as told by the Sages. ||36||

<meta>This page continues the technical discussion of astrological decans (Drekkana) and begins the concluding summary of the entire treatise, listing the chapters in order.</meta>

<page-num>443</page-num>
<header>With the Sanskrit commentary of Bhattotpala and the Hindi vernacular explanation</header>

**Special Meaning —** The purposes of the *Drekkana* <note>A decan; a 10-degree division of a zodiac sign</note> have been mentioned previously, such as: "The Moon imparts the qualities of the lord of the decan it occupies, whether it be its own or a friend's." Furthermore, these are used at the time of starting a journey (*Yatra*) and in identifying the appearance and location of a thief. For example:

> "One should predict results based on the form, movement, and qualities of the decan. In a gentle-looking decan, or one associated with flowers, fruits, and vessels of gems, success is indicated.
> If aspected by benefics, there is victory at the time of battle; if aspected by malefics, there is defeat,
> confusion, or even imprisonment—especially if the decan is associated with snakes or fetters and the person is thirsty." <note>original: 'द्रेष्काणाकारचेष्टागुणसदृशफलं...' - This verse outlines how the visual symbolism of a decan predicts the outcome of an event.</note>

**The underlying meaning is—** The appearance, behavior, and qualities of the native are similar to the appearance, behavior, and qualities of the decan rising at birth. A journey undertaken during a decan described as gentle, or associated with flowers, fruits, and gold, leads to victory and profit. A journey during a decan described as terrifying, associated with snakes or nooses, or described as thirsty or hungry, leads to loss, defeat, and bondage. Similarly, in the *Shatpanchashika* <note>A famous work on Horary astrology by Prithuyashas</note>:

**"The stolen object is known from the Navamsha; the thieves are known from the Drekkana.**
**The time, direction, and place are known from the Signs, and the age and caste from the Lord of the Ascendant." This is the clear meaning. ||36||**

# Chapter 28: On the Conclusion of the Work

Now, the Chapter on the Conclusion is explained. The summary of the chapters is stated in the *Upajati* meter:

**The divisions of the signs, the nature of the planetary sources, non-human births, and the time of conception.**
**Birth, then immediate death, as well as longevity, the ripening of the planetary periods, and the system known as Ashtakavarga. ||1||**

Regarding "The divisions of the signs" etc. — The first chapter is the Divisions of the Signs; the second is the Nature of Planetary Sources; the third is Non-human Births; the word "then" implies sequence. The fourth is the Time of Conception; the fifth is the Manner of Birth; then "Immediate Death" refers to the sixth chapter on Arishta (misfortunes); the seventh is the Division of Longevity; the eighth is the Division of Planetary Periods (*Dasha*); the ninth is known as the *Ashtakavarga* system. ||1||

->Now the summary of the remaining chapters is stated in the *Shalini* meter:<-

**Livelihood, Royal Yogas, Celestial Yogas, Lunar Yogas, and Yogas of two or more planets.**
**Renunciation, then the character of the signs, aspects, and the houses; thereafter the "Support" Yogas and the Miscellaneous chapter. ||2||**

Regarding "Livelihood" etc. — Livelihood is the tenth; the chapter on Royal Yogas (*Raja Yoga*) is the eleventh; Celestial Yogas refers to the chapter on *Nabhas* Yogas, which is the twelfth; Lunar Yogas refers to the chapter on *Sunapha* and other lunar combinations, the thirteenth; the chapter on combinations of two, three, or more planets is the fourteenth; the chapter on Yogas for Renunciation (*Pravrajya*) is the fifteenth; thereafter, the chapter on the Character of the Signs is the sixteenth; the chapter on the Results of Aspects is the seventeenth; following that, the chapter on the Houses (*Bhava*) is the eighteenth; then the chapter on "Support" (*Ashraya*) Yogas is the nineteenth; and the Miscellaneous chapter is the twentieth. ||2||

<header>The Great Birth Chart: Chapter on the Conclusion</header>

->Now, he summarizes the remaining chapters in the Shalini meter:<-

### The unfavorable combinations, the horoscopy of women, the departure (death), the lost birth chart, and the decans;
### Twenty chapters plus five have been told regarding birth; now I shall describe the triad of travel. || 3 ||

"The unfavorable combinations" etc. The chapter on unfavorable combinations is the twenty-first; the chapter on the horoscopy of women <note>Sanskrit: *stri-jataka*</note> is the twenty-second; the departure, or the chapter on the knowledge of death, is the twenty-third; the chapter on the lost birth chart <note>Calculating a chart when the birth time is unknown</note> is the twenty-fourth; and the chapter on the nature of the decans <term>Drekkana: a 10-degree division of a zodiac sign</term> is the twenty-fifth. <gloss>(1)</gloss> Thus, twenty chapters plus five have been spoken of and declared regarding birth in this *Jataka* (horoscopy) text. || 3 ||

**Vernacular Translation—** 1. Classification of Signs, 2. Classification of Planetary Natures, 3. Non-human Births, 4. Conception, 5. Birth, 6. Evils (Arishta), 7. Longevity, 8. Planetary Periods (Dasha), 9. The Eight-fold Division (Ashtakavarga), 10. Profession, 11. Royal Combinations (Raja Yoga), 12. Celestial Combinations (Nabhasa Yoga), 13. Lunar Combinations, 14. Two-Planet Combinations, 15. Renunciation (Asceticism), 16. Influence of the Signs, 17. Results of Aspects, 18. Results of the Houses, 19. General Combinations, 20. Miscellaneous Topics, 21. Unfavorable Combinations, 22. Female Horoscopy, 23. Departure (Death), 24. Lost Birth Charts, and 25. The Decans—thus twenty-five (25) chapters are said to comprise the *Jataka*. In this specific book, by counting the 1. Character of Nakshatras, 2. Character of the Moon in Signs, and the Conclusion as 3 separate chapters, there are 28 chapters in total. || 1-3 ||

->Now I shall state the summary of chapters composed regarding travel (Yatra).<-
->He speaks of this in the Upajati meter:<-

### Queries, the lunar day, the asterism, the solar day, the moment, the moon, and the rising sign, then the divisions of the rising sign;
### The purification of the planets, then the exceptions, the chapter called "The Mixed," and the quivering of the body. || 4 ||

"Queries, the lunar day" etc. Queries refers to the chapter on different types of questions; the lunar day <term>Tithi</term> refers to the chapter on the strength of lunar days; the asterism <term>Bham</term> refers to the names of the Nakshatras; the solar day refers to the names of the days and the results of the weekday; the moment <term>Kshana</term> refers to the instruction on Muhurtas (auspicious moments); the moon refers to the chapter on the strength of the moon; the rising sign <term>Lagna</term> refers to the determination of the ascendant; then the divisions of the rising sign refers to the characteristics and results of the Hora, Drekkana, Navamsha, Dwadashamsha, and Trimshamsha <note>These are the various divisional charts used in Vedic astrology</note>; the purification of the planets refers to the results of the positions of all planets in the circular chart <term>Kundalika</term>; then follows the chapter on exceptions; the chapter called "The Mixed" <note>Vimishraka</note>; and the quivering of the body <note>Tanu-vepanam: physical omens or twitching</note>. || 4 ||

->He speaks of the naming of the remaining chapters in the Upajati meter:<-

### After this comes the worship of the Guhyakas, then the dreams, then the rules for ritual bathing are prescribed;
### The sacrifice to the planets, then the departure, and in order, the instruction on omens. || 5 ||

From this point forward... After this, the worship of the Guhyakas <note>original: "Guhyakapujanam"; semi-divine beings or guardians of wealth</note> should take place, followed by the chapter on dreams <note>original: "Svapnadhyayah"</note>. This is the summary of the section on journeys. ||5||

->Now he describes the remaining collection of topics in the Upajati meter:<-

**The time for marriage, the calculation of the planets, and its extensive branch have been stated separately. This compendium of astrology has been made by me in three <term>Skandhas</term> <note>literally "branches" or "trunks" of the tree of knowledge</note> for the benefit of astrologers. ||6||**

Regarding the time for marriage... The time for marriage is discussed in the section on marriage <note>original: "Vivahapatala"</note>. The calculation of the planets was stated and explained separately in the *Five Treatises* <note>original: "Panchasiddhantika"</note>. To understand the auspicious and inauspicious effects of those calculations, an extensive branch was described. Through these three <term>Skandhas</term>—named <term>Ganita</term> <note>mathematical astronomy</note>, <term>Hora</term> <note>natal astrology</note>, and <term>Samhita</term> <note>omens and mundane astrology</note>—this compendium of the science of light <note>astrology/astronomy</note> has been composed by me, the teacher <term>Varahamihira</term>, for the benefit of <term>Daivavids</term> <note>those who know the divine/fate; astrologers</note>. Having studied the vast scriptures, I have made this in a condensed form. ||6||

Vernacular explanation: Chapter 1 on Queries, 2 on the strength of Lunar Days, 3 on the strength of Constellations, 4 on the strength of Solar Days, 5 on Auspicious Moments, 6 on the strength of the Moon, 7 on calculating the Ascendant, 8 on the divisions of the Ascendant (the <term>Hora</term>, <term>Drekkana</term>, etc., varga divisions), 9 on the purification of Planets, 10 on Exceptions, 11 on Miscellaneous topics, 12 on the Throbbing of Limbs, 13 on the ritual for worshipping Guhyakas, 14 on the chapter on Dreams, 15 on the rules for Ritual Bathing, 16 on the Sacrifice to the Planets, 17 on Departure (decisions for travel), 18 on the chapter on Omens, 19 on the Marriage section—these are the subjects related to travel (that is, the astrology of choosing the right moment). Furthermore, the cause/calculation of the planets (as told in the <term>Panchasiddhantika</term>) and its vast branches—in this way, I (Varahamihira) have compiled this astrology in three <term>Skandhas</term> (in the forms of <term>Jataka</term> <note>birth charts</note>, <term>Samhita</term>, and <term>Ganita</term>) for the benefit of astrologers. ||4-6||

->He states this in the Malini meter:<-

**This entire science was composed extensively by others; subsequently, this was made by me in a brief form to express the essence of those places. This work is indeed capable of purifying the intellect; whatever has been said here by me, may the virtuous people forgive it. ||7||**

Regarding "composed extensively by others"... This entire science was described in great detail by other teachers such as the Lord of the Greeks <note>original: "Yavaneshvara"</note> and others. Following that, I have made this very same subject more beautiful and brief to convey the meaning of those teachings. Even if it is brief, the meaning contained here is the essential purpose. Because this work was created in this science to cleanse the impurities of the intellect...

# Brihat Jataka: Chapter on Conclusion

<page-num>446</page-num>
<header>In the Brihat Jataka, now begins the Chapter on Conclusion</header>

This work has been completed, being capable of purifying and sharpening the horn of the intellect <note>The "horn of the intellect" is a metaphor for sharp, discerning wisdom</note>. Whatever I have stated in this compendium that may be improper or poorly expressed, may the virtuous scholars forgive me for that; that is to say, it should be pardoned. || 7 ||

**Vernacular Translation—** Other teachers (such as the Greeks <note>original: "Yavanas"</note> and others) have described this science of astrology in great detail. Following them, I have summarized all the subjects mentioned in those scriptures. In this book, I have presented subtle subjects specifically to make the horn of the intellect stainless (sharp). Whatever errors I may have committed herein, may the noble-minded gentlemen forgive them. || 7 ||

->Now, regarding the restoration of what is poorly done or omitted due to the passage of time,<-
->he addresses the request of the virtuous in the Vasantatilaka meter:<-

->**Wherever this work, in its travels, meets with ruin**<-
->**through errors in writing or the oral transmission of the unlearned,**<-
->**or whatever I have poorly done or left incomplete here,**<-
->**the wise should rectify that, casting aside all prejudice.**<- || 8 ||

**Commentary:** "Wherever this work..." etc. As this book circulates, whatever destruction it meets—meaning whatever is lost due to the faults of scribes—the wise scholar, having understood the proper sequence from the mouths of the "highly learned" (those who have heard much scripture), should rectify it in the proper order, abandoning "prejudice" or malice. Such scholars are capable of refinement through their desire for the true meaning of the scriptures. Alternatively, whatever has been "poorly done" (badly composed) by me, or is "incomplete" (unfinished), should be corrected after careful reflection. || 8 ||

**Vernacular Translation—** Through the promotion of this book, whatever letters or words are destroyed due to the faults of scribes and others, or whatever improper things I myself have done, or whatever has been minimized or omitted through oversight—let the discerning people, through the words of the highly learned or by their own expanded intellect, purify those parts after abandoning all jealousy. || 8 ||

Now, in the Vasantatilaka meter, he mentions the name of his father, Aditya-dasa; the village named Kapitthaka; how he obtained the arrival of knowledge from his father; his own residence in Ujjain; and the name of this Horoscopy scripture:

->**The son of Aditya-dasa, from whom he obtained his knowledge,**<-
->**having received a boon of grace from the Sun God at Kapitthaka,**<-
->**Varahamihira of Avanti, having thoroughly studied the teachings of the Sages,**<-
->**composed this beautiful work on Horoscopy.**<- || 9 ||

**Commentary:** "The son of Aditya-dasa..." etc. There was a Brahmin named Aditya-dasa; his son is the one who obtained "knowledge" (wisdom) from that very father. In the village called Kapitthaka...

<vocab>Brihat Jataka (The Great Birth Chart), Chapter on Conclusion, Varahamihira (the author), Aditya-dasa (his father), Kapitthaka (his birthplace), Avanti (modern Ujjain), Horoscopy (Hora-shastra), Astrology (Jyotish)</vocab>

<summary>Varahamihira concludes his seminal work on astrology by asking future scholars to correct any scribal errors or authorial oversights and provides his biographical details, identifying himself as a devotee of the Sun God from Ujjain.</summary>

# Commentary by Bhattotpala with Hindi Translation

In the village <note>Kapitthaka</note>, he who obtained a boon and grace from the Lord Savitar <note>the Sun God</note>. A resident of Avanti, or the city of Ujjain. Who is he? Varahamihira. Having observed and reflected upon the opinions of the Sages <note>the ancient Rishis</note> and their composed scriptures, and having accurately grasped the reality of things, he created this beautiful and accessible *Hora* <term>Horoscopy/Natal Astrology</term> scripture. || 6 ||

**Vernacular Translation—** The teacher named Varahamihira—son of the Brahmin Adityadasa, a resident of the city of Ujjain—having received knowledge from that same Adityadasa (his father) and having obtained the gift of a boon through the worship of Lord Suryanarayana <note>the Sun</note> located in the village of Kapittha, composed this charming *Hora* (Natal) scripture after examining the views of the Sages. || 6 ||

*Now, having begun the scriptures with salutations to the virtuous and concluding them likewise, he offers a final salutation to the ancient authors in this Arya verse:*

> This scripture has been compiled by one whose intellect was graced by bowing at the feet of the Sun, the Sages, and his Teacher. Salutations be to the ancient composers. || 10 ||

->Thus ends the Brihat Jataka composed by the Teacher Varahamihira<-
->The Twenty-Eighth Chapter: Conclusion<-

**"The Sun..." etc.—** The Sun (the Day-maker) and all the other planets; the Sages such as Vashistha and others; and the Teacher, Adityadasa. By bowing at their feet, grace and compassion were obtained. By me, whose intellect was guided by that grace obtained through bowing at the feet of the Sun, the Sages, and my Teacher, this scripture has been compiled and accepted. Therefore, let there be a salutation to the ancient composers, the makers of the earlier scriptures. Through this salutation, grace is achieved. "Salutations"—let there be well-being. || 10 ||

->Thus ends the Twenty-Eighth Chapter, the Conclusion, in the Commentary on the Brihat Jataka composed by the illustrious Bhattotpala<-

**Vernacular Translation—** Having obtained wisdom through the compassion received by bowing at the lotus-feet of the Lord Sun, the Sages like Vashistha, and my Teacher (my worshipful father Adityadasa), I (Varahamihira) have compiled this book. Therefore, may my salutations be to those Sages who were the ancient composers of the scriptures. || 10 ||

## Chapter on Conclusion in the Brihat Jataka

Whatever I have omitted in this explanation, whatever is devoid of logic, or whatever has been written in error, may all that be brought to clarity <note>The author is humbly asking future scholars to correct any mistakes found in his commentary</note>. ||4||
On the fifth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Chaitra <note>March/April</note>, on a Thursday, in the Shaka year measured by the Vasus (8), the eights (8), and the eights (8) — that is, 888 <note>approximately 966 CE</note> — this commentary was completed by me. ||5||
By composing this commentary on this science, whatever little merit I have earned, may people become free from envy and adorned with goodness through it. ||6||
<note>Verse 7 contains complex technical word-play regarding the author's lineage and the physical production of the manuscript</note> This commentary by Utpala <note>Bhattotpala</note> was caused to be written while residing in the place of learning. ||7||

->**Thus ends the Commentary on the Brihat Jataka composed by Bhattotpala.**<-

In the Vikrama year measured by the full (0), the fires (3), the voids (0), and the eyes (2) — that is, 2030 <note>approximately 1973 CE</note> — on the thirteenth lunar day of the bright fortnight of Chaitra, on a Sunday;
This commentary named *Sarartha Deepika* <note>The Lamp of Essential Meaning</note> on this work called *Brihat Jataka* spoken by Varahamihira, has reached completion.
By Shri Sitarama Sharma, a resident of Chaugama village in the heart of the Mithila region, who teaches students in Kashi <note>Varanasi</note>;
This was created to reside in the hearts of the community of readers and good people. Having pierced the darkness of ignorance, may it be known as a true explanation.

->**Thus ends the commentary named Sarartha Deepika in the vernacular exposition of the Brihat Jataka composed by Varahamihira.**<-

***

(1) Here, the reading "in the Shaka year measured by the Vasus, eights, and eights" is appropriate. Because the birth of Bhattotpala occurred after the birth of Bhaskaracharya <note>A famous 12th-century mathematician/astronomer</note>, as he himself says in the opening verse of this very work:
> "From the contact of the sun's rays, the orb of nectar <note>the moon</note> shines with moonlight in the direction of the sun."

Bhattotpala relies on this as evidence. And the time of Bhaskaracharya's birth is stated at the end of the *Siddhanta Shiromani*:
> "My birth occurred in the Shaka year measured by the flavors (6), the qualities (3), the void (0), and the earth (1) — 1036 <note>1114 CE</note>. At the age of thirty-four (34), I composed the Siddhanta Shiromani."

By this, the Shaka year 1036 is certain. Therefore, some time after the Shaka year 1036, Bhattotpala set out to write his commentary. Thus, the year can be imagined as 1088 Shaka <note>The editor is correcting the 888 date mentioned above to 1088 to resolve a perceived historical conflict</note>. Wise men should consider that the digit for "one thousand" was likely lost through the errors of scribes, teachers, or students.

->— FINIS —<-

# Supplementary Edition
## Chapter on Auspicious Timing (Muhurta)

> Whichever lunar day, zodiac sign, degree, or lunar mansion is pierced <note>original: "viddham"; refers to Vedha, an astronomical interference or "piercing" by a planet</note> by a cruel planet <note>malefic planets like Mars or Saturn</note>, one should diligently avoid that for all auspicious activities. (1)

If the lunar day, zodiac sign, degree <note>specifically the Navamsha or ninth-part division</note>, or lunar mansion <note>Nakshatra</note> is afflicted by a malefic planet, one must make every effort to abandon it for any favorable undertaking. (1)

> One does not find joy in marriage, one does not return from a journey, and a patient is not released from disease if the endeavor is begun during a time of piercing <note>Vedha-vela</note>. (2)

If a marriage is performed during these afflicted timings, there is no happiness; if a journey is started, one does not return; and if a disease begins at such a time, the patient is not cured. (2)

> Destruction of one's position occurs from the piercing of the zodiac sign; loss occurs from the piercing of the lunar mansion; and death occurs from the piercing of the degree. This is the result of cruel planets. (3)

If a malefic planet afflicts the zodiac sign, it leads to the loss of one's place or status; if it afflicts the lunar mansion, it causes general loss; if it afflicts the degree, it results in death. If all three are afflicted, death is certain; there is no doubt in this. (3)

> When the zodiac sign, lunar mansion, and degree are pierced, death occurs and not otherwise. Wherever the gaze <note>Drishti; planetary aspect</note> of a cruel planet falls, one should avoid auspicious work there. (4)
> Where the gaze of the Sun falls, the mind suffers distress. In the gaze of Mars, slaughter, war, and death certainly occur. (5)

One should also abandon any auspicious work in those zodiac signs or divisions upon which the gaze of malefic planets falls. (4) The gaze of the Sun causes mental sorrow; the gaze of Mars leads to violence, conflict, and certain death. (5)

> In the gaze of Saturn, there is loss and bodily pain. Rahu <note>the North Node of the Moon</note> causes injury and falls, and Ketu <note>the South Node of the Moon</note> provides poison. (6)
> If there is a gaze from auspicious planets, success in all things is produced. In the gaze of Mercury, there is wisdom; when the gaze of Jupiter occurs... (7)

The gaze of Saturn brings about loss and physical suffering; the gaze of Rahu causes accidents or injuries; and the gaze of Ketu results in poisoning. (6) Conversely, if an auspicious planet <note>benefics like Jupiter, Venus, or a strong Moon</note> casts its gaze, then success is achieved in all types of work. The gaze of Mercury grants intelligence, and when the gaze of Jupiter falls [upon a sign]...

<note>The text ends mid-sentence, continuing the benefits of Jupiter's aspect on the following page.</note>

It contrasts these with the positive effects of beneficial planets like Mercury and Jupiter.</summary>

# Chapter on Disease

-> If an affliction caused by a cruel planet occurs at the time of illness, retrograde motion leads to death, while rapid motion leads to prolonged suffering. <note>original: "रोगकाले भवेद्वेध: क्रूरखेचरसंभव: । वक्रगत्या भवेन्मृत्यु: शीघ्रगत्या रुजान्वित: ॥१॥"</note> <-

At the time of illness, if the affliction <term>Vedha|A technical term in astrology referring to the 'piercing' or interference of a planet's influence on a specific point</term> is caused by a "cruel" planet <note>Malefics like Mars or Saturn</note> in retrograde motion, the patient dies. If the planet is in rapid motion, the disease persists. ||1||

-> Under the Sun, there is suffering from fever; Mars causes life-threatening diseases. Fear of epilepsy occurs under Rahu, and under Saturn, one should point to sharp piercing pains. When combined with an affliction of the birth star, eye pain is produced, as well as mental distress, agitation, and confusion of the mind. <note>original: "आदित्ये ज्वरपीडा स्याद्बौमश्च प्राणरोगद: । अपस्मारभयं राहौ मन्दे शूलं विनिर्दिशेत् ॥२॥ नक्षत्रवेधसंयुक्ते चक्षु:पीडा प्रजायते । मनस्तापं तथोद्वेगं मतिभ्रमोऽथ जायते ॥३॥"</note> <-

If the Sun is the afflicting agent during the time of illness, there is suffering from fever; if it is Mars, there are life-threatening diseases (such as respiratory issues or chronic cough); if it is Rahu or Ketu <note>The north and south nodes of the Moon</note>, there is fear of epilepsy; and if it is Saturn, one should predict colic or sharp piercing pains. ||2|| If the affliction of a cruel planet falls upon the Nakshatra <note>The star constellation associated with the person's name</note>, it causes eye pain, mental anguish, agitation, and the intellect becomes corrupted. ||3||

-> When the letters of the name are afflicted by cruel planets, burning sensations, wasting away, and fever occur. The wise should know this as an excess of bile and vomiting. <note>original: "क्रूरैर्नामाक्षरैर्विद्धे दाह: शोषो ज्वरो भवेत् । पित्तोद्रेकस्तथा छर्दिरिति ज्ञेयं विचक्षणै: ॥४॥"</note> <-

If the affliction of a cruel planet falls upon the specific letters of the individual's name, there is a burning sensation in the body, wasting or pulmonary consumption, suffering from fever, and distress such as vomiting caused by an excess of bile. ||4||

-> In an affliction of the vowels, there is pain in the mouth and likewise ear disease. There is also the aching of teeth when there is a cruel affliction; of this there is no doubt. <note>original: "स्वरे वेधे मुखे पीड़ा कर्णव्याधिस्तथैव च । दन्तानां पीडनं तत्र क्रूरवेधे न संशय: ॥५॥"</note> <-

If the affliction of a cruel planet falls upon the vowels of the name, there will be disease in the mouth, toothache, and pain in the ear. There is no doubt about this. ||5||

-> In an affliction of the lunar day, there is pain of the skin, as well as tumors and abdominal swellings. There is headache, swelling of the feet, and pain in all the joints. <note>original: "तिथिवेधे त्वचां पीडा गडगुल्मादिका तथा । शिरोर्तिपादशोथश्च सर्वसन्धिषु पीडनम् ॥६॥"</note> <-

->If the piercing occurs in the Zodiac Sign, there will be disease, loss of digestive fire, and outbursts of anger.<-
->Phlegm is produced there, and there will be pain in the internal channels. ||7||<-

If the <term>Vedha</term> <note>Vedha refers to a "piercing" or astrological aspect where a planet's position aligns with and affects another point in the grid.</note> of a cruel planet <note>Malefic planets like Mars or Saturn.</note> falls upon the Name-Tithi <note>The lunar day associated with the first letter of a person's name.</note>, there will be suffering such as itching of the skin, diseases like abdominal tumors, pain in the head, swelling in the feet, and extreme pain in all the joints. ||6|| If the Vedha of a cruel planet falls upon the Name-Sign, there will be the disease of <term>Agnimandya</term> <note>A weakened digestive fire or metabolic depression.</note>, injury from water etc., outbursts of anger, disorders of phlegm (<term>Kapha</term>), and distress of the internal channels, meaning a disease of the internal organs. ||7||

->In the pierced location, there is defeat in battle; in a fort, a breach is created.<-
->If a poet/strategist enters there, there is surely a wound from combat. ||8||<-

If one wages war in a pierced direction, there will be defeat (meaning, in the <term>Sarvatobhadra Chakra</term>, the direction in which the constellations etc. are pierced from the east onwards, defeat comes from that direction). Similarly, if the <term>Kala</term> <note>A specific unit of time or lunar phase in the grid.</note> is pierced, it is broken; and if a "Kavi" <note>Literally "poet," but here referring to a clever strategist or commander.</note> enters the pierced location (meaning, if one suddenly attacks a powerful enemy when the opportunity arises), he will receive wounds from the battle. ||8||

### Section on the Setting of Directions

->In whichever direction from the East onwards the Sun resides in Taurus and the following signs,<-
->That direction is known as "Set" (Asta); the remaining three are always "Risen" (Udita). ||1||<-

In this Sarvatobhadra Chakra, groups of three zodiac signs each are written in the directions starting from the East. That is: Taurus, Gemini, and Cancer are in the East; Leo, Virgo, and Libra are in the South; Scorpio, Sagittarius, and Capricorn are in the West; and Aquarius, Pisces, and Aries are written in the North. Among these, whichever direction contains the signs where the Sun is currently positioned, that one direction remains "set" <note>Astrologically inactive or obscured.</note> for three months, and the three directions of the remaining nine signs remain "risen" <note>Active or auspicious.</note> for 6 months. ||1||

->The vowels in the Northeast are known in the East; those in the Southeast are in the South.<-
->Those in the Southwest are in the West; those in the Northwest are considered in the North. ||2||<-
->Constellations, vowels, letters, signs, lunar days, and directions—<-
->All these are known to be "set" where the Sun resides for three months. ||3||<-

The vowels in the Northeast corner set with the East; the vowels in the Southeast corner set with the South; the vowels in the Southwest corner set with the West; and the vowels in the Northwest corner set with the North. That is, these vowels set along with these directions. ||2|| The constellations (<term>Nakshatras</term>), vowels, letters, zodiac signs, lunar days (<term>Tithis</term>), and the direction itself belonging to the direction where the Sun is positioned must all be understood as "set" for three months. And the constellations etc. of the remaining three directions should be known as "risen" for 6 months. ||3||

# Appendix Edition of the Brihat Jataka

## Chapter on the Ascendant of Inquiry
<note>Sanskrit: Prashna-lagna-prakaranam. This section deals with 'Prashna' or Horary astrology, where a chart is cast for the exact moment a question is asked.</note>

One should first consider the "piercing" <term>Vedha; an astronomical interference or aspect</term> of the first letter of the words spoken by the inquirer. If a malefic planet causes this interference, the result is declared evil; the primary obstacles should be explained accordingly. ||1||

<note>The following is a commentary on the verse above:</note>
One should first consider whether there is an interference (Vedha) by any planet on the first letter of the words uttered by the inquirer's mouth. If there is an interference, the auspicious or inauspicious result of that question depends on the planet causing the interference. If there is no interference at all, then the result should be determined according to the school of Kerala or according to the Ascendant of the inquiry. ||1||

At the time of inquiry, if the Ascendant is pierced by cruel planets <note>malefics like Mars or Saturn</note>, it is known as corrupted. If by gentle planets <note>benefics like Jupiter or Venus</note>, it is auspicious. If by both, the result is considered mixed. ||2||

The result of an Ascendant that is not pierced by planets should be understood by the master astrologer according to the inherent nature of that sign—whether it is "movable" or otherwise—as has been spoken in the tradition. ||3||

If a **Movable Ascendant** <term>Chara Lagna; signs that indicate change and movement</term> is rising: a lost object is difficult to recover, a patient may face death, and a child born at that time is said to have a short lifespan. ||4||

If a **Fixed Ascendant** <term>Sthira Lagna; signs that indicate stability and permanence</term> is rising: a lost object is recovered in a short time, a patient recovers after a long period, and a child born then possesses a long life. ||5||

In the case of a **Dual Ascendant** <term>Dvisvabhava Lagna; signs of a fluctuating or double nature</term>: there is a quick recovery of a lost item, a patient improves quickly, and a child born then will certainly have a medium lifespan. ||6||

In this manner, for all undertakings, the wise should determine the auspicious or inauspicious results by recognizing the movable or other natures of the Ascendant at the time of inquiry. ||7||

The four **Movable Ascendants** are Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn. Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius are **Fixed**. The remaining <insert>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces</insert> are known as **Dual** signs. ||8||

<summary>This page explains how to predict the outcome of a question based on the astrological sign rising at the moment of inquiry, categorizing signs into movable, fixed, and dual types to determine longevity, health, and the recovery of lost items.</summary>

# Chapter on the Affliction of Countries via the Tortoise Diagram

**If the three-star groups starting with Krittika are pierced by cruel planets according to the Tortoise Diagram,**
**The countries corresponding to the navel and other body parts are destroyed in sequence. ||1||**

In the *Kurma Chakra* <note>Tortoise Diagram: a traditional astrological map of India where the country is envisioned as a tortoise facing East</note>, the constellations starting from Krittika are divided into groups of three across the nine parts of the tortoise's body. Whichever body part's constellations are "pierced" <note>term: Vedha (piercing/affliction); an astrological aspect where a planet's influence strikes a specific point</note> by a cruel planet <note>term: Krura Graha; malefic planets like Mars, Saturn, or Rahu</note>, the countries associated with that body part face destruction. ||1||

->Knowledge of Countries via Constellations<-

**Krittika, Rohini, and the Lunar constellation <note>original: "Saumya" referring to Mrigashira</note> reside in the navel of the Tortoise.**
**Saketa, Mithila, Champa, Kaushambi, and Kaushiki; ||2||**
**Ahichhatra, Gaya, Vindhya, Antarvedi, Mekhala,**
**Kanyakubja, and Prayaga—the Middle Country is destroyed. ||3||**

Krittika, Rohini, and Mrigashira—these three constellations are in the center (navel) of the Tortoise Diagram. If these are afflicted by a malefic planet, then the "Middle Countries" <note>term: Madhyadesha; the central heartland of Northern India</note> such as Saketa (Ayodhya), Mithila, Champa, Kaushambi, Kaushiki, Ahichhatra, Gaya, the Vindhya region, Antarvedi, Mekhala, Kanyakubja (Kannauj), and Prayaga (Allahabad) are destroyed. ||2-3||

**Ardra <note>original: "Raudra"</note>, Punarvasu, and Pushya are situated in the head of the Tortoise.**
**Gauda, Hastibandha, Pancharashtra, and Kamarupa; ||4||**
**Aindra and Magadha likewise,**
**The banks of the Reva and Mevasa—the Eastern regions are destroyed. ||5||**

Ardra, Punarvasu, and Pushya—these three constellations are in the head (East) of the Tortoise Diagram. If these are afflicted by a malefic planet, then the Eastern countries such as Gauda (Bengal), Hastibandha, Pancharashtra, Kamarupa (Assam), Aindra, Magadha (Bihar), the banks of the Reva (Narmada river), and Mevasa are destroyed. ||4-5||

**Ashlesha, Magha, and Purva-Phalguni are in the foot of the South-East.**
**Anga, Vanga, Kalinga, Kurvaja, and Kosala; ||6||**
**Dahala, Jayandra, and Stulanjika,**
**Uddiyana and Varata—the South-Eastern region is destroyed. ||7||**

Ashlesha, Magha, and Purva-Phalguni—these three constellations are in the South-East foot of the Tortoise Diagram. If these are afflicted by a malefic planet, then the South-Eastern countries such as Anga, Vanga (Bengal), Kalinga (Odisha), Kurvaja, Kosala, Dahala, Jayandra, Tulanjika, Uddiyana (Orissa), and Varata are destroyed. ||6-7||

**Uttara-Phalguni, Hasta, and Chitra reside in the Southern belly.**
**Dardura, Mahendra, Vanavasa, and Sinhala; ||8||**
**Tapi, Bhimaratha, Lanka, Trikuta, and Malaya,**
**Shriparvata and Kishkindha—these are destroyed in the South. ||9||**

The northern countries, including Kashmir, Ghazni, Khorasan, Mathura, the lands of the <term>Mlechhas</term><note>A term used historically to refer to non-Vedic or foreign peoples</note>, the Khashas, Kedarmandal, and those residing in the Himalayas, face destruction. ||16-17||

**Revati, Ashwini, and Bharani are in the North-East quadrant.**

The three <term>Nakshatras</term><note>Lunar mansions or star clusters used in Vedic astrology</note>—Revati, Ashwini, and Bharani—reside in the North-East foot of the <term>Kurma Chakra</term><note>Literally "Tortoise Wheel," a traditional astrological map that overlays the stars onto the geography of the earth</note>. The countries associated with the body part <note>of the "Earth-Tortoise"</note> where malefic planets are positioned suffer destruction in various ways. Furthermore, the countries associated with the body part whose stars are "pierced" <note>original: "vedha"; an astrological aspect or intersection</note> by malefic planets will surely experience some form of agony. However, in the regions where auspicious planets are situated or where there is an auspicious "piercing," all kinds of favorable results occur. If there is a mixture of both, one should understand the result to be mixed. ||16-20||

**The Earth-Tortoise has been described, starting from Krittika and ending with Bharani.**
**For countries and other entities, the same sequence is remembered, starting from their own respective stars. ||21||**

In the aforementioned "Earth-Tortoise" model, nine divisions were made using groups of three stars each, beginning with Krittika and ending with Bharani. Similarly, for the "Tortoise" of a country, city, village, or field, one should create nine divisions in the same sequence, starting with the specific star associated with its name. Then, the effects of the planetary "piercing" should be understood according to the previously mentioned method. ||21||

**Weighed goods, vessels, liquids, grains, and four-legged animals like elephants and horses;**
**Everything becomes expensive wherever a malefic planet is established. ||22||**

Where the arrangement of malefic planetary "piercing" exists, weighed goods <note>items sold by weight</note>, vessels <note>interpreted here as precious stones/jewelry</note>, liquids <note>such as honey or syrups</note>, grains <note>such as wheat</note>, and four-legged animals like elephants and horses all become "greatly valued" <note>original: "maharghata"; meaning they become very expensive or rare even for those with much wealth</note>. ||22||

**The letters of the names of countries and goods which are pierced by auspicious or inauspicious planets;**
**Their fortune or misfortune is specifically determined through the Sarvatobhadra Chakra. ||23||**

If the letters in the name of a country and a specific commodity are simultaneously "pierced" by an auspicious planet, that commodity becomes cheaper in that country. If pierced by an inauspicious planet, it becomes more expensive. If pierced by both types of planets, the result follows the more powerful planet. A detailed decision on this will be written later in the section on prices <note>original: "Arghaprakaran"</note>. ||23||

Header: Cycle of Sub-periods within the Vimshottari Great Period 463

# Cycle of Sub-periods within the Vimshottari Great Period
<note>The Vimshottari Dasha is a 120-year planetary cycle used in Vedic astrology to predict the timing of events. Each "Great Period" (Mahadasha) is ruled by a planet and subdivided into smaller nested intervals.</note>

### Within the Great Period of Jupiter: Jupiter Sub-period
->Sub-sub-periods<-
->2 years 1 month 18 days<-

| Planet | Month | Day | Ghati |
